title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text: 雲南鄉試錄〔嘉靖二十二年〕
punctuated: 《雲南鄉試錄》〔嘉靖二十二年〕
translation_en: Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination〔Twenty-second year of Jiajing (1543)〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄序
夫命鄉論秀其猶古之遺乎
然而法制之畀藝極之陳風
聲之樹蓋至我
聖朝而獨備矣茲歲丙午大比維
期先時禮部覈故事集羣議
請于
===
上乃降發
綸音凡以登賢剔弊申敕有加雲
南於諸藩最遠尤汲汲先事
之備維歲首月巡按御史郝
銘輒謀于藩臬緘詞束幣走
使四方徵校職以司文柄其
他繕塲屋庀器具以至筐篚
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄序

夫命鄉論秀，其猶古之遺乎？然而法制之畀、藝極之陳、風聲之樹，蓋至我聖朝而獨備矣。茲歲丙午，大比維期。先時，禮部覈故事，集羣議，請于上，乃降發綸音，凡以登賢剔弊，申敕有加。雲南於諸藩最遠，尤汲汲先事之備。維歲首月，巡按御史郝銘輒謀于藩臬，緘詞束幣，走使四方，徵校職以司文柄。其他繕塲屋、庀器具，以至筐篚
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

The command that local communities assess their outstanding men—is this not a surviving practice of antiquity? Yet the provision of laws and regulations, the establishment of standards for literary accomplishment [?], and the cultivation of an exemplary influence attained their full realization only under our sagely dynasty. This year, bingwu, the triennial examination fell due. In advance, the Ministry of Rites examined precedents, gathered opinions, and submitted a request to His Majesty. An imperial rescript was then issued, reinforcing the injunctions for promoting worthy men and eliminating abuses.

Yunnan, the most distant of the provinces, was especially diligent in making preparations beforehand. In the first month of the year, Regional Inspector Hao Ming consulted with the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions. He sealed letters, bundled gifts of silk, and dispatched messengers in all directions to recruit educational officials to take charge of literary assessment. Other preparations included repairing the examination compound and providing equipment, down to baskets and hampers…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
餼牽之細咸戒有司調度以
需期且届御史劉廷儀奉
命代至毅然曰惟是監臨豈異人
任爰殫厥心力諸所規畫益
愼而詳于時鎮守黔國公沐
朝輔素敦儒雅樂觀
盛典巡撫右僉都御史應大猷
綏懷善類式增士氣考試官
則佐偕教諭彭洛同考試官
則教諭莫遺賢胡悊劉濟民
羅萬鵬咸應聘而至提調則
右參政劉伯躍右參議沈繼
美監試則副使譙孟龍僉事
李文鳳自餘百執事咸愼簡
punctuated: 餼牽之細，咸戒有司調度以需。期且届，御史劉廷儀奉命代至，毅然曰：「惟是監臨，豈異人任？」爰殫厥心力，諸所規畫，益愼而詳。于時，鎮守黔國公沐朝輔素敦儒雅，樂觀盛典；巡撫右僉都御史應大猷綏懷善類，式增士氣。考試官則佐偕教諭彭洛，同考試官則教諭莫遺賢、胡悊、劉濟民、羅萬鵬，咸應聘而至。提調則右參政劉伯躍、右參議沈繼美，監試則副使譙孟龍、僉事李文鳳。自餘百執事，咸愼簡
translation_en:
…down to such details as provisions and livestock, the responsible officials were all instructed to arrange supplies in readiness. As the appointed date approached, Censor Liu Tingyi arrived under imperial orders to take over. He declared resolutely: “As for supervising this examination, how could that be someone else’s responsibility?” He therefore devoted all his energy to the task, making every arrangement still more careful and detailed. At this time, Mu Chaofu, Duke of Qianguo, who commanded the garrison, had long cultivated Confucian learning and refinement and gladly witnessed this grand ceremony. Ying Dayou, Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, nurtured and reassured worthy men, thereby raising the scholars’ spirits.

The Examiners were Zuo and Confucian School Instructor Peng Luo; the Associate Examiners were Confucian School Instructors Mo Yixian, Hu Zhe, Liu Jimin, and Luo Wanpeng. All came in response to invitations. The Proctors were Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Liu Boyue and Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner Shen Jimei. The examination monitors were Surveillance Vice Commissioner Qiao Menglong and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Li Wenfeng. All the remaining functionaries were carefully selected…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以充比入鎖院乃合陞任提
學副使吳鵬署管僉事楊儒
魯所選士千五百有奇三試
之拔其雋者四十人幷錄文
之優者以
獻蓋昔者解額嘗羨于此而貴
州之士附焉今雖稍損而雲
===
南之士顓之顧人文勃鬱以
興主司有不獲盡取之憾亶
乎盛哉事既竣佐乃再拜颺
言曰首庶物而寧萬國者惟
聖乎曠千載而幸一遘者惟
時乎雲南山川形勢之勝誠
亦天地奧區然故靡莫之域
punctuated:
以充。比入鎖院，乃合陞任提學副使吳鵬、署管僉事楊儒魯所選士千五百有奇，三試之，拔其雋者四十人，幷錄文之優者以獻。蓋昔者解額嘗羨于此，而貴州之士附焉；今雖稍損，而雲南之士顓之。顧人文勃鬱以興，主司有不獲盡取之憾，亶乎盛哉！
事既竣，佐乃再拜颺言曰：「首庶物而寧萬國者，惟聖乎！曠千載而幸一遘者，惟時乎！雲南山川形勢之勝，誠亦天地奧區，然故靡莫之域
translation_en:
…to fill the posts. When we entered the examination compound and were confined within it, we assembled the more than fifteen hundred candidates selected by Wu Peng, promoted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, and Yang Rulu, the Surveillance Assistant Commissioner acting in charge. We examined them in three sessions and selected forty of the most outstanding, also transcribing the best essays for presentation to the throne. Formerly, the quota for provincial graduates had exceeded this number, but candidates from Guizhou were then included. Although the quota has now been somewhat reduced, it belongs exclusively to candidates from Yunnan. Yet literary talent flourishes so abundantly that the examiners regret being unable to select all who deserve it. Truly, what a flourishing age!
When the work was complete, Zuo bowed twice and proclaimed: “Who but the sage sovereign presides over all things and brings peace to the myriad states! What an age, which one is fortunate to encounter but once in a thousand years! With its magnificent mountains, rivers, and terrain, Yunnan is indeed a secluded treasure of Heaven and Earth. Yet it was formerly the territory of the Mimo…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而西南徼外地也唐虞聲敎
所未之訖成周禮樂所未之
覃秦漢而降威嚴綏輯所未
之能必而定也迨我
聖祖高皇帝混一寰區誕敷文德
籍其地而郡邑之淑其人而
庠校之斂其才而科目之蓋
===
始駸駸乎振起莫不誦法孔
子而業專經術矣重以
列聖休澤熈洽
皇上道化彌隆沾濡涵煦百八十
禩于茲蒸蒸乎蜚英騰茂人
懷利賓固其宜也易恆之彖
曰聖人久於其道而天下化
punctuated: 而西南徼外地也，唐虞聲敎所未之訖，成周禮樂所未之覃，秦漢而降威嚴綏輯所未之能必而定也。迨我聖祖高皇帝混一寰區，誕敷文德，籍其地而郡邑之，淑其人而庠校之，斂其才而科目之，蓋始駸駸乎振起，莫不誦法孔子而業專經術矣。重以列聖休澤熈洽，皇上道化彌隆，沾濡涵煦百八十禩于茲，蒸蒸乎蜚英騰茂，人懷利賓，固其宜也。《易》恆之彖曰：「聖人久於其道而天下化
translation_en: …and was a land beyond the southwestern frontier, unreached by the civilizing teachings of Tang and Yu, untouched by the rites and music of the flourishing Zhou, and a place that, from the Qin and Han onward, neither stern authority nor pacification could reliably bring under settled rule. Only when our Sagely Progenitor, Emperor Gao, unified the realm and spread his civil virtue far and wide did he register its lands and organize them into prefectures and counties, cultivate its people by establishing schools, and gather its talented men through the examination system. Then, at last, it began rapidly to flourish: all recited and followed Confucius, devoting their studies to the learning of the Classics. To this were added the beneficent blessings of successive sage emperors, spreading in harmonious abundance, and the ever more exalted moral transformation wrought by His Majesty. Nourished and nurtured for these one hundred and eighty years, its men have increasingly gained illustrious reputations and displayed outstanding talents. That each should cherish the prospect of being received as a guest at court is surely fitting. The Commentary on the Judgment for the hexagram Constancy in the Book of Changes says: “The sage abides long in his Way, and all under Heaven is transformed…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
成夫恒之為卦有雷風相與
之象焉風行雷動含生之類
莫不鬯達昭蘇矧靈秀攸鍾
有弗靡然響應其庸以遐阻
自外乎雖然古之取士或以
德進或以事舉或以言揚言
固其又次也至論不朽有三
===
立德立功立言復並舉之蓋
功以德立臯夔旦奭其選也
言以德立典謨訓誥其選也
夫何軒輕之有諸士今之見
錄有司固惟其言矣嗣是宣
猷展采惟所任使以圖稱塞
無寧弗以道德自命邪誠自
punctuated: 成。」夫恒之為卦，有雷風相與之象焉。風行雷動，含生之類莫不鬯達昭蘇，矧靈秀攸鍾，有弗靡然響應，其庸以遐阻自外乎？雖然，古之取士，或以德進，或以事舉，或以言揚，言固其又次也。至論不朽有三，立德、立功、立言，復並舉之。蓋功以德立，臯夔旦奭其選也；言以德立，典謨訓誥其選也。夫何軒輕之有？諸士今之見錄有司，固惟其言矣。嗣是宣猷展采，惟所任使，以圖稱塞，無寧弗以道德自命邪？誠自
translation_en:
…is accomplished.” Now the hexagram Heng (Constancy) contains the image of thunder and wind acting together. As wind courses and thunder stirs, all living things flourish and revive. How much more must those endowed with the finest spiritual gifts respond readily! Could they exclude themselves on account of their remote and inaccessible location? Nevertheless, in antiquity men were selected for service variously through advancement for virtue, recommendation for accomplishments, or recognition for their words. Words certainly ranked after the others. Yet when discussing the three forms of immortality—establishing virtue, establishing achievements, and establishing enduring words—all three are again mentioned together. Achievements are established through virtue: Gao Yao, Kui, Dan (the Duke of Zhou), and Shi (the Duke of Shao) are outstanding examples. Words are established through virtue: the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of the Book of Documents are outstanding examples. What distinction of higher and lower standing, then, is there [?]?

You gentlemen have now been selected by the responsible officials solely on the strength of your words. Hereafter, as you set forth your plans and carry out your undertakings, whatever duties you are assigned, you must seek to discharge them adequately. Surely you would not fail to take the Way and virtue as your own calling? If you truly take upon yourselves…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
命以道德乃明庶敷納有功
不惟敘言不惟服斯未之信
也夫昔也猶未免鄉國之士
矣茲進而與天下士埒又安
得弗尚友古之人邪詩有之
高山仰止景行行止嚮往之
志曷惟其已昔祁奚能舉善
===
人之稱之也曰唯善故能舉
其類佐也不佞竊願徼有榮
譽于諸士是舉也綜理于外
則右布政使劉佐右叅政程
資左叅議郝維嶽副使余承
業僉事文衡安如山都指揮
僉事石邦憲汪勳其宣力維
punctuated:
命以道德，乃明庶敷納，有功不惟敘，言不惟服，斯未之信也。夫昔也，猶未免鄉國之士矣；茲進而與天下士埒，又安得弗尚友古之人邪？詩有之：「高山仰止，景行行止。」嚮往之志，曷惟其已？昔祁奚能舉善，人之稱之也曰：「唯善，故能舉其類。」佐也不佞，竊願徼有榮譽于諸士。
是舉也，綜理于外，則右布政使劉佐、右叅政程資、左叅議郝維嶽、副使余承業、僉事文衡、安如山、都指揮僉事石邦憲、汪勳，其宣力維
translation_en:
…take morality as your own calling, and then, when your abilities are assessed and your words received [?], I cannot believe that your achievements would go unrewarded or your words unheeded. Formerly, you were still merely scholars of your native locality; now you have advanced to stand alongside scholars throughout the realm. How, then, could you fail to seek friendship with the men of antiquity? The Book of Odes says: “We look up to the lofty mountain; we follow the great road.” How could your aspiration toward them ever cease? Long ago, Qi Xi was able to recommend worthy men. Those who praised him said: “Only because he is worthy can he recommend others of his kind.” I, Zuo, am untalented, yet privately hope to gain some honor through you scholars.
For this examination, those who managed affairs outside the examination quarters were Liu Zuo, Right Administration Commissioner; Cheng Zi, Right Vice Administration Commissioner; Hao Weiyue, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; Yu Chengye, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Wen Heng and An Rushan, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Shi Bangxian and Wang Xun, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. Their exertions were…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
均者也從役于公則左布政
使曾存仁左參政黃行可按
察使蔡雲程副使岑萬皆先
事與勞者也宜備書焉
直隸池州府建德縣儒學教
諭朱佐謹序
punctuated:
均者也。從役于公，則左布政使曾存仁、左參政黃行可、按察使蔡雲程、副使岑萬，皆先事與勞者也，宜備書焉。
直隸池州府建德縣儒學教諭朱佐謹序。
translation_en:
…whose contributions were equal. Those who undertook duties in this public service—Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zeng Cunren, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Huang Xingke, Surveillance Commissioner Cai Yuncheng, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Cen Wan—all labored in preparation for the examination. It is fitting to record them all here.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Zhu Zuo, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiande County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試
監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史劉廷儀〔汝修太醫院籍浙江慈谿縣人戊戌進士〕
提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政劉伯躍〔起之江西南昌縣人己丑進士〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參議沈繼美〔子充四川保寧府守禦千戶所人丙戌進士〕
監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司副使譙孟龍〔乾甫四川南充縣人乙未進士〕
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事李文鳳〔廷儀廣西慶遠衛人壬辰進士〕
===
考試官
直隸池州府建德縣儒學教諭朱佐〔思忠浙江海寧衛人甲午貢士〕
河南開封府中牟縣儒學教諭彭洛〔中父江西浮梁縣人庚子貢士〕
同考試官
江西南安府南康縣儒學教諭莫遺賢〔堯卿廣西蒼梧縣人辛卯貢士〕
應天府江浦縣儒學教諭胡悊〔明叔湖廣沅州人甲午貢士〕

印卷官
punctuated:
嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按雲南監察御史劉廷儀〔汝修，太醫院籍，浙江慈谿縣人，戊戌進士〕。

提調官：
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政劉伯躍〔起之，江西南昌縣人，己丑進士〕。
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參議沈繼美〔子充，四川保寧府守禦千戶所人，丙戌進士〕。

雲南等處提刑按察司副使譙孟龍〔乾甫，四川南充縣人，乙未進士〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事李文鳳〔廷儀，廣西慶遠衛人，壬辰進士〕。

直隸池州府建德縣儒學教諭朱佐〔思忠，浙江海寧衛人，甲午貢士〕。

江西南安府南康縣儒學教諭莫遺賢〔堯卿，廣西蒼梧縣人，辛卯貢士〕。

印卷官：
translation_en:
Yunnan Provincial Examination, the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing (1546).

Supervising Official:
Liu Tingyi, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Yunnan. His courtesy name was Ruxiu; he was registered with the Imperial Medical Office and was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuxu year.

Proctors:
Liu Boyue, Right Administration Vice Commissioner in the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Qizhi; he was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the jichou year.
Shen Jimei, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner in the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Zichong; he was from the Guard Battalion of Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, and became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:
Qiao Menglong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner in the Yunnan Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Qianfu; he was a native of Nanchong County, Sichuan, and became a metropolitan graduate in the yiwei year.
Li Wenfeng, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner in the Yunnan Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Tingyi; he was from Qingyuan Guard, Guangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.

Examiners:
Zhu Zuo, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jiande County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His courtesy name was Sizhong; he was from Haining Guard, Zhejiang, and became a tribute student (gongshi) in the jiawu year.
Peng Luo, Instructor at the Confucian School of Zhongmou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he was a native of Fuliang County, Jiangxi, and became a tribute student in the gengzi year.

Associate Examiners:
Mo Yixian, Instructor at the Confucian School of Nankang County, Nan'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Yaoqing; he was a native of Cangwu County, Guangxi, and became a tribute student in the xinmao year.
Hu Zhe, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jiangpu County, Yingtian Prefecture. His courtesy name was Mingshu; he was a native of Yuanzhou, Huguang, and became a tribute student in the jiawu year.
Liu Jimin, Instructor at the Confucian School of Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His courtesy name was Daoqing; he was a native of Luoyang County, Henan, and became a tribute student in the jiawu year.
Luo Wanpeng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yang County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi. His courtesy name was Tengxiao; he was a native of Nanchong County, Sichuan, and became a tribute student in the wuzi year.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷邵元〔子仁浙江仁和縣人監生〕

===

曲靖軍民府推官王一夔〔樂仲，浙江永嘉縣人，監生〕。
translation_en:
Shao Yuan, Manager of the Registry in the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Ziren and was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang. He was an Imperial University student.
Fan Dongzhe, Manager of the Registry in the Yunnan Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Tianqi and was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang. He was an Imperial University student.

Officials responsible for the custody of examination papers:
Chen Guanghua, Prefect of Yunnan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Daoyun and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the sichou [?] year.
Zheng Zhongwei, Prefect of Lin’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zixiu and was a native of Jianli County, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Officials receiving examination papers:
Cai Shaoke, Prefect of Dali Prefecture, had the courtesy name Hongzhe and was a native of Huangyan County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the dingmao year.
Lin Bin, Prefect of Xundian Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Daochun and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He was a tribute student of the renwu year.
Dai Xihao, Vice Prefect of Yongchang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xiufu. He was registered with Liuzhou Guard, Guangxi, and was a native of Ningxiang County, Huguang; he was a tribute student of the simao [?] year.
Wu Wei, Subprefect of Lunan Subprefecture in Chengjiang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Liangchen and was a native of Hanyang County, Huguang. He was a tribute student of the renwu year.

Officials sealing candidates’ identifying information:
Li Dajian, Vice Prefect of Yunnan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Keda and was a native of Rong County, Guangxi. He was a tribute student of the renwu year.
Hong Tingshi, Subprefect of Beisheng Subprefecture, had the courtesy name Deguang and was a native of Nan’an County, Fujian. He was a tribute student of the yiyou year.
Zhu Guan, Subprefect of Binchuan Subprefecture in Dali Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yanchen. He was registered with Anzhuang Guard, Guizhou, and was a native of Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture; he was a tribute student of the wuzi year.
Sun Yi, Magistrate of Baoshan County in Yongchang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yizhi. He was registered with Qingping Guard, Guizhou, and was a native of Rugao County, Zhili; he was a tribute student of the xinmao year.
Wang Pei, Magistrate of Dayao County, Yao Subprefecture, in Yao’an Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhongde. He was registered with Guizhou Guard in Guizhou and was a native of Pengze County, Jiangxi; he was a tribute student of the dingyou year.

Transcription officials:
Wang Yikui, Judge of Qujing Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Lezhong and was a native of Yongjia County, Zhejiang. He was an Imperial University student.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南右衛指揮使楊翺〔鵬舉江西豐城縣人〕
廣南衛指揮使賀景〔維賢直隸壽州人〕
雲南右衛指揮同知趙昻〔子顒江西宜春縣人〕
雲南中衛指揮同知唐助〔順卿直隸盱眙縣人〕

雲南右衛指揮使楊翺〔鵬舉，江西豐城縣人〕。廣南衛指揮使賀景〔維賢，直隸壽州人〕。雲南右衛指揮同知趙昻〔子顒，江西宜春縣人〕。雲南中衛指揮同知唐助〔順卿，直隸盱眙縣人〕。雲南左衛指揮僉事席璋〔廷用，直隸定遠縣人〕。雲南前衛指揮僉事袁爵〔子修，直隸太常縣人〕。

雲南都指揮使司經歷司經歷金湛〔澄夫，應天府上元縣人，監生〕。雲南都指揮使司斷事司斷事戴璞〔美中，四川梁山縣人，監生〕。雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事胡約〔心甫，江西盧陵縣人，監生〕。雲南等處承宣布政使司照磨所檢校張熲〔宗儒，四川仁壽縣人，監生〕。雲南府通判吳全〔才仲，廣西儀衛司籍，浙江慶元縣人，己卯貢士〕。曲靖軍民府馬龍州同知姜楠〔器之，浙江天台縣人，監生〕。曲靖軍民府霑益州同知張棟〔士隆，直隸涇縣人，監生〕。永昌衛經歷司經歷胡應占〔姚亨，浙江崇德縣人，監生〕。廣南衛經歷司知事宋鸞〔汝和，廣西柳州衛人，監生〕。楚雄衛經歷司知事李勳〔大功，山西廣靈縣人，監生〕。雲南府照磨所照磨曾棐〔思周，江西新淦縣人，監生〕。
translation_en:
Yang Ao, Commander of the Yunnan Right Guard, had the courtesy name Pengju and was from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi.

He Jing, Commander of the Guangnan Guard, had the courtesy name Weixian and was from Shouzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

Zhao Ang, Vice Commander of the Yunnan Right Guard, had the courtesy name Ziyong and was from Yichun County, Jiangxi.

Tang Zhu, Vice Commander of the Yunnan Central Guard, had the courtesy name Shunqing and was from Xuyi County, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

Xi Zhang, Assistant Commander of the Yunnan Left Guard, had the courtesy name Tingyong and was from Dingyuan County, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

Yuan Jue, Assistant Commander of the Yunnan Front Guard, had the courtesy name Zixiu and was from Taichang County [?], in the directly administered metropolitan region.

Provisioning Officials

Jin Zhan was Registrar in the Registry of the Yunnan Regional Military Commission. His courtesy name was Chengfu; he was from Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was an Imperial University student.

Dai Pu was Judge in the Judicial Office of the Yunnan Regional Military Commission. His courtesy name was Meizhong; he was from Liangshan County, Sichuan, and was an Imperial University student.

Hu Yue was Office Manager in the Registry of the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Xinfu; he was from Luling County [?], Jiangxi, and was an Imperial University student.

Zhang Jiong was Investigator in the Records Office of the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Zongru; he was from Renshou County, Sichuan, and was an Imperial University student.

Wu Quan was Assistant Prefect of Yunnan Prefecture. His courtesy name was Caizhong; he was registered with the Guangxi Ceremonial Guard Office, was a native of Qingyuan County, Zhejiang, and was a tribute scholar of the jimao year.

Jiang Nan was Vice Magistrate of Malong Subprefecture, Qujing Military and Civil Prefecture. His courtesy name was Qizhi; he was from Tiantai County, Zhejiang, and was an Imperial University student.

Zhang Dong was Vice Magistrate of Zhanyi Subprefecture, Qujing Military and Civil Prefecture. His courtesy name was Shilong; he was from Jing County, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was an Imperial University student.

Hu Yingzhan was Registrar in the Registry of the Yongchang Guard. His courtesy name was Yaoheng [?]; he was from Chongde County, Zhejiang, and was an Imperial University student.

Song Luan was Clerk in the Registry of the Guangnan Guard. His courtesy name was Ruhe; he was from the Liuzhou Guard, Guangxi, and was an Imperial University student.

Li Xun was Clerk in the Registry of the Chuxiong Guard. His courtesy name was Dagong; he was from Guangling County, Shanxi, and was an Imperial University student.

Zeng Fei was Records Examiner in the Records Office of Yunnan Prefecture. His courtesy name was Sizhou; he was from Xingan County, Jiangxi, and was an Imperial University student.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
孔子曰君子有九思視思明聽思聰色思
温貌思恭言思忠事思敬疑思問忿思
難見得思義
可以賛天地之化育則可以與天地參矣
夫世祿滕固行之矣詩云雨我公田遂及
我私惟助爲有公田由此觀之雖周亦
助也設爲庠序學校以敎之庠者養也
===
校者敎也序者射也夏曰校殷曰序周
曰庠學則三代共之皆所以明人倫也
人倫明於上小民親於下
易
文言曰坤至柔而動也剛至靜而德方
豚魚吉信及豚魚也
子曰易有聖人之道四焉者此之謂也
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

孔子曰：「君子有九思：視思明，聽思聰，色思温，貌思恭，言思忠，事思敬，疑思問，忿思難，見得思義。」

可以賛天地之化育，則可以與天地參矣。

夫世祿，滕固行之矣。詩云：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」惟助爲有公田。由此觀之，雖周亦助也。設爲庠序學校以敎之。庠者養也，校者敎也，序者射也。夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠。學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。人倫明於上，小民親於下。

易

文言曰：「坤至柔而動也剛，至靜而德方。」

豚魚吉，信及豚魚也。

子曰：「易有聖人之道四焉」者，此之謂也。

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Confucius said: “The gentleman has nine considerations: in looking, he considers how to see clearly; in listening, how to hear distinctly; in his expression, how to be mild; in his bearing, how to be respectful; in speaking, how to be sincere; in conducting affairs, how to be reverent; when in doubt, how to inquire; when angry, what trouble may follow; and when he sees something to gain, whether taking it accords with righteousness.”

If one can assist the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth, one can then stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third.

As for hereditary emoluments, Teng has indeed already instituted them. The Book of Odes says: “Let rain fall on our common field, and then reach our private fields.” Only the assistance system has common fields. Viewed in this light, even the Zhou used the assistance system. Establish xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools to instruct the people. Xiang means nurturing; xiao means teaching; xu means archery. Under the Xia, schools were called xiao; under the Yin, xu; and under the Zhou, xiang. The xue school was common to all three dynasties. All served to elucidate human relationships. When human relationships are made clear among those above, the common people below become affectionate toward one another.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Words of the Text says: “Kun is supremely yielding, yet firm in its movement; supremely still, yet square in its virtue.”

“Good fortune with piglets and fish” means that trustworthiness extends even to piglets and fish.

This is what is meant by the Master's statement: “The Book of Changes contains four aspects of the Way of the sages.”

In ancient times, when the sages made the Book of Changes, they intended thereby to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, and the Way of Earth as yielding …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
慎徽五典五典克從納于百揆百揆時敘
賓于四門四門穆穆
若金用汝作礪若濟巨川用汝作舟楫若
歲大旱用汝作霖雨
公其以予萬億年敬天之休
===
惟周公克慎厥始惟君陳克和厥中惟公
克成厥終三后恊心同底于道道洽政
治澤潤生民
詩
于以盛之維筐及筥于以湘之維錡及釜
牧人乃夢衆維魚矣旐維旟矣大人占之
衆維魚矣實維豐年旐維旟矣室家溱
溱
王遣申伯路車乘馬我圖爾居莫如南土
punctuated:
與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書
慎徽五典，五典克從；納于百揆，百揆時敘；賓于四門，四門穆穆。
若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。
公其以予萬億年敬天之休。
惟周公克慎厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。三后恊心，同底于道，道洽政治，澤潤生民。

詩
于以盛之？維筐及筥。于以湘之？維錡及釜。
牧人乃夢：衆維魚矣，旐維旟矣。大人占之：衆維魚矣，實維豐年；旐維旟矣，室家溱溱。
王遣申伯，路車乘馬。我圖爾居，莫如南土。
translation_en:
…and the firm; they established the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They encompassed the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and doubled each; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin and yang and employed yielding and firm lines alternately; thus the six positions in the Changes form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents
He carefully promoted the five cardinal relationships, and they were duly observed. He was appointed to oversee the hundred offices, and all were brought into proper order. He received guests at the four gates, and at all four gates there was reverent harmony.
If I am metal, I shall use you as my whetstone; if I am crossing a great river, I shall use you as my boat and oars; if the year brings a great drought, I shall use you as abundant rain.
May you, Duke, enable me to reverence Heaven’s blessings for countless ages.
The Duke of Zhou carefully attended to the beginning; Jun Chen maintained harmony in the middle; and you, Duke, can bring the work to completion. These three lords, united in purpose, all attained the Way. The Way prevailed, government was well ordered, and their beneficence nourished the people.

Book of Odes
In what shall we gather them? In square baskets and round baskets. In what shall we cook them? In cauldrons with legs and pots without legs.
The herdsmen dreamed: the multitudes became fish, and tortoise-and-serpent banners became falcon banners. The diviner interpreted this: the multitudes becoming fish foretells a plentiful harvest; tortoise-and-serpent banners becoming falcon banners foretells households teeming with people.
The king sent forth Shen Bo, the Earl of Shen, with a grand carriage and a team of four horses. “I have considered where you should dwell; nowhere is better than the southern lands.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
錫爾介圭以作爾寶往近王舅南土是
保
懷柔百神及河喬嶽
春秋
滕子來朝桓公二年齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰
田定公十年
春齊人陳人曹人伐宋莊公十有四年
盟于召陵僖公四年會于蕭魚襄公十有
一年
===
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷定公十
年
禮記
先王之立禮也有本有文忠信禮之本也
義理禮之文也無本不立無文不行
善歌者使人繼其聲善教者使人繼其志
然後聖人作爲父子君臣以爲紀綱紀綱
旣正天下大定天下大定然後正六律
和五聲弦歌詩頌
punctuated:
錫爾介圭，以作爾寶。往近王舅，南土是保。

懷柔百神，及河喬嶽。

春秋
「滕子來朝。」桓公二年。「齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田。」定公十年。
「春，齊人陳人曹人伐宋。」莊公十有四年。
「盟于召陵。」僖公四年。「會于蕭魚。」襄公十有一年。
「夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。」定公十年。

禮記
先王之立禮也，有本有文。忠信，禮之本也；義理，禮之文也。無本不立，無文不行。
善歌者使人繼其聲，善教者使人繼其志。
然後聖人作爲父子君臣，以爲紀綱。紀綱旣正，天下大定。天下大定，然後正六律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌。
translation_en:
…I bestow upon you a great jade tablet, to serve as your treasure. Go forth, the king’s maternal uncle [?]; safeguard the southern lands.

He brings peace to the hundred spirits, including those of the Yellow River and the lofty mountains.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“The Viscount of Teng came to pay court.” Second year of Duke Huan.
“The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” Tenth year of Duke Ding.
“In spring, the men of Qi, Chen, and Cao attacked Song.” Fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
“They made a covenant at Shaoling.” Fourth year of Duke Xi.
“They met at Xiaoyu.” Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.
“In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu.” Tenth year of Duke Ding.

Book of Rites
When the former kings established ritual, it had both a foundation and an outward form. Loyalty and trustworthiness are the foundation of ritual; righteousness and proper principles are its outward form. Without a foundation, it cannot stand; without outward form, it cannot be put into practice.

A skilled singer enables others to continue his song; a skilled teacher enables others to carry on his aspirations.

Then the sages arose and established the relationships of father and son, ruler and minister, as the guiding framework. Once this framework was set right, all under Heaven attained great stability. Once all under Heaven had attained great stability, they then set the six pitch standards correctly, harmonized the five notes, and sang the poems and hymns to the accompaniment of stringed instruments.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
此五行者足以正身安國矣彼國安而天
下安故曰吾觀於鄉而知王道之易易
也
第貳塲
論
道以中庸爲至
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢議可以佐百姓者詔後元年
擬唐以狄仁傑爲侍御史誥儀鳳元年
===
擬宋建邇英延義二閣成羣臣賀表景祐
二年
判語五條
同僚代判署文案
器用布絹不如法
見任官輒自立碑
隱匿孳生官畜產
官吏詞訟家人訴
第參塲
punctuated:
此五行者，足以正身安國矣。彼國安而天下安，故曰：「吾觀於鄉而知王道之易易也。」

第貳塲
論
道以中庸爲至。

詔誥表內科一道
擬漢議可以佐百姓者詔，後元年。
擬唐以狄仁傑爲侍御史誥，儀鳳元年。
擬宋建邇英延義二閣成羣臣賀表，景祐二年。

判語五條
同僚代判署文案。
器用布絹不如法。
見任官輒自立碑。
隱匿孳生官畜產。
官吏詞訟家人訴。

第參塲
translation_en:
These five practices suffice to rectify oneself and bring peace to the state. When the state is at peace, all under Heaven is at peace. Thus it is said: “By observing the village ceremony, I understand how very easy the kingly Way is to put into practice.”

Second Session
Discourse
The Way finds its highest expression in the Mean.

One topic to be selected [?] from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials:
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han, calling for deliberation on measures that could assist the common people: first year of the Later Era.
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang, appointing Di Renjie as Investigating Censor: first year of Yifeng.
Compose a congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials in the manner of the Song, on the completion of the Erying and Yanyi pavilions: second year of Jingyou.

Five Legal Judgments
A colleague renders decisions and signs documents on another official’s behalf.
Utensils, cotton cloth, or silk fail to meet legal standards.
An incumbent official erects a commemorative stele for himself without authorization.
The offspring of government-owned livestock are concealed.
Family members bring lawsuits on behalf of officials or clerks.

Third Session

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第五道
問先聖後聖其揆一也矧一代之興創守
中興之賢聖祖孫相紹盛德大業宜無
有不一者如成湯建中高宗協德文武
受命宣王中興其德業相望者可徵矣
自漢以下光武之於高祖豁達大度史
稱同符憲宗之於文皇勵精求治庶幾
貞觀似矣其視商周果若是班乎洪惟
我
===
太祖高皇帝肇建華夏功德之盛誠有以軼殷
周而陋漢唐矣迨我
皇上晉臨區宇懋昭大德並隆治功丕顯丕承
猗歟休哉顧其間致治之迹雖不能以
皆同然亦有黙契焉者本諸身而達之
家國天下不知凡幾其大且著者昭如
日月則天下臣民之所共仰也可得聞
歟仰惟
至德至治宜無待仰賛一詞而臣子愛
punctuated:
第五道
問：先聖後聖，其揆一也。矧一代之興，創守中興之賢聖，祖孫相紹，盛德大業，宜無有不一者。如成湯建中，高宗協德，文武受命，宣王中興，其德業相望者可徵矣。自漢以下，光武之於高祖，豁達大度，史稱同符；憲宗之於文皇，勵精求治，庶幾貞觀，似矣。其視商周，果若是班乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇建華夏，功德之盛，誠有以軼殷周而陋漢唐矣。迨我皇上晉臨區宇，懋昭大德，並隆治功，丕顯丕承，猗歟休哉！顧其間致治之迹，雖不能以皆同，然亦有黙契焉者。本諸身而達之家國天下，不知凡幾。其大且著者，昭如日月，則天下臣民之所共仰也，可得聞歟？仰惟至德至治，宜無待仰賛一詞，而臣子愛…
translation_en:
Fifth Policy Question
The question asks: The sages of earlier and later ages followed the same standards. How much more should this hold within a single dynasty, where worthy and sage rulers founded, maintained, and restored its fortunes, and ancestors and descendants succeeded one another? Their abundant virtue and great achievements should surely have been consistent throughout. Thus Cheng Tang established the mean, Gaozong brought virtue into harmony, Wen and Wu received Heaven’s mandate, and King Xuan restored the dynasty. Evidence can be found of how their virtue and achievements matched one another across the generations. From the Han onward, the histories describe Guangwu and Gaozu as alike in their open-mindedness and magnanimity; Xianzong, in relation to Emperor Wen of the Tang, devoted himself to seeking good government and came close to the achievements of the Zhenguan era. These seem to be cases of such resemblance. Yet, measured against the Shang and Zhou, were they truly in the same class?
We reverently reflect that our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, founded his rule over Huaxia. The greatness of his achievements and virtue truly surpassed the Yin and Zhou and made the Han and Tang appear meager. Now our reigning emperor has ascended to rule the realm, diligently manifesting his great virtue and bringing the achievements of government to equal eminence, gloriously displaying and continuing his inheritance. Ah, how splendid! Although the particular ways in which they brought about good government cannot all have been identical, there were also points of unspoken accord. Rooted in their own persons and extending to their families, the state, and all under Heaven, these are too numerous to count. The greatest and most conspicuous shine like the sun and moon and are admired alike by the officials and people of the realm. May we hear an account of them?
We reverently consider that such consummate virtue and government should need no word of praise from below; yet the love that subjects bear…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
君之誠尤有不能自已者不知我
太祖聖神功化之極可爲
今日中興萬一之助者何歟諸士子躬逢其
盛鋪張揚厲之下必有先得我心之所
同然者願備陳之以共效芹曝之獻
問古樂之作可以感神人移風俗世之君
子嘗究心焉試舉其槩與諸士商之粤
自易象豫雷書命后夔樂作教興邃矣
大矣然音起於聲而調於均均之調爲
===
難於是古樂遂廢而其說固在也觀諸
大司樂掌成均之灋以樂德樂語樂舞
教國子而和之以六律六同之聲音伶
州鳩亦謂古之神瞽考中聲而量之以
制度律均鍾因并著六律六閒之名義
而中聲之說世尤宗焉何歟自漢以下
類多作者惟蔡元定律呂新書明白淵
深縝密通暢諸儒莫及而元定又謂律
呂之器不可復見然古人制樂之意則
punctuated:
君之誠，尤有不能自已者。不知我太祖聖神功化之極，可爲今日中興萬一之助者何歟？諸士子躬逢其盛，鋪張揚厲之下，必有先得我心之所同然者，願備陳之，以共效芹曝之獻。

問：古樂之作，可以感神人，移風俗，世之君子嘗究心焉。試舉其槩，與諸士商之。粤自《易》象豫雷，《書》命后夔，樂作教興，邃矣，大矣！然音起於聲，而調於均，均之調爲難。於是古樂遂廢，而其說固在也。觀諸大司樂掌成均之灋，以樂德、樂語、樂舞教國子，而和之以六律六同之聲音。伶州鳩亦謂古之神瞽考中聲而量之以制，度律均鍾，因并著六律六閒之名義，而中聲之說，世尤宗焉，何歟？自漢以下，類多作者，惟蔡元定《律呂新書》明白淵深，縝密通暢，諸儒莫及。而元定又謂律呂之器不可復見，然古人制樂之意則
translation_en:
…their sincere love for their ruler is especially something they cannot restrain. What aspects of our Taizu’s supremely sagely and divine achievements and transforming influence might contribute even the smallest measure toward today’s restoration? You candidates have personally encountered this flourishing age. In expounding and celebrating it, you will surely anticipate convictions shared in my own heart. I hope you will set them forth fully, so that together we may offer our humble contributions, like gifts of cress or the warmth of the sun.

Question: The performance of ancient music could move spirits and human beings and transform customs. Gentlemen of later ages have devoted themselves to investigating it. Let us outline its essentials and discuss them with you candidates. From the thunder in the image of the Yu hexagram in the Book of Changes and the charge to Kui in the Book of Documents, music was instituted and instruction flourished: how profound and how great! Yet musical tones arise from sounds and are harmonized through tuning standards; establishing those standards is difficult. Ancient music consequently fell into disuse, but its teachings certainly survive. Consider how the Grand Director of Music administered the regulations of the Chengjun school, teaching the sons of the state through musical virtues, musical speech, and musical dance, and bringing them into harmony through the sounds of the six yang pitch standards and six yin pitch standards. The music master Ling Zhoujiu likewise said that the divinely gifted blind musicians of antiquity examined the central tone and measured it according to established standards, determining pitches and tuning bells. He also set out the names and meanings of the six pitch standards and the six intervening pitches. Why has his account of the central tone been particularly revered by later generations? From the Han onward, there have been many writers of this kind. Yet Cai Yuanding’s New Treatise on the Pitch Standards alone is clear and profound, meticulous and coherent, beyond the attainments of other scholars. Yuanding further said that the instruments embodying the pitch standards could no longer be seen, but as for the intentions of the ancients in establishing music…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
猶可考其詳可得聞歟玆欲上窮作樂
之本下達樂制之宜推其異而合之同
舉其粗而會之精不泥於形器而能深
契作者之意以成一代之制如之何則
可
問古帝王當治平之時恒以閱武爲重乆
安長治良必由之是故大司馬四時各
有所敎名各不同義亦迥異且一歲之
間王再臨焉而幷及蒐狩何歟漢唐宋
===
立國代有其制軍儀詡然載在史冊班
班可考于時嗣君遵而行之有講武于
平樂于驪山于近郊于東武者雖優劣
不同要皆足以作將士之氣懾華夷之
心非以好大而窮黷也我
國家經制大備悉倣諸古維是大閱之儀尚
少遺焉豈有待哉邇者殘胡豨突本兵
旰食諸臣論列蓋亦廣矣何將士驕惰
邊務縱弛猶夫昔也議者謂宜稽古制
punctuated:
猶可考。其詳可得聞歟？玆欲上窮作樂之本，下達樂制之宜，推其異而合之同，舉其粗而會之精，不泥於形器而能深契作者之意，以成一代之制，如之何則可？

問：古帝王當治平之時，恒以閱武爲重，乆安長治良必由之。是故大司馬四時各有所敎，名各不同，義亦迥異。且一歲之間，王再臨焉，而幷及蒐狩，何歟？漢唐宋立國，代有其制，軍儀詡然載在史冊，班班可考。于時嗣君遵而行之，有講武于平樂、于驪山、于近郊、于東武者。雖優劣不同，要皆足以作將士之氣，懾華夷之心，非以好大而窮黷也。我國家經制大備，悉倣諸古，維是大閱之儀尚少遺焉，豈有待哉？邇者殘胡豨突，本兵旰食，諸臣論列蓋亦廣矣。何將士驕惰，邊務縱弛，猶夫昔也？議者謂宜稽古制
translation_en:
…can still be investigated. May we hear the details? We now wish to probe to the very foundations of making music and extend our inquiry to the appropriate arrangements for its institutions; to examine its differences and reconcile them in a common unity; to take its broad outlines and comprehend their subtleties; and, without becoming bound by material forms and instruments, to grasp deeply the intentions of its creators, thereby establishing a musical system for our dynasty. How may this be achieved?

Question: When the emperors and kings of antiquity enjoyed orderly and peaceful rule, they invariably attached great importance to military reviews. Lasting peace and enduring good government surely depended upon these. Thus the Minister of War provided particular instruction in each of the four seasons, with different names and markedly different meanings. Moreover, within a single year the king attended twice, and this also encompassed the spring and winter hunts. Why was this?

When the Han, Tang, and Song founded their states, each dynasty had its own institutions. Their military ceremonies are impressively recorded in the histories and can be clearly investigated. Successive rulers observed and carried them out, conducting military exercises at Pingle, at Lishan, in the nearby suburbs, and at Dongwu. Though their merits varied, all were sufficient to rouse the spirit of officers and soldiers and strike awe into the hearts of Chinese and non-Chinese alike. They were not undertaken out of a love of grandeur or a desire to exhaust resources through reckless warfare.

Our dynasty’s established institutions are comprehensive, all modeled on antiquity. Yet the ceremonial arrangements for the grand military review still have some omissions. Can it be that they await something? Recently, the remnant Hu have charged in like wild boars, and the Minister of War has been eating only late in the day. The various officials have already discussed and presented their arguments at considerable length. Why, then, are officers and soldiers still arrogant and indolent, and frontier affairs still neglected and lax, just as before? Those offering proposals say that we should examine the ancient institutions…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而作六師則轉移之機有不令而從者
果然歟抑别有鼓舞駕馭之術安邊固
圉之策歟諸士子抱藝而來必有識時
務賛
廟謨者試陳之毋讓
問能自得師學者事也古之君子言道德
則孔孟言功業則伊周宋人乃曰立志
以明道希文自期待何歟且自宋祖開
基天象兆祥英賢輩出有沉潛體道者
===
有剛毅自立者有明睿燭幾者有誠篤
憤悱者其道德豈不足多或者獨以孟
子之後一人稱明道者豈無謂歟無亦
以其所賦之美所學之正徵諸處已接
人事君澤物者知其中之所存果有大
過人歟慶曆以後名臣接踵有豐功偉
量者有清忠粹德者有抗論虜庭者有
文章擅名者其功業豈不足尚或者惟
以第一流人物稱希文者抑獨何歟無
punctuated:
而作六師，則轉移之機有不令而從者，果然歟？抑别有鼓舞駕馭之術、安邊固圉之策歟？諸士子抱藝而來，必有識時務、賛廟謨者，試陳之，毋讓。
問：能自得師，學者事也。古之君子，言道德則孔孟，言功業則伊周。宋人乃曰：「立志以明道、希文自期待。」何歟？且自宋祖開基，天象兆祥，英賢輩出，有沉潛體道者，有剛毅自立者，有明睿燭幾者，有誠篤憤悱者，其道德豈不足多？或者獨以孟子之後一人稱明道者，豈無謂歟？無亦以其所賦之美、所學之正，徵諸處已接人、事君澤物者，知其中之所存果有大過人歟？慶曆以後，名臣接踵，有豐功偉量者，有清忠粹德者，有抗論虜庭者，有文章擅名者，其功業豈不足尚？或者惟以第一流人物稱希文者，抑獨何歟？無
translation_en:
…and rouse the Six Armies, would there then be an opportunity to transform affairs, with men obeying even without orders? Is this indeed so? Or are there other methods of inspiring and directing them, other policies for securing the frontier and strengthening its defenses? You examination candidates have come equipped with learning; surely some among you understand the needs of the times and can assist the deliberations of the imperial court. Set forth your views without holding back.
Question: Finding a teacher for oneself is the learner’s task. Among the gentlemen of antiquity, when speaking of moral virtue one looked to Kongzi and Mengzi; when speaking of achievements in government, to Yi Yin and Zhou Gong. Yet a man of the Song said, “In setting your aspirations, take Mingdao and Xiwen as the standards you expect yourself to attain.” Why? From the time the Song founder established his dynasty, celestial signs heralded good fortune, and outstanding worthies appeared in succession. Some deeply contemplated and embodied the Way; some were resolute and independent; some possessed penetrating intelligence that discerned the first stirrings of events; some were sincere and earnest, struggling to understand and express what they had learned. Was their moral virtue not amply worthy of praise? Yet some singled out Mingdao [Cheng Hao] as the one man since Mengzi. Surely this judgment had a reason? Might it be that, examining the excellence of his natural endowment and the correctness of his learning as manifested in his conduct toward himself [?] and others, his service to his ruler, and his beneficence toward all beings, they recognized that what he held within truly far surpassed other men?
After the Qingli era, eminent ministers followed one another in succession. Some had great achievements and extraordinary magnanimity; some possessed unsullied loyalty and pure virtue; some argued fearlessly at the courts of foreign foes; some won renown through their writings. Were their accomplishments not amply worthy of esteem? Yet some reserved the designation “a person of the first rank” for Xiwen [Fan Zhongyan]. Why him alone? Might it not be…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
乃即其直亮之節仁明之才發諸匡時
濟世知人料敵者驗其志之所向果非
尋常可及歟今明道希文之所以自待
與諸賢門人之所以稱之者固在也豈
皆無可議歟然志士尚友惟以是爲的
歟抑將進於是歟今之學者類能談道
德功業以聖賢自期其於體用本末視
二子果能兼舉否歟愛其人故得其行
事之詳況願學如明道希文者乎盍各
===
言之以觀諸士子之志
問滇古黔中之地靡莫哀牢之屬也自南
詔啓土中國人士多流寓焉逮我
太祖取而郡縣之揆文奮武休養生息以迄于
今其山河之固人材之盛固足以防患
而飾治矣然散處之民尚有可虞黌序
之建尚多未備議者謂宜設險以衞民
生明教以興民德然歟滇有故城
國初又爲增築諸城往日草竊之生或恃有
punctuated:
乃即其直亮之節、仁明之才，發諸匡時濟世、知人料敵者，驗其志之所向，果非尋常可及歟？今明道、希文之所以自待，與諸賢門人之所以稱之者，固在也，豈皆無可議歟？然志士尚友，惟以是爲的歟？抑將進於是歟？今之學者類能談道德功業，以聖賢自期，其於體用本末，視二子果能兼舉否歟？愛其人，故得其行事之詳，況願學如明道、希文者乎？盍各言之，以觀諸士子之志？

問：滇，古黔中之地，靡莫、哀牢之屬也。自南詔啓土，中國人士多流寓焉。逮我太祖取而郡縣之，揆文奮武，休養生息，以迄于今，其山河之固、人材之盛，固足以防患而飾治矣。然散處之民尚有可虞，黌序之建尚多未備。議者謂宜設險以衞民生，明教以興民德，然歟？滇有故城，國初又爲增築諸城。往日草竊之生，或恃有
translation_en:
…might it be that his upright and candid integrity and his humane and discerning abilities, manifested in rectifying his age, aiding the world, judging men, and assessing enemies, attest to the direction of his aspirations as truly beyond the reach of ordinary people? The standards Mingdao and Xiwen set for themselves, and the grounds on which worthy men and their disciples praised them, remain on record. Are they all beyond discussion? Yet when men of aspiration seek friendship with the worthies of the past, should they take these alone as their goal, or should they advance beyond them? Scholars today can generally discourse on moral virtue and achievement, aspiring to become sages and worthies. But in substance and function, root and branch, can they truly embrace both as these two men did? Love for a man leads one to learn the particulars of his deeds; how much more should this apply to those who wish to emulate Mingdao and Xiwen? Let each of you speak, so that we may discern your aspirations.

Question: Dian was anciently the territory of Qianzhong, belonging to such peoples as the Mimo and Ailao. Since Nanzhao opened up its territory, many men of learning from the Central Lands migrated there and settled. When our Taizu conquered it and organized it into prefectures and counties, he directed civil affairs and exerted military might, allowing the people to recuperate and prosper. Down to the present, its strong mountain and river defenses and its abundance of talented men have surely sufficed to guard against trouble and lend lustre to good government. Yet there remain grounds for concern about the people living in scattered settlements, and much remains incomplete in the establishment of schools. Some argue that defensive positions should be established to protect the people's livelihoods, and moral instruction made clear to promote their virtue. Is this correct? Dian had old walled towns, and at the beginning of our dynasty additional town walls were built. When banditry arose in former days, some relied on having …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
城而無恐或以無城而大被荼毒者故
鑑此請城鶴慶是已然宜城者豈獨鶴
慶已乎舍近而圖遠均之未爲衞也滇
舊有學
國初又爲增建諸學近日人材之出或以有
學而益盛或以無學而日就荒落者故
緣此請建馬龍諸學是已然宜建者豈
獨馬龍已乎舉彼而遺此猶之未爲興
也或又有勞民費財徒設無益之譏何
===
歟將事有重且大者宜不計小費不恤
浮言歟諸士子生長玆土平居相與得
諸輿人之誦審矣願計其便
punctuated: 城而無恐，或以無城而大被荼毒者。故鑑此請城鶴慶，是已。然宜城者，豈獨鶴慶已乎？舍近而圖遠，均之未爲衞也。滇舊有學，國初又爲增建諸學。近日人材之出，或以有學而益盛，或以無學而日就荒落者。故緣此請建馬龍諸學，是已。然宜建者，豈獨馬龍已乎？舉彼而遺此，猶之未爲興也。或又有勞民費財、徒設無益之譏，何歟？將事有重且大者，宜不計小費，不恤浮言歟？諸士子生長玆土，平居相與得諸輿人之誦審矣，願計其便。
translation_en: …city walls and thus felt no fear, while others, lacking walls, suffered grievous devastation. In light of this, the proposal to build walls around Heqing is sound. Yet is Heqing alone in need of walls? To neglect nearby places while making plans for distant ones is still to leave protection unprovided. Yunnan already had schools, and at the beginning of our dynasty additional schools were established. In recent years, some places have produced ever more men of talent because they have schools, while others, lacking schools, have fallen into increasing decline. Accordingly, the proposal to establish schools in Malong and other places is sound. Yet is Malong alone in need of them? To provide for those places while overlooking these is likewise to leave education unpromoted. Others, however, criticize these measures as burdening the people and wasting resources, creating institutions that serve no useful purpose. Why is this? Or should matters of such importance and magnitude be pursued without counting minor expenses or heeding idle talk? You examination candidates were born and raised in this land; in your everyday dealings with one another, you have gained thorough knowledge of what the people say. I ask you to consider what measures would be most beneficial.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
孔子曰君子有九思視思明聽思聰色思
溫貌思恭言思忠事思敬疑思問忿思
難見得思義
石雷
同考試官教諭莫批約而達雅而健結復合九
思為一蓋有得於本原者錄之
考試官教諭彭批精當
===
考試官教諭朱批整潔
聖人論君子慎思之學皆求得乎理而已夫理
無不在而思則得之也君子之所思者何往而
非求得其理哉夫子欲學者之求諸心也故其
言曰心主乎一身而其體足以管乎衆理理散
於天下而其妙不外乎一心人惟未之思也則
心學荒而離道遠矣君子隨事窮理已豫夫致
知之功觀物察則罔忽於物交之感其有感而
思者大凡有九焉何則目以司視耳以司聽聰
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

孔子曰：「君子有九思：視思明，聽思聰，色思溫，貌思恭，言思忠，事思敬，疑思問，忿思難，見得思義。」

石雷

同考試官教諭莫批：「約而達，雅而健，結復合九思為一，蓋有得於本原者，錄之。」

考試官教諭彭批：「精當。」

考試官教諭朱批：「整潔。」

聖人論君子慎思之學，皆求得乎理而已。夫理無不在，而思則得之也。君子之所思者，何往而非求得其理哉？夫子欲學者之求諸心也，故其言曰：「心主乎一身，而其體足以管乎衆理；理散於天下，而其妙不外乎一心。人惟未之思也，則心學荒而離道遠矣。君子隨事窮理，已豫夫致知之功；觀物察則，罔忽於物交之感。其有感而思者，大凡有九焉。何則？目以司視，耳以司聽，聰
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Confucius said: “The gentleman has nine considerations: when looking, he considers how to see clearly; when listening, how to hear distinctly; in his expression, how to be gentle; in his bearing, how to be respectful; in speaking, how to be sincere; in conducting affairs, how to be reverent; when in doubt, how to inquire; when angry, what troubles may follow; and when he sees an opportunity for gain, what is right.”

Shi Lei

Comment by Associate Examiner Mo, Instructor: “Concise yet expressive, elegant yet vigorous. The conclusion reunites the nine considerations into one. This is surely someone who has grasped their fundamental source. Selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: “Precise and apt.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Orderly and polished.”

In discussing the gentleman’s learning through careful reflection, the Sage speaks only of seeking to apprehend principle. Principle is present everywhere, and reflection enables one to apprehend it. Wherever the gentleman directs his reflection, is he not seeking to apprehend the principle therein? The Master wished learners to seek it within their own minds; hence his words mean: “The mind governs the whole person, and its essential constitution suffices to encompass all principles. Principle is distributed throughout the world, yet its wondrous operation does not lie outside the single mind. It is only because people fail to reflect upon it that learning concerning the mind falls into neglect and they stray far from the Way. The gentleman investigates principle as each affair arises, having already undertaken the work of extending knowledge. He observes things and examines their governing patterns, neglecting none of the stirrings occasioned by encounters with things. Broadly speaking, there are nine kinds of occasions on which he is moved and reflects. Why is this? The eyes govern seeing, and the ears govern hearing. Keenness of hearing…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
明者乃其德之懿也君子則思其作哲思其作
謀而聰明適得吾體焉耳色見於面貌動乎容
温恭者固其則之嘉也君子則思其可親思其
可象而温恭不失吾常焉耳言不忠事不敬弗
可行也君子必慮其終而思忠焉稽其敝而思
敬焉蓋於言行無所苟而已矣疑不問忿不懲
將益滋也君子必思問以解其惑焉思難而平
其氣焉蓋於私意無所留而已矣見得則利心
生焉人之恒也君子則以取與之未審恐性分
===
之有累如其義焉斯受之矣非其義也肯苟取
乎吁君子可謂善事其心者矣玆其非夫人之
可及也與雖然君子之學分而言之固有九思
合而言之實一理而已苟無得於大本大原之
所在徒欲因事而思逐物而會則其心益病其
思益鑿其學無統矣然則將廢思乎曰居敬以
立其本主靜以致其功則思作睿睿作聖無思
而無不通矣其善學哉
可以贊天地之化育則可以與天地參矣
punctuated:
明者，乃其德之懿也。君子則思其作哲，思其作謀，而聰明適得吾體焉耳。色見於面，貌動乎容，温恭者固其則之嘉也。君子則思其可親，思其可象，而温恭不失吾常焉耳。言不忠，事不敬，弗可行也。君子必慮其終而思忠焉，稽其敝而思敬焉，蓋於言行無所苟而已矣。疑不問，忿不懲，將益滋也。君子必思問以解其惑焉，思難而平其氣焉，蓋於私意無所留而已矣。見得則利心生焉，人之恒也。君子則以取與之未審，恐性分之有累。如其義焉，斯受之矣；非其義也，肯苟取乎？吁！君子可謂善事其心者矣！玆其非夫人之可及也與！雖然，君子之學，分而言之，固有九思；合而言之，實一理而已。苟無得於大本大原之所在，徒欲因事而思，逐物而會，則其心益病，其思益鑿，其學無統矣。然則將廢思乎？曰：居敬以立其本，主靜以致其功，則思作睿，睿作聖，無思而無不通矣。其善學哉！

可以贊天地之化育，則可以與天地參矣。
translation_en:
…acuity of hearing and clarity of sight constitute the excellence of these faculties. The gentleman therefore considers how seeing may yield wisdom and hearing may yield sound deliberation; thus acuity and clarity find their proper realization in his own person. Expression appears in the face, and bearing manifests itself in deportment. Warmth and reverence are surely the finest standards for these. The gentleman considers how to be approachable and how to be worthy of emulation; thus warmth and reverence remain his constant disposition.

Words lacking sincerity and actions lacking reverence are unacceptable. The gentleman must consider the outcome of his words and give thought to sincerity; he must examine the failings of his actions and give thought to reverence. This simply means being careless in neither word nor deed. If doubts go unquestioned and anger goes unchecked, they will only increase. The gentleman must think of asking questions to resolve his perplexities, and think of the troubles anger may bring so as to calm his temper. This simply means allowing no selfish intentions to linger.

When an opportunity for gain appears, the desire for profit arises: this is common to people. The gentleman, however, fears that insufficient scrutiny of taking and giving may impair his endowed nature. If receiving something accords with righteousness, he accepts it; if it does not, would he take it heedlessly? Ah! The gentleman may indeed be called one who knows well how to tend his mind! Surely this is beyond the reach of the ordinary person!

Nevertheless, considered separately, the gentleman’s learning certainly comprises nine objects of thought; considered as a whole, it is in fact a single principle. If one has gained no understanding of where the great root and source lie, but merely seeks to think as affairs arise and to comprehend things by pursuing them, one’s mind will become increasingly afflicted, one’s thinking increasingly forced, and one’s learning devoid of a unifying thread. Should one then abandon thought? The answer is: abide in reverence to establish the foundation, and take stillness as the guiding principle to bring the work to fruition. Then thought produces perspicacity, and perspicacity produces sagehood; without deliberate thought, there will be nothing one does not comprehend. How well such a person learns!

“If one can assist the transforming and nourishing processes of Heaven and Earth, one can then form a triad with Heaven and Earth.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
蘭𣸸

聖人成天地之能斯成位乎其中矣夫贊化育
而參天地功用之盛莫可尚矣非至誠盡性其
孰能與於此哉宜中庸舉之以明天道也意謂
人立天地之中以生繼善之初本與同體神化
===
之極實與同功未始不相配也自夫梏於私而
窒於化其違也遠矣至誠者既合己與人物之
性而盡之而黎民時雍焉萬物咸若焉大業炳
煥於無疆至和充周於無間是天地以生成爲
德而歉於政猶未免有所偏也聖人盡財成之
道而後化育有全功則托其始者天地也所以
代其終者存乎聖矣非以其所及贊其所不及
邪乾坤以易簡爲能而限於分猶若將有所待
也聖人盡輔相之宜而後化理無餘憾則啓其
punctuated:
蘭𣸸

同考試官教諭羅批：講參贊處，體認親切，文思清新，機軸迥異凡作。其識造理有得之士邪？允宜高薦。
考試官教諭彭批：明潔。
考試官教諭朱批：純確。

聖人成天地之能，斯成位乎其中矣。夫贊化育而參天地，功用之盛，莫可尚矣。非至誠盡性，其孰能與於此哉？宜《中庸》舉之以明天道也。意謂人立天地之中以生，繼善之初，本與同體；神化之極，實與同功，未始不相配也。自夫梏於私而窒於化，其違也遠矣。至誠者既合己與人物之性而盡之，而黎民時雍焉，萬物咸若焉，大業炳煥於無疆，至和充周於無間。是天地以生成爲德，而歉於政，猶未免有所偏也。聖人盡財成之道，而後化育有全功，則托其始者天地也，所以代其終者存乎聖矣。非以其所及贊其所不及邪？乾坤以易簡爲能，而限於分，猶若將有所待也。聖人盡輔相之宜，而後化理無餘憾，則啓其
translation_en:
Lan Tian 蘭𣸸

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: In discussing participation in and assistance to Heaven and Earth, the author demonstrates an intimate understanding. His literary conception is fresh, and his approach stands far apart from ordinary compositions. Surely he is a scholar whose insight has attained an understanding of principle? He certainly merits a high recommendation.
Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: Clear and clean.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Pure and precise.

The sage brings to completion the capacities of Heaven and Earth and thereby establishes his place between them. To assist their transforming and nurturing activity and stand alongside Heaven and Earth—nothing can surpass the grandeur of this achievement. Unless one possesses utmost sincerity and fully realizes one’s nature, who could participate in this? It is fitting that the Doctrine of the Mean invokes this to elucidate the Way of Heaven. Its meaning is that human beings come to life standing between Heaven and Earth. At the inception of their continuation of goodness, they are fundamentally one in substance with them; at the culmination of their wondrous transformation, they truly share in their work. Never have they failed to correspond to one another. Once people become fettered by selfishness and obstructed in their transformation, however, their divergence becomes great indeed.

The person of utmost sincerity unites his own nature with those of other people and things and fully realizes them all. The common people then live in harmony, and the myriad things all accord with their proper order. His great undertaking shines forth without bounds, and supreme harmony fills every space without a gap. Heaven and Earth thus take generation and completion as their virtue, yet are deficient in governance [?], and so still cannot avoid a measure of partiality. Only after the sage fully carries out the way of regulating and completing their work does transformation and nurture achieve its full effect. Thus Heaven and Earth initiate it, while its completion on their behalf rests with the sage. Does he not use what lies within his reach to assist with what lies beyond theirs?

Qian and Kun—the Creative and the Receptive—take ease and simplicity as their capacities, yet are constrained by their respective roles, as though still awaiting assistance. Only after the sage fully provides the appropriate support does the ordering of transformation leave nothing wanting. Thus those that initiate its…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
幾者天地也所以代其工者存乎聖矣非以其
所能助其所不能邪夫至誠之賛化育如此雖
曰法象莫大乎天地也然異形同體惟肖之理
存焉異質同神三才之道備焉乾稱曰父坤稱
曰母聖人以父母天下爲王道有以中天下而
立矣天位乎上地位乎下聖人易簡而天下之
理得可以成位乎其中矣若然則天地不可謂
之大也聖人不可謂之小也參之奚歉哉是何
也盡性至命乃爲功用之全而不能踐形者斯
===
無以作配也否則聖人之於民亦類耳何其首
出而特盛也哉嘗稽之易曰復其見天地之心
又曰天下雷行物與無妄則人身皆具一天地
矣惟聖盡倫惟王盡制豈於性分有加邪故盡
性者卽中和之致參賛者卽位育之義學者不
遠是復而法先王茂對之仁則天地之配可幾
也若不探性命而欲論禮樂語經濟者末矣又
何足與議參賛之道
夫世祿滕固行之矣詩云雨我公田遂及
punctuated:
幾者天地也，所以代其工者存乎聖矣，非以其所能助其所不能邪？夫至誠之賛化育如此，雖曰法象莫大乎天地也，然異形同體，惟肖之理存焉；異質同神，三才之道備焉。乾稱曰父，坤稱曰母，聖人以父母天下爲王道，有以中天下而立矣。天位乎上，地位乎下，聖人易簡而天下之理得，可以成位乎其中矣。若然，則天地不可謂之大也，聖人不可謂之小也，參之奚歉哉？是何也？盡性至命，乃爲功用之全，而不能踐形者，斯無以作配也。否則，聖人之於民亦類耳，何其首出而特盛也哉？嘗稽之《易》曰：「復，其見天地之心。」又曰：「天下雷行，物與無妄。」則人身皆具一天地矣。惟聖盡倫，惟王盡制，豈於性分有加邪？故盡性者卽中和之致，參賛者卽位育之義。學者不遠是復，而法先王茂對之仁，則天地之配可幾也。若不探性命而欲論禮樂、語經濟者，末矣，又何足與議參賛之道？

夫世祿，滕固行之矣。《詩》云：「雨我公田，遂及
translation_en:
…it is Heaven and Earth that initiate the incipient workings; yet it rests with the sage to carry out their work on their behalf. Is this not to use what he can do to assist them in what they cannot? Such is the way utmost sincerity assists transformation and nurture. Although it is said that among models and images none is greater than Heaven and Earth, the sage and they differ in form yet share one substance: herein lies the principle of likeness. They differ in material constitution yet share one spiritual efficacy: herein the Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—is complete. Qian is called father, and Kun is called mother. The sage takes acting as father and mother to all under Heaven as the kingly Way, and thus has the means to stand at the center of the world. Heaven occupies its position above, and Earth its position below. Through ease and simplicity, the sage grasps the principles of all under Heaven and can establish his position between them. If this is so, Heaven and Earth cannot be called greater, nor the sage lesser. What does he lack, then, in forming a triad with them? Why is this? Only by fully realizing one's nature and reaching one's allotted destiny can one's efficacy be complete; those unable to fulfill what their bodily form entails have no means of becoming their counterpart. Otherwise, the sage would merely be of the same kind as the common people: how could he stand foremost and be uniquely preeminent?

I have examined this in the Book of Changes, which says, “Return: in this may we see the heart of Heaven and Earth.” It also says, “Thunder moves beneath Heaven; all things partake of freedom from falsehood.” Thus every human person contains a Heaven and Earth. Only the sage fully realizes human relationships; only the true king fully realizes institutions. How could this add anything to what is allotted by nature? Thus fully realizing one's nature is precisely bringing equilibrium and harmony to their utmost; forming a triad with Heaven and Earth and assisting them is precisely the meaning of their taking their proper positions and the myriad things being nurtured. If learners return before straying far, and emulate the former kings' benevolence in abundantly responding to Heaven, they may hope to become counterparts of Heaven and Earth. But those who, without investigating human nature and destiny, wish to discuss rites and music and speak of ordering the world and aiding the people concern themselves with mere secondary matters. How could they be fit to discuss the Way of forming a triad with Heaven and Earth and assisting them?

As for hereditary emoluments, Teng has certainly already put them into practice. The Book of Odes says, “Let rain fall upon our public fields, and then reach…”

我私。惟助爲有公田。由此觀之，雖周亦助也。設爲庠序學校以敎之。庠者，養也；校者，敎也；序者，射也。夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠，學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。人倫明於上，小民親於下。

translation_en:
…our private fields. Only under the assistance system are there public fields. Viewed in this light, even the Zhou employed the assistance system. Establish xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools to instruct the people. Xiang means nurturing; xiao means teaching; xu means archery. Under the Xia they were called xiao, under the Yin, xu, and under the Zhou, xiang; xue was common to all three dynasties. All served to clarify human relationships. When human relationships are made clear among those above, the common people below live in affection with one another.

Li Tingzhao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Writers addressing long topics generally tend toward superficiality, diffuseness, verbosity, and clutter. This piece alone integrates the essential principles, while its language is also clear and orderly. It deserves inclusion as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: Its interweaving and composition display brilliant literary elegance.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: It profoundly grasps the purport of Mencius’s counsel to Duke Wen of Teng.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Concise yet elegant.

The great worthy explained to the ruler of Teng that the assistance system ought to be implemented, and thereby showed him that moral instruction ought to be made a priority. Hereditary stipends depend upon the assistance system, and moral instruction flourishes amid material sufficiency. Examining antiquity and testing it against the present, is not the way of governing plainly apparent? It was fitting that Mencius should enlighten Duke Wen of Teng on these matters. His meaning was that the people’s livelihood and their cultivation of virtue are, in principle, interconnected and inseparable; the ruler’s efforts to enrich and educate them are mutually complementary methods, neither of which may be neglected. Thus, for regulating holdings and levying contributions from the people, truly nothing surpasses the assistance system. The assistance system provides generously for the common people, while hereditary stipends accord weight to the governing elite. Yet only after fields have been apportioned can stipends be established, and the occupations of those above and below…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
定焉自今觀之世禄之法滕固已行之矣助法
獨所未舉則取民無制豈王政之本乎體國經
野吾且有徵於周矣詩云雨我公田遂及我私
然惟助為有公田而上下之分辨焉由此觀之
助法之善雖周亦行之矣滕獨在所不講則憲
章未備豈法祖之治乎誠能取之有道則民生
可阜矣養之有素則民行可興矣設為庠序學
校所以教之也綱維制度豈無所於稽邪庠取
諸養校取諸教序取諸射鄉學之建義各有攸
===
當也夏則曰校殷則曰序周則曰庠國學之崇
名則其所同也緣道立教一皆人倫之是明因
性牖民使其帝則之必察夫惟教隆於上而五
品遜焉有以昭率乂於大公由是俗美於下而
百姓親焉有以成雍睦於大順正德厚生畢遂
其願為國之道不外此而得之矣滕君尚知所
力行也哉抑可見孟子之學識其大者焉論學
原諸性善而必稱堯舜論治惟重教養而必徵
諸三代之盛王豈以滕文果足與有為而告之
punctuated: 定焉。自今觀之，世禄之法，滕固已行之矣；助法獨所未舉，則取民無制，豈王政之本乎？體國經野，吾且有徵於周矣。《詩》云：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」然惟助為有公田，而上下之分辨焉。由此觀之，助法之善，雖周亦行之矣；滕獨在所不講，則憲章未備，豈法祖之治乎？誠能取之有道，則民生可阜矣；養之有素，則民行可興矣。設為庠序學校，所以教之也。綱維制度，豈無所於稽邪？庠取諸養，校取諸教，序取諸射，鄉學之建，義各有攸當也。夏則曰校，殷則曰序，周則曰庠，國學之崇，名則其所同也。緣道立教，一皆人倫之是明；因性牖民，使其帝則之必察。夫惟教隆於上，而五品遜焉，有以昭率乂於大公；由是俗美於下，而百姓親焉，有以成雍睦於大順。正德厚生，畢遂其願，為國之道，不外此而得之矣。滕君尚知所力行也哉！抑可見孟子之學，識其大者焉。論學原諸性善，而必稱堯舜；論治惟重教養，而必徵諸三代之盛王。豈以滕文果足與有為，而告之
translation_en:
…are thereby settled. Looking at the matter now, Teng has indeed already implemented hereditary stipends. Only the assistance system of taxation remains unimplemented, so that exactions from the people have no fixed limits. Can this be the foundation of kingly government? For the ordering of the capital and the demarcation of the countryside, I can moreover find evidence in Zhou practice. The Book of Odes says: “Let rain fall on our public fields, and then reach our private fields.” Only the assistance system has public fields, clearly distinguishing the shares of ruler and subjects. Viewed in this light, the assistance system is so beneficial that even the Zhou practised it. If Teng alone fails to give it consideration, its institutions remain incomplete. Can this be government that follows the ancestors?

If what is taken from the people accords with the Way, their livelihood can flourish; if their sustenance is regularly provided for, their moral conduct can be elevated. Establishing xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools is the means of teaching them. Surely there are precedents against which to examine their organizing principles and institutional arrangements? Xiang derives its meaning from nourishing, xiao from teaching, and xu from archery: each designation appropriately expresses the purpose for which local schools were established. Under the Xia they were called xiao, under the Yin xu, and under the Zhou xiang; as for the state schools they honoured, their name was common to all three dynasties. Teaching established in accordance with the Way serves entirely to clarify human relationships. Enlightening the people in accordance with their nature ensures that they discern the standards of the Supreme Lord.

When teaching flourishes above and the five human relationships are harmoniously ordered, obedience and good governance can be made manifest in perfect impartiality. Consequently, customs below become admirable and the common people are affectionate toward one another, bringing concord and amity to fulfilment in complete harmony. With virtue rectified and livelihoods enriched, all their aspirations are fulfilled. The way to govern a state is attained without going beyond this. May the ruler of Teng recognize what he should strive to put into practice!

Here we can also see that Mencius’s learning grasped what was fundamental. In discussing learning, he traced it to the goodness of human nature and invariably invoked Yao and Shun; in discussing government, he placed particular emphasis on teaching and nurturing the people and invariably drew evidence from the illustrious kings of the Three Dynasties. Could it have been because he considered Duke Wen of Teng truly capable of working with him to accomplish something that he told him…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以是以廣其所未聞也乎噫此帝德之盛王道
之全也雖謂爲萬世立準焉可也故先儒謂孟
子之學識其大
易
文言曰坤至柔而動也剛至靜而德方
湯憲
同考試官教諭羅批講柔剛靜方處辭不繁而
意自足子其深於易者邪
考試官教諭彭批理趣深長筆力精健
===
考試官教諭朱批脫去陳言當是作者
文言闡坤德極其順而健也夫柔靜者坤之順
剛方則健矣順而健坤德其至矣哉夫子文言
釋牝馬之貞意謂天下之言坤者則順而已矣
孰知其有不倚於順者乎試以貞言之是故應
乾從事居後爲得而無所於擅夫坤可謂至柔
也已至柔若不足於剛矣然承天以爲動也氣
閉而卽藏大化不愆其期道斂而卽歸成物不
失其令翕然闔者其機也浩然成者其勢也舉
punctuated:
以是，以廣其所未聞也乎？噫！此帝德之盛，王道之全也，雖謂爲萬世立準焉可也。故先儒謂孟子之學識其大。

易

文言曰：「坤至柔而動也剛，至靜而德方。」

湯憲

同考試官教諭羅批：「講柔剛靜方處，辭不繁而意自足。子其深於易者邪？」

考試官教諭彭批：「理趣深長，筆力精健。」

考試官教諭朱批：「脫去陳言，當是作者。」

文言闡坤德，極其順而健也。夫柔靜者，坤之順；剛方則健矣。順而健，坤德其至矣哉！夫子文言釋牝馬之貞，意謂天下之言坤者，則順而已矣，孰知其有不倚於順者乎？試以貞言之。是故應乾從事，居後爲得，而無所於擅，夫坤可謂至柔也已。至柔若不足於剛矣，然承天以爲動也，氣閉而卽藏，大化不愆其期；道斂而卽歸，成物不失其令。翕然闔者，其機也；浩然成者，其勢也。舉
translation_en:
…with this, to broaden what he had not yet heard? Ah! This is imperial virtue at its height and the kingly Way in its entirety. One may indeed say that it establishes a standard for ten thousand generations. Thus earlier Confucian scholars said that Mencius, in his learning, understood what was greatest.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) says: “Kun is utterly yielding, yet firm in its movement; utterly still, yet square in its virtue.”

Tang Xian

Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “In explaining yielding and firmness, stillness and squareness, the language is concise yet fully conveys the meaning. Are you perhaps one who has a profound understanding of the Changes?”

Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: “The import of the principles is profound and far-reaching; the writing is refined and vigorous.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “He has cast off stale expressions and surely deserves to be called an accomplished writer.”

The Commentary on the Words of the Text elucidates Kun’s virtue, fully setting forth its compliance together with its strength. Yielding and stillness constitute Kun’s compliance; firmness and squareness constitute its strength. Compliant yet strong: how consummate is Kun’s virtue! In the Commentary on the Words of the Text, the Master explains the constancy of the mare. His meaning is that those throughout the world who speak of Kun regard it simply as compliant. Who recognizes that it possesses something that does not rest solely upon compliance? Let us discuss this in terms of constancy. Thus Kun responds to Qian in carrying out its work, finds its proper place in following behind, and presumes to act in nothing on its own authority. Kun may indeed be called utterly yielding. Such utter yielding might seem deficient in firmness. Yet in its movement it receives and follows Heaven: when the vital force closes, it immediately stores itself away, and the great transformation does not miss its appointed time; when the Way contracts, it immediately returns, and the completion of things does not miss its appointed season. Its workings close in gathered stillness; its momentum brings things to completion with vast power. Throughout…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天下莫之能撓而亦莫之能禦也何剛如之夫
柔與剛本相悖也動焉而剛豈坤之戾其常哉
蓋柔之一者乃所以爲剛否則爲懦弱而不振
矣何以言天下之至柔也故柔不足以盡坤柔
而剛焉斯其至矣神功收斂機緘不露而無所
於擾夫坤可謂至靜也已至靜若不足於方矣
然生物以爲德也萬一各正不顯其致役之勞
大小有定咸囿於代終之化羣而分者物也區
以別者類也亘古今莫之有改而亦莫之或紊
===
也何方如之夫靜與方非一致也靜焉而方豈
坤之過其則哉蓋靜之極者乃所以爲方否則
爲雜亂而不恒矣何以言天下之至靜也故靜
不足以盡坤靜而方焉斯其至矣用是而觀柔
以爲剛剛非外於柔也靜以爲方方非外於靜
也靜柔而剛方以寓坤之道貞夫一而已矣抑
天之陰陽也地之柔剛也人之仁義也天地人
之至理也奈何夫人失之於動也擾之於靜也
六鑿攘而三極荒至德孤而大道隱始與天地
punctuated:
天下莫之能撓，而亦莫之能禦也，何剛如之！夫柔與剛本相悖也，動焉而剛，豈坤之戾其常哉？蓋柔之一者，乃所以爲剛；否則爲懦弱而不振矣，何以言天下之至柔也？故柔不足以盡坤，柔而剛焉，斯其至矣。神功收斂，機緘不露，而無所於擾，夫坤可謂至靜也已。至靜若不足於方矣，然生物以爲德也，萬一各正，不顯其致役之勞；大小有定，咸囿於代終之化。羣而分者，物也；區以別者，類也。亘古今莫之有改，而亦莫之或紊也，何方如之！夫靜與方非一致也，靜焉而方，豈坤之過其則哉？蓋靜之極者，乃所以爲方；否則爲雜亂而不恒矣，何以言天下之至靜也？故靜不足以盡坤，靜而方焉，斯其至矣。用是而觀，柔以爲剛，剛非外於柔也；靜以爲方，方非外於靜也。靜柔而剛方以寓，坤之道貞夫一而已矣。

抑天之陰陽也，地之柔剛也，人之仁義也，天地人之至理也。奈何夫人失之於動也，擾之於靜也？六鑿攘而三極荒，至德孤而大道隱，始與天地
translation_en:
…nothing under Heaven can bend it, nor can anything withstand it. What firmness could equal this! Now yielding and firmness are inherently opposed. Yet when Kun acts, it is firm: could this mean that Kun departs from its constant nature? It is precisely its undivided yielding that enables it to be firm. Otherwise, it would be feeble and unable to rouse itself. How could it then be called the utmost yielding under Heaven? Thus yielding alone does not fully describe Kun. Yielding yet firm: herein lies its perfection.

Its wondrous efficacy is gathered inward; its workings remain concealed, and it is free from disturbance. Kun may indeed be called perfectly still. Perfect stillness might seem insufficient for squareness. Yet bringing things into being is its virtue: the myriad and the individual each attain their proper condition [?], without revealing the toil of its service; the great and the small have their appointed places, all encompassed within the transforming process by which it brings things to completion on Heaven’s behalf. Things gather in groups yet remain distinct; kinds are divided and differentiated. From antiquity to the present, nothing has altered this order, nor has anything confused it. What squareness could equal this! Now stillness and squareness are not the same. Yet Kun is still and square: could this mean that it exceeds its proper bounds? It is precisely the utmost stillness that enables it to be square. Otherwise, it would be confused and inconstant. How could it then be called the utmost stillness under Heaven? Thus stillness alone does not fully describe Kun. Still yet square: herein lies its perfection. Viewed in this light, yielding gives rise to firmness; firmness is not external to yielding. Stillness gives rise to squareness; squareness is not external to stillness. Within its stillness and yielding reside firmness and squareness. The Way of Kun is simply to remain steadfast in unity.

Furthermore, yin and yang in Heaven, yielding and firmness in Earth, and benevolence and righteousness in human beings are the ultimate principles of Heaven, Earth, and humanity. Why, then, do people lose these principles in activity and disturb them in stillness? The six bodily apertures contend, and the three ultimate principles fall into neglect; perfect virtue stands forsaken, and the Great Way becomes hidden. Only then do people begin, in relation to Heaven and Earth, to …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不相似矣兼體而不累者其惟聖人乎君子脩
之敬義而已矣
子曰易有聖人之道四焉者此之謂也
蘭漵
同考試官教諭羅批論易道而歸於聖人之神
非有得於易者不能到可以式矣
考試官教諭彭批潔淨精微僅見此作
考試官教諭朱批說理明瑩讀之令人豁然
大傳論易道歸於聖人者以易用之原於聖人
===
也蓋辭占象變易之所有者也而皆原於聖心
之神爲之則謂之聖人之道宜矣大傳歷言人
之尚易而歸功於聖人蓋曰人非易無以制其
用而易非聖人無以妙其用故爲用而不尚諸
易何以妙推行之利語易而不歸諸聖何以發
精微之蘊哉彼繫辭以盡言因變以著占是辭
也占也乃易所以開天下之物通天下之志者
也而極其精矣極數以定象化裁以爲變是象
也變也乃易所以定天下之業成天下之務者
punctuated:
不相似矣。兼體而不累者，其惟聖人乎！君子脩之，敬義而已矣。
子曰：「易有聖人之道四焉」者，此之謂也。
蘭漵
同考試官教諭羅批：論易道而歸於聖人之神，非有得於易者不能到，可以式矣。
考試官教諭彭批：潔淨精微，僅見此作。
考試官教諭朱批：說理明瑩，讀之令人豁然。
大傳論易道歸於聖人者，以易用之原於聖人也。蓋辭、占、象、變，易之所有者也，而皆原於聖心之神爲之，則謂之聖人之道宜矣。大傳歷言人之尚易，而歸功於聖人，蓋曰人非易無以制其用，而易非聖人無以妙其用。故爲用而不尚諸易，何以妙推行之利？語易而不歸諸聖，何以發精微之蘊哉？彼繫辭以盡言，因變以著占，是辭也、占也，乃易所以開天下之物、通天下之志者也，而極其精矣。極數以定象，化裁以爲變，是象也、變也，乃易所以定天下之業、成天下之務者
translation_en:
…no longer resemble Heaven and Earth. Surely only the sage can embody both without being encumbered by them! The gentleman cultivates this through reverence and righteousness alone.
When the Master said, “The Changes contains four aspects of the way of the sages,” this is what he meant.
Lan Xu 蘭漵
Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: This discussion of the way of the Changes traces it back to the numinous power of the sages. Only someone who has gained an understanding of the Changes could reach this point. It may serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: Purity and subtle precision—I have seen these only in this composition.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Its exposition of principle is lucid and luminous; reading it brings sudden clarity.
The Great Commentary, in discussing the way of the Changes, traces it back to the sages because the functioning of the Changes originates with them. Statements, divinations, images, and transformations are all contained in the Changes, yet all originate in the workings of the numinous power of the sages’ minds. It is therefore fitting to call them the way of the sages. The Great Commentary describes in succession how people esteem the Changes, yet attributes the achievement to the sages. Its meaning is that without the Changes people could not regulate their practical undertakings, while without the sages the Changes could not function with such wondrous efficacy. Thus, if in practical undertakings one does not esteem the Changes, how can one wondrously realize the benefits of putting things into operation? If one discusses the Changes without tracing it back to the sages, how can one reveal its subtle and profound inner meanings?
They appended statements to give full expression in words, and drew upon transformations to make divinations manifest. These statements and divinations are the means by which the Changes discloses the things of the world and gives passage to the intentions of all under Heaven, carrying its precision to the utmost. They fathomed numbers to establish images, and adapted and fashioned things to produce transformations. These images and transformations are the means by which the Changes establishes the undertakings of all under Heaven and brings their affairs to completion…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也而極其變矣是四者皆變化之道神之爲也
無一而非易之蘊則無一而非易之道矣乃謂
易有聖人之道者正以辭占至精而所以精者
易不得而與也乃聖人以其至精之神而極之
也深極於聖人則聖人之精因易以示矣象變
至變而所以變者易不得而與也乃聖人以其
至變之神而研之也幾研於聖人則聖人之變
因易以發矣深以通志而其通也極天下之至
神聖人精神心術之所運也豈易之自能邪幾
===
以成務而其成也極天下之至妙聖人妙道精
義之所發也豈易之自爲邪所謂易有聖人之
道者以此此其所以爲人所尚而有功於天下
也與雖然深也幾也神也一而已矣不在易而
在吾心者也是故洗心退藏齋戒神明聖人之
心何假於物哉人惟無得於象數之外而惟滯
於形器之粗意見梏而虛靈蔽則吾心亦物而
易道隱矣乃欲假區區術數以自神如京房延
壽之爲吁易之神固如此哉
punctuated: 也，而極其變矣。是四者，皆變化之道、神之爲也。無一而非易之蘊，則無一而非易之道矣。乃謂易有聖人之道者，正以辭占至精，而所以精者，易不得而與也，乃聖人以其至精之神而極之也。深極於聖人，則聖人之精因易以示矣。象變至變，而所以變者，易不得而與也，乃聖人以其至變之神而研之也。幾研於聖人，則聖人之變因易以發矣。深以通志，而其通也，極天下之至神，聖人精神心術之所運也，豈易之自能邪？幾以成務，而其成也，極天下之至妙，聖人妙道精義之所發也，豈易之自爲邪？所謂易有聖人之道者，以此。此其所以爲人所尚，而有功於天下也與！雖然，深也，幾也，神也，一而已矣。不在易而在吾心者也。是故洗心退藏，齋戒神明，聖人之心何假於物哉？人惟無得於象數之外，而惟滯於形器之粗，意見梏而虛靈蔽，則吾心亦物，而易道隱矣。乃欲假區區術數以自神，如京房延壽之爲，吁！易之神固如此哉？
translation_en: …and bring its transformations to their utmost extent. These four are all the way of change and transformation, the workings of the numinous. Since none lies outside the inner substance of the Book of Changes, none lies outside its Way. Yet the statement that the Changes contains the Way of the sages rests precisely on this: its statements and prognostications are supremely refined, but what makes them refined is not something the Changes itself can contribute. Rather, the sages bring them to their utmost through their supremely refined numinous power. When the sages fathom the depths to the utmost, their refinement is revealed through the Changes. Its images and transformations exhibit change to the utmost, but what makes them change is not something the Changes itself can contribute. Rather, the sages investigate them through their numinous power of utmost transformation. When the sages investigate the incipient signs of change, their powers of transformation unfold through the Changes. Through depth, they comprehend intentions; this comprehension reaches the utmost numinous efficacy under Heaven and is the operation of the sages’ spiritual energies and arts of the mind. How could the Changes accomplish this on its own? Through incipient signs, they accomplish affairs; this accomplishment reaches the utmost subtlety under Heaven and issues from the sages’ wondrous Way and refined understanding of what is right. How could the Changes do this by itself? This is what is meant by saying that the Changes contains the Way of the sages. Surely this is why people esteem it and why it benefits all under Heaven! Nevertheless, depth, incipient signs, and numinous efficacy are but one. They reside not in the Changes but in our own minds. Thus the sages cleanse their minds and withdraw into concealment; they purify themselves through fasting and attain spiritual illumination. What need have their minds to depend on external things? People gain no understanding beyond images and numbers and remain confined to the coarseness of material forms and implements. Their opinions fetter them, and their minds’ receptive luminosity is obscured. Then our minds too become mere things, and the Way of the Changes is hidden. Yet they seek to make themselves numinously powerful through petty divinatory techniques, as Jing Fang and Yanshou did. Alas! Is the numinous efficacy of the Changes really like this?

書
