歲大旱用汝作霖雨
石雷
同考試官教諭莫批高宗命傅說納誨屢託之
喻眞有見於相道之關君德如此是篇形容殆盡宜
錄以式
考試官教諭彭批親切
考試官教諭朱批典實
===
賢王命大臣以納誨必屢託喻以深致其望焉
夫相道之繋於君德也大矣賢王屢託喻以求
誨其望治之心不亦切乎想高宗之命傅說及
此意謂上下交而德業成君臣之相須也久矣
我之望汝納誨者何以擬諸其形容哉彼金所
以利用非礪則金無所成顧予德有未脩而弗
類之偏不能以自克者似之也其用汝以作礪
乎則夫斷同心之利以變化其氣質燋淬礪之
功以堅定其德性者於汝有深賴焉猶未也險
punctuated:
書

「若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。」

石雷

同考試官教諭莫批：「高宗命傅說納誨，屢託之喻，眞有見於相道之關君德如此。是篇形容殆盡，宜錄以式。」
考試官教諭彭批：「親切。」
考試官教諭朱批：「典實。」

賢王命大臣以納誨，必屢託喻以深致其望焉。夫相道之繋於君德也大矣！賢王屢託喻以求誨，其望治之心不亦切乎？想高宗之命傅說及此，意謂上下交而德業成，君臣之相須也久矣。我之望汝納誨者，何以擬諸其形容哉？彼金所以利用，非礪則金無所成。顧予德有未脩，而弗類之偏不能以自克者似之也。其用汝以作礪乎？則夫斷同心之利，以變化其氣質；燋淬礪之功，以堅定其德性者，於汝有深賴焉。猶未也，險
translation_en:
Book of Documents

“If I am metal, I shall employ you as a whetstone; if I am crossing a great river, I shall employ you as a boat and oars; if the year brings a great drought, I shall employ you as soaking rain.”

Shi Lei

Associate Examiner Mo, an Instructor, comments: “Gaozong commanded Fu Yue to offer admonition, repeatedly conveying his request through metaphors. He truly understood how the minister’s role bears upon the ruler’s virtue. This essay expresses that relationship almost exhaustively and should be recorded as a model.”
Examiner Peng, an Instructor, comments: “Direct and apt.”
Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “Classically grounded and substantial.”

When a worthy king commands a great minister to offer admonition, he must repeatedly resort to metaphors to convey the depth of his expectations.

The minister’s role has a great bearing upon the ruler’s virtue! When a worthy king repeatedly employs metaphors to seek admonition, is his longing for good government not earnest? Imagine Gaozong, when his charge to Fu Yue reached this point, meaning as follows: “Through interaction between those above and below, virtue and achievement are brought to fulfillment. Ruler and minister have long depended upon each other. What comparison can give form to my hope that you will offer admonition?

“Metal becomes a useful implement only through sharpening: without a whetstone, it cannot be brought to completion. I reflect that my virtue remains uncultivated, and that I cannot myself overcome my wayward inclinations; my condition resembles this. Shall I not employ you as a whetstone? In attaining the cutting power of united hearts, so as to transform my disposition, and in the work of firing, tempering, and sharpening [?], so as to make my moral nature firm, I depend profoundly upon you.

“Yet this is not all. As for peril…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
莫甚於巨川非舟楫則無以利涉顧予德有未
進而向往之機罔知津涯者似之也其用汝作
舟楫乎則夫引其不逮以弘濟乎艱難示我攸
往以誕登于道岸者於汝尤深賴焉猶未也大
旱之於霖雨望莫切焉者也顧予樹德之滋弗
遂而罔顯之學就荒者猶夫大旱也其用汝作
霖雨乎則夫發久閼之蒙以資潤身之德沛時
雨之化以植澤物之本者又非賴汝相須以有
成邪吁高宗命傅說至此言愈切而意愈深矣
===
則夫說之納誨以輔德者豈容已哉抑論高宗
奮起積衰恭默思道以端化理似無藉於臣之
啟沃矣今觀其託物之喻真若弗類而惓惓焉
厥後麴糵鹽梅之喻股肱惟人之喻不一而足
真聖不自聖之心也嗚呼憲天法祖遜志典學
之訓說之獻納於高宗者亦詳矣卒之君臣協
德為有商一代之賢君名佐有自哉
公其以予萬億年敬天之休
陶鑾
punctuated:
莫甚於巨川，非舟楫則無以利涉。顧予德有未進，而向往之機罔知津涯者似之也。其用汝作舟楫乎？則夫引其不逮，以弘濟乎艱難；示我攸往，以誕登于道岸者，於汝尤深賴焉。猶未也，大旱之於霖雨，望莫切焉者也。顧予樹德之滋弗遂，而罔顯之學就荒者，猶夫大旱也。其用汝作霖雨乎？則夫發久閼之蒙，以資潤身之德；沛時雨之化，以植澤物之本者，又非賴汝相須以有成邪？吁！高宗命傅說至此，言愈切而意愈深矣。則夫說之納誨以輔德者，豈容已哉？抑論高宗，奮起積衰，恭默思道，以端化理，似無藉於臣之啟沃矣。今觀其託物之喻，真若弗類而惓惓焉。厥後麴糵鹽梅之喻、股肱惟人之喻，不一而足，真聖不自聖之心也。嗚呼！憲天法祖、遜志典學之訓，說之獻納於高宗者亦詳矣。卒之君臣協德，為有商一代之賢君名佐，有自哉！

公其以予萬億年敬天之休。

陶鑾
translation_en:
…no danger is greater than a mighty river: without a boat and oars, there is no means of crossing safely. Consider how my virtue has yet to advance, and how, though moved to seek progress, I do not know the ford or the shore: my situation resembles this. Shall I employ you as my boat and oars? In guiding me where I fall short, so that I may fully surmount difficulties, and showing me where to go, so that I may ascend to the shore of the Way, I depend upon you still more deeply. Nor is this all. During a great drought, nothing is more urgently awaited than plentiful rain. Consider how my cultivation of virtue fails to flourish, while my learning, still unenlightened, falls into neglect: this resembles a great drought. Shall I employ you as plentiful rain? In dispelling the ignorance that has long remained pent up, thus nourishing the virtue that enriches the person, and abundantly dispensing the transforming influence of timely rain, thus establishing the foundation for benefiting all things, do I not again depend upon your assistance to achieve success?

Ah! At this point in Gaozong’s charge to Fu Yue, his words grow ever more earnest and his meaning ever deeper. How, then, could Yue possibly cease offering instruction to assist his ruler’s virtue? Yet consider Gaozong: he roused himself amid accumulated decline, reverently kept silence, and pondered the Way, thereby setting moral transformation and government on a proper course. It would seem that he had no need for a minister to enlighten and nourish his mind. Yet when we now examine his analogies drawn from things, he appears truly to regard himself as falling short, and to be deeply concerned about it. Later came the analogies of yeast and malt, of salt and plums, and of arms and legs in relation to the human body—too many to enumerate. This was truly the heart of a sage who did not deem himself a sage. Ah! Yue’s instructions to Gaozong—to take Heaven as his pattern and his ancestors as his models, and to humble his aspirations and devote himself steadfastly to learning—were also detailed. That ruler and minister ultimately united in virtue and became a worthy sovereign and a renowned minister of the Shang dynasty certainly had its foundation here!

“May you, Duke, enable me for countless years to reverently receive Heaven’s blessings.”

Tao Luan.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭莫批文氣沛然周公謀國之忠
發揮殆盡且結内體出終不果遷之故尤見學識錄
之
考試官教諭彭批通暢
考試官教諭朱批得旨
賢王於大臣之宅洛而美其遠有所期也夫洛
邑之作將以凝天命於無窮也成王叙以美之
其深識周公之心哉且其授使者復公之詞若
曰人臣之愛君也深故其謀國也遠公之作洛
===
也而豈徒哉彼朝諸侯而撫商民天固眷我有
周矣使自服土中者無其地則克紹上帝者無
其基何以永承天休邪辨方位而卜洛都公固
作周匹休矣然經始之既周則區畫之必當抑
豈近謀逸豫邪披其圖而審其勢規模弘遠蓋
欲我宅中圖大兢兢焉祗承天眷於無窮即其
卜而稽其兆思慮深長蓋欲我居重馭輕翼翼
焉敬迓天休於勿替故自今以至萬億年之久
恒來百辟之享則恒受申命之休而昌而富俾
punctuated:
同考試官教諭莫批：文氣沛然，周公謀國之忠發揮殆盡，且結内體出終不果遷之故，尤見學識，錄之。
考試官教諭彭批：通暢。
考試官教諭朱批：得旨。
賢王於大臣之宅洛，而美其遠有所期也。夫洛邑之作，將以凝天命於無窮也。成王叙以美之，其深識周公之心哉！且其授使者復公之詞，若曰：「人臣之愛君也深，故其謀國也遠。公之作洛也，而豈徒哉？彼朝諸侯而撫商民，天固眷我有周矣。使自服土中者無其地，則克紹上帝者無其基，何以永承天休邪？辨方位而卜洛都，公固作周匹休矣。然經始之既周，則區畫之必當，抑豈近謀逸豫邪？披其圖而審其勢，規模弘遠，蓋欲我宅中圖大，兢兢焉祗承天眷於無窮；即其卜而稽其兆，思慮深長，蓋欲我居重馭輕，翼翼焉敬迓天休於勿替。故自今以至萬億年之久，恒來百辟之享，則恒受申命之休，而昌而富，俾
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Mo, an Instructor, comments: “The writing flows with abundant vigor and gives almost complete expression to the Duke of Zhou’s loyal concern in planning for the state. Moreover, the conclusion brings out the reason why the move was ultimately not carried through, particularly revealing the writer’s learning and discernment. Select it.”
Examiner Peng, an Instructor, comments: “Clear and fluent.”
Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “Grasps the purport.”
The worthy king, considering his great minister’s establishment of a residence at Luo, praised the far-reaching hopes behind it. The building of Luoyi was intended to secure Heaven’s Mandate for all time. King Cheng set forth his praise: how deeply he understood the Duke of Zhou’s heart! The words he entrusted to the messenger in reply to the duke were as though he said:
“A minister’s love for his ruler is profound; hence his plans for the state reach far into the future. Could your building of Luo, my duke, have been without purpose? In receiving the regional lords at court and bringing peace to the people of Shang, our Zhou assuredly enjoys Heaven’s favor. Yet if there were no place from which to govern in the center of the land, there would be no foundation for carrying forward the charge of the Lord on High. How, then, could we receive Heaven’s blessings forever? By determining the directions and positions and divining the site of the capital at Luo, you have indeed brought Zhou blessings matching those of Heaven. Since your initial planning was comprehensive, your disposition of the site must have been fitting. Could you have been merely seeking ease and pleasure in the immediate future? When I unfold the plans and examine the configuration of the site, I see a design vast in scale and far-reaching in purpose. Surely you wish me to dwell at the center and plan great undertakings, reverently and watchfully receiving Heaven’s favor for all time. When I examine the divination and consider its omens, I see thought both profound and far-sighted. Surely you wish me to occupy the commanding center and control the lesser dependencies, cautiously and reverently welcoming Heaven’s blessings without interruption. Thus, from now through countless millions of years, if the offerings of all the lords continually arrive, we shall continually receive the blessing of the renewed Mandate, flourishing and prospering, so that …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
卜休之兆眞有符焉耳永奠商民之居則永膺
申祐之眷益隆益熾俾恒吉之徵眞有見焉耳
可大之業寔寓夫可久之規天之基命定命予
雖弗及知也而以人驗天竊自慶其貽翼之有
託矣相宅定宅公雖略示其槩也而以意逆志
已預覘其遠猷之有在矣噫周公忠君愛國之
心非成王其孰能知之哉雖然伻來命寧之後
卒不果遷者何也蓋自時中乂者周公之心亦
召公之心也而未欲捨鎬京以廢祖宗之舊者
===
則成王意也且祈天之實敬德誠民爲要區區
形勢抑其次耳則又何擇於鎬與洛之都也善
觀有周卜世之長者當在此而不在彼矣
詩
牧人乃夢衆維魚矣旐維旟矣大人占之
衆維魚矣實維豐年旐維旟矣室家溱
溱
李廷詔
同考試官教諭劉批〔作文不知關鍵雖文無益〕
punctuated:
卜休之兆眞有符焉耳。永奠商民之居，則永膺申祐之眷，益隆益熾，俾恒吉之徵眞有見焉耳。可大之業，寔寓夫可久之規。天之基命定命，予雖弗及知也，而以人驗天，竊自慶其貽翼之有託矣。相宅定宅，公雖略示其槩也，而以意逆志，已預覘其遠猷之有在矣。噫！周公忠君愛國之心，非成王，其孰能知之哉？雖然，伻來命寧之後，卒不果遷者，何也？蓋自時中乂者，周公之心，亦召公之心也；而未欲捨鎬京以廢祖宗之舊者，則成王意也。且祈天之實，敬德誠民爲要，區區形勢，抑其次耳。則又何擇於鎬與洛之都也？善觀有周卜世之長者，當在此而不在彼矣。

詩

牧人乃夢：衆維魚矣，旐維旟矣。大人占之：衆維魚矣，實維豐年；旐維旟矣，室家溱溱。

李廷詔

同考試官教諭劉批〔作文不知關鍵，雖文無益〕
translation_en:
…so that the auspicious signs foretold by divination truly find their fulfillment. By securing forever the dwelling places of the people of Shang, we shall forever receive Heaven’s renewed favor and protection, growing ever more flourishing and prosperous, so that the signs of lasting good fortune truly become manifest. An undertaking capable of greatness indeed embodies a plan capable of enduring. Though I cannot fully comprehend how Heaven establishes and confirms its mandate, by examining Heaven through human affairs I privately rejoice that the provision made for future generations has a firm foundation. Though the Duke has shown only the broad outlines of his selection and establishment of the capital, by apprehending his intentions I have already glimpsed the import of his far-reaching plans.

Ah! Who but King Cheng could understand the Duke of Zhou’s heart, loyal to his ruler and devoted to his state? Nevertheless, why was the move ultimately not carried out after the Duke sent a messenger to report that the site had been settled? To govern from this central place was the intention of the Duke of Zhou and also of the Duke of Shao; but it was King Cheng’s wish not to abandon Haojing and thereby forsake the ancestral seat. Moreover, the substance of seeking Heaven’s favor lies chiefly in revering virtue and dealing sincerely with the people; mere geographical advantages are secondary. What need, then, to choose between Hao and Luo as the capital? Anyone who properly considers the long succession of generations foretold for Zhou should look to this, rather than to that.

Book of Odes

The herdsmen dreamed: the multitudes became fish; tortoise-and-snake banners became falcon banners. The diviner interpreted them: “The multitudes becoming fish means a year of abundant harvests; tortoise-and-snake banners becoming falcon banners means households teeming with people.”

Li Tingzhao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔“In composing an essay, if one does not understand its crucial point, even literary polish is of no use.”〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也是篇美牧事而歸重富庶足闡詩人之旨末復推
本明德仁民又發詩人所未發者滇士有此可爲西
南得人慶矣
同考試官教諭胡批理眞辭達
考試官教諭彭批形容中興氣象宛然在目
是善作雅義者
考試官教諭朱批宏偉
詩人敘牧人感夢之異而兆富庶之祥焉蓋庶
而且富國家莫大之福也牧人感夢而兆是祥
===
非宣王中興之盛何以致之哉此詩美牧事有
成作也意謂天下之治無往不復國家之興有
開必先不驗諸今日中興之盛乎維彼牧人知
自盡其有事而已感夢之異則非緣舊於習心
者焉故其精神凝會之餘夢眾也而維魚也變
動莫之或居宜必有未然之徵也夢旐也而維
旟也恍惚不可爲象宜必有非常之應也於是
獻之天子占之大人蓋以曰眾曰魚皆以豐年
而後盛者也然人之多猶不若魚之多今夢眾
punctuated:
也。是篇美牧事而歸重富庶，足闡詩人之旨。末復推本明德仁民，又發詩人所未發者。滇士有此，可爲西南得人慶矣。
同考試官教諭胡批：理眞辭達。
考試官教諭彭批：形容中興氣象，宛然在目，是善作雅義者。
考試官教諭朱批：宏偉。
詩人敘牧人感夢之異，而兆富庶之祥焉。蓋庶而且富，國家莫大之福也。牧人感夢而兆是祥，非宣王中興之盛，何以致之哉？此詩美牧事有成作也。意謂天下之治，無往不復；國家之興，有開必先。不驗諸今日中興之盛乎？維彼牧人，知自盡其有事而已。感夢之異，則非緣舊於習心者焉。故其精神凝會之餘，夢眾也而維魚也，變動莫之或居，宜必有未然之徵也；夢旐也而維旟也，恍惚不可爲象，宜必有非常之應也。於是獻之天子，占之大人。蓋以曰眾曰魚，皆以豐年而後盛者也。然人之多猶不若魚之多，今夢眾
translation_en:
…This essay praises the work of herdsmen while placing its chief emphasis on prosperity and a flourishing population, adequately elucidating the poet’s intent. At the end it further traces these blessings to illuminating virtue and treating the people benevolently, bringing out what the poet himself left unexpressed. That a scholar of Yunnan can produce such work is cause to celebrate the southwest’s acquisition of a worthy talent.
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: The principles are sound and the language conveys them clearly.
Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: The depiction of the age of restoration brings its atmosphere vividly before our eyes. This is someone skilled at composing an exposition of the Odes of the Kingdom.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Grand and imposing.
The poet recounts the marvel of the herdsmen’s dreams, which portend the blessings of prosperity and a flourishing population. For a populous and prosperous realm is the greatest blessing a state can enjoy. The herdsmen’s dreams foretold these blessings: what could have brought this about except the flourishing restoration under King Xuan? This poem was composed to praise success in tending the herds. Its meaning is that good order in the world, once departed, will return, and that a state’s rise is necessarily preceded by signs of its coming. Is this not borne out by the flourishing restoration of the present day? Those herdsmen knew only to fulfill their duties to the utmost. The marvels of their dreams did not arise from familiar experiences ingrained in their minds. Thus, when their vital energies and spirits had gathered in concentration, they dreamed of multitudes, yet these were fish. Such transformations have no fixed form; surely they must signify something yet to occur. They dreamed of tortoise-and-snake banners, yet these were falcon banners. These elusive visions could not be given definite shape; surely they must correspond to something extraordinary. Accordingly, they presented the dreams to the Son of Heaven, and the great diviner interpreted them. For both the multitudes and the fish flourish only after years of abundant harvests. Yet even multitudes of people are not so numerous as fish. Now they dreamed of multitudes…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
維魚其豐年之占乎君德厚於斂福天命錫以
平康四時和焉百穀成焉所謂豐年穰穰者信
有之矣夫食民之天也旣富矣而民有不若其
生者哉曰旐曰旟皆民庶所由統者也然旐所
統猶不若旟之衆今夢旐維旟其人衆之占乎
上帝昭求莫之鑒大君溥安集之恩四方歸焉
兆民殖焉所謂室家溱溱者胥得之矣夫民邦
之本也旣庶矣而邦有不孚於休者哉是則夢
感於牧人而所以成其夢者非牧人所能與也
===
占究於大人而所以獲其占者非大人所能知
也天將啓中興之治特假此洩其微耳夫豈偶
然者哉抑王政有本焉有序焉仁民愛物其序
也明德其本也故時雍咸若惟克明峻德者致
之茁葭恩及庶類說者以爲鵲巢之應宣王聽
納脫簪之諫側脩雲漢之憂所以成中興盛治
有自也無羊之詩豈溢美哉善學者可以觀矣
懷柔百神及河喬嶽 萬谷
punctuated:
維魚，其豐年之占乎？君德厚於斂福，天命錫以平康，四時和焉，百穀成焉，所謂「豐年穰穰」者信有之矣。夫食，民之天也；旣富矣，而民有不若其生者哉？曰旐曰旟，皆民庶所由統者也。然旐所統猶不若旟之衆，今夢旐維旟，其人衆之占乎？上帝昭求莫之鑒，大君溥安集之恩，四方歸焉，兆民殖焉，所謂「室家溱溱」者胥得之矣。夫民，邦之本也；旣庶矣，而邦有不孚於休者哉？是則夢感於牧人，而所以成其夢者，非牧人所能與也；占究於大人，而所以獲其占者，非大人所能知也。天將啓中興之治，特假此洩其微耳，夫豈偶然者哉？抑王政有本焉，有序焉：仁民愛物，其序也；明德，其本也。故時雍咸若，惟克明峻德者致之。茁葭恩及庶類，說者以爲《鵲巢》之應。宣王聽納脫簪之諫，側脩《雲漢》之憂，所以成中興盛治有自也。《無羊》之詩豈溢美哉？善學者可以觀矣。
懷柔百神，及河喬嶽。萬谷
translation_en:
…become fish: is this not an omen of a plentiful year? The ruler’s virtue is abundant in gathering blessings, and Heaven’s mandate bestows peace and well-being. The four seasons are harmonious, and all the grains ripen. What is called “a plentiful year of abundant harvests” will surely come to pass. Food is the people’s Heaven; once they are prosperous, how could any fail to enjoy a favorable livelihood? The banners called zhao and yu both serve to muster the common people. Yet those assembled under a zhao banner are fewer than those under a yu banner. Now, in the dream, zhao banners become yu banners: is this not an omen of a numerous population? The Lord on High manifestly seeks, with none to scrutinize [?]; the great ruler extends to all his kindness in settling and gathering the people. All regions turn to him, and the multitudes increase. What is called “households teeming with people” is thus everywhere attained. The people are the foundation of the state; once they are numerous, how could the state fail to accord with goodness? Thus, although the dream is inspired in the herdsmen, what brings it to fulfillment lies beyond their power to influence. Although the great diviner fully investigates the omen, what brings its promise to fruition lies beyond his knowledge. Heaven, about to inaugurate an era of resurgent government, merely uses this means to disclose its hidden workings. How could this be accidental?
Yet kingly government has both a foundation and an order of progression. Showing benevolence to the people and love for other creatures is its order of progression; making virtue manifest is its foundation. Thus universal harmony and concord are brought about only by one who can make lofty virtue manifest. In the lines about flourishing reeds, kindness reaches all kinds of creatures; commentators regard this as the response to the influence of “The Magpie’s Nest.” King Xuan accepted the remonstrance offered when his queen removed her hairpin, and anxiously cultivated himself amid the cares expressed in “The Milky Way” [?]. His achievement of flourishing government through dynastic resurgence therefore had its source. How could the poem “No Sheep” be excessive praise? Those skilled in learning may discern this here.
“He brings peace to the hundred spirits, including the River and the lofty mountains.” — Wan Gu

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭劉批〔見理明而氣復鬯達允宜高薦〕
同考試官教諭胡批〔題難形容平正通達僅有此耳〕
考試官教諭彭批〔字字體貼明確是善作者〕
考試官教諭朱批〔語和而莊〕
周王舉祭告而徧格乎神可以觀天受矣盖有
天下者祭百神也然則天之右序有周豈不可
驗諸羣神之格哉此巡守而朝會祭告之樂歌
===
也意謂我周方集大統於會朝卽行時巡於天
下豈獨朝會而諸侯震疊已哉天子者百神爾
主者也景命維新則告報在所當先也為之置
茅蕝設表望以招徠之而百神之效靈者咸翕
然於萃渙之始大典肇行則儀物在所當備也
為之奠圭幣將牲醴以妥侑之而百神之效順
者皆安然於覲薦之餘夫神之佑助者信也我
周明信昭焉故懷之而罔不懷來格如在乎其
上耳神所馮依者德也我周明德馨焉故柔之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭劉批〔見理明而氣復鬯達，允宜高薦。〕
同考試官教諭胡批〔題難形容，平正通達，僅有此耳。〕
考試官教諭彭批〔字字體貼明確，是善作者。〕
考試官教諭朱批〔語和而莊。〕
周王舉祭告而徧格乎神，可以觀天受矣。盖有天下者祭百神也，然則天之右序有周，豈不可驗諸羣神之格哉？此巡守而朝會祭告之樂歌也。意謂我周方集大統於會朝，卽行時巡於天下，豈獨朝會而諸侯震疊已哉？天子者，百神爾主者也。景命維新，則告報在所當先也。為之置茅蕝、設表望以招徠之，而百神之效靈者咸翕然於萃渙之始。大典肇行，則儀物在所當備也。為之奠圭幣、將牲醴以妥侑之，而百神之效順者皆安然於覲薦之餘。夫神之佑助者信也，我周明信昭焉，故懷之而罔不懷，來格如在乎其上耳。神所馮依者德也，我周明德馨焉，故柔之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: “His understanding of principle is clear, and his expressive vigor is also free-flowing and expansive. He truly deserves a high recommendation.”
Associate Examiner Hu, an Instructor, comments: “The topic is difficult to express fully. For balanced, correct, and lucid treatment, this alone suffices.”
Examiner Peng, an Instructor, comments: “Every word fits the subject closely and precisely. This is a skilled writer.”
Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “The language is harmonious yet dignified.”
The king of Zhou performed sacrifices and ritual announcements, reaching all the spirits; through this one may discern Heaven’s acceptance [?]. For whoever possesses All under Heaven sacrifices to the hundred spirits. Could Heaven’s aid to, and ordering of, Zhou not therefore be verified through the arrival of the assembled spirits? This is a ritual song for royal inspection tours, court assemblies, sacrifices, and announcements.
Its meaning is this: our Zhou was just consolidating its unified rule through the court assembly and undertaking seasonal inspection tours throughout All under Heaven. Could this merely have been a court assembly at which the feudal lords trembled in awe? The Son of Heaven is your lord, O hundred spirits. With the great mandate newly bestowed, ritual announcements and offerings of recompense must take precedence. Bundles of thatch were placed and markers for distant worship erected to summon the spirits; all those manifesting their numinous power gathered in concord as the rites of assembly and dispersal began. With the great ceremony first being performed, the ritual furnishings and offerings had to be fully prepared. Jade tablets and silk were laid out, and sacrificial animals and sweet wine presented, to settle and entertain the spirits; all those manifesting their compliance rested at ease after the audience and presentation of offerings.
Now, what the spirits aid and support is sincerity. Our Zhou’s manifest sincerity shines forth. Thus, when it draws them near, none fails to draw near: they come and arrive as though present above the worshippers. What the spirits rely upon is virtue. Our Zhou’s luminous virtue spreads its fragrance. Thus it brings them peace…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而罔不柔居歆如見乎其位耳以神之大者言
之深廣有河祀及於河之神焉則翕猶率其性
固已鑒精意於淵泉矣崇高維嶽祀及於嶽之
神焉則艮止安其常固已垂降臨於峻極矣以
興雲雨以取財用河嶽皆祀典之所載也感通
若甚難也今信以孚之果何限於崇深邪以毓
靈秀以發精英河嶽皆聖王之所隆也昭假之
未易也今德以動之又何間於高大邪河嶽且
格而況深廣非河者乎況崇高非嶽者乎於此
===
益驗百神之受職昊天之右序也周王之君天
下也豈不信然也哉抑武王執競之心至此若
可少紓矣噫聖人純一不已者也方且審慶讓
黜陟之典斂戎器而陳之文德其致謹於天人
之際以嚴保命之防者至矣八百年靈長之祚
夫豈偶然哉
春秋
春齊人陳人曹人伐宋莊公十有四年
胡然
punctuated:
而罔不柔，居歆如見乎其位耳。以神之大者言之，深廣有河，祀及於河之神焉，則翕猶率其性，固已鑒精意於淵泉矣；崇高維嶽，祀及於嶽之神焉，則艮止安其常，固已垂降臨於峻極矣。以興雲雨，以取財用，河嶽皆祀典之所載也。感通若甚難也，今信以孚之，果何限於崇深邪？以毓靈秀，以發精英，河嶽皆聖王之所隆也。昭假之未易也，今德以動之，又何間於高大邪？河嶽且格，而況深廣非河者乎？況崇高非嶽者乎？於此益驗百神之受職、昊天之右序也。周王之君天下也，豈不信然也哉？抑武王執競之心，至此若可少紓矣。噫！聖人純一不已者也，方且審慶讓黜陟之典，斂戎器而陳之文德。其致謹於天人之際，以嚴保命之防者至矣。八百年靈長之祚，夫豈偶然哉！
春秋
春，齊人、陳人、曹人伐宋。莊公十有四年。
胡然
translation_en:
…and none failed to be conciliated; they abode there and accepted the offerings, as though visibly present in their places. Speaking of the greatest spirits: there is the deep and broad He, the Yellow River. When sacrifices reached its spirit, it harmoniously followed its nature [?], and already perceived the sincerity of their intentions in its deep waters. There are the lofty sacred mountains. When sacrifices reached their spirits, they rested in stillness, secure in their constancy, and already deigned to descend upon the towering heights. For raising clouds and rain and supplying material resources, the river and the sacred mountains are all included in the sacrificial canon. Establishing communion with them might seem exceedingly difficult; yet now that sincerity wins their trust, what barrier could height or depth impose? For nurturing numinous excellence and bringing forth the finest essences, the river and the sacred mountains are all exalted by sage kings. Reaching them through manifest virtue is no easy matter; yet now that virtue moves them, what separation could their height and grandeur create? If even the river and the sacred mountains come into the divine presence, how much more those that are deep and broad but are not the river, or lofty but are not the sacred mountains? Here is further proof that the hundred spirits receive their appointed duties and that August Heaven lends its aid and establishes order. Is it not indeed true that the king of Zhou rules all under Heaven?
Perhaps King Wu’s resolve to maintain his strength could now relax a little. Ah! The sage remains wholly single-minded without cease. He was still carefully examining the institutions of rewards and reprimands, dismissals and promotions, gathering in the weapons of war and displaying civil virtue. His care at the juncture of Heaven and humanity, maintaining strict safeguards for preserving the Mandate, reached the utmost degree. Could the dynasty’s enduring, auspicious tenure of eight hundred years possibly have been accidental?
Spring and Autumn Annals
“In spring, men of Qi, Chen, and Cao attacked Song.” The fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
Hu Ran

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:

之深廣有河祀及於河之神焉則翕猶率其性

translation_en:
…and none failed to be placated; they took their places and enjoyed the offerings, as though visibly present at their appointed stations. Speaking of the greater spirits: there is the deep and broad Yellow River. When sacrifice reached its spirit, it followed its nature in harmonious movement [?], and already discerned the worshipper’s pure intent in its deep waters. There are the lofty Sacred Peaks. When sacrifice reached their spirits, they rested in stillness, abiding in their constancy, and already deigned to descend upon their towering summits. Could the enduring blessing of an eight-hundred-year dynasty possibly have been accidental?
Spring and Autumn Annals
“In spring, men of Qi, Chen, and Cao attacked Song.” 〔The fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
Hu Ran

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
域中而抗衡之國自服南莫强於荆楚也而有
以摧之西莫勁於秦晉也而有以抑之率天下
而莫能與之爭者謂非今日休養之效不可也
向使桓仲君臣輕謀淺慮恃其方興之勢而毒
衆以逞不爲厚下之圖而悉賦以從則四出之
征亦難乎其繼一匡之業安必其能成乎故伐
宋之役三國稱人非貶之也蓋曰將卑師少云
爾所以予其用兵有制而賦於民薄也於是見
桓公之霸不爲無關於世故仲父之佐不爲無
===
益於人國聖人有取焉豈徒然哉嗟夫兵凶戰
危王者用之於誅暴禁亂非得已也春秋之時
無名妄動者踵接矣其所以予桓者亦謂彼善
於此爾北杏之會爲平宋難尋復背之無乃巳
德有關而何遽以兵加之乎故傳有之曰桓文
之節制不如湯武之仁義
盟于召陵僖公四年會于蕭魚襄公十有
一年
楊一麒
punctuated:
域中，而抗衡之國自服。南莫强於荆楚也，而有以摧之；西莫勁於秦晉也，而有以抑之。率天下而莫能與之爭者，謂非今日休養之效，不可也。向使桓仲君臣輕謀淺慮，恃其方興之勢而毒衆以逞，不爲厚下之圖，而悉賦以從，則四出之征亦難乎其繼，一匡之業安必其能成乎？故伐宋之役，三國稱人，非貶之也，蓋曰將卑師少云爾，所以予其用兵有制而賦於民薄也。於是見桓公之霸不爲無關於世故，仲父之佐不爲無益於人國。聖人有取焉，豈徒然哉！嗟夫！兵凶戰危，王者用之於誅暴禁亂，非得已也。春秋之時，無名妄動者踵接矣。其所以予桓者，亦謂彼善於此爾。北杏之會爲平宋難，尋復背之，無乃巳德有關，而何遽以兵加之乎？故傳有之曰：「桓文之節制，不如湯武之仁義。」

盟于召陵，僖公四年；會于蕭魚，襄公十有一年。
楊一麒
translation_en:
…within the realm, and the states that rivaled him submitted of their own accord. In the south none was stronger than Jing-Chu, yet he had the means to crush it; in the west none was more formidable than Qin and Jin, yet he had the means to restrain them. He led all under Heaven, and none could contend with him: one cannot deny that this resulted from the respite and recuperation afforded the people at this time. Had Duke Huan and Guan Zhong, ruler and minister, made rash plans with little foresight, relying on their rising power to oppress the people and gratify their ambitions, making no provision for enriching those below but exacting all their resources to support their campaigns, even their expeditions in every direction would have been difficult to sustain. How could they have been sure of accomplishing the great task of setting the realm in order? Thus, in the campaign against Song, the three states are referred to as “men,” not to disparage them, but simply to indicate that their commanders were of low rank and their forces small. This commends their restraint in deploying troops and the lightness of their levies on the people. Here we see that Duke Huan’s hegemony was not without relevance to the affairs of the age, and that the assistance of Zhongfu [Guan Zhong] was not without benefit to a ruler’s state. Could the Sage’s approval have been groundless?

Alas! Arms are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is perilous. True kings employ them to punish violence and suppress disorder only when they have no alternative. In the Spring and Autumn period, those who recklessly took up arms without just cause followed one another in succession. The approval accorded Duke Huan means merely that his conduct was better than theirs. The meeting at Beixing was held to settle the troubles in Song, yet soon afterward Song again repudiated the agreement. Might there not have been some deficiency in his own virtue [?], and why did he so hastily attack Song with troops? Thus the commentary says: “The discipline and restraint of Dukes Huan and Wen fell short of the benevolence and righteousness of Tang and Wu.”

“They covenanted at Shaoling”—the fourth year of Duke Xi; “They met at Xiaoyu”—the eleventh year of Duke Xiang.
Yang Yiqi.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭彭批深得聖人美桓悼之意
考試官教諭朱批春秋之時惟詐力是競不
知禮與誠為何物矣僅於召陵蕭魚見之故聖人不
得已而有予於桓悼也子能善發其蘊錄出以式
創伯禮以服外繼伯誠以感貳春秋胥著其美
焉蓋召陵之盟蕭魚之會桓悼二伯之美績也
是故見予於春秋且召陵何為而盟邪齊桓伐
楚按兵陘亭因屈完如師而為是盟也當是時
納款雖勤應對未屈使桓也惟戰勝攻克是期
===
則浸強之夷何以厭其心乃今知天下無不可
制之敵惟患吾禮有未盡也退師召陵徼與同
好而不遂焉威霽於觀兵之際信孚於共歃之
間以兵戈則既戢矣以文告則既脩矣以驕暴
則既斂而泯矣彼楚人者亦安得不降心而輸
款哉噫舞干息而因壘遠王者之事弗可復見
孰圖桓之庶幾乎此論者謂為五伯之盛信矣
蕭魚何為而會邪晉悼伐鄭觀兵東門因伯駢
行成而為是會也當是時內附雖切從違靡常
punctuated:
考試官教諭彭批：深得聖人美桓悼之意。
考試官教諭朱批：春秋之時，惟詐力是競，不知禮與誠為何物矣。僅於召陵、蕭魚見之，故聖人不得已而有予於桓悼也。子能善發其蘊，錄出以式。
創伯禮以服外，繼伯誠以感貳，春秋胥著其美焉。蓋召陵之盟、蕭魚之會，桓悼二伯之美績也，是故見予於春秋。且召陵何為而盟邪？齊桓伐楚，按兵陘亭，因屈完如師而為是盟也。當是時，納款雖勤，應對未屈。使桓也惟戰勝攻克是期，則浸強之夷何以厭其心？乃今知天下無不可制之敵，惟患吾禮有未盡也。退師召陵，徼與同好而不遂焉。威霽於觀兵之際，信孚於共歃之間。以兵戈則既戢矣，以文告則既脩矣，以驕暴則既斂而泯矣。彼楚人者，亦安得不降心而輸款哉？噫！舞干息而因壘遠，王者之事弗可復見，孰圖桓之庶幾乎此？論者謂為五伯之盛，信矣。
蕭魚何為而會邪？晉悼伐鄭，觀兵東門，因伯駢行成而為是會也。當是時，內附雖切，從違靡常。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: This thoroughly grasps the Sage’s intention in praising Dukes Huan and Dao.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: In the Spring and Autumn period, men competed only in deception and force, knowing nothing of ritual propriety and sincerity. These qualities appear only at Shaoling and Xiaoyu; thus the Sage could not but accord some approval to Dukes Huan and Dao. You have skillfully brought out the underlying meaning. This answer is selected for inclusion as a model.
The founding hegemon used ritual propriety to bring outsiders into submission; a succeeding hegemon used sincerity to move those of divided allegiance. The Spring and Autumn Annals makes manifest the excellence of both. The covenant at Shaoling and the meeting at Xiaoyu were indeed fine achievements of the two hegemons, Dukes Huan and Dao. For this reason they receive approval in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why, then, was a covenant concluded at Shaoling? Duke Huan of Qi attacked Chu and halted his army at Xingting. When Qu Wan came to the army, this covenant was concluded. At that time, although Chu was diligent in offering amity, its responses remained unyielding. Had Duke Huan sought only victory in battle and conquest by assault, how could these increasingly powerful outsiders have satisfied his ambitions? He now understood that there was no enemy under Heaven that could not be brought under control; his only concern was that his own ritual propriety might fall short. He withdrew his army to Shaoling, seeking to share friendly relations without pressing his purpose to the end [?]. His threatening might subsided amid the display of troops, and mutual trust took hold as they together sipped the covenant blood. Weapons had been put away; formal proclamations had been duly prepared; arrogance and violence had been restrained and extinguished. How could the people of Chu fail to humble themselves and offer their allegiance? Alas! The dancing with shields had ceased, and the age of “yin lei” was distant [?]. The deeds of true kings could no longer be witnessed. Who would have imagined that Duke Huan might come so close to them? Those who discuss this call it the height of achievement among the Five Hegemons. Truly so!
Why was a meeting held at Xiaoyu? Duke Dao of Jin attacked Zheng and displayed his troops at its eastern gate. When Bo Pian negotiated peace, this meeting was held. At that time, although Zheng was eager to submit, its obedience and defiance were inconstant …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
使悼也惟刑牲歃血是爲則攜貳之鄭何以堅
其從乃今知天下無不可感之人惟患吾誠之
未至也卽彼蕭魚請服于會而弗疑焉推赤心
以相與置明神而罔徼以斥候則納之也以侵
掠則禁之也以俘囚則禮而歸之也彼鄭人者
亦安得不心悅而誠服哉噫盟詛煩而約劑亂
傾危之俗不可復挽孰圖悼之推誠若此論者
謂其有君子之資信矣是則桓公之績莫大於
制楚悼公之功莫大於服鄭斯皆一經之僅見
===
者也聖人大書特書豈容已哉抑齊之能致楚
者始於管仲之對楚之不能爭鄭者由於知罃
之謀桓悼二公善用而聽焉斯其所以成伯烈
也雖然盟會非春秋之所貴也召陵蕭魚玆其
深美之者美其事也非予其盟與會也其亦聖
人不得已之意也夫
禮記
善歌者使人繼其聲善教者使人繼其志〔陳瑞麟〕
punctuated:
使悼也惟刑牲歃血是爲，則攜貳之鄭何以堅其從？乃今知天下無不可感之人，惟患吾誠之未至也。卽彼蕭魚，請服于會而弗疑焉，推赤心以相與，置明神而罔徼。以斥候則納之也，以侵掠則禁之也，以俘囚則禮而歸之也。彼鄭人者亦安得不心悅而誠服哉？噫！盟詛煩而約劑亂，傾危之俗不可復挽，孰圖悼之推誠若此？論者謂其有君子之資，信矣。是則桓公之績莫大於制楚，悼公之功莫大於服鄭，斯皆一經之僅見者也。聖人大書特書，豈容已哉？抑齊之能致楚者，始於管仲之對；楚之不能爭鄭者，由於知罃之謀。桓、悼二公善用而聽焉，斯其所以成伯烈也。雖然，盟會非春秋之所貴也。召陵、蕭魚，玆其深美之者，美其事也，非予其盟與會也。其亦聖人不得已之意也夫！

禮記

善歌者使人繼其聲，善教者使人繼其志。〔陳瑞麟〕
translation_en:
…Had Duke Dao concerned himself solely with slaughtering sacrificial animals and smearing blood upon the lips in covenant, how could he have secured the steadfast allegiance of the wavering state of Zheng? We now see that there is no one under Heaven who cannot be moved; our only concern should be that our own sincerity has not reached its fullest extent. At Xiaoyu, he accepted without suspicion Zheng’s request to submit at the meeting. He dealt with them with an utterly sincere heart, setting aside appeals to the divine powers and seeking no guarantees from them. He recalled the scouts, prohibited raids and plunder, and treated the captives courteously and sent them home. How could the people of Zheng fail to rejoice in their hearts and submit sincerely? Alas! Covenant oaths had grown burdensome and agreements confused; the prevailing habits of treachery and insecurity seemed beyond reversal. Who could have imagined that Duke Dao would extend sincerity in this way? Those who judge him say that he possessed the qualities of a gentleman. Indeed he did.

Thus, none of Duke Huan’s achievements surpassed his restraining Chu, and none of Duke Dao’s accomplishments surpassed his winning Zheng’s submission. These were both rare occurrences in this Classic. How could the Sage refrain from recording them prominently and with special emphasis? Moreover, Qi’s success in bringing Chu to terms began with Guan Zhong’s reply, while Chu’s inability to contend for Zheng resulted from Zhi Ying’s strategy. Dukes Huan and Dao listened to these men and employed them well: this was how they achieved the glorious accomplishments of hegemons. Nevertheless, covenants and assemblies are not what the Spring and Autumn Annals prizes. Its profound praise of Shaoling and Xiaoyu praises what was accomplished there; it does not endorse the covenant and the assembly themselves. Surely this, too, expresses the Sage’s recognition that circumstances left no alternative!

Book of Rites

“One who sings well enables others to continue his voice; one who teaches well enables others to carry on his aspirations.” 〔Chen Ruilin〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭彭批意新語健夐異衆作宜錄
以式
考試官教諭朱批講二使字能說出善歌善
教者之意
記者卽善歌以明教必各著其所以善也蓋教
益於人斯其爲善也大矣記者卽歌以明之其
事異而理同者歟學記之意以爲道由師傳學
貴有得然爲師之道何以能使學者之有得哉
觀乎善歌也可見矣蓋歌者直巳而陳德者也
===
寧無肄之者乎使倡之也非善焉則孰從而繼
其聲也唯夫善歌者依永之聲自動夫同然之
契而和聲之律默感其聽德之聰如抗如墜固
無心於聆者之協一也然音響雋永同好翕然
以相應在夫人也猶夫在巳也中鈞中矩教固
無望於聽者之合一也然意趣悠揚同聲繹如
以相成其在彼也猶夫在此也是繼其聲者雖
人也而鼓其幾者歌之者使之也謂非善歌可
乎夫歌曲藝也其善且然而況於善教者哉蓋
punctuated:
考試官教諭彭批：意新語健，夐異衆作，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭朱批：講二使字，能說出善歌、善教者之意。
記者卽善歌以明教，必各著其所以善也。蓋教益於人，斯其爲善也大矣。記者卽歌以明之，其事異而理同者歟？學記之意，以爲道由師傳，學貴有得。然爲師之道，何以能使學者之有得哉？觀乎善歌也，可見矣。蓋歌者，直巳而陳德者也，寧無肄之者乎？使倡之也非善焉，則孰從而繼其聲也？唯夫善歌者，依永之聲，自動夫同然之契；而和聲之律，默感其聽德之聰。如抗如墜，固無心於聆者之協一也；然音響雋永，同好翕然以相應，在夫人也，猶夫在巳也。中鈞中矩，教固無望於聽者之合一也；然意趣悠揚，同聲繹如以相成，其在彼也，猶夫在此也。是繼其聲者雖人也，而鼓其幾者，歌之者使之也，謂非善歌可乎？夫歌，曲藝也，其善且然，而況於善教者哉？蓋
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: The conception is fresh and the language vigorous, far surpassing the other compositions. It should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: In explaining the two occurrences of “cause,” this brings out the meaning of being skilled at singing and skilled at teaching.
The compiler of the Record uses skill in singing to illuminate teaching, necessarily showing what makes each excellent. Teaching benefits others: great indeed is its excellence. The compiler illustrates it through singing. Are these not different activities sharing the same principle? The meaning of the Record of Learning is that the Way is transmitted through teachers, and that what matters in learning is making it one's own. Yet how can the practice of teaching enable learners to attain such understanding? We can see this by considering skill in singing. Singing gives upright expression to oneself and sets forth virtue. Surely there are people who practice it? If someone leads the singing without skill, who will follow and continue his sound? Only in a skilled singer does the sound, following the sustained chant, spontaneously stir a sympathetic accord grounded in what people share; the measures of its harmonious tones silently move listeners' capacity to discern virtue. Whether the sound seems lifted up or falling down, the singer certainly has no deliberate intention of making listeners join in unison. Yet its resonance has a lasting savor, and those who share his taste respond together in harmony: what is in others is just as it is in himself. It accords with the compass and the square; the teaching [?] certainly has no expectation that listeners will unite as one. Yet its expressive feeling carries far, and kindred voices follow continuously, bringing one another to fulfillment: what is there is just as it is here. Thus, although it is others who continue his sound, it is the singer who causes this by stirring their incipient impulses. Could one deny that this is skill in singing? Singing is a minor art, yet its excellence achieves even this. How much more must this be true of one skilled at teaching! For…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
敎者長善而救失者也寧無師之者乎使喻之
也非善焉則孰從而繼其志也唯夫善敎者無
言之感適觸其有覺之天開導之機時遂其憤
悱之願語默隨宜固嘗因性以牖之也而起予
之益殆發其未傳之蘊博約異施固嘗因材而
篤之也而心解之神實闡其獨得之眞是繼其
志者雖人也而啓其思者敎之者使之也謂非
善敎可乎是知繼之云者學者之深於得也使
之云者則敎者之妙於喻也能善是斯可以爲
===
師矣雖然繼志之敎固師之善而所以能繼其
志者亦學者之善也否則投之無幾受之無地
雖有善將安施哉是故四勿方傳請事隨繼一
貫之唯洞然不疑顏曾之外無聞焉聖人之敎
固無私也君子之學可自諉乎
此五行者足以正身而安國矣彼國安而
天下安故曰吾觀於鄕而知王道之易
易也
周佐
punctuated:
敎者，長善而救失者也，寧無師之者乎？使喻之也非善焉，則孰從而繼其志也？唯夫善敎者，無言之感，適觸其有覺之天；開導之機，時遂其憤悱之願。語默隨宜，固嘗因性以牖之也，而起予之益，殆發其未傳之蘊；博約異施，固嘗因材而篤之也，而心解之神，實闡其獨得之眞。是繼其志者雖人也，而啓其思者，敎之者使之也，謂非善敎可乎？是知繼之云者，學者之深於得也；使之云者，則敎者之妙於喻也。能善是，斯可以爲師矣。雖然，繼志之敎固師之善，而所以能繼其志者，亦學者之善也。否則，投之無幾，受之無地，雖有善，將安施哉？是故四勿方傳，請事隨繼；一貫之唯，洞然不疑。顏曾之外，無聞焉。聖人之敎固無私也，君子之學可自諉乎？
此五行者，足以正身而安國矣。彼國安而天下安，故曰：「吾觀於鄕，而知王道之易易也。」
周佐
translation_en:
…Teaching nurtures goodness and remedies failings. Surely there are people who take the teacher as their master? If he is not skilled in bringing them to understanding, who will follow him and carry forward his intent? Only a skilled teacher can, through wordless influence, touch the learner’s innate capacity for awareness, and offer guidance at the right moment to satisfy the learner’s desire to understand what he cannot yet grasp or express. Speaking or remaining silent as circumstances require, he opens the learner’s understanding in accordance with his nature; yet the benefit of the learner’s response—“you have enlightened me”—may bring forth implications the teacher has not yet conveyed. Applying broad learning and concentrated essentials differently, he develops each learner according to his capacities; yet the marvel of understanding in the heart truly unfolds the truth the learner has grasped for himself. Thus, although it is another person who carries forward the teacher’s intent, it is the teacher who causes that person’s thinking to awaken. Can this be called anything but skilled teaching? We therefore know that “carrying forward” refers to the depth of the learner’s understanding, while “causing” refers to the teacher’s subtle skill in bringing him to understanding. Someone who excels at this can serve as a teacher.
Nevertheless, teaching that enables others to carry forward one’s intent certainly reflects the teacher’s excellence, but the ability to carry forward that intent also reflects the learner’s excellence. Otherwise, instruction offered finds no incipient understanding to engage and no ground in which to be received. However great the teacher’s skill, where could he apply it? Thus, as soon as the four prohibitions were transmitted, a request to put them into practice followed; and the assent to the teaching of “one thread running through all” expressed lucid understanding without doubt. Beyond Yan Hui and Zeng Shen, no such instances have been heard of. The sage’s teaching is surely impartial. Can the gentleman evade his own responsibility for learning?
These five practices suffice to rectify oneself and bring peace to the state. When that state is at peace, all under Heaven will be at peace. Thus it is said: “By observing the village ceremony, I know how very easy the Kingly Way is to realize.”
Zhou Zuo

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭彭批黜浮崇雅詞旨明當佳士
也
考試官敎諭朱批純正可觀
聖人舉鄉飲備衆善而裕於治因以見其言之
有徵也甚矣禮敎之足以裕治也聖人觀於鄉
而知其易易焉其深有感於是夫記鄉飲酒者
意謂人知王道之成也其效大而不知禮敎之
達也其幾同彼鄉飲之行貴賤明也隆殺辨也
弟長而無遺也安燕而不亂也和樂而不流也
===
是五者之行也足以立百順大化之基矣推而
行之安往而弗獲哉吾見以之而脩身也則利
用安身懋著夫作孚之表崇德脩慝丕成夫齊
正之階身不由是而正邪以之而安國也則德
溥化光一國遂太和之效道成政洽一方臻至
治之休國不由是而安邪國旣安矣將見信義
篤而禮讓行九有興和敬之俗賢能衆而治功
美萬方成秩敘之風天下不由是而安乎夫大
本立而萬化行王者之所以致治也今觀於鄉
punctuated:
考試官敎諭彭批：黜浮崇雅，詞旨明當，佳士也。
考試官敎諭朱批：純正可觀。
聖人舉鄉飲，備衆善而裕於治，因以見其言之有徵也。甚矣，禮敎之足以裕治也！聖人觀於鄉而知其易易焉，其深有感於是夫！記鄉飲酒者，意謂人知王道之成也，其效大，而不知禮敎之達也，其幾同。彼鄉飲之行，貴賤明也，隆殺辨也，弟長而無遺也，安燕而不亂也，和樂而不流也。是五者之行也，足以立百順大化之基矣。推而行之，安往而弗獲哉？吾見以之而脩身也，則利用安身，懋著夫作孚之表；崇德脩慝，丕成夫齊正之階。身不由是而正邪？以之而安國也，則德溥化光，一國遂太和之效；道成政洽，一方臻至治之休。國不由是而安邪？國旣安矣，將見信義篤而禮讓行，九有興和敬之俗；賢能衆而治功美，萬方成秩敘之風。天下不由是而安乎？夫大本立而萬化行，王者之所以致治也。今觀於鄉
translation_en:
Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: “He rejects superficiality and esteems refinement. His language and meaning are clear and appropriate: a fine scholar.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Pure and orthodox, and worthy of attention.”
The sage cited the village drinking ceremony, which encompasses many virtues and amply contributes to good government, thereby showing that his words had substantiation. How greatly ritual instruction can enrich government! The sage observed the village ceremony and knew how very easy kingly government could be. Surely he was deeply moved by this! The author of the account of the village drinking ceremony meant that people know the great results achieved when the Kingly Way is realized, but do not know that ritual instruction, when fully extended, works through much the same underlying mechanism. In the performance of the village drinking ceremony, distinctions between noble and lowly are made clear; degrees of ceremonial elaboration and reduction are distinguished; respect for elders leaves no one out; feasting proceeds peacefully without disorder; and harmonious enjoyment does not lapse into excess. The practice of these five things suffices to establish the foundation for every form of proper conduct and for great moral transformation. If extended and put into practice, where could they fail to bring results?
I see that, when applied to cultivating oneself, they make one’s actions beneficial and one’s person secure, splendidly displaying an example that inspires trust; they exalt virtue and correct faults, fully establishing the steps toward personal order and rectitude. Would not the person thereby be set right? When applied to securing the state, virtue spreads widely and transforming influence shines forth, so that the whole state attains the effects of supreme harmony; the Way is realized and government reaches everywhere, so that an entire region attains the blessings of consummate order. Would not the state thereby be made secure?
Once the state is secure, we shall see trustworthiness and righteousness firmly established, and ritual propriety and deference practiced, so that customs of harmony and reverence arise throughout the Nine Regions. Worthy and capable people will abound and the achievements of government will flourish, so that orderly customs prevail in every land. Would not all under Heaven thereby be brought to peace? Establishing the great foundation so that every transforming influence can take effect is how a true king achieves good government. Now, observing the village …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
飲而昭然斯義之攸存朝廷正而天下治王道
之所以爲大也今行是五者而秩然斯理之攸
寓故雖未施於有政也然舉斯心而加諸彼信
乎措之而無難雖未及以化民也然見其禮而
知其政允矣推之而自易吾之所觀其足徵乎
吁卽鄉飲之行而知王道之易如此則先王制
禮之善聖人精義之神豈不皆可見哉抑是禮
也聖王務焉五帝憲三王乞言其由來遠矣然
必有敬德之存於中而後禮文將於外是故皇
===
極建而彝訓行峻德明而黎民變也否則文焉
耳矣安能爲脩齊治平之具也哉故曰恭敬者
幣之未將者也夫子有志於大道之行而未逮
於是乎有感焉學者卽此求之則其化成天下
之意從可識矣
第貳塲
論
道以中庸爲至
李廷詔
punctuated:
飲而昭然斯義之攸存。朝廷正而天下治，王道之所以爲大也。今行是五者，而秩然斯理之攸寓。故雖未施於有政也，然舉斯心而加諸彼，信乎措之而無難；雖未及以化民也，然見其禮而知其政，允矣推之而自易。吾之所觀，其足徵乎！吁！卽鄉飲之行而知王道之易如此，則先王制禮之善、聖人精義之神，豈不皆可見哉？抑是禮也，聖王務焉，五帝憲，三王乞言，其由來遠矣。然必有敬德之存於中，而後禮文將於外。是故皇極建而彝訓行，峻德明而黎民變也。否則文焉耳矣，安能爲脩齊治平之具也哉？故曰：「恭敬者，幣之未將者也。」夫子有志於大道之行而未逮，於是乎有感焉。學者卽此求之，則其化成天下之意從可識矣。
第貳塲
論
道以中庸爲至
李廷詔
translation_en:
…in the village drinking ceremony, we see clearly where this principle resides. When the court is upright, all under Heaven is well governed: herein lies the greatness of the Kingly Way. Now, in carrying out these five practices, this principle is embodied in their orderly arrangement. Thus, although it has not yet been applied to government, if one takes this disposition of mind and extends it to that sphere, putting it into practice will surely present no difficulty. Although it has not yet been used to transform the people, by observing these rites one can understand the government they imply; extending them will indeed be easy. Is what I have observed not sufficient evidence?
Ah! If the practice of the village drinking ceremony shows that the Kingly Way is easy to carry out in this manner, can we not see both the excellence of the former kings’ institution of rites and the wondrous penetration of the sage’s understanding of their meaning? Moreover, this rite was a concern of the sage kings. The Five Emperors took their elders as models, and the Three Kings solicited their counsel: its origins are ancient indeed. Yet reverent virtue must first reside within; only then can the outward forms of ritual give it expression. Thus, when the August Ultimate is established, the constant teachings prevail; when lofty virtue is made manifest, the common people are transformed. Otherwise, there are merely outward forms. How could these serve as instruments for cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven? Hence it is said: “Reverence is what precedes the presentation of ceremonial gifts.” The Master aspired to the practice of the Great Way but did not live to see it realized, and so was moved to reflection by this. If students investigate this matter, they can understand his intention to transform and perfect all under Heaven.
Second Session
Discourse
“The Way Attains Its Highest Expression in the Mean (Zhongyong)”
Li Tingzhao 李廷詔

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭劉批題涉理學最難發揮此篇
順理修詞畧無阻礙取之
同考試官敎諭胡批是作浩浩千餘言剷去險
棘若無甚高論亦非卑之苟同於俗議蓋能體認中
庸旨趣矣敬羨敬羨
考試官敎諭彭批才氣充盈理致明正非徒
騁浮蔓爾也宜錄以傳
考試官敎諭朱批沛以渥蓋涵濡有得者
道有極致也而見之偏者失之是故憂道者不
===
能已於言矣夫道散於天下而極於萬殊之不
齊若汗漫無所底止而要其極致則有一定而
不可易者探之冥冥索之茫茫始有以偏見病
道者矣道在此而見騖於高則踰道固未嘗踰
也道在此而見溺於卑則歉道固未嘗歉也弗
踰弗歉道之極也而夫人者乃以偏見病之聖
人固能已於言乎師也過商也不及皆非至乎
其道者夫子以爲過猶不及蓋所以示之的也
子朱子則曰道以中庸爲至夫苟能中庸矣而
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭劉批：題涉理學，最難發揮。此篇順理修詞，畧無阻礙，取之。

同考試官敎諭胡批：是作浩浩千餘言，剷去險棘，若無甚高論，亦非卑之苟同於俗議，蓋能體認中庸旨趣矣。敬羨！敬羨！

考試官敎諭彭批：才氣充盈，理致明正，非徒騁浮蔓爾也，宜錄以傳。

考試官敎諭朱批：沛以渥，蓋涵濡有得者。

道有極致也，而見之偏者失之。是故憂道者不能已於言矣。夫道散於天下，而極於萬殊之不齊，若汗漫無所底止；而要其極致，則有一定而不可易者。探之冥冥，索之茫茫，始有以偏見病道者矣。道在此，而見騖於高則踰，道固未嘗踰也；道在此，而見溺於卑則歉，道固未嘗歉也。弗踰弗歉，道之極也，而夫人者乃以偏見病之，聖人固能已於言乎？師也過，商也不及，皆非至乎其道者。夫子以爲過猶不及，蓋所以示之的也。子朱子則曰：「道以中庸爲至。」夫苟能中庸矣，而
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: The topic concerns the learning of principle and is most difficult to expound. This essay follows principle and fashions its language without the slightest impediment. Accept it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: This composition flows expansively for more than a thousand words, clearing away thorny difficulties. Though it seems to offer no exceptionally lofty argument, neither does it stoop to facile agreement with commonplace opinions. The author has evidently grasped the purport of the Mean. My respectful admiration! My respectful admiration!

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: Abundant in talent and spirit, clear and correct in its reasoning, this is more than a mere display of superficial verbosity. It should be recorded for transmission.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Copious and rich: evidently the work of someone who has steeped himself in the learning and gained understanding.

The Way has an ultimate perfection, yet those whose view of it is one-sided miss it. Thus those concerned for the Way cannot refrain from speaking. The Way is dispersed throughout the world and extends to the utmost diversity of its myriad particulars, seeming boundless and without limit. Yet, when its ultimate perfection is grasped, there is something fixed and unalterable. When people probe for it in darkness and seek it in the vast unknown, they come to impair the Way through one-sided views. The Way is here, but when their views pursue the lofty, they overshoot it; the Way itself has never gone too far. The Way is here, but when their views sink into the lowly, they fall short; the Way itself has never fallen short. Neither exceeding nor falling short is the perfection of the Way. Yet people impair it through their one-sided views: could the sage indeed refrain from speaking? Shi went too far, and Shang fell short; neither had attained perfection in the Way. The Master held that going too far was just like falling short, thereby showing them the target. Master Zhu said: “The Way finds its ultimate perfection in the Mean.” Now, if one can indeed achieve the Mean, then …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
何過不及之有邪是真有得於聖人之至教者
矣然則聖賢之心其憂道之心乎且夫道之大
原出於天也而天地之中民受以生焉道具於
人之一心心統性情者也而喜怒哀樂之未發
則謂之中焉夫其本於天然而隱於未發也寂
然不動何有於中何有於不中也其本體固如
是也夫其本體如是也吾人者均性同體則宜
其皆合於中適於庸而奚至於有所謂偏倚過
不及之差者顧惟道之同不能不雜於氣禀之
===
異而决擇之未精向往之或悖則始有偏執其
所見以為道而不悟者而道始病矣嗚呼人以
私智臆見病道而道未嘗病也道者萬世無敝
者也泰山之高有却走而不見者矣有見而不
至其趾者矣有至其趾而不及其巔者矣而泰
山未始有變也百步之的有射而越焉者矣有
射而不至者矣而的固不移也泰山也的也其
至也至其至者人也登泰山而不至其巔者非
登山者也射而越之者而未至者均之不中乎
punctuated:
何過不及之有邪？是真有得於聖人之至教者矣。然則聖賢之心，其憂道之心乎？且夫道之大原出於天也，而天地之中，民受以生焉。道具於人之一心，心統性情者也，而喜怒哀樂之未發，則謂之中焉。夫其本於天然而隱於未發也，寂然不動，何有於中？何有於不中也？其本體固如是也。夫其本體如是也，吾人者均性同體，則宜其皆合於中、適於庸，而奚至於有所謂偏倚過不及之差者？顧惟道之同，不能不雜於氣禀之異，而决擇之未精、向往之或悖，則始有偏執其所見以為道而不悟者，而道始病矣。

嗚呼！人以私智臆見病道，而道未嘗病也。道者，萬世無敝者也。泰山之高，有却走而不見者矣，有見而不至其趾者矣，有至其趾而不及其巔者矣，而泰山未始有變也。百步之的，有射而越焉者矣，有射而不至者矣，而的固不移也。泰山也，的也，其至也；至其至者，人也。登泰山而不至其巔者，非登山者也。射而越之者而未至者，均之不中乎
translation_en:
…what excess or shortcoming could there be? This is truly to have grasped the highest teaching of the sage. Then is not the concern of the sages and worthies a concern for the Way? The great source of the Way issues from Heaven, and the people receive the equilibrium of Heaven and Earth through which they come to life. The Way is fully present in each person's mind. The mind governs both human nature and the emotions; before joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are aroused, this is called equilibrium. Rooted in what is naturally so and hidden before the emotions arise, it is still and unmoving. How could there be any question of equilibrium or its absence? Such indeed is its original substance. Since its original substance is thus, and we all share the same nature and substance, we ought all to accord with equilibrium and conform to constancy. How, then, do the deviations called partiality, excess, and shortcoming arise? It is simply that the sameness of the Way inevitably becomes mingled with differences in people's endowments of vital energy. When their discernment is insufficiently refined and their aspirations sometimes go astray, people begin to cling one-sidedly to their own views, taking them for the Way without recognizing their error. Thus the Way begins to suffer impairment.

Alas! People impair the Way through their private cleverness and conjectural opinions, yet the Way itself has never been impaired. The Way endures for ten thousand generations without deterioration. Such is the height of Mount Tai: some turn back and never see it; some see it but never reach its foot; some reach its foot but fail to attain its summit. Yet Mount Tai itself has never changed. With a target a hundred paces away, some shoot beyond it, while others shoot short of it; yet the target itself does not move. Mount Tai and the target each represent the point of ultimate attainment; it is people who must reach that point. Those who climb Mount Tai but do not reach its summit do not count as having climbed the mountain. Those who shoot beyond and those who fall short alike fail to hit…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
的也徒射者也古有所謂聖人者堯舜禹湯文
武是也執中者握其至用中者神其至建中建
極者立其至以軌天下也聖人固以事變交於
前而吾之所以應之者無將迎無內外無歆羨
無畔援惟求協於中焉爾矣協於中則固未甞
不庸也中庸即道也人不皆聖人而其道未始
有異也道不異於聖人而卒不能同夫聖人者
偏之為害焉耳今夫天地之高厚也四海九州
之廣也彝倫之大也事物之微也三千三百之
===
儀也一語一默之形也八政九經之操縱也變
有萬形而皆會於道道有萬殊而必極於中庸
中庸也者性之德也心之端也道之大本也其
體渾然而不雜其則一定而不移其矩至正而
不頗其用至神而不滯其機至速而不難坦夷
而不亢也典常而不異也止乎其域而不遷也
動乎其天而不二也叩之而即應也率之而即
是也昏以料想則惑矣參以巧力則鑿矣戰以
攻取則擾矣飾以雕琢則偽矣離以須臾則偏
punctuated: 的也，徒射者也。古有所謂聖人者，堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武是也。執中者，握其至；用中者，神其至；建中建極者，立其至以軌天下也。聖人固以事變交於前，而吾之所以應之者，無將迎，無內外，無歆羨，無畔援，惟求協於中焉爾矣。協於中，則固未甞不庸也。中庸即道也。人不皆聖人，而其道未始有異也。道不異於聖人，而卒不能同夫聖人者，偏之為害焉耳。今夫天地之高厚也，四海九州之廣也，彝倫之大也，事物之微也，三千三百之儀也，一語一默之形也，八政九經之操縱也，變有萬形而皆會於道，道有萬殊而必極於中庸。中庸也者，性之德也，心之端也，道之大本也。其體渾然而不雜，其則一定而不移，其矩至正而不頗，其用至神而不滯，其機至速而不難。坦夷而不亢也，典常而不異也，止乎其域而不遷也，動乎其天而不二也。叩之而即應也，率之而即是也。昏以料想則惑矣，參以巧力則鑿矣，戰以攻取則擾矣，飾以雕琢則偽矣，離以須臾則偏
translation_en:
…the target; they are merely people who shoot. Those whom antiquity called sages were Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. To hold fast to the Mean is to grasp its ultimate perfection; to apply the Mean is to give that perfection wondrous efficacy; to establish the Mean and the supreme standard is to set up that perfection as a rule for all under Heaven. As affairs and changing circumstances converge before the sage, his way of responding neither anticipates nor pursues, distinguishes neither inner nor outer, and admits neither covetous admiration nor wayward attachment. He seeks only accord with the Mean. What accords with the Mean is invariably constant. The Mean and the Constant are precisely the Way. Not everyone is a sage, yet their Way has never been different. That their Way does not differ from the sages’ and yet they ultimately cannot equal the sages is simply the harm wrought by partiality.

Consider the height of Heaven and the depth of Earth, the breadth of the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, the magnitude of the enduring human relationships, the minutiae of affairs and things, the three thousand and three hundred ritual observances, the manifestations of each utterance and each silence, and the conduct of the eight branches of government and nine guiding principles. Change takes myriad forms, yet all converge upon the Way; the Way has myriad distinctions, yet all must find their ultimate standard in the Mean and the Constant. The Mean and the Constant are the virtue of human nature, the guiding principle of the heart-mind, and the great foundation of the Way. Their substance is an integral whole, unmixed; their rule is fixed and unchanging; their measure is perfectly correct and without deviation; their operation is supremely wondrous and unimpeded; their responsiveness is supremely swift and effortless. They are level and even, without excess; regular and constant, without anomaly. They rest within their proper bounds without departing, and move according to their Heaven-endowed nature without division. Touch them and they immediately respond; follow them and one is immediately right. Obscure them with conjecture, and confusion results; mingle them with clever contrivance, and forced distortion results; contend for them through attack and acquisition, and disturbance results; embellish them with carving and polishing, and falsity results; depart from them for even an instant, and one becomes partial…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
倚矣加以毫末則太過矣減以秒忽則不及矣
誠所謂天理之當然精微之極致也下愚而不
移百姓日用而不知蓋自棄於道不知其不及
者也過為詭異而淫用匪彝則敢於叛道不知
其過者也至於執其一偏之見以庶幾於道雖
非棄與叛道者之比然有之不虛執之大固擬
議之間不自知其墮於過與不及也而要其所
至終亦不免於偏倚駁雜之弊矣是故師之好
為苟難望道於高者也而不知道也者愚夫愚
===
婦之所能知之所能行也何甞失之於太高邪
商之篤信謹守泥道於卑者矣而不知道也者
天地聖人之所不能盡何甞失之於太卑邪道
匪高也亦匪卑也而二子者乃欲以一偏之見
盡之將以求道適以病道矣子貢以為師愈於
商則亦擬道於高者也夫子教之曰過猶不及
的之以歸於中焉耳不曰中而但曰過猶不及
悟二子而使自得之也聖人立教傳道之心亦
切矣而門人不皆善學也是則夫子之所憂也
punctuated:
倚矣，加以毫末則太過矣，減以秒忽則不及矣。誠所謂天理之當然，精微之極致也。下愚而不移，百姓日用而不知，蓋自棄於道、不知其不及者也。過為詭異，而淫用匪彝，則敢於叛道、不知其過者也。至於執其一偏之見，以庶幾於道，雖非棄與叛道者之比，然有之不虛，執之大固，擬議之間，不自知其墮於過與不及也。而要其所至，終亦不免於偏倚駁雜之弊矣。
是故師之好為苟難，望道於高者也，而不知道也者，愚夫愚婦之所能知之所能行也，何甞失之於太高邪？商之篤信謹守，泥道於卑者矣，而不知道也者，天地聖人之所不能盡，何甞失之於太卑邪？道匪高也，亦匪卑也，而二子者乃欲以一偏之見盡之，將以求道，適以病道矣。子貢以為師愈於商，則亦擬道於高者也。夫子教之曰：「過猶不及。」的之以歸於中焉耳。不曰中，而但曰「過猶不及」，悟二子而使自得之也。聖人立教傳道之心亦切矣，而門人不皆善學也，是則夫子之所憂也。
translation_en:
…it becomes skewed. Add even a hair’s breadth, and there is excess; subtract even the slightest fraction, and there is deficiency. This is truly what is meant by the proper order of Heaven’s principle and the utmost refinement of its subtleties. Those of the lowest understanding who remain unchanged, and the common people who use it daily without knowing it, are those who abandon themselves with respect to the Way, unaware of their deficiency. Those who go to extremes in strange and aberrant conduct, recklessly employing what violates constant norms, dare to rebel against the Way, unaware of their excess. As for those who cling to a partial view in hopes of approaching the Way, although they cannot be classed with those who abandon or rebel against it, they hold their view without an open mind and cling to it too firmly. In their deliberations, they do not themselves realize that they fall into excess or deficiency. Ultimately, whatever they attain cannot escape the faults of partiality, imbalance, and admixture.
Thus Shi 師 [Zizhang], fond of undertaking what is difficult merely for difficulty’s sake, sought the Way in lofty heights. Yet he did not understand that the Way is something ordinary men and women can know and practice. How could it ever err by being too lofty? Shang 商 [Zixia], steadfast in belief and cautious in observance, confined the Way to what is lowly. Yet he did not understand that the Way is something even Heaven and Earth and the sages cannot exhaust. How could it ever err by being too lowly? The Way is neither lofty nor lowly, yet these two disciples wished to encompass it through a partial view. Intending to seek the Way, they only impaired it. Zigong 子貢 considered Shi superior to Shang, so he too conceived of the Way as something lofty. The Master instructed him, saying, “Going too far is just like not going far enough.” He merely pointed him toward a return to the mean. Rather than speaking of the mean, he said only, “Going too far is just like not going far enough,” to awaken the two disciples and enable them to grasp it for themselves. The sage’s desire to establish his teaching and transmit the Way was indeed earnest; yet his disciples were not all adept at learning. This was what troubled the Master.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
顏氏之子其殆庶幾乎亞聖之才優於師矣乃
不違如愚得一善則拳拳服膺而勿失曾子之
才其魯似商也真積力久於一貫之旨而能默
契焉夫一善也一貫也皆中庸之道也顏子不
以其高而忽之曾子不以其魯而自已此所以
終於聞道而非二子之所能及也雖然義命哀
敬之論而執德之弘信道之篤則亦幾於仁者
師也顧豈終於太過者乎博學篤志切問近思
之功徑造於爲仁而河西之民擬於夫子則商
===
也亦非終於不及者矣記曰過之者俯而就之
不及焉者跂而及之夫子之道之教之化何嘗
豐於顏曾而嗇於師商也哉抑因是而知中庸
之道似易而實難也以孔門親炙之徒尚不能
頓悟而遽到而況未及其門者乎是故持異說
以爭鳴於天下者紛如也而行之不恊於中不
可爲常不求其至者皆非有得於道者也是又
夫子之所深憂也故曰中庸其至矣乎民鮮能
久矣嗚呼聖人憂道之心見矣使非夫子昭然
punctuated: 顏氏之子，其殆庶幾乎！亞聖之才優於師矣，乃不違如愚，得一善則拳拳服膺而勿失。曾子之才，其魯似商也，真積力久於一貫之旨，而能默契焉。夫一善也，一貫也，皆中庸之道也。顏子不以其高而忽之，曾子不以其魯而自已，此所以終於聞道，而非二子之所能及也。雖然，義命哀敬之論，而執德之弘、信道之篤，則亦幾於仁者，師也，顧豈終於太過者乎？博學篤志、切問近思之功，徑造於爲仁，而河西之民擬於夫子，則商也，亦非終於不及者矣。《記》曰：「過之者俯而就之，不及焉者跂而及之。」夫子之道之教之化，何嘗豐於顏曾而嗇於師商也哉！抑因是而知中庸之道似易而實難也。以孔門親炙之徒，尚不能頓悟而遽到，而況未及其門者乎？是故持異說以爭鳴於天下者紛如也，而行之不恊於中、不可爲常、不求其至者，皆非有得於道者也。是又夫子之所深憂也，故曰：「中庸其至矣乎！民鮮能久矣。」嗚呼！聖人憂道之心見矣。使非夫子昭然
translation_en:
The son of the Yan family surely came close! His talent, worthy of a sage of the second rank, surpassed that of Shi (Zizhang); yet he never departed from the teaching and seemed foolish, and whenever he acquired a single good principle, he held it reverently to his heart and never lost it. Master Zeng’s dullness of aptitude resembled that of Shang (Zixia), yet through genuine accumulation and sustained effort he came to a tacit understanding of the purport of the single thread running through the Way. A single good principle and the single unifying thread alike belong to the Way of the Mean. Master Yan did not neglect it because of his lofty talent, nor did Master Zeng give up because of his dullness. This is why they ultimately came to hear the Way, attaining what the other two disciples could not reach.
Nevertheless, through his discussions of righteousness and destiny, grief and reverence, and through his broad commitment to virtue and firm faith in the Way, Shi too approached humaneness. How could he have remained forever one who went too far? Through the work of learning broadly and holding firmly to his purpose, questioning earnestly and reflecting on what lay close at hand, Shang advanced directly toward the practice of humaneness; the people of Hexi even likened him to the Master. Thus he too did not remain forever one who fell short. The Record of Rites says: “Those who go beyond it bend down to reach it; those who fall short rise on tiptoe to attain it.” How could the Master’s Way, teaching, and transforming influence ever have been generous toward Yan and Zeng but sparing toward Shi and Shang?
From this, moreover, we know that the Way of the Mean seems easy but is in fact difficult. Even disciples who personally received instruction at Confucius’s school could not comprehend it at once and immediately attain it. How much less could those who had never entered his school! Thus those who uphold divergent doctrines and vie to make themselves heard throughout the world are innumerable. Yet those whose conduct does not accord with the Mean and cannot serve as a constant standard, and who do not seek its highest attainment, have all failed to grasp the Way. This too was a source of profound concern to the Master. Hence he said: “How consummate is the Mean! Long have the people been few who could practice it.” Alas! Here we see the sage’s concern for the Way. Had the Master not clearly…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以示之的則天下後世之學者固將限於氣禀
溺於見聞蔽於學術而中庸之道益晦而益塞
矣然則朱子之言固淵源之有自憂道之心其
亦猶之夫子也歟噫中庸之道至矣求之有要
乎書曰若升高必自下若陟遐必自邇易曰君
子以順德積小以高大夫苟能存心以極其廣
大之體致知以盡其精微之妙誠明以達夫性
命之原約之不外夫一心而放之可以參乎天
地則至德備於我而中庸之道不其可至矣乎
===
故曰苟不至德至道不凝焉
表
擬宋建邇英延義二閣成羣臣賀表〔景祐〕
〔二年〕
石雷
同考試官教諭莫 批 組繹駢麗用事切當真傑
作也宜冠本房
考試官教諭彭 批 博洽麗藻四六中之佳者
考試官教諭朱 批 典則
punctuated:
以示之的，則天下後世之學者，固將限於氣禀，溺於見聞，蔽於學術，而中庸之道益晦而益塞矣。然則朱子之言，固淵源之有自，憂道之心，其亦猶之夫子也歟？噫！中庸之道至矣，求之有要乎？書曰：「若升高，必自下；若陟遐，必自邇。」易曰：「君子以順德，積小以高大。」夫苟能存心以極其廣大之體，致知以盡其精微之妙，誠明以達夫性命之原，約之不外夫一心，而放之可以參乎天地，則至德備於我，而中庸之道不其可至矣乎？故曰：「苟不至德，至道不凝焉。」

表
擬宋建邇英延義二閣成羣臣賀表〔景祐〕〔二年〕
石雷

同考試官教諭莫批：「組繹駢麗，用事切當，真傑作也，宜冠本房。」
考試官教諭彭批：「博洽麗藻，四六中之佳者。」
考試官教諭朱批：「典則。」
translation_en:
…to present it as a standard, scholars throughout the world and in later ages would surely have remained confined by their endowments of vital energy, submerged in what they had seen and heard, and obscured by their scholarly doctrines; the Way of the Mean would have grown ever more obscure and obstructed. Thus Master Zhu’s words assuredly had their source, and was his concern for the Way not like that of Confucius himself? Ah! The Way of the Mean is supreme. Is there an essential method for seeking it? The Book of Documents says: “To climb high, one must begin below; to travel far, one must begin nearby.” The Book of Changes says: “The gentleman thereby follows virtue, accumulating small things to attain height and greatness.” If one can preserve the mind so as to realize fully its vast substance, extend knowledge so as to comprehend its subtle marvels completely, and through sincerity and illumination reach the source of human nature and Heaven’s mandate—gathering all this into nothing beyond the single mind, yet extending it so as to stand alongside Heaven and Earth—then supreme virtue will be complete within oneself. Could the Way of the Mean then not be attained? Hence it is said: “Without supreme virtue, the supreme Way does not become firmly established.”

Memorial
A proposed congratulatory memorial by the assembled officials upon the completion of the Ruiying and Yanyi Pavilions under the Song dynasty 〔second year of Jingyou〕
By Shi Lei.

Associate Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: “The composition is interwoven and developed [?], with beautiful parallel phrasing; its allusions are precisely appropriate. Truly a masterpiece. It should rank first among the scripts in this examining room.”

Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: “Broad learning and splendid diction: an excellent example of four-and-six prose.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and exemplary.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
景祐二年某月某日臣某等伏遇
皇上建邇英延義閣成謹奉
表稱
賀者伏以
紫氣凌雲象魏藹宜春之盛
賁庸挂斗天門垂營宿之光大惟王以渙居
勤若考之作室飛翬棘矢匪徒侈乎美觀
重道親賢實有裨於至治臣等誠懽誠抃
稽首頓首竊以正位奠居一人建極宅中
===
圖大萬國具瞻大壯豫風雨之防惟上棟
而下宇聖人肇宮室之建斯合土以范金
非壯麗無以重威始景觀終焉協吉策勳
布政玄堂極於八階諦序通神清廟妥乎
七世堯卑三尺猶懸貝於鳩宮舜闢四門
乃頒瑞於羣后受命隆鑣庭之禮洽德呈
蒿柱之祥古道旣湮頹風不振匏居陋乎
柏寢露臺靡於雪宮驅石探奇平壽何勞
望海蘭亭競技天策奚貴登瀛花萼聯輝
punctuated:
景祐二年某月某日，臣某等伏遇皇上建邇英延義閣成，謹奉表稱賀者。伏以：紫氣凌雲，象魏藹宜春之盛；賁庸挂斗，天門垂營宿之光。大惟王以渙居，勤若考之作室。飛翬棘矢，匪徒侈乎美觀；重道親賢，實有裨於至治。臣等誠懽誠抃，稽首頓首。
竊以正位奠居，一人建極；宅中圖大，萬國具瞻。大壯豫風雨之防，惟上棟而下宇；聖人肇宮室之建，斯合土以范金。非壯麗無以重威，始景觀終焉協吉。策勳布政，玄堂極於八階；諦序通神，清廟妥乎七世。堯卑三尺，猶懸貝於鳩宮；舜闢四門，乃頒瑞於羣后。受命隆鑣庭之禮，洽德呈蒿柱之祥。古道旣湮，頹風不振。匏居陋乎柏寢，露臺靡於雪宮。驅石探奇，平壽何勞望海；蘭亭競技，天策奚貴登瀛；花萼聯輝
translation_en:
On a certain day of a certain month in the second year of Jingyou [1035], we, your servants So-and-so and others, humbly mark Your Majesty’s completion of the Ruiying and Yanyi Pavilions and respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation.
We humbly reflect: purple vapors rise above the clouds, and the palace gates glow with the splendor of a welcoming spring. Glorious adornment hangs beside the Dipper [?], and the celestial gates shed the radiance of the Encampment constellation. Great indeed is the king’s establishing his dwelling, as taught by Dispersion; diligent is he, like the son who builds the house his father planned. Like pheasants in flight and arrows poised straight, these buildings do more than lavish beauty upon the eye. Honoring the Way and drawing worthy men near, they truly contribute to perfect government. We, your servants, rejoice and clap our hands, bowing our heads and knocking our foreheads upon the ground.
We venture to reflect that, by taking his proper position and establishing his dwelling, the One Man sets the supreme standard; dwelling at the center and planning great undertakings, he becomes the focus of all the myriad states. Great Power teaches provision against wind and rain, with a ridgepole above and eaves below. When the sages first built palaces and chambers, they worked earth and cast metal. Without grandeur and beauty, there is no means of lending weight to imperial authority; planning the beginning and considering the outcome brings an auspicious result [?]. For recording merit and promulgating government, the Dark Hall reached the full complement of eight stairways; for ordering sacrifices and communicating with the spirits [?], the Pure Temple gave repose to seven generations. Yao kept his terrace low, at three feet, yet shells still hung in his modest palace [?]. Shun opened the four gates and distributed jade tokens to the assembled lords. Receiving Heaven’s mandate brought exalted ceremonies in the Biao court [?]; all-pervading virtue manifested the auspicious sign of wormwood pillars [?].
Once the ancient Way had fallen into oblivion, declining customs could not be revived. Gourd-shaped dwellings seemed mean beside the Cypress Chamber; the Dew Terrace was extravagant in comparison with the Snow Palace [?]. Driving stones to seek marvels—why trouble Pingshou with gazing out to sea? Competing in accomplishments at the Orchid Pavilion—what made ascent to Yingzhou so prized in the Court of Heavenly Strategy [?]? The calyx and blossoms shine together…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
庸敷恩於棠棣綺春騁望祗導欲於沉檀
惟天祿燃藜蓋以校歷朝典籍而凌煙畫
象直爲表一代功臣德愧前王時需
今日兹蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
體道應樞
凝神立極
巍巍覆物
穆穆含章
===
禹儉湯寛至仁自依乎安宅
陽施春盎大化允暨於茅簷孝竭
慈闈
親臨孔廟求言之詔屢下睦族之禮是崇耕
耤田而重乘屋之風置說書而究攸居之
義罷犀却蛤以四海爲一家發廩賑荒視
饑民猶同室深思底法益厚丕基秘館崇
文已見貽於百世玉清昭應矧可改於三
年言廣鴻圖式興鼎建載營
punctuated: 庸敷恩於棠棣，綺春騁望，祗導欲於沉檀。惟天祿燃藜，蓋以校歷朝典籍；而凌煙畫象，直爲表一代功臣。德愧前王，時需今日。兹蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，體道應樞，凝神立極，巍巍覆物，穆穆含章。禹儉湯寛，至仁自依乎安宅；陽施春盎，大化允暨於茅簷。孝竭慈闈，親臨孔廟；求言之詔屢下，睦族之禮是崇。耕耤田而重乘屋之風，置說書而究攸居之義。罷犀却蛤，以四海爲一家；發廩賑荒，視饑民猶同室。深思底法，益厚丕基。秘館崇文，已見貽於百世；玉清昭應，矧可改於三年。言廣鴻圖，式興鼎建，載營
translation_en:
…thereby extending favor to brothers, figured as the blossoms of the cherry tree. At Qichun, gazing into the distance merely encouraged a craving for aloeswood and sandalwood. Only the burning goosefoot torch at Tianlu served to collate the canonical writings of successive dynasties; and the painted portraits at Lingyan served simply to honor the meritorious ministers of an age. In virtue they fell short of former kings; the times awaited this very day.

Now we humbly encounter [〇〇〇〇: honorific designation untranscribed], who embodies the Way and responds to the celestial pivot, concentrates his spirit and establishes the supreme standard, majestically shelters all things, and solemnly harbors radiant virtue. With Yu’s frugality and Tang’s generosity, his consummate benevolence naturally rests in its peaceful abode. His beneficence spreads like the sun, abundant as spring; his great transforming influence truly reaches even thatched cottages. He fulfills his filial devotion in the apartments of the Empress Dowager and personally visits the temple of Confucius. He repeatedly issues edicts soliciting counsel and honors the rites that foster harmony among imperial kinsmen. By plowing the imperial ritual field, he gives weight to the ethos of tending the household roof; by appointing Expositors, he investigates the meaning of dwelling securely. He discontinues rhinoceros horn and rejects clams [?], treating all within the four seas as one family. He opens the granaries to relieve famine, regarding the starving people as members of his own household. He reflects deeply on establishing enduring standards, further strengthening the great foundation. In the exaltation of letters within the palace library, we already see a legacy for a hundred generations; how much more might Yuqing Zhaoying be altered within three years [?]. To enlarge his grand design, he thus initiates a great work of construction and begins to build…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
二閣爰僝羣工揆日定方悉經綸於内地慮
材審曲雄結構於中天神屆竣功豈曰雉
門新作子來趨事何殊靈囿速成積翠流
丹盤龍錯鳳金鋪玉井昭回日月之光桂
棟蘭橑納擁嵩河之秀五宮抱文昌之府
乾象在茲二室聯王屋之城坤靈遙應獨
摛
藻思特表
璇題
===
扁揭邇英銳意英儒之接
名垂延義虚心義理之求親君子而遠小人
孚惠心於
九五集衆思以廣忠益協問道於
重華煥東壁之星躔羣賢畢至邁西崑之冊
府多士維禎納陛駿奔猶信百工之諫倚
天鵠立不遺二史之書鼓鐘于宮君臣胥
悅鶴鳴在野天地同和蓋一時之偉觀而
天下所快覩者也臣等敝屋貯寒拙工執
punctuated: 二閣，爰僝羣工，揆日定方，悉經綸於内地；慮材審曲，雄結構於中天。神屆竣功，豈曰雉門新作；子來趨事，何殊靈囿速成。積翠流丹，盤龍錯鳳；金鋪玉井，昭回日月之光；桂棟蘭橑，納擁嵩河之秀。五宮抱文昌之府，乾象在茲；二室聯王屋之城，坤靈遙應。獨摛藻思，特表璇題。扁揭邇英，銳意英儒之接；名垂延義，虚心義理之求。親君子而遠小人，孚惠心於九五；集衆思以廣忠益，協問道於重華。煥東壁之星躔，羣賢畢至；邁西崑之冊府，多士維禎。納陛駿奔，猶信百工之諫；倚天鵠立，不遺二史之書。鼓鐘于宮，君臣胥悅；鶴鳴在野，天地同和。蓋一時之偉觀，而天下所快覩者也。臣等敝屋貯寒，拙工執
translation_en:
…the two pavilions, and thereupon set the many craftsmen to work. An auspicious day was chosen and the orientation determined; every detail was planned within the imperial precincts. Timber was considered and its curves examined, and majestic structures rose into the sky. With wondrous speed the work reached completion: how could this be called merely the rebuilding of the Pheasant Gate? The people hastened to the task like children coming to their father—how did this differ from the swift completion of King Wen’s Spirit Park? Massed kingfisher green and flowing vermilion, coiling dragons and interwoven phoenixes; golden door fittings and jade caisson ceilings reflected the radiance of sun and moon. Cinnamon beams and orchid rafters gathered in [?] the finest influences of Mount Song and the Yellow River. The five celestial palaces embrace the seat of Wenchang: Heaven’s configurations are present here. The two Shi peaks link with the citadel of Mount Wangwu: Earth’s numinous powers respond from afar.

Your Majesty alone unfolded your splendid literary thoughts and specially bestowed precious inscriptions. The plaque proclaims “Drawing Near to the Worthy” (Er’ying), expressing your keen resolve to receive outstanding Confucian scholars; the name “Extending Righteousness” (Yanyi) preserves your open-minded pursuit of moral principle. Drawing near to gentlemen and keeping petty men at a distance, you manifest a trustworthy, benevolent heart in the sovereign’s position of the fifth yang line. Gathering the thoughts of many to broaden the benefit of loyal counsel, you emulate Chonghua, the sage Shun, in inquiring into the Way. Brilliant as the course of the Eastern Wall stars, the pavilions attract all the worthy; surpassing the book repository of Western Kunlun, they possess in their many scholars an auspicious blessing. Those admitted to the steps hasten forward, and you still give credence to the remonstrances of the hundred craftsmen. Standing tall as a swan against the sky, you leave nothing unrecorded by the two historiographers. Bells sound within the palace, and ruler and ministers rejoice together; cranes call in the open country, and Heaven and Earth share in harmony. Truly this is a magnificent spectacle of our age, which all under Heaven delight to behold.

We, your servants, whose shabby dwellings hold only cold, are unskilled craftsmen plying…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
藝志存向上愧無臺閣文章目眩仰瞻敢
許國家楨榦樗朽不裨尺寸蔦綿豈任攴
持直以從繩固劣智於公輸之巧喜惟大
木常盡心於秦隴之求實實枚枚同效閟
宮之頌熈熈皞皞聿興衢室之歌伏願
新又日新戸牖對刻銘之警
立之斯立帲幪覃大廈之推稽古訓於先王
屏依無逸率攸行於
烈祖門豁洞開
===
道切羹墻敬存翼翼
學深堂奧靜體安安
止所止以綏兆民作聖亶終於完美
居廣居而首庶物配天峻極於高明宏規鞏
不拔之基大業衍無疆之慶臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖懽忭踴躍之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
punctuated:
藝，志存向上，愧無臺閣文章；目眩仰瞻，敢許國家楨榦？樗朽不裨尺寸，蔦綿豈任攴持？直以從繩，固劣智於公輸之巧；喜惟大木，常盡心於秦隴之求。實實枚枚，同效閟宮之頌；熈熈皞皞，聿興衢室之歌。
伏願新又日新，戸牖對刻銘之警；立之斯立，帲幪覃大廈之推。稽古訓於先王，屏依無逸；率攸行於烈祖，門豁洞開。道切羹墻，敬存翼翼；學深堂奧，靜體安安。止所止以綏兆民，作聖亶終於完美；居廣居而首庶物，配天峻極於高明。宏規鞏不拔之基，大業衍無疆之慶。
臣等無任瞻天仰聖、懽忭踴躍之至，謹奉表稱賀以
translation_en:
…our craft. Our aspirations are directed upward, yet we are ashamed to lack the literary accomplishments of the court. Gazing upward, our eyes dazzled, dare we claim to be pillars of the state? Like rotten ailanthus wood, we contribute not the slightest use; how could clinging vines [?] bear the task of support? In straightening wood to follow the marking cord, our understanding certainly falls short of Gongshu’s skill; yet, delighting in great timber, we always devote ourselves wholeheartedly to seeking it in Qin and Long. With timbers sturdy and abundant, we join in offering praise like that of “The Secluded Temple”; in joy and harmony, we raise a song of the sovereign’s hall of consultation.
We humbly wish that Your Majesty may renew yourself, daily and ever anew, facing at doors and windows the admonitions of carved inscriptions; that, establishing the people so that they stand established, you may extend shelter as broadly as a great mansion. Examine the ancient instructions of the former kings, keeping “Against Idleness” beside your throne as a screen; follow the course of your illustrious ancestors, with the gates thrown wide open. May your devotion to the Way be as intimate as seeing the sages in your soup and upon your walls, and may your reverence remain ever vigilant. May your learning penetrate the innermost chambers, and may you embody tranquil ease in stillness. Rest where you ought to rest, thereby bringing peace to the myriad people, and surely bring the achievement of sagehood to perfection. Dwell in the broad dwelling of benevolence and preside over all beings; match Heaven, reaching the utmost height and brilliance. May your grand designs secure an unshakable foundation, and your great undertaking extend blessings without end.
We, your servants, cannot contain our utmost joy and exultation as we gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty. We respectfully present this memorial of congratulation in order to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
李廷詔
同考試官敎諭劉批我
皇上至治同於
太祖者由於至德士子類能言之求其稱述詳盡而詞不費者僅得此篇
同考試官敎諭胡批敷對嚴整佳士佳士
===
考試官敎諭彭批是作我
聖祖
皇上聖德神功歷歷如見允宜錄出以昭我
國家謨烈之盛
考試官敎諭朱批寓忠愛於稱頌之末此臣
子自獻之誠也錄之
聖人爲治之迹未嘗必其皆同而自無不
同者有至德以爲之本也治也者德之迹
也德也者治之本也惟本立而後天下之
punctuated:
聞。

第叁塲
策
第一問
李廷詔

同考試官敎諭劉批：我皇上至治同於太祖者，由於至德。士子類能言之，求其稱述詳盡而詞不費者，僅得此篇。

同考試官敎諭胡批：敷對嚴整，佳士！佳士！

考試官敎諭彭批：是作，我聖祖、皇上聖德神功歷歷如見，允宜錄出，以昭我國家謨烈之盛。

考試官敎諭朱批：寓忠愛於稱頌之末，此臣子自獻之誠也。錄之。

聖人爲治之迹，未嘗必其皆同，而自無不同者，有至德以爲之本也。治也者，德之迹也；德也者，治之本也。惟本立而後天下之
translation_en:
…to Your Majesty’s attention.

Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Li Tingzhao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Our Emperor’s consummate governance equals that of Taizu because of his consummate virtue. Candidates generally can explain this, but in seeking an account both comprehensive and economical in expression, I found only this essay.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: The response is rigorous and well ordered. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: In this composition, the sagely virtue and wondrous achievements of our sagely founder and our Emperor appear so distinctly that one seems to behold them. It truly deserves to be selected for inclusion, to display the grandeur of our dynasty’s plans and accomplishments.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: He incorporates loyalty and love for the sovereign at the close of his praise. This is the sincerity with which a subject offers himself in service. Include it.

The outward manifestations of sages’ governance need not all be identical. Yet that they are naturally alike in every respect is because consummate virtue serves as their foundation. Governance is the outward manifestation of virtue; virtue is the foundation of governance. Only when the foundation is established can all under Heaven …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
治成惟治成而後聖人之德著是故觀其
治則知其德矣觀其德則知其同矣此詩
書所稱徽猷懿德曠世而相感我
太祖
皇上聖德神功異世而同符者固可以仰窺萬
一矣請敬陳之且聖人之生固爲不偶而
理在天下無或有間也况父子之相傳祖
孫之相續精神命脉之相爲流通性情道
德之相爲畀予而有異乎哉是故成湯建
===
中以裕後昆高宗協德以光先烈文武緝
熈執兢而大周室之基宣王側身修行而
建中興之治要之能垂謨烈監成憲聖聖
相承授受一道考諸說命之辭雅頌之詩
可知也漢之光武同符高祖似矣然規模
皆在其範圍唐之憲宗治追貞觀似矣然
怠心遽萌於平蔡安在其爲同也仰惟我
太祖高皇帝以上聖之資掃胡元之亂中天下
而立爲民物綱常之主其聰明天縱固無
punctuated: 治成。惟治成而後聖人之德著。是故觀其治，則知其德矣；觀其德，則知其同矣。此《詩》《書》所稱徽猷懿德，曠世而相感，我太祖、皇上聖德神功，異世而同符者，固可以仰窺萬一矣。請敬陳之。且聖人之生，固爲不偶，而理在天下，無或有間也。况父子之相傳，祖孫之相續，精神命脉之相爲流通，性情道德之相爲畀予，而有異乎哉？是故成湯建中以裕後昆，高宗協德以光先烈，文武緝熈執兢而大周室之基，宣王側身修行而建中興之治。要之，能垂謨烈，監成憲，聖聖相承，授受一道，考諸《說命》之辭、《雅》《頌》之詩可知也。漢之光武同符高祖，似矣，然規模皆在其範圍；唐之憲宗治追貞觀，似矣，然怠心遽萌於平蔡，安在其爲同也？仰惟我太祖高皇帝，以上聖之資，掃胡元之亂，中天下而立，爲民物綱常之主。其聰明天縱，固無
translation_en:
…order is achieved. Only after order is achieved does the sage’s virtue become manifest. Thus, by observing his governance, we know his virtue; by observing his virtue, we know what sages have in common. The splendid counsels and admirable virtues praised in the Book of Odes and Book of Documents resonate across distant ages. From this we may reverently glimpse a fraction of the sagely virtue and divine achievements of our Taizu and His Majesty, which accord despite their different ages. Permit me respectfully to set this forth.

Sages are indeed born only rarely, yet the principle present throughout the world never suffers any interruption. How much more is this so when father transmits to son and grandfather is succeeded by grandson: their spirit and vital continuity flow from one to another, and their nature, dispositions, moral way, and virtue are passed on. How could there be any difference? Thus Cheng Tang established the mean to enrich his descendants; Gaozong brought his virtue into accord to glorify his predecessor’s achievements; Wen and Wu continued in brilliance, maintaining reverent vigilance, and enlarged the foundations of the Zhou royal house; and King Xuan humbled himself and cultivated his conduct to establish the governance of a restoration. In essence, they could bequeath counsels and achievements and take established precedents as their models. Sage succeeded sage, transmitting and receiving a single Way. This can be understood by examining the words of “The Charge to Yue” in the Book of Documents and the poems of the “Elegantiae” and “Hymns” in the Book of Odes.

Guangwu of Han seemed to accord with Gaozu, yet the scope of all his undertakings remained within the latter’s bounds. Xianzong of Tang seemed to achieve governance rivaling that of the Zhenguan era, yet a complacent heart suddenly arose in him upon the pacification of Cai. Where, then, was their sameness?

Reverently considering our Emperor Taizu Gao: endowed with the qualities of the highest sage, he swept away the disorder of the non-Han Yuan, took his stand at the center of all under Heaven, and became the sovereign upholding the cardinal bonds and constant norms for the people and all things. His intelligence was Heaven-bestowed, and he certainly had no…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
待於學也且汲汲於治心存於中者皆堯
舜之心施諸治者有仁義爲本則正心脩
身之間其盛德固已溥博淵泉矣由是推
之以正
宮闈則內外之防嚴由是推之以馭近習則
干預之漸杜由是推之事
親則感孝養不逮而悲咽
太子諸王皆感泣由是推之享
帝則返視却聽上契冲漠體道迎神誠一弗貳
===
由是推之制禮作樂則
親定山川岳瀆孔子之祀禮制
圜丘大祀先聖歷代帝王之樂章由是推之恤
刑則因傳讞之奏而有惕然决遣之語由
是推之捄荒則於西安鳳翔之旱災遂有
涸魚之喻凡若此者難以悉舉皆我
太祖德化之隆巍然煥然固天下臣民之所共
仰也我
皇上龍飛江漢君臨萬邦至性夙成至德淵微
punctuated:
待於學也，且汲汲於治。心存於中者皆堯舜之心，施諸治者有仁義爲本，則正心脩身之間，其盛德固已溥博淵泉矣。由是推之以正宮闈，則內外之防嚴；由是推之以馭近習，則干預之漸杜；由是推之事親，則感孝養不逮而悲咽，太子諸王皆感泣；由是推之享帝，則返視却聽，上契冲漠，體道迎神，誠一弗貳；由是推之制禮作樂，則親定山川岳瀆孔子之祀禮，制圜丘大祀先聖歷代帝王之樂章；由是推之恤刑，則因傳讞之奏而有惕然决遣之語；由是推之捄荒，則於西安鳳翔之旱災遂有涸魚之喻。凡若此者，難以悉舉，皆我太祖德化之隆，巍然煥然，固天下臣民之所共仰也。
我皇上龍飛江漢，君臨萬邦，至性夙成，至德淵微。
translation_en:
…depend upon learning; moreover, he worked urgently for good government. What he harbored within was entirely the heart of Yao and Shun, and what he applied in governing took benevolence and righteousness as its foundation. Thus, in rectifying his heart and cultivating his person, his abundant virtue was already broad and vast, deep and inexhaustible as a wellspring. Extending this to ordering the palace apartments, he strictly maintained the separation between inner and outer quarters. Extending it to controlling his intimate attendants, he forestalled their encroachment upon government.
