Extending it to serving his parents, he sobbed with grief that he could no longer support them with filial devotion, moving the crown prince and the other princes alike to tears. Extending it to sacrificing to the Lord on High, he turned his sight inward and withdrew his hearing, communed above with the silent and formless, embodied the Way, and welcomed the spirits with single-minded, undivided sincerity. Extending it to establishing rites and composing music, he personally determined the sacrificial rites for mountains and rivers, the sacred peaks and great waterways, and Confucius, and composed the musical texts for the great sacrifice at the Circular Mound and for sacrifices to the former sages and the emperors and kings of successive dynasties. Extending it to compassionate administration of punishments, he responded to a memorial forwarding cases for judicial review with words of anxious concern over their disposition. Extending it to famine relief, he used the analogy of fish in dried-up waters when drought struck Xi’an and Fengxiang. Instances such as these are too numerous to enumerate fully. All display the flourishing of our Taizu’s transforming moral influence, lofty and radiant, which the officials and people throughout the realm alike revere.
Our reigning emperor rose like a dragon from the Jiang and Han region to rule over the myriad lands. His consummate moral nature matured early, and his consummate virtue is profound and subtle…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
悉源於
睿皇之授受固無待於學矣猶且不自滿假以
敬一自箴以無逸作所深宮大庭罔有弗臧
食息起居罔有弗敬仁聲義聞充塞天壤
則我
皇上之所以正心脩身者方諸
太祖何如也麟趾之化久而益孚貂璫之流戢
而莫肆則我
皇上之所以正
===
內治嚴近習者方諸
太祖何如也極尊親於
睿考隆孝養於
慈闈
郊祀之儀經制大備
上帝之敬終始不渝則我
皇上之所以事
親享
帝者方諸
punctuated: 悉源於睿皇之授受，固無待於學矣。猶且不自滿假，以敬一自箴，以無逸作所。深宮大庭，罔有弗臧；食息起居，罔有弗敬。仁聲義聞，充塞天壤。則我皇上之所以正心脩身者，方諸太祖何如也？麟趾之化，久而益孚；貂璫之流，戢而莫肆。則我皇上之所以正內治、嚴近習者，方諸太祖何如也？極尊親於睿考，隆孝養於慈闈。郊祀之儀，經制大備；上帝之敬，終始不渝。則我皇上之所以事親享帝者，方諸
translation_en:
…all derive from the transmission received from Emperor Rui, and thus assuredly require no learning. Yet His Majesty remains free of complacency, admonishing himself to maintain reverent single-mindedness and making freedom from ease his dwelling. Within the secluded palace and the great court, nothing is without goodness; in eating, resting, rising, and retiring, nothing is without reverence. His reputation for benevolence and righteousness fills heaven and earth. How, then, do our Emperor’s efforts to rectify his mind and cultivate his person compare with those of Taizu?

The transforming influence celebrated in “The Qilin’s Hoof” grows ever more firmly established with time; the ranks of eunuchs, with their sable ornaments, are restrained and dare not act wantonly. How, then, do our Emperor’s efforts to set the governance of the inner palace in order and strictly regulate his intimate attendants compare with those of Taizu?

He accords the utmost honor to his parent, his late father Emperor Rui, and lavishes filial care upon the Empress Dowager. The rites of the suburban sacrifices are fully provided for in their regulations and institutions; his reverence for the Lord on High remains unwavering from beginning to end. How, then, do our Emperor’s efforts to serve his parents and offer sacrifices to the Lord on High compare with…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
太祖何如也隆
先師之禮訂
明倫之典正冠服之章審聲音之本作
九廟之歌新樂舞之器則我
皇上之所以制禮作樂者方諸
太祖何如也每歲論囚旋輒報罷十餘年間
皇恩汪濊泣罪之仁有光夏禹四方水旱每厪
賑貸或
遣大臣以親臨或發官帑而散給子惠之德
===
遠配成湯則我
皇上之所以恤刑捄荒者方諸
太祖何如也凡若此者難以具陳然卽是觀之
則我
太祖之與我
皇上雖相去百餘年而其德業之隆功化之盛
如出一轍誠足以侔德商周矣豈漢唐諸
君所可彷彿其萬一也哉執事於此猶有
望焉此固賢臣忠愛之盛心愚也敢不求
punctuated:
太祖何如也？隆先師之禮，訂明倫之典，正冠服之章，審聲音之本，作九廟之歌，新樂舞之器，則我皇上之所以制禮作樂者，方諸太祖何如也？每歲論囚，旋輒報罷。十餘年間，皇恩汪濊，泣罪之仁有光夏禹。四方水旱，每厪賑貸，或遣大臣以親臨，或發官帑而散給，子惠之德，遠配成湯。則我皇上之所以恤刑捄荒者，方諸太祖何如也？

凡若此者，難以具陳。然卽是觀之，則我太祖之與我皇上，雖相去百餘年，而其德業之隆、功化之盛，如出一轍，誠足以侔德商周矣。豈漢唐諸君所可彷彿其萬一也哉？執事於此猶有望焉，此固賢臣忠愛之盛心。愚也敢不求
translation_en:
…how does he compare with Taizu? He has enhanced the rites honoring the First Teacher, Confucius; settled the Canon for Clarifying Human Relationships (Minglun zhi dian); rectified the regulations governing caps and robes; examined the foundations of musical sound; composed songs for the Nine Ancestral Temples; and renewed the instruments and implements for music and dance. How, then, do His Majesty’s institutions of ritual and music compare with those of Taizu? Each year, when the cases of condemned prisoners are reviewed, the proposals are promptly returned without approval. For more than ten years, imperial grace has flowed abundantly, and his compassion, like that of one who wept over offenders, has added luster to the example of Yu of the Xia. Whenever floods or droughts strike anywhere in the realm, he takes care to provide relief grants and loans, sometimes dispatching high officials to oversee matters in person, sometimes releasing treasury funds for distribution. His virtue in nurturing the people as his children matches that of Cheng Tang in distant antiquity. How, then, does His Majesty’s care in administering punishments and relieving famine compare with that of Taizu?

Such deeds are too numerous to recount in full. Yet even these examples show that, although our Taizu and His Majesty are separated by more than a hundred years, the grandeur of their virtuous achievements and the abundance of their accomplishments and transforming influence follow the same course. Truly, their virtue is sufficient to rival that of the Shang and Zhou. How could the rulers of the Han and Tang approximate even one ten-thousandth of it? That you, honored sir, still entertain further hopes in this regard surely expresses the profound loyalty and affection of a worthy minister. How could I, in my ignorance, dare fail to seek…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
所以副之乎間嘗伏讀史臣之賛我
太祖其略有曰彌勤為治孜孜不息於戯
聖祖此心其純一不已之心乎
皇上之心其亦
聖祖之心乎蓋於
法宮燕閒之地隱微幽獨之中雖
聖德日新與天並運然終始典學在
聖心乾乾不息者臣子何足以窺其微哉愚也
囿於過化存神之內竊謂
===
皇上功德同於
太祖者性焉安焉不期然而然者也
今日克明峻德式於九圍日慎一日雖休勿
休上追
太祖孜孜不息之念遠紹文王純一不已之誠
以臻聖神功化之極者在我
皇上加之意耳疎遠賤士不識忌諱惟進而教
之幸甚
第二問
punctuated:
所以副之乎？間嘗伏讀史臣之賛我太祖，其略有曰：「彌勤為治，孜孜不息。」於戯！聖祖此心，其純一不已之心乎？皇上之心，其亦聖祖之心乎？蓋於法宮燕閒之地，隱微幽獨之中，雖聖德日新，與天並運，然終始典學，在聖心乾乾不息者，臣子何足以窺其微哉？愚也囿於過化存神之內，竊謂皇上功德同於太祖者，性焉安焉，不期然而然者也。
今日克明峻德，式於九圍，日慎一日，雖休勿休，上追太祖孜孜不息之念，遠紹文王純一不已之誠，以臻聖神功化之極者，在我皇上加之意耳。疎遠賤士，不識忌諱，惟進而教之，幸甚。
第二問
translation_en:
…the means to fulfill those hopes? I once reverently read the court historian’s encomium to our Taizu, which says in part: “Ever more diligent in governing, he labored tirelessly without cease.” Ah! Was not this heart of our sage ancestor one of perfect singleness and unceasing devotion? Is not His Majesty’s heart likewise the heart of our sage ancestor? In the quiet leisure of the imperial palace, amid its hidden recesses and solitude, His Majesty’s sagely virtue is renewed daily and moves in concert with Heaven. Yet how could we, his subjects, fathom the subtleties of that steadfast devotion to learning, from beginning to end, which works tirelessly within his sagely heart? Dwelling, in my ignorance, within the reach of his transforming influence and spiritual presence, I venture to say that His Majesty’s achievements and virtue equal Taizu’s by his very nature, with effortless ease: they are so without his intending them to be so.
Today, brilliantly manifesting his lofty virtue and serving as a model for all the realm, growing more vigilant each day, and never resting even amid blessings, he may pursue Taizu’s tireless resolve and carry forward the perfect singleness and unceasing sincerity of King Wen. To attain thereby the utmost in sagely and divine achievement and transforming influence requires only that His Majesty give this further attention. I am a humble scholar far removed from court and ignorant of its taboos. If you would take me forward and instruct me, I would count myself most fortunate.
Second Question

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
陳瑞麟
考試官教諭彭批古樂情文兼備非聖人不
能作此篇考究精詳蓋達於樂者也
考試官教諭朱批能言音樂之詳如此者絕
少
作樂之道有本焉有變焉天地人心之和
古今之所同此其本也器數制度之末古
今之所異此其變也窮其本之同而知其
變之異不拘拘於異而卒會於同於是乎
===
可與言樂矣非天下之至神其孰能與於
此且樂之未作蘊諸天地及其作也寓諸
律呂故自豫之象著而天地之蘊泄矣自
夔之教行而陰陽之妙彰矣甚矣古樂之
足以善治也記曰奮至德之光動四氣之
和以著萬物之理又曰脩身及家平均天
下是樂之道擬聖德之形容順陰陽之代
運闡民彝物則之幽致脩齊治平之效若
之何其可緩也然嘗慨夫語樂於三代之
punctuated:
陳瑞麟。

考試官教諭彭批：「古樂情文兼備，非聖人不能作。此篇考究精詳，蓋達於樂者也。」

考試官教諭朱批：「能言音樂之詳如此者絕少。」

作樂之道，有本焉，有變焉。天地人心之和，古今之所同，此其本也；器數制度之末，古今之所異，此其變也。窮其本之同，而知其變之異，不拘拘於異，而卒會於同，於是乎可與言樂矣。非天下之至神，其孰能與於此？且樂之未作，蘊諸天地；及其作也，寓諸律呂。故自《豫》之象著，而天地之蘊泄矣；自夔之教行，而陰陽之妙彰矣。甚矣，古樂之足以善治也！《記》曰：「奮至德之光，動四氣之和，以著萬物之理。」又曰：「脩身及家，平均天下。」是樂之道，擬聖德之形容，順陰陽之代運，闡民彝物則之幽，致脩齊治平之效，若之何其可緩也？然嘗慨夫語樂於三代之
translation_en:
Chen Ruilin.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: “Ancient music possessed both inner feeling and outward form in full measure; only a sage could create it. This essay’s investigations are meticulous and detailed: its author surely understands music.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Very few can discuss music in such detail.”

The way of creating music has its fundamentals and its variations. The harmony of Heaven, Earth, and human hearts is common to antiquity and the present: this is its foundation. The subsidiary details of instruments, numerical arrangements, institutions, and regulations differ between antiquity and the present: these are its variations. Only when someone thoroughly explores what is common in its foundation and understands the differences in its variations, without becoming bound by those differences and ultimately comprehending their underlying unity, can one discuss music with him. Who but a person of the most wondrous spiritual insight in all the world could attain this?

Before music was created, it lay latent in Heaven and Earth; once created, it was embodied in the pitch standards, lü and lü. Thus, once the Image of the hexagram Yu (Enthusiasm) was set forth, what lay hidden in Heaven and Earth was revealed; once Kui’s teaching was put into practice, the subtleties of yin and yang became manifest. How great was ancient music’s capacity to bring about good government! The Book of Rites says: “It brings forth the radiance of consummate virtue and stirs the harmony of the vital energies of the four seasons, thereby manifesting the principles of the myriad things.” It also says: “Cultivate oneself and extend this to the family, bringing equity and order to all under Heaven.” Thus the way of music represents the outward expression of sagely virtue, accords with the alternating movements of yin and yang, elucidates the hidden depths of human moral norms and the principles governing things, and brings about the effects of cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven. How could it be treated as a matter to be deferred? Yet I have often lamented that, when speaking of music in relation to the Three Dynasties …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
前夫人能知之也語樂於三代之後雖君
子亦未之或知也何也古之君子之論樂
曰其數可陳也其義難知也今之君子之
論樂曰其義可知也其器難明也蓋制度
之末當時之所通知故棄而不載而所載
者精微玄妙而已耳孰知千載之下其器
不可復見而其制無復能知由是古樂遂
廢而好古之士尚猶幸夫名義之存由精
以求粗因時以制宜不能無望於積德百
===
年之餘也故觀諸大司樂以樂德敎國子
其曰中和祗庸孝友者本諸身也以樂語
敎國子其曰興道諷誦言語者和其聲也
以樂舞敎國子其曰雲門大卷大咸大磬
大夏大濩大武者觀其成也以六律六同
和聲音變呂言同亦或謂之間者獨陰獨
陽其能同乎陰配於陽樂斯同矣呂間於
律聲斯和矣州鳩之言曰律所以立均出
度也古之神瞽考中聲而量之以制度律
punctuated:
前，夫人能知之也；語樂於三代之後，雖君子亦未之或知也。何也？古之君子之論樂曰：「其數可陳也，其義難知也。」今之君子之論樂曰：「其義可知也，其器難明也。」蓋制度之末，當時之所通知，故棄而不載，而所載者精微玄妙而已耳。孰知千載之下，其器不可復見，而其制無復能知？由是古樂遂廢，而好古之士尚猶幸夫名義之存，由精以求粗，因時以制宜，不能無望於積德百年之餘也。
故觀諸大司樂，以樂德敎國子，其曰中和祗庸孝友者，本諸身也；以樂語敎國子，其曰興道諷誦言語者，和其聲也；以樂舞敎國子，其曰雲門大卷大咸大磬大夏大濩大武者，觀其成也。以六律六同和聲音，變呂言同，亦或謂之間者，獨陰獨陽，其能同乎？陰配於陽，樂斯同矣；呂間於律，聲斯和矣。州鳩之言曰：「律所以立均出度也。古之神瞽考中聲而量之以制，度律
translation_en:
…before the Three Dynasties, everyone could understand it; when music is discussed after the Three Dynasties, even gentlemen may fail to understand it. Why? Gentlemen of antiquity, discussing music, said: “Its numerical relations can be set forth, but its meaning is difficult to understand.” Gentlemen today, discussing music, say: “Its meaning can be understood, but its instruments are difficult to comprehend.” The details of its institutions and regulations were common knowledge at the time, so they were omitted from the records; what was recorded consisted only of subtle and profound principles. Who could have foreseen that, a thousand years later, its instruments could no longer be seen and its regulations could no longer be understood? Thus ancient music fell into disuse. Yet scholars devoted to antiquity still rejoice that its names and meanings survive. Seeking the tangible through the subtle, and devising suitable arrangements in accordance with the times, they cannot help placing their hopes in an age that has accumulated virtue for more than a hundred years.
Consider, therefore, the Grand Director of Music. He taught the sons of the state through musical virtues: centrality, harmony, reverence, constancy, filial devotion, and brotherly affection. These were rooted in personal conduct. He taught them through musical speech: evocation, guidance, recitation, chanting, speaking, and conversation. These harmonized their voices. He taught them through musical dances: Cloud Gate (Yunmen), Great Scroll (Dajuan), Great Concord (Daxian), Great Chime (Daqing [?]), Great Xia (Daxia), Great Beneficence (Dahuo), and Great Martial Dance (Dawu). These displayed their accomplishments. He harmonized sounds through the six yang pitch standards and the six yin pitch standards. Why replace the term lü for the yin standards with tong, “concord,” or sometimes call them “intervals”? Could yin alone or yang alone achieve concord? When yin is paired with yang, music achieves concord; when the yin standards alternate with the yang standards, sounds achieve harmony. Zhou Jiu said: “Pitch standards are the means by which tonal balance is established and measures are derived. The spirit-gifted blind musicians of antiquity examined the central tone and measured it to establish a system, gauging the pitch standards…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
均鍾平之以六成於十二天之道也夫六
中之色也故名之曰黃所以宣養六氣九
德也二曰太簇所以金奏贊陽出滯也三
曰姑洗所以脩潔百物考神納賓也四曰
蕤賓所以安靖神人獻酬交錯也五曰夷
則所以咏歌九則平民無貳也六曰無射
所以宣布哲人之令德示民軌儀也爲之
六閒以陽沉伏而黜散越也元閒大呂助
宣物也二閒夾鍾出四隙之細也三閒中
===
呂宣中氣也四閒林鍾和展百事俾莫不
任肅純恪也五閒南呂贊陽秀也六閒應
鍾均利器用俾應復也律呂不易無姦物
也細均有鍾無鏄昭其大也大均有鏄無
鍾甚大無鏄鳴其細也大昭小鳴和之道
也此其名義居然可見其所謂中聲者實
作樂之要也是黃鍾之聲也卽所謂元聲
也兹義也在樂爲中聲在天爲中氣在人
爲喜怒哀樂之未發及發而中節者也其
punctuated:
均鍾，平之以六，成於十二，天之道也。夫六，中之色也，故名之曰黃，所以宣養六氣九德也。二曰太簇，所以金奏贊陽出滯也。三曰姑洗，所以脩潔百物，考神納賓也。四曰蕤賓，所以安靖神人，獻酬交錯也。五曰夷則，所以咏歌九則，平民無貳也。六曰無射，所以宣布哲人之令德，示民軌儀也。爲之六閒，以陽沉伏而黜散越也。元閒大呂，助宣物也。二閒夾鍾，出四隙之細也。三閒中呂，宣中氣也。四閒林鍾，和展百事，俾莫不任肅純恪也。五閒南呂，贊陽秀也。六閒應鍾，均利器用，俾應復也。律呂不易，無姦物也。細均有鍾無鏄，昭其大也；大均有鏄無鍾，甚大無鏄，鳴其細也。大昭小鳴，和之道也。」
此其名義，居然可見。其所謂中聲者，實作樂之要也，是黃鍾之聲也，卽所謂元聲也。兹義也，在樂爲中聲，在天爲中氣，在人爲喜怒哀樂之未發，及發而中節者也。其
translation_en:
… tuning the bells, balancing them through six pitches and completing them in twelve: this is the Way of Heaven. Now ‘six’ is the color of the center [?], and so it is named Huang, ‘Yellow’; it serves to diffuse and nourish the six vital energies and the nine virtues. The second is called Taicu; it serves, through performances on metal instruments, to assist yang and release what is obstructed. The third is called Guxian; it serves to cleanse and purify all things, honor the spirits, and receive guests. The fourth is called Ruibin; it serves to bring peace to spirits and humans, with offerings and reciprocal toasts passing back and forth. The fifth is called Yize; it serves to sing of the nine rules and bring the people into harmony without divided allegiance. The sixth is called Wuyi; it serves to proclaim the excellent virtue of wise men and show the people standards of conduct. For these, six intervening pitches were established, to support yang when it lies submerged and hidden, and to expel what dissipates or exceeds its bounds. The first intervening pitch, Dalü, assists the unfolding of things. The second, Jiazhong, brings forth the subtle energies of the four interstices [?]. The third, Zhonglü, diffuses the central vital energy. The fourth, Linzhong, harmonizes and advances the hundred affairs, so that all are undertaken with solemnity, purity, and reverence. The fifth, Nanlü, assists yang in bringing things to maturity. The sixth, Yingzhong, balances and sharpens implements for use, enabling them to respond to the returning cycle. When the yang and yin pitch standards remain unaltered, nothing aberrant arises. In the higher tuning there are zhong bells but no bo bells [?], to make its greater tones manifest; in the lower tuning there are bo bells but no zhong bells, while in the very lowest there are no bo bells, to make its finer tones sound. Making the greater manifest and the smaller sound is the way of harmony.”
The meanings of these names can thus be clearly seen. What is called the central tone is indeed the essential basis for making music. It is the tone of Huangzhong, also called the primordial tone. This principle is the central tone in music, the central vital energy in Heaven, and, in human beings, joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure before they arise, as well as their attaining due measure when they do arise. Its …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
輕重清濁疾徐之節蓋有促之不能使之
密豁之不能使之疎損之不能使之少益
之不能使之多者漢初古樂猶存文帝謙
讓未遑武帝雖有志於樂然所好者特世
俗之樂非先王之制也嗣是魏用杜夔隋
用鄭譯何妥宋用和峴胡瑗輩非不留心
於鍾律而卒無所得焉惟蔡元定旁搜遠
取巨細不捐積之累年乃若冥契著爲新
書明白而淵深縝密而通暢不爲牽合附
===
會之談其言雖出於近世之所未講而實
無一字不本古人已試之成法觀其黃鍾
圍徑之法則漢斛之積分可考寸以九分
爲法則淮南太史小司馬之說可推五聲
二變之數變律半聲之例則杜氏通典具
焉變宮變徵之不得爲調則孔氏之禮疏
在焉元定嘗曰律呂之器不可復見然古
人制樂之意則猶可考信斯言也則其書
固在而作者之意固可推也然古樂終不
punctuated: 輕重清濁疾徐之節，蓋有促之不能使之密，豁之不能使之疎，損之不能使之少，益之不能使之多者。漢初古樂猶存，文帝謙讓未遑，武帝雖有志於樂，然所好者特世俗之樂，非先王之制也。嗣是魏用杜夔，隋用鄭譯、何妥，宋用和峴、胡瑗輩，非不留心於鍾律，而卒無所得焉。惟蔡元定旁搜遠取，巨細不捐，積之累年，乃若冥契，著爲新書，明白而淵深，縝密而通暢，不爲牽合附會之談。其言雖出於近世之所未講，而實無一字不本古人已試之成法。觀其黃鍾圍徑之法，則漢斛之積分可考；寸以九分爲法，則淮南、太史、小司馬之說可推；五聲二變之數、變律半聲之例，則杜氏《通典》具焉；變宮變徵之不得爲調，則孔氏之《禮疏》在焉。元定嘗曰：「律呂之器不可復見，然古人制樂之意則猶可考。」信斯言也，則其書固在，而作者之意固可推也。然古樂終不
translation_en:
…As for its measured degrees of weight and lightness, clarity and depth, speed and slowness, there is something that cannot be made denser by compression, sparser by expansion, less by subtraction, or more by addition. At the beginning of the Han, ancient music still survived. Emperor Wen, in his modest deference, had not found time to attend to it. Although Emperor Wu aspired to cultivate music, what he favored was merely the popular music of his age, not the institutions of the former kings. Subsequently, the Wei employed Du Kui; the Sui employed Zheng Yi and He Tuo; and the Song employed men such as He Xian and Hu Yuan. They certainly devoted attention to bells and pitch standards, yet ultimately achieved nothing.

Only Cai Yuanding searched widely and drew upon distant sources, discarding nothing, great or small. After accumulating material over many years, he seemed to arrive at an unspoken understanding and composed a new book. It was clear yet profound, meticulous yet lucid, and avoided strained connections and forced interpretations. Although his statements addressed matters unexplored in recent times, in truth not a single word lacked a basis in established methods already tested by the ancients. Consider his method for determining the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe: the computation of the Han hu measure’s volume can be examined as evidence. For his rule that one cun comprises nine fen, the explanations of Huainan, the Grand Astrologer, and the Younger Sima can be worked out. The numerical values of the five notes and the two altered notes, and the rules for altered pitch standards and half-length pitches, are fully recorded in Du’s Comprehensive Institutions. That the altered gong and altered zhi cannot serve as the basis of modes is documented in Kong’s Subcommentary on the Rites.

Yuanding once said: “The instruments embodying the pitch standards can no longer be seen, but the intentions behind the ancients’ creation of music can still be examined.” If these words are true, then his book certainly survives, and the intentions of those who created the music can certainly be inferred. Yet ancient music ultimately could not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
可復者豈世無古之人邪吁必待后夔而
後作樂必待師曠而後聽音斯人不世出
而樂在天下不可一日無也而音豈不可
聽哉世無后夔師曠而后夔之心師曠之
耳則固未嘗無也故房庶有曰古樂與今
樂本末不遠上古世質而聲樸後世稍變
焉亦猶大輅起於椎輪龍艘生於桼葉耳
庶之言及此其達樂之變乎方今重煕累
洽和氣薫蒸眞所謂大定大順之世此千
===
載一時也然則魯兩生之說詎可緩乎誠
得夫開物成務之才妙解音律之士叅酌
乎周禮大師之所掌禮運樂記之所記國
語之所述史記之所書因文焉以會其意
引緒焉以求其端即名義度數之可稽達
天人淵微之至妙會而通之與時宜之隨
絲竹金石秬黍之所寓均之而使適其宜
裁之而使中其度古樂之宜於古而復宜
於今者則因之宜於古而不宜於今者則
punctuated:
可復者，豈世無古之人邪？吁！必待后夔而後作樂，必待師曠而後聽音，斯人不世出，而樂在天下不可一日無也，而音豈不可聽哉？世無后夔、師曠，而后夔之心、師曠之耳，則固未嘗無也。故房庶有曰：「古樂與今樂，本末不遠。上古世質而聲樸，後世稍變焉，亦猶大輅起於椎輪，龍艘生於桼葉耳。」庶之言及此，其達樂之變乎！

方今重煕累洽，和氣薫蒸，眞所謂大定大順之世，此千載一時也。然則魯兩生之說詎可緩乎？誠得夫開物成務之才、妙解音律之士，叅酌乎《周禮》大師之所掌、《禮運》《樂記》之所記、《國語》之所述、《史記》之所書，因文焉以會其意，引緒焉以求其端，即名義度數之可稽，達天人淵微之至妙，會而通之，與時宜之，隨絲竹金石秬黍之所寓，均之而使適其宜，裁之而使中其度。古樂之宜於古而復宜於今者，則因之；宜於古而不宜於今者，則
translation_en:
…cannot be restored—is this because the world lacks men like those of antiquity? Ah! If we must await a Hou Kui before making music, and a Shi Kuang before judging tones, such men do not appear in every age; yet the world cannot go a single day without music. Can tones therefore not be judged? Though the world lacks a Hou Kui or a Shi Kuang, it has certainly never lacked minds like Hou Kui’s or ears like Shi Kuang’s. Thus Fang Shu said: “Ancient and present-day music are not far apart in their foundations and developments. In high antiquity, the world was simple and its sounds unadorned; later ages gradually changed them. This is just as the grand carriage arose from the primitive solid wheel, and the dragon ship developed from the lacquer leaf [?].” In saying this, did not Fang Shu comprehend how music changes?

Today, successive ages of prosperity and accumulated good order prevail, and harmonious influences pervade all. This is truly what is called an age of great stability and concord, an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years. Can the pronouncement of the two scholars of Lu, then, justify delay? If we could indeed obtain men with the talent to illuminate things and bring undertakings to completion, men with a subtle understanding of musical tones and pitch standards, they could compare and weigh the responsibilities of the Music Master in the Rites of Zhou, the records in “The Evolution of Rites” and “The Record of Music,” the accounts in the Discourses of the States, and the writings in the Records of the Grand Historian. Through these texts they could grasp the underlying intent; following their threads, they could seek their beginnings. Proceeding from verifiable names, meanings, measures, and numbers, they could penetrate the utmost subtleties of the profound relationship between Heaven and humanity. They could bring these together into a coherent understanding and adapt them to the times. Working through their embodiment in strings and bamboo pipes, bells and chime stones, and black millet used for pitch measurement, they could tune them to their proper balance and adjust them to the correct measures. Whatever in ancient music suited antiquity and also suits the present should be retained; whatever suited antiquity but does not suit the present should then…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
變之因其所當因變其所可變或由今之
器以寄古之聲或以古之器而象今之德
去其恇懘靡曼之聲而歸之中和雅正之
樂則音容節奏之間可以備天地萬物之
理而臻雍熈太和之盛矣是固
聖人在天子之位建中和之極操制作之柄者
之能事也記曰五帝殊時不相沿樂迂儒
是古而非今曲士貴耳而賤目故曰非常
之原黎民懼焉及臻厥成天下晏如也執
===
事以爲何如
第三問
蘭漵
同考試官教諭批策士非徒取其記問蓋欲
驗其才識此作援古證今確有定見末歸之選將之
精待將之厚馭將之嚴非出入韜略者不能及此
考試官教諭彭批駕馭之策統馭之才子皆
兼之矣敬服敬服
考試官教諭朱批有籌略有斷制
punctuated:
變之。因其所當因，變其所可變，或由今之器以寄古之聲，或以古之器而象今之德，去其恇懘靡曼之聲，而歸之中和雅正之樂，則音容節奏之間，可以備天地萬物之理，而臻雍熈太和之盛矣。是固聖人在天子之位，建中和之極，操制作之柄者之能事也。《記》曰：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂。」迂儒是古而非今，曲士貴耳而賤目。故曰：「非常之原，黎民懼焉；及臻厥成，天下晏如也。」執事以爲何如？

第三問
蘭漵

同考試官教諭批：策士非徒取其記問，蓋欲驗其才識。此作援古證今，確有定見，末歸之選將之精、待將之厚、馭將之嚴，非出入韜略者不能及此。

考試官教諭彭批：駕馭之策，統馭之才，子皆兼之矣。敬服！敬服！

考試官教諭朱批：有籌略，有斷制。
translation_en:
…change it. Preserve what ought to be preserved and change what may be changed. One might use present-day instruments to convey ancient sounds, or ancient instruments to represent the virtue of the present age. Eliminate agitated, discordant, and sensuously alluring sounds, and return to music that is balanced, harmonious, refined, and correct. Then its sounds, bearing, rhythms, and measures can fully embody the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, attaining the flourishing condition of concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony. This is indeed the accomplishment proper to a sage who occupies the Son of Heaven’s position, establishes the highest standard of balance and harmony, and wields the authority to create institutions. The Book of Rites says: “The Five Emperors lived in different ages and did not perpetuate one another’s music.” Pedantic scholars approve antiquity and condemn the present; narrow-minded scholars value what they hear and disparage what they see. Thus it is said: “At the inception of an extraordinary undertaking, the common people are afraid; once it reaches completion, all under Heaven are at ease.” What is your judgment, sir?

Third Question
Lan Xu 蘭漵

Comment by the Associate Examiner, an Instructor: Examining scholars through policy questions is not merely a matter of testing their memorized learning; its purpose is to assess their ability and discernment. This composition draws on antiquity to substantiate its arguments about the present and offers firm, well-founded judgments. It concludes by emphasizing discrimination in selecting generals, generosity in treating them, and strictness in controlling them. Only someone thoroughly versed in military strategy could attain this level.

Comment by Examiner Peng, an Instructor: You possess both the strategies for directing others and the talent for exercising command. I admire you! I admire you!

Comment by Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: You have strategic resourcefulness and decisive judgment.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
兵無常形在鼓舞之何如耳將無常能在
駕馭之何如耳何則人有勇怯而鼓舞之
也存乎倡將有賢愚而駕馭之也原於擇
倡則勇者成其能擇則賢者畢其用是故
聖人之治兵親簡閱以定其趨慎選擇而
重其託是以六師奮而四夷寧兆民安而
外患息轉移之機其在茲乎夫兵者國之
大事也愚嘗讀商周之書究韜略之旨而
知其槩矣又嘗竊怪夫漢之文帝時當承
===
平雍容謙讓若無事於武者一旦匈奴擾
其北鄙帝也赫然震怒拊髀興懷思得頗
牧之將勞軍細柳亟稱亞夫之能卒之匈
奴北去兵雖不試他日七國之變終收亞
夫之功何其英明哉幾於大勇矣是故經
武之要不可不講也講武之禮不可不行
也易曰隨無故也蠱則飭也夫隨以無故
而偷安蠱以有事而始飭故鐫金石者其
功難摧枯朽者其力易勢則然也周禮大
punctuated: 兵無常形，在鼓舞之何如耳；將無常能，在駕馭之何如耳。何則？人有勇怯，而鼓舞之也存乎倡；將有賢愚，而駕馭之也原於擇。倡則勇者成其能，擇則賢者畢其用。是故聖人之治兵，親簡閱以定其趨，慎選擇而重其託。是以六師奮而四夷寧，兆民安而外患息。轉移之機，其在茲乎！夫兵者，國之大事也。愚嘗讀商周之書，究韜略之旨，而知其槩矣。又嘗竊怪夫漢之文帝，時當承平，雍容謙讓，若無事於武者。一旦匈奴擾其北鄙，帝也赫然震怒，拊髀興懷，思得頗牧之將；勞軍細柳，亟稱亞夫之能。卒之匈奴北去，兵雖不試，他日七國之變，終收亞夫之功。何其英明哉！幾於大勇矣。是故經武之要，不可不講也；講武之禮，不可不行也。《易》曰：「隨，無故也；蠱則飭也。」夫隨以無故而偷安，蠱以有事而始飭。故鐫金石者其功難，摧枯朽者其力易，勢則然也。《周禮》大
translation_en:
Troops have no fixed disposition: all depends on how they are inspired. Generals have no fixed capacity: all depends on how they are directed. Why is this? Men may be brave or timid, but inspiring them depends upon leadership; generals may be worthy or foolish, but directing them begins with selection. With leadership, the brave realize their abilities; with selection, the worthy put their talents fully to use. Thus, in managing troops, the sage personally selects and reviews them to establish their direction, chooses commanders carefully, and gives due weight to the responsibilities entrusted to them. Consequently, the Six Armies are roused and the peoples of the four quarters remain peaceful; the myriad people enjoy security and external threats cease. Surely the key to transforming the situation lies here!

Military affairs are a great concern of the state. I, in my humble understanding, have read the writings of the Shang and Zhou and investigated the principles of military strategy, thereby gaining a general understanding of them. I have also privately marveled at Emperor Wen of the Han. Living in a time of established peace, he was composed, modest, and deferential, seemingly unconcerned with military affairs. Yet when the Xiongnu disturbed his northern frontier, the emperor flared with anger. Slapping his thigh in deep emotion, he longed to obtain generals like Lian Po and Li Mu. Visiting the troops at Xiliu to reward their service, he repeatedly praised Zhou Yafu’s ability. In the end, the Xiongnu withdrew northward. Although the troops were not put to the test then, during the later Rebellion of the Seven States, Yafu’s achievements ultimately vindicated him. How discerning he was! He approached true greatness in courage.

Thus, the essentials of military preparation must be studied, and the rites of military training must be performed. The Book of Changes says: “Following means freedom from troubles; Decay means putting things in order.” In Following, one enjoys ease because there are no troubles; in Decay, one begins to restore order only when trouble arises. Thus, engraving metal and stone is difficult work, while breaking dry and rotten wood requires little effort: the circumstances make it so. The Rites of Zhou, in its section on the Grand …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
司馬中春敎振旅中夏敎茇舍中秋敎治
兵中冬敎大閱振旅者所以斂耕作之民
也茇舍者所以敎夜戰之法也治兵者所
以敎晝戰之法也至於大閱則合三時而
敎之矣中春振旅王執路鼓中秋治兵王
載太常是一歲之間天子再臨焉又於簡
閱之後因行蒐狩之禮其所往也有地其
與期也有時有地則不害稼有時則不妨
農一遊一豫惟禮惟仁而豈徒哉是以將
帥士卒有所畏而各精其能夷狄姦宄有
所警而各戢其暴周所以延八百年之祚
者不爲無助也由周而下稱治者漢唐宋
也漢當十月之時行斬牲之禮會五營之
兵爲八陳之肄貙劉以誓衆乘之以習兵
乘輿駕白馬朱鬣親臨幸焉唐於中冬之
月定講武之期兵部承詔將士爲墠尚書
肅奉引之儀將帥嚴旗鼓之節天子乘革
輅至墠歲一臨焉宋制始於建隆而定於
punctuated:
司馬：「中春敎振旅，中夏敎茇舍，中秋敎治兵，中冬敎大閱。」振旅者，所以斂耕作之民也；茇舍者，所以敎夜戰之法也；治兵者，所以敎晝戰之法也。至於大閱，則合三時而敎之矣。中春振旅，王執路鼓；中秋治兵，王載太常。是一歲之間，天子再臨焉。又於簡閱之後，因行蒐狩之禮。其所往也有地，其與期也有時。有地則不害稼，有時則不妨農。一遊一豫，惟禮惟仁，而豈徒哉！是以將帥士卒有所畏而各精其能，夷狄姦宄有所警而各戢其暴。周所以延八百年之祚者，不爲無助也。
由周而下，稱治者漢、唐、宋也。漢當十月之時，行斬牲之禮，會五營之兵，爲八陳之肄。貙劉以誓衆，乘之以習兵。乘輿駕白馬朱鬣，親臨幸焉。唐於中冬之月，定講武之期。兵部承詔，將士爲墠；尚書肅奉引之儀，將帥嚴旗鼓之節。天子乘革輅至墠，歲一臨焉。宋制始於建隆而定於
translation_en:
…the Minister of War: “In mid-spring, teach the mustering of troops; in mid-summer, teach encampment; in mid-autumn, teach the ordering of troops; in mid-winter, teach the grand review.” Mustering troops serves to gather the people who cultivate the fields; encampment serves to teach the methods of night warfare; ordering troops serves to teach the methods of daytime warfare. The grand review combines the instruction of all three seasons. At the mid-spring muster, the king holds the great drum; at the mid-autumn ordering of troops, the king carries the great banner on his chariot. Thus, within a single year, the Son of Heaven attends twice. Moreover, after inspecting the troops, he proceeds to conduct the rites of the seasonal hunts. There are designated places to which he goes and appointed times for these gatherings. Designated places prevent damage to the crops; appointed times prevent interference with farming. Every excursion and every pleasure accords with ritual and benevolence: how could these be mere diversions? Thus commanders and soldiers have something to hold in awe, and each perfects his abilities; the Yi and Di peoples and evildoers have something to warn them, and each restrains his violence. These practices contributed to the Zhou dynasty’s eight hundred years of rule.
After the Zhou, the dynasties renowned for good government were the Han, Tang, and Song. In the tenth month, the Han performed the rite of slaughtering sacrificial animals, assembled the troops of the Five Encampments, and practiced the eight battle formations. Through the chuli sacrificial hunt, they administered an oath to the assembled troops, following this with military exercises. The emperor personally attended in his carriage, drawn by white horses with vermilion manes. The Tang fixed a date for military exercises in mid-winter. The Ministry of War received the imperial command, and officers and soldiers prepared a cleared parade ground. The minister solemnly observed the ceremonial procedures for leading the imperial procession, while the commanders strictly maintained the prescribed signals of flags and drums. The Son of Heaven rode to the parade ground in the leather-covered chariot, attending once each year. The Song system began in the Jianlong reign period and was definitively established in…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
咸平其教射之法教陳之規尤爲精嚴講
武之日帝乗馬登臺臨觀焉然中平之世
講武於平樂觀先天之初講武於驪山宋
太宗講武於近郊眞宗講武於東武村此
四君者雖人品不同其車馬之盛紀律之
嚴足以嚴内治備外攘者則一而已矣就
而論之玄宗正郭元振唐紹虧失軍容之
罪奬薛訥解琬戎陳堅肅之美其得將將
之道乎太宗嚴木鏃相射之法定韋矟相
===
擊之等其得練士之道乎其所以身致太
平取威制勝誠萬世所宜法也我
國家簡閲之制操練有時更番有期遴選而
爲三千諸營合之而爲十二大團營有大
將以總督之有參將諸臣以分攝之可謂
精且練矣然邇者殘胡爲寇戕我邊鄙雖
無足慮而守備空虚上廑
宵旰之憂臣工論列章數十上備禦之策似
已詳盡然求其威敵制勝之將投石超距
punctuated:
咸平。其教射之法、教陳之規，尤爲精嚴。講武之日，帝乗馬登臺臨觀焉。然中平之世，講武於平樂觀；先天之初，講武於驪山；宋太宗講武於近郊，眞宗講武於東武村。此四君者，雖人品不同，其車馬之盛、紀律之嚴，足以嚴内治、備外攘者，則一而已矣。就而論之，玄宗正郭元振、唐紹虧失軍容之罪，奬薛訥、解琬戎陳堅肅之美，其得將將之道乎？太宗嚴木鏃相射之法，定韋矟相擊之等，其得練士之道乎？其所以身致太平、取威制勝，誠萬世所宜法也。
我國家簡閲之制，操練有時，更番有期，遴選而爲三千諸營，合之而爲十二大團營。有大將以總督之，有參將諸臣以分攝之，可謂精且練矣。然邇者殘胡爲寇，戕我邊鄙，雖無足慮，而守備空虚，上廑宵旰之憂。臣工論列，章數十上，備禦之策似已詳盡。然求其威敵制勝之將、投石超距
translation_en:
…the Xianping reign period. Its methods for teaching archery and its rules for teaching formations were especially exacting and rigorous. On days of military exercises, the emperor rode out and ascended a platform to observe them in person. During the Zhongping reign, military exercises were held at Pingle Belvedere; at the beginning of the Xiantian reign, they were held at Mount Li. Emperor Taizong of the Song held military exercises in the nearby suburbs, and Emperor Zhenzong at Dongwu Village. Although these four rulers differed in personal character, they were alike in this: the magnificence of their chariots and horses and the strictness of their discipline sufficed to strengthen internal order and prepare to repel external enemies. To consider particular instances, Xuanzong punished Guo Yuanzhen and Tang Shao for impairing military order and decorum, and commended Xue Ne and Xie Wan for the firmness and discipline of their formations. Had he not grasped the art of commanding commanders? Taizong rigorously enforced the rules for shooting at one another with wooden arrowheads and established grades for contests with leather-covered spears. Had he not grasped the art of training soldiers? The means by which they personally brought about peace, established their authority, and secured victory are indeed worthy of emulation for all ages.
Under our dynasty’s system of military selection and inspection, drills take place at set times and rotations follow fixed schedules. Selected troops form the Three Thousand and other camps, which are combined into the Twelve Great Divisional Camps. Senior generals exercise overall command, while assistant regional commanders and other officers take charge of their respective divisions. These forces may well be called select and well trained. Recently, however, remnant barbarian forces have raided and ravaged our borderlands. Though they are no great cause for alarm, our defenses are depleted, troubling His Majesty with cares that keep him working before dawn and late into the day. Officials have discussed and presented their views in dozens of memorials, and their plans for defense seem already exhaustive. Yet when one seeks generals who can overawe the enemy and secure victory, and men capable of throwing stones and leaping great distances…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之兵尚未有聞焉議者以爲演武之地近
在北郊竊有望於
翠華之臨以示親閲六師之義賞其戎陣之
嚴整者罰其行伍之失次者抜其梟健之
可用者汰其老弱之不堪者威嚴之下號
令一新鼓舞之餘旗幟皆變使天下曉然
知選將練兵之誠攘夷固圉之意非襲故
常非飾虛文則庶幾上可以備一代未備
之制下可以動天下將士之心是俄頃功
===
化足以昭文德張武威
大聖人之所作爲出於尋常萬萬矣兵法曰器
械不利以其卒予敵也卒不練習以其將
予敵也將不知兵以其君予敵也君不擇
將以其國予敵也是故講武所以練兵也
所以選將也選將也者尤練兵之首事也
奈之何膏粱紈綺世代因仍平時飾貌作
威旣乏統馭之才有警束手無策安望守
禦之績變而通之庸可泥乎魏元忠言於
punctuated:
之兵，尚未有聞焉。議者以爲，演武之地近在北郊，竊有望於翠華之臨，以示親閲六師之義。賞其戎陣之嚴整者，罰其行伍之失次者，抜其梟健之可用者，汰其老弱之不堪者。威嚴之下，號令一新；鼓舞之餘，旗幟皆變。使天下曉然知選將練兵之誠、攘夷固圉之意，非襲故常，非飾虛文，則庶幾上可以備一代未備之制，下可以動天下將士之心。是俄頃功化，足以昭文德，張武威，大聖人之所作爲，出於尋常萬萬矣。
兵法曰：「器械不利，以其卒予敵也；卒不練習，以其將予敵也；將不知兵，以其君予敵也；君不擇將，以其國予敵也。」是故講武，所以練兵也，所以選將也。選將也者，尤練兵之首事也。奈之何膏粱紈綺，世代因仍，平時飾貌作威，旣乏統馭之才，有警束手無策，安望守禦之績？變而通之，庸可泥乎？魏元忠言於
translation_en:
…such soldiers have yet to be heard of. Those discussing the matter hold that the grounds for military exercises lie nearby in the northern suburbs, and venture to hope that Your Majesty’s imperial carriage will visit them, demonstrating the principle of personally reviewing the Six Armies. Reward those whose battle formations are disciplined and orderly; punish those whose ranks fall into disorder; promote the fierce and vigorous who are fit for service; and discharge the old and weak who are unfit. In the presence of imperial majesty, commands would be renewed; inspired and heartened, all the banners would take on a new aspect. Let all under Heaven clearly understand the sincerity of the effort to select commanders and train troops, and the intention to repel the barbarians and secure the frontiers: this is no mere repetition of established routines or embellishment of empty formalities. Then it might both complete institutions still lacking in this dynasty and stir the hearts of commanders and soldiers throughout the realm. The transformative achievement of this brief moment would suffice to manifest civil virtue and extend military might. The actions of the great sage would surpass the ordinary ten thousandfold.
The military treatise says: “If weapons and equipment are not sharp and serviceable, this is to hand one’s soldiers over to the enemy. If the soldiers are not trained, this is to hand one’s commander over to the enemy. If the commander does not understand warfare, this is to hand one’s ruler over to the enemy. If the ruler does not select his commanders carefully, this is to hand his state over to the enemy.” Thus, military exercises serve to train troops and to select commanders. Selecting commanders is, above all, the first task in training troops. How, then, can those reared on rich food and clothed in fine silks continue to succeed one another generation after generation? In peacetime they cultivate appearances and put on an air of authority, yet lack the ability to command; when an alarm comes, they stand helpless, without a plan. How can one expect achievements in defense from them? Changes must be made so that the system can function: how can one cling to established practice? Wei Yuanzhong said to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其君曰今朝廷用人類取將門子弟及死
事之家彼皆庸人豈足當閫外之任古之
名將皆出貧賤而立殊功未聞其家代爲
將也忠也斯言其見今時之弊於千載之
上何其明且智哉誠用元忠之言博求材
武之士不拘一途若衞青之在奴僕郭子
儀之在儒臣畢誠之在侍從狄青之在走
卒皆得以見推於縉紳列名於將帥而陰
令本兵徐察其能而爲之等第以備
===
萬幾之暇時
賜召見或詢其謀或試其勇或較其藝或辨
其材將必有卓異者出於其間然後倣古
人推轂之儀體唐人親送之意授之以節
鉞之柄予之以賞罰之權厚其所以充賞
之貲嚴其所以致罰之條不牽之以文法
使之得以行其志俟其賞罰旣行號令旣
一人心旣齊地利旣熟則可投之所向無
不如意俾之練兵則援枹而鼓義不反顧
punctuated: 其君曰：「今朝廷用人，類取將門子弟及死事之家，彼皆庸人，豈足當閫外之任？古之名將，皆出貧賤而立殊功，未聞其家代爲將也。」忠也斯言，其見今時之弊於千載之上，何其明且智哉！誠用元忠之言，博求材武之士，不拘一途，若衞青之在奴僕、郭子儀之在儒臣、畢誠之在侍從、狄青之在走卒，皆得以見推於縉紳，列名於將帥，而陰令本兵徐察其能，而爲之等第，以備萬幾之暇，時賜召見，或詢其謀，或試其勇，或較其藝，或辨其材，將必有卓異者出於其間。然後倣古人推轂之儀，體唐人親送之意，授之以節鉞之柄，予之以賞罰之權，厚其所以充賞之貲，嚴其所以致罰之條，不牽之以文法，使之得以行其志。俟其賞罰旣行，號令旣一，人心旣齊，地利旣熟，則可投之，所向無不如意。俾之練兵，則援枹而鼓，義不反顧，
translation_en:
…to his ruler, saying: “When the court now employs men, it generally selects sons and younger brothers of military families and members of families whose men have died in service. These are all ordinary men: how could they be equal to the responsibility of independent military command? The famous generals of antiquity all rose from poverty and humble station to achieve exceptional merit. We have never heard that their families served as generals generation after generation.” How clear-sighted and wise Yuanzhong was in these words, discerning the abuses of our own time a thousand years beforehand!

If we truly adopt Wei Yuanzhong’s advice, broadly seeking men of ability and martial prowess without restricting recruitment to a single avenue, then men such as Wei Qing among household slaves, Guo Ziyi among civil officials [?], Bi Cheng among palace attendants [?], and Di Qing among common soldiers could all receive recommendations from the gentry and enter the ranks of commanders. The Minister of War should then be secretly instructed to assess their abilities gradually and rank them, so that, in moments free from the myriad affairs of government, Your Majesty might occasionally grant them an audience. By questioning their plans, testing their courage, comparing their skills, or discerning their talents, men of outstanding distinction would surely emerge among them.

Then, emulating the ancient ceremony of pushing a departing general’s carriage forward and embodying the spirit of the Tang rulers’ personal send-offs, confer upon them the authority symbolized by the command tally and battle-axe, and grant them power to reward and punish. Provide ample funds for their rewards and make strict the provisions governing their punishments. Do not constrain them with bureaucratic regulations; allow them to carry out their intentions. Once their rewards and punishments have taken effect, their commands have become unified, the men’s minds have become united, and they have thoroughly learned the advantages of the terrain, they may be deployed, and wherever they turn, everything will go as intended. Set them to training troops, and they will take up the drumstick and beat the drum, advancing in duty without looking back…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聞命而趨馬首是瞻赴湯蹈火殆將能之
而况使之嘗敵乎俾之備邊則遠斥候詞
敵情敵來或堅壁清野憑城審勢以待其
惰歸或輕騎斫營據險逆擊以奪其銳氣
梟敵得儁往無不利而何有於堅敵乎俾
之爲大將則申嚴戎政務存大體而無幸
功之心俾之爲偏裨則賈勇深入直趨虜
帳而破敵人之膽是衛郭畢狄皆在任使
何憂乎套虜何畏乎殘胡何言乎借才於
===
異代也哉雖然擇將貴精待將貴厚而馭
之之道尤貴於嚴何者三軍之命繫於一
人一方之恃在於一將北虜之衆不足以
當中國之一大縣然莫之禦者法之玩也
僨軍而必罰者古今之大法也明法以肅
令者人主之大柄也罰一人而千萬人懼
又使千萬人皆全其生天下之至仁也或
者猶以爲疑皆未足以語兵也是故正樊
愛能之辟者五季之頹風且振責陳曙之
punctuated:
聞命而趨，馬首是瞻，赴湯蹈火，殆將能之，而况使之嘗敵乎？俾之備邊，則遠斥候，詞敵情；敵來，或堅壁清野，憑城審勢，以待其惰歸；或輕騎斫營，據險逆擊，以奪其銳氣。梟敵得儁，往無不利，而何有於堅敵乎？俾之爲大將，則申嚴戎政，務存大體，而無幸功之心；俾之爲偏裨，則賈勇深入，直趨虜帳，而破敵人之膽。是衛郭畢狄，皆在任使，何憂乎套虜？何畏乎殘胡？何言乎借才於異代也哉！

雖然，擇將貴精，待將貴厚，而馭之之道尤貴於嚴。何者？三軍之命繫於一人，一方之恃在於一將。北虜之衆，不足以當中國之一大縣，然莫之禦者，法之玩也。僨軍而必罰者，古今之大法也；明法以肅令者，人主之大柄也；罰一人而千萬人懼，又使千萬人皆全其生，天下之至仁也。或者猶以爲疑，皆未足以語兵也。是故正樊愛能之辟者，五季之頹風且振；責陳曙之
translation_en:
…On hearing an order, they would hasten forward, following wherever their commander's horse led. They would likely be capable even of plunging into boiling water and treading through fire—how much more, then, of being sent to probe the enemy! If such a man were charged with defending the frontier, he would send scouts far afield and ascertain [?] the enemy's circumstances. When the enemy came, he might strengthen the fortifications and clear the countryside, relying on the city walls and assessing the situation while awaiting their weary withdrawal. Or he might raid their camp with light cavalry, occupy strategic terrain, and intercept their advance to break their fighting spirit. Beheading enemies and securing victories, he would succeed wherever he went: what difficulty would a formidable enemy present? If appointed commander-in-chief, he would rigorously enforce military administration, attend to the overall situation, and harbor no desire to win merit by luck. If appointed a subordinate commander, he would display his courage by penetrating deep into enemy territory, advancing straight upon their tents and shattering their resolve. Thus, men like Wei, Guo, Bi, and Di are all to be found among those available for employment. Why worry about the raiders of the Hetao? Why fear the remaining Hu forces? Why speak of borrowing talent from another age?

Nevertheless, generals must be chosen with discrimination and treated generously, while strictness is especially essential in controlling them. Why? The lives of the armies depend upon one man; the security of a region rests upon one general. The northern enemy's numbers do not equal those of a single large county in China. Yet no one repels them, because the law is treated lightly. That anyone who brings an army to ruin must be punished is a fundamental law, ancient and modern. Making the law clear so that orders are strictly obeyed is a principal instrument of the ruler's authority. Punishing one man so that tens of thousands are made fearful, thereby preserving all their lives, is the greatest benevolence under Heaven. Those who still doubt this are not yet qualified to discuss military affairs. Thus, when Fan Aineng received his prescribed punishment, even the decayed military ethos of the Five Dynasties was revived; when Chen Shu was held accountable for his…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
敗者崑崙之露布尚傳彼何人也一轉移
之間猶足以振頹而告捷況天下之大四
海之廣握是以馭之能無濟乎
第四問
石雷
同考試官教諭莫批道德功業本非二致然必
體用本末兼舉斯爲合一之學是作得之
考試官教諭彭批是蓋志明道希文而有得
者
===
考試官教諭朱批發言不羣可以知其志矣
善學者求諸聖人而已矣善學聖人者求
諸賢人而已矣賢之與聖其道本無不同
而希賢與聖其序自不容紊也循其序以
至於道此入聖之途也作聖之階也陵節
焉則銳躐等焉則疎銳與疎非學也故曰
行遠自邇也登高自卑也夫是謂之善學
夫是謂之有本之學是故君子慎趨而戒
速此執事發問意也且孔孟之道德伊周
punctuated:
敗者，崑崙之露布尚傳。彼何人也？一轉移之間，猶足以振頹而告捷，況天下之大、四海之廣，握是以馭之，能無濟乎？

第四問
石雷

同考試官教諭莫批：「道德功業，本非二致，然必體用本末兼舉，斯爲合一之學。是作得之。」

考試官教諭彭批：「是蓋志明道、希文而有得者。」

考試官教諭朱批：「發言不羣，可以知其志矣。」

善學者，求諸聖人而已矣；善學聖人者，求諸賢人而已矣。賢之與聖，其道本無不同，而希賢與聖，其序自不容紊也。循其序以至於道，此入聖之途也，作聖之階也。陵節焉則銳，躐等焉則疎，銳與疎，非學也。故曰：「行遠自邇也，登高自卑也。」夫是謂之善學，夫是謂之有本之學。是故君子慎趨而戒速，此執事發問意也。且孔孟之道德，伊周
translation_en:
…who held him accountable for defeat—the public proclamation of victory at Kunlun is still transmitted. What sort of men were they? With a single change of course, they could still reverse decline and announce victory. How much more, then, with all the vastness of the realm and the breadth of the Four Seas: if one grasps this principle and governs by it, could one fail to achieve results?

Fourth Policy Question
Shi Lei

Comment by Associate Examiner Mo, Instructor: “Moral cultivation and meritorious achievement are fundamentally not two separate pursuits. Yet only by attending together to substance and function, root and branches, can learning unite them as one. This composition has grasped that.”

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: “This is surely the work of someone who aspires to emulate Mingdao and Xiwen and has gained some understanding.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “His words rise above the ordinary; from them one can discern his aspirations.”

Those who learn well seek guidance from the sages, and nothing more. Those who learn well from the sages seek guidance from the worthies, and nothing more. The Way of worthies and sages is fundamentally the same, but the sequence of aspiring to become a worthy and then a sage must not be confused. Following that sequence to reach the Way is the path to sagehood, the stairway to becoming a sage. Overstepping the stages leads to impetuosity; skipping the grades leads to superficiality. Neither impetuosity nor superficiality constitutes learning. Thus it is said: “To travel far, begin nearby; to ascend high, begin below.” This is what is called learning well; this is what is called learning with a foundation. Therefore the gentleman proceeds carefully and guards against haste. This is the intent of the question you have posed. Now, as for the moral virtue of Confucius and Mencius, and Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之事業人皆仰之然或以其道大且至而
其世遠且乆則望之若不可企及由是向
慕之心或幾乎息羹墻之念無由以興也
故胡安國曰立志以明道希文自期待豈
非以聞知者不若見知者之爲詳取法於
古者不若取法於今之者之易於感發乎
去明道希文之世若此其甚近也而可忽
乎哉粤自有宋開基忠厚立國五星聚奎
旣朕兆賢哲之生仁育義正復培植豪傑
===
之氣故至仁宗之時英賢輩出窮理盡性
咸達精微之蘊若周敦頤之沉潜體道張
載之剛毅自立邵雍之明睿燭幾謝良佐
之誠篤憤悱其於道統之傳皆能有得程
頤於明道獨稱之曰孟子之後一人何哉
蓋其資稟超邁氣質純粹得諸天者固非
諸賢之所可及沉潜六經寤寐羣聖淑諸
人者亦非諸賢之所能盡也是故雲淡風
輕之咏浴沂之氣象也春陽和氣之度申
punctuated: 之事業，人皆仰之。然或以其道大且至，而其世遠且乆，則望之若不可企及。由是向慕之心或幾乎息，羹墻之念無由以興也。故胡安國曰：「立志以明道、希文自期待。」豈非以聞知者不若見知者之爲詳，取法於古者不若取法於今之者之易於感發乎？去明道、希文之世若此其甚近也，而可忽乎哉？粤自有宋開基，忠厚立國，五星聚奎，旣朕兆賢哲之生；仁育義正，復培植豪傑之氣。故至仁宗之時，英賢輩出，窮理盡性，咸達精微之蘊。若周敦頤之沉潜體道，張載之剛毅自立，邵雍之明睿燭幾，謝良佐之誠篤憤悱，其於道統之傳皆能有得。程頤於明道獨稱之曰：「孟子之後一人。」何哉？蓋其資稟超邁，氣質純粹，得諸天者固非諸賢之所可及；沉潜六經，寤寐羣聖，淑諸人者亦非諸賢之所能盡也。是故雲淡風輕之咏，浴沂之氣象也；春陽和氣之度，申
translation_en:
…and their achievements, everyone looks up to them. Yet some, considering their Way great and consummate and their age remote and long past, regard them as impossible to attain. Thus their admiration and longing may almost cease, and the yearning to behold them in soup and against the wall has no means of arising. Hence Hu Anguo said: “In setting your resolve, take Mingdao and Xiwen as the measure of what you expect of yourself.” Is this not because knowledge gained through hearing is less detailed than knowledge gained through seeing, and taking contemporaries as models more readily inspires one than taking the ancients as models [?]? We are so very close to the age of Mingdao and Xiwen—how could we disregard them?

When the Song dynasty first laid its foundations, it established the state upon loyalty and generosity. The conjunction of the five planets in the Kui constellation already portended the birth of worthy and wise men; nurturing through benevolence and rectifying through righteousness further cultivated the spirit of outstanding men. Thus, by the reign of Renzong, eminent worthies appeared in succession. Investigating principle and fully realizing human nature, they all penetrated its subtle profundities. Zhou Dunyi deeply immersed himself in embodying the Way; Zhang Zai stood independently with firmness and resolve; Shao Yong illuminated the incipient workings of things with clarity and insight; and Xie Liangzuo, sincere and earnest, strove to comprehend and articulate what eluded him. All gained something from the transmission of the succession of the Way. Yet Cheng Yi singled out Mingdao for the praise, “The one man since Mengzi.” Why?

His natural endowments were exceptional, and his disposition pure: what he received from Heaven was indeed beyond the reach of the other worthies. He immersed himself deeply in the Six Classics and dwelt upon the sages waking and sleeping: what he gained through human instruction was likewise beyond what the other worthies could fully attain. Thus his verse about pale clouds and a gentle breeze expressed the spirit of bathing in the Yi River; his bearing, like the warm sun and harmonious air of spring, was shen [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天之容色也致君堯舜責難之恭也視民
如傷安人之仁也此其泛應曲當渾然天
成庶幾乎廓然太公物來順應之域矣其
言曰以聖人之訓爲必當從先王之治爲
必可法呂大臨曰其自任之重寧學聖人
而未至不以一善而成名朱光庭亦曰先
生得聖人之誠者也才周萬物而不自以
爲高學際三才而不自以爲足行貫神明
而不自以爲異識照古今而不自以爲得
===
蓋其所知上極堯舜帝王三代之治其所
包博大悠遠上下與天地而同流斯言也
明道非眞有所見則趨向取舍何以致若
是之決諸生非眞登明道之堂安能形容
至此乎是故明道當之無愧色稱諸後世
無異詞此其所以大過人者哉固萬世學
者之師也若夫慶曆之間名臣接踵多所
建樹以成一代之治若韓琦之豐功偉量
司馬光之清忠粹德富弼之抗論虜庭歐
punctuated:
天之容色也。致君堯舜，責難之恭也；視民如傷，安人之仁也。此其泛應曲當，渾然天成，庶幾乎廓然太公、物來順應之域矣。其言曰：「以聖人之訓爲必當從，先王之治爲必可法。」呂大臨曰：「其自任之重，寧學聖人而未至，不以一善而成名。」朱光庭亦曰：「先生得聖人之誠者也。才周萬物而不自以爲高，學際三才而不自以爲足，行貫神明而不自以爲異，識照古今而不自以爲得。蓋其所知，上極堯舜帝王三代之治；其所包，博大悠遠，上下與天地而同流。」斯言也，明道非眞有所見，則趨向取舍何以致若是之決？諸生非眞登明道之堂，安能形容至此乎？是故明道當之無愧色，稱諸後世無異詞。此其所以大過人者哉！固萬世學者之師也。
若夫慶曆之間，名臣接踵，多所建樹，以成一代之治。若韓琦之豐功偉量，司馬光之清忠粹德，富弼之抗論虜庭，歐
translation_en:
…a relaxed and cheerful countenance [?]. Bringing his ruler to the level of Yao and Shun expressed the respect that demands difficult accomplishments of a sovereign; regarding the people as though they were wounded expressed the benevolence that brings others peace. His responses to every circumstance were fitting in every detail, wholly natural and unforced. He thus approached the realm of complete openness and impartiality [?], responding appropriately to things as they arose. He said: “The teachings of the sages must assuredly be followed, and the government of the former kings can assuredly serve as a model.” Lü Dalin said: “So weighty were the responsibilities he took upon himself that he preferred to study the sages, even without attaining their level, rather than establish his reputation through a single good deed.” Zhu Guangting also said: “The Master attained the sincerity of the sages. His abilities embraced all things, yet he did not consider himself exalted; his learning encompassed the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—yet he did not consider it sufficient. His conduct penetrated the spiritual powers, yet he did not consider himself extraordinary; his understanding illuminated past and present, yet he did not consider himself accomplished. His knowledge reached back to the government of Yao and Shun, the emperors and kings, and the Three Dynasties. What he embraced was broad and vast, far-reaching and enduring, flowing together with Heaven and Earth above and below.” As these words show, had Mingdao not truly attained insight, how could his aims and choices have been so decisive? Had his students not truly entered Mingdao’s hall of learning, how could they have described him so well? Thus Mingdao could accept this praise without embarrassment, and later generations have voiced no disagreement in praising him. Surely this is what made him so greatly surpass others! He is indeed a teacher for scholars of all ages.
During the Qingli era, eminent ministers appeared in succession and accomplished much, bringing about good government for their age. Such were Han Qi’s abundant achievements and magnificent breadth of mind, Sima Guang’s unsullied loyalty and pure virtue, Fu Bi’s forthright arguments at the foreign court, and Ou…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
陽脩之文章擅名其於事功之建皆能成
章朱熹於希文獨稱之曰有宋第一流人
物何哉蓋其自秀才時便以天下為已任
其於富貴貧賤毀譽欣戚不一動其心是
故論上壽之儀去貪墨之吏識胡瑗之賢
發中庸之蘊服富弼之心策韓琦之敗妙
捄荒之術溥南園之施此其規模宏闊莫
窺其際庶幾乎一夫不獲時予之辜矣其
言曰先天下之憂而憂後天下之樂而樂
===
又曰不得為宰相則願為良醫曾鞏稱之
曰事有天下非之君子非之而公獨曰是
天下是之君子是之而公獨曰非其既也
君子自以為不及天下亦曰范公之守是
也斯言也希文非真有所得則負荷擔當
何以能如是之審子固非真知希文之心
何以揄揚至此乎是故即希文之自待與
子固之所以稱之者誠非尋常可及者哉
固萬世學者之宗也夫明道所學聖人之
punctuated:
陽脩之文章擅名，其於事功之建，皆能成章。朱熹於希文獨稱之曰：「有宋第一流人物。」何哉？蓋其自秀才時，便以天下為已任，其於富貴貧賤、毀譽欣戚，不一動其心。是故論上壽之儀，去貪墨之吏，識胡瑗之賢，發中庸之蘊，服富弼之心，策韓琦之敗，妙捄荒之術，溥南園之施。此其規模宏闊，莫窺其際，庶幾乎「一夫不獲，時予之辜」矣。其言曰：「先天下之憂而憂，後天下之樂而樂。」又曰：「不得為宰相，則願為良醫。」曾鞏稱之曰：「事有天下非之，君子非之，而公獨曰是；天下是之，君子是之，而公獨曰非。其既也，君子自以為不及，天下亦曰：『范公之守是也。』」斯言也，希文非真有所得，則負荷擔當何以能如是之審？子固非真知希文之心，何以揄揚至此乎？是故即希文之自待與子固之所以稱之者，誠非尋常可及者哉！固萬世學者之宗也。

夫明道所學，聖人之
translation_en:
…Ouyang Xiu was renowned for his literary compositions; in establishing practical achievements, all these men attained distinction. Yet Zhu Xi singled out Xiwen (Fan Zhongyan) for the praise, “A figure of the very first rank in the Song dynasty.” Why? From his days as a student, he took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself. Wealth and honor, poverty and low station, slander and praise, joy and sorrow—none could stir his heart. Thus he discussed the ceremonial offering of birthday felicitations, dismissed corrupt officials, recognized Hu Yuan’s worth, elucidated the profound meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean, won Fu Bi’s heartfelt submission, and foresaw Han Qi’s defeat. He devised ingenious methods of famine relief and extended his beneficence at the Southern Garden [?]. So expansive was the scope of his endeavors that none could discern its limits. He came close to the spirit of the saying, “If even one person fails to find his proper place, the fault is mine.” He said, “Be anxious before all under Heaven become anxious, and rejoice only after all under Heaven rejoice.” He also said, “If I cannot become a chief councilor, I wish to become a good physician.” Zeng Gong praised him, saying: “There were matters that everyone under Heaven condemned, and that gentlemen condemned, yet he alone declared right; matters that everyone under Heaven approved, and that gentlemen approved, yet he alone declared wrong. In the end, the gentlemen themselves acknowledged that they fell short of him, and everyone under Heaven likewise said, ‘Lord Fan was right in what he upheld.’” Considering these words: had Xiwen not truly attained understanding, how could he have been so sure in shouldering his responsibilities? Had Zigu (Zeng Gong) not truly understood Xiwen’s heart, how could he have praised him to this degree? Thus, judging both by what Xiwen demanded of himself and by the grounds on which Zigu praised him, were these not indeed beyond the reach of ordinary men? He is assuredly an exemplar for scholars of all ages.

Now, what Mingdao (Cheng Hao) studied was the sages’…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
事也而其所至則顏孟之域也希文所學
亦聖人之事也而其所得則伊尹之任也
大而未化也復而未至也是學者之軌也
循其軌而漸造其域至其域則亦大有所
得矣抑安敢自畫自棄而負天之所以與
我者乎世之士聰明才辨非不多談道德
功業非不廣然或得其體而不適其用或
專徇其末而莫探其本其最下者猶或藉
此爲蹊徑陰以徼名而侔利則亦安望其
===
窺二子之藩籬而與之論道德功業也哉
雖然君子不敢有輕天下之心也精以擇
之仁以居之勇以行之不爲詭異之行不
趨世俗之名道德也而孔孟而業未甞不
廣功業也而伊周而德未甞不崇是故聖
人學之的也弗至弗止者學者事也又安
知天下果無若人乎是豪傑之士也嗚呼
聖人吾不得而見之矣得見明道希文者
斯可矣志明道希文之志以奮乎五百年
punctuated:
事也，而其所至則顏孟之域也。希文所學亦聖人之事也，而其所得則伊尹之任也。大而未化也，復而未至也，是學者之軌也。循其軌而漸造其域，至其域則亦大有所得矣。抑安敢自畫自棄，而負天之所以與我者乎？世之士，聰明才辨非不多，談道德功業非不廣，然或得其體而不適其用，或專徇其末而莫探其本；其最下者，猶或藉此爲蹊徑，陰以徼名而侔利，則亦安望其窺二子之藩籬，而與之論道德功業也哉！
雖然，君子不敢有輕天下之心也。精以擇之，仁以居之，勇以行之，不爲詭異之行，不趨世俗之名。道德也，而孔孟而業未甞不廣；功業也，而伊周而德未甞不崇。是故聖人，學之的也；弗至弗止者，學者事也。又安知天下果無若人乎？是豪傑之士也。嗚呼！聖人吾不得而見之矣，得見明道、希文者斯可矣。志明道、希文之志，以奮乎五百年
translation_en:
…such endeavors, and the realm he attained was that of Yan Hui and Mengzi. What Xiwen studied was likewise the work of the sages, and what he attained was Yi Yin’s sense of responsibility. Greatness without yet achieving transformation, a return without yet reaching the destination: these mark the course for learners. By following that course, one gradually approaches their realm; upon reaching it, one will likewise have gained much. How could we dare to set limits upon ourselves and abandon ourselves, betraying what Heaven has bestowed upon us? Among the scholars of the age, intelligence, talent, and eloquence are far from rare, and discussions of moral virtue and meritorious achievement are far from limited. Yet some grasp the substance without putting it to fitting use, while others pursue only the ramifications without exploring the root. The lowest may even use these things as a shortcut, secretly seeking fame and grasping for profit. How could we expect them even to glimpse the outer bounds of these two masters’ learning, or discuss moral virtue and meritorious achievement with them?
Even so, the gentleman dares not harbor contempt for the people of the world. He chooses his course with discernment, abides in it with benevolence, and carries it out with courage. He neither engages in eccentric conduct nor pursues worldly fame. As for moral virtue, Kongzi and Mengzi’s achievements were never anything but extensive [?]; as for meritorious achievement, Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou’s virtue was never anything but lofty [?]. Thus, the sage is the goal of learning, and refusing to stop until one reaches that goal is the learner’s task. How can we know that the world truly has no such people? These are men of outstanding resolve. Alas! I cannot hope to meet a sage; it would suffice to meet someone like Mingdao or Xiwen. To make Mingdao’s and Xiwen’s aspirations one’s own and rouse oneself five hundred years…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之後者存乎其人耳愚生亦竊有志焉而
未之逮也惟執事與其進
第五問
楊一麒
考試官教諭彭批築城建學乃滇中第一事
是作卓識遠見鑿鑿可行昔人謂識時務者在俊傑
子非其人邪
考試官教諭朱批老成練達不鑿不浮佳士
也
===
爲治之道二安民也養士也安民而求以
衞其生則安之也至矣養士而求以興其
德則養之也至矣是故爲之城焉爲之學
焉匪徒爲目前之謀而責效旦夕者將以
垂可久可大之規也執事爲滇謀尚有踰
此者乎愚雖不敏請誦其所聞以備采擇
焉夫滇在星野屬井鬼之墟在禹貢爲梁
州之域三代以前未始通中國也漢武時
始隸益州沿至南詔屢入西蜀取其士民
punctuated:
之後者，存乎其人耳。愚生亦竊有志焉，而未之逮也，惟執事與其進。
第五問
楊一麒
考試官教諭彭批：築城建學，乃滇中第一事。是作卓識遠見，鑿鑿可行。昔人謂識時務者在俊傑，子非其人邪？
考試官教諭朱批：老成練達，不鑿不浮，佳士也。
爲治之道二：安民也，養士也。安民而求以衞其生，則安之也至矣；養士而求以興其德，則養之也至矣。是故爲之城焉，爲之學焉，匪徒爲目前之謀而責效旦夕者，將以垂可久可大之規也。執事爲滇謀，尚有踰此者乎？愚雖不敏，請誦其所聞，以備采擇焉。夫滇在星野屬井鬼之墟，在《禹貢》爲梁州之域，三代以前未始通中國也。漢武時始隸益州，沿至南詔，屢入西蜀，取其士民
translation_en:
…after five hundred years—it rests with the individual himself. I, your humble student, also privately cherish this aspiration, though I have yet to attain it. I ask only that you encourage my progress.
Fifth Policy Question
Yang Yiqi
Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: Building city walls and establishing schools are the foremost task in Yunnan. This essay displays outstanding discernment and foresight; its proposals are demonstrably practicable. An ancient saying holds that those who understand the needs of the times are outstanding men. Are you not such a man?
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Mature and experienced, neither strained nor superficial: a fine scholar.
There are two principles of government: securing the people's well-being and nurturing scholars. To secure the people's well-being by seeking to protect their lives is to provide security to the utmost; to nurture scholars by seeking to cultivate their virtue is to nurture them to the utmost. Thus city walls are built for them, and schools established for them. These are not merely plans for immediate needs, from which results are demanded overnight; they are intended to bequeath a framework capable of enduring and expanding. In your planning for Yunnan, could anything surpass these measures? Though I am slow of understanding, allow me to recount what I have heard for your consideration and selection.
Yunnan, in the celestial division corresponding to its territory, belongs to the region of the lunar lodges Well and Ghost; in the Tribute of Yu, it falls within the territory of Liangzhou. Before the Three Dynasties, it had not yet established communication with the Central States. Only in the time of Emperor Wu of the Han did it come under Yizhou. Later, in the Nanzhao period, repeated incursions were made into western Shu, taking away its scholars and common people…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而分置之文物之美漸以繁矣及洪武十
五年我
太祖遣三將軍帥師二十萬取其土地而郡縣
之治化之敷漸以溥矣繼而復徙天下豪
右以實之先後三十萬休養百餘年至於
今民庶煕煕人材彬彬外戶之不閉也垣
墉之不限也郁乎鄒魯之名區也淳乎蘇
湖之風聲也固將因俗順治與斯人相忘
於逸樂可也然或者以為意外之虞雖盛
===
世所不免目前之患在今日所當鑒也且
其地西通西域北接吐蕃南連交廣東限
羅夷俯而視之不知其幾千里誠邊徼沃
衍之所也人生其間者性習殊途風俗異
齊變故百出難於逆覩是故屯營之獷悍
也夷漢之侵侮也撲拇之相噬也僰猡之
相訾也沙儂之角毒也蒲縹之獰肆也雖
平定安集之謀招徠拊循之策在所當急
然久安長治之道潜移默化之術尤不可
punctuated: 而分置之，文物之美漸以繁矣。及洪武十五年，我太祖遣三將軍帥師二十萬，取其土地而郡縣之，治化之敷漸以溥矣。繼而復徙天下豪右以實之，先後三十萬，休養百餘年。至於今，民庶煕煕，人材彬彬，外戶之不閉也，垣墉之不限也，郁乎鄒魯之名區也，淳乎蘇湖之風聲也。固將因俗順治，與斯人相忘於逸樂可也。然或者以為意外之虞，雖盛世所不免；目前之患，在今日所當鑒也。且其地西通西域，北接吐蕃，南連交廣，東限羅夷，俯而視之，不知其幾千里，誠邊徼沃衍之所也。人生其間者，性習殊途，風俗異齊，變故百出，難於逆覩。是故屯營之獷悍也，夷漢之侵侮也，撲拇之相噬也，僰猡之相訾也，沙儂之角毒也，蒲縹之獰肆也，雖平定安集之謀、招徠拊循之策，在所當急，然久安長治之道、潜移默化之術，尤不可
translation_en:
…and settled them in separate places, so that the splendor of its cultural accomplishments gradually flourished. In the fifteenth year of Hongwu [1382], our Taizu dispatched three generals commanding an army of two hundred thousand to seize its territory and organize it into prefectures and counties. The reach of governance and moral transformation gradually broadened. Subsequently, powerful families from throughout the realm were again relocated there to populate it, numbering three hundred thousand in successive groups. After more than a hundred years of rest and recuperation, the common people now live in contentment, and men of talent abound in cultivated refinement. Outer doors need not be shut, and enclosing walls impose no barriers. In cultural flourishing, it is a distinguished region like Zou and Lu; in the purity of its prevailing customs, it resembles Suzhou and Huzhou. Surely one might govern in accordance with its customs and, together with its people, live so comfortably and happily as to forget one another.

Some, however, consider that unforeseen dangers cannot be avoided even in a flourishing age, and that present troubles ought to serve as warnings today. Moreover, this territory communicates with the Western Regions to the west, adjoins Tufan to the north, connects with Jiao and Guang to the south, and is bounded by the Luo peoples to the east. Looking down over it, one cannot tell how many thousands of li it extends: it is indeed a fertile and expansive frontier region. Those born among its inhabitants differ in disposition and habits, and their customs are not uniform. Disruptions arise in countless forms and are difficult to foresee. Thus there are the fierceness of the military colonies and camps, the encroachments and insults between non-Han and Han, the mutual attacks of the Pumu [?], the mutual recriminations of the Boluo [?], the vicious contests of the Sha and Nong, and the savage license of the Pupiao [?]. Although plans for pacification and peaceful settlement, and policies for attracting people to allegiance and reassuring and caring for them, require urgent attention, the way to lasting peace and enduring good government, and the means of gradual, imperceptible moral transformation, above all must not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
無者故建城廣教此今日之所當預而圖
之當以漸者也易曰天險不可升也地險
山川丘陵也王公設險以守其國因天地
之險而爲之城池緩急有所恃而趨焉此
聖人保民之心也後世若周城朔方以防
狄患漢令縣邑城以剗秦弊蓋亦有見乎
此滇之有故城惟雲南大理洪武中沐英
等增脩之又分命將校相地築城始於曲
靖達於騰衝南竟臨安西掎景東衞所相
===
望大小相維可謂周悉矣然土地旣廣城
郭自遠往日安鳳之變起於尋甸首犯鄰
境嵩明之民扶老攜幼以奔滇城賊尾其
後慘不可言向使是州有城可恃且戰且
守與楊林相爲掎角非惟可以保其室家
而烏合之衆豈敢徑趨滇城哉近築鶴慶
之城雖微意所在不敢與知然鶴慶當城
而澂江廣西諸府獨不當城乎昆陽晉寧
新興石屏劔川路南諸州縣獨不當城乎
punctuated: 無者。故建城廣教，此今日之所當預而圖之、當以漸者也。《易》曰：「天險不可升也，地險山川丘陵也。王公設險以守其國。」因天地之險而爲之城池，緩急有所恃而趨焉，此聖人保民之心也。後世若周城朔方以防狄患，漢令縣邑城以剗秦弊，蓋亦有見乎此。滇之有故城，惟雲南、大理。洪武中，沐英等增脩之，又分命將校相地築城，始於曲靖，達於騰衝，南竟臨安，西掎景東，衞所相望，大小相維，可謂周悉矣。然土地旣廣，城郭自遠。往日安鳳之變起於尋甸，首犯鄰境，嵩明之民扶老攜幼以奔滇城，賊尾其後，慘不可言。向使是州有城可恃，且戰且守，與楊林相爲掎角，非惟可以保其室家，而烏合之衆豈敢徑趨滇城哉？近築鶴慶之城，雖微意所在不敢與知，然鶴慶當城，而澂江、廣西諸府獨不當城乎？昆陽、晉寧、新興、石屏、劔川、路南諸州縣獨不當城乎？
translation_en:
…must not be lacking. Thus building city walls and extending instruction are matters that we ought now to plan for in advance and undertake gradually. The Book of Changes says: “Heaven’s natural defenses cannot be scaled; earth’s natural defenses are mountains, rivers, hills, and heights. Kings and lords establish defenses to safeguard their states.” Taking advantage of the natural defenses of heaven and earth, they construct walls and moats so that, when emergencies arise, people have something to rely on and somewhere to seek refuge. This expresses the sages’ concern to protect the people. Later examples, such as the Zhou building walls at Shuofang to guard against the Di and the Han ordering county towns to be walled to eliminate the harmful legacy of the Qin, probably also reflect an understanding of this principle.

In Yunnan, only Yunnan and Dali had old city walls. During the Hongwu reign, Mu Ying and others enlarged and repaired them. They also separately ordered military officers to survey sites and build walls, beginning at Qujing and extending to Tengchong, reaching Lin’an in the south and securing the western flank at Jingdong. Guards and battalions stood within sight of one another, the larger and smaller mutually supporting one another. These arrangements may be called comprehensive. Yet because the territory is so extensive, the walled towns are naturally far apart.

Formerly, when An Feng’s rebellion arose in Xundian, its first attacks fell upon neighboring territory. The people of Songming supported their elderly and carried their children as they fled toward the provincial capital, with the rebels pursuing them. Their suffering was beyond description. Had this subprefecture possessed walls to rely on, its people could have fought while maintaining their defenses and formed mutually supporting positions with Yanglin. Not only could they have protected their households: how would that motley rabble have dared to advance directly upon the provincial capital?

Recently, walls were built at Heqing. Although I dare not presume to know the underlying intention, if Heqing ought to have walls, should the prefectures of Chengjiang and Guangxi alone not have them? Should the subprefectures and counties of Kunyang, Jinning, Xinxing, Shiping, Jianchuan, and Lunan alone not have them?

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
夫一人之失所吾之憂也而況不止於一
人乎誠能超然遠覽度地相時順人心之
所欲籍和雇以鳩工而版築興焉諸處並
舉而不以為勞盡出官帑而不以為費數
年之後城郭完固無事則散處以就耕牧
之便有警則入保以免劫掠之虞此萬世
之安也記曰古之教者家有塾黨有庠州
有序國有學因人性之同教之以學校明
道義而需器使焉此聖人養士之心也後
===
世若漢令天下郡邑建學唐四夷遣子入
學要亦有得乎此滇之舊有學亦惟雲南
大理洪武中張紞等增置之乃令各有司
隨處建學因其郡縣相其州衛師儒有所
廩餼有常相觀而善相師以成可謂詳備
矣然初制有禁生徒未繁近日科目之盛
多在城市間及附郭下邑之士遠涉乆出
以就師友力有不足業自中廢若使隨處
有學可依且耕且讀與諸生相為切磋非
punctuated:
夫一人之失所，吾之憂也，而況不止於一人乎？誠能超然遠覽，度地相時，順人心之所欲，籍和雇以鳩工，而版築興焉，諸處並舉而不以為勞，盡出官帑而不以為費，數年之後，城郭完固，無事則散處以就耕牧之便，有警則入保以免劫掠之虞，此萬世之安也。
記曰：「古之教者，家有塾，黨有庠，州有序，國有學。」因人性之同，教之以學校，明道義而需器使焉，此聖人養士之心也。後世若漢令天下郡邑建學，唐四夷遣子入學，要亦有得乎此。滇之舊有學，亦惟雲南、大理。洪武中，張紞等增置之，乃令各有司隨處建學，因其郡縣，相其州衛，師儒有所，廩餼有常，相觀而善，相師以成，可謂詳備矣。然初制有禁，生徒未繁。近日科目之盛，多在城市，間及附郭。下邑之士遠涉乆出，以就師友，力有不足，業自中廢。若使隨處有學可依，且耕且讀，與諸生相為切磋，非
translation_en:
Even one person deprived of a secure place is a cause of concern to me; how much more so when there is more than one! If we could truly rise above immediate concerns and take the long view, assess the terrain and the appropriate time, follow the wishes of the people, assemble laborers through hiring by agreement, and begin building rammed-earth walls—undertaking the work everywhere together without regarding it as burdensome, and paying entirely from public funds without begrudging the expense—then after several years the city walls would be complete and strong. In peaceful times, people could live dispersed for convenient farming and herding; when an alarm arose, they could enter the walls for protection and escape the danger of plunder. This would provide security for ten thousand generations.
The Book of Rites says: “In the teaching of antiquity, there was a school for each residential group, a school in each neighborhood, a school in each district, and an academy in each state.” Recognizing the shared nature of human beings, the sages educated them through schools, clarified the Way and righteousness, and prepared them for employment according to their abilities. Such was the sages’ intention in nurturing scholars. In later ages, the Han ordered commanderies and towns throughout the realm to establish schools, and under the Tang the peoples of the four quarters sent their sons to study. These, too, grasped something of that intention.
In earlier times, the only places in Dian with schools were Yunnan and Dali. During the Hongwu reign, Zhang Dan and others established additional schools, ordering the responsible authorities to build them in their respective localities, adapting to the prefectures and counties and assessing the subprefectures and guards. Teachers had places to teach, and provisions were regularly supplied. Students improved by observing one another and brought their learning to fruition by teaching one another. These arrangements could be called comprehensive indeed. Yet the original regulations imposed restrictions, and students were not numerous. Recently, success in the examinations has been concentrated largely in cities, extending occasionally to their surrounding areas. Scholars from outlying towns travel far and remain away for long periods to seek teachers and fellow students; when their resources prove insufficient, their studies inevitably lapse midway. If schools were available everywhere for them to attend, they could both farm and study, refining their learning together with the other students; not only …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
惟可以必其成就而比屋之民寧不樂歸
至化哉近馬龍六涼祿豐之建學雖其情
懇乃爲之請然馬龍六涼祿豐宜建學而
新興霑益獨不宜建乎武定路南彌勒建
水廣通定邊諸州縣獨不宜建乎夫一士
之失所吾之責也而況不止於一士乎誠
能毅然必行有教無類合酋長之子第羣
民間之俊秀而黌舍興焉雖徧設之而不
以爲多常廩之而不以爲濫數年之後風
===
俗丕變家誦詩書戶習禮樂入以事其父
兄出以事其長上此萬世之功也或曰是
役也必勞民必傷財作無益害有益譬之
牧者驅之廣野順其性焉可也是不然凡
吾府庫之所有者皆吾民之所共者也吾
民之所有者皆府庫之所未共者也吾之
積也凡以濟民以利用者也出吾之所有
以衛吾民吾民安則一境之內舉安旣安
且富則民自足府庫之未共者可長共也
punctuated:
惟可以必其成就，而比屋之民寧不樂歸至化哉？近馬龍、六涼、祿豐之建學，雖其情懇，乃爲之請。然馬龍、六涼、祿豐宜建學，而新興、霑益獨不宜建乎？武定、路南、彌勒、建水、廣通、定邊諸州縣獨不宜建乎？夫一士之失所，吾之責也，而況不止於一士乎？誠能毅然必行，有教無類，合酋長之子第、羣民間之俊秀，而黌舍興焉，雖徧設之而不以爲多，常廩之而不以爲濫。數年之後，風俗丕變，家誦詩書，戶習禮樂，入以事其父兄，出以事其長上，此萬世之功也。

或曰：「是役也，必勞民，必傷財，作無益害有益。譬之牧者，驅之廣野，順其性焉，可也。」是不然。凡吾府庫之所有者，皆吾民之所共者也；吾民之所有者，皆府庫之所未共者也。吾之積也，凡以濟民、以利用者也。出吾之所有以衛吾民，吾民安，則一境之內舉安。旣安且富，則民自足，府庫之未共者可長共也。
translation_en:
…only could their achievement be assured, but would not the people of every household gladly submit to the highest moral transformation? Recently, schools have been established in Malong, Liuliang, and Lufeng; it was indeed the earnestness of their appeals that prompted petitions on their behalf. Yet if schools ought to be established in Malong, Liuliang, and Lufeng, should they not also be established in Xinxing and Zhanyi? Should they not also be established in the subprefectures and counties of Wuding, Lunan, Mile, Jianshui, Guangtong, and Dingbian? If even one scholar lacks a proper place, that is our responsibility; how much more so when more than one scholar is affected! If we can truly act with determination, providing instruction without distinction of kind, bringing together the sons and younger kinsmen [?] of native chieftains and the outstanding talents among the common people, and establishing school buildings for them, then even schools established everywhere would not be considered too numerous, nor would regular grain allowances for their students be considered excessive. Within a few years, customs would be greatly transformed: every family would recite the Odes and the Documents, and every household would practice rites and music. At home they would serve their fathers and elder brothers; outside they would serve their elders and superiors. This would be an achievement benefiting ten thousand generations.

Some say: “This undertaking will surely burden the people and deplete resources. To undertake what is useless harms what is useful. Take a herdsman as an analogy: he need only drive his animals into open country and let them follow their nature.” This is not so. Everything in our public storehouses and treasuries has been supplied by our people; everything our people possess is what has not yet been supplied to those storehouses and treasuries. All that we accumulate is intended to aid the people and provide for practical needs. If we expend what we possess to protect our people, then, when our people are secure, the whole territory will be secure. Once secure and prosperous, the people will have enough for themselves, and what they have not yet supplied to the public storehouses and treasuries can continue to be supplied for years to come.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
惟可以必其成就而比屋之民寧不樂歸
至化哉近馬龍六凉祿豐之建學雖其情
懇乃爲之請然馬龍六凉祿豐宜建學而
新興霑益獨不宜建乎武定路南彌勒建
水廣通定邊諸州縣獨不宜建乎夫一士
之失所吾之責也而况不止於一士乎誠
能毅然必行有教無類合酋長之子弟羣
民間之俊秀而黌舍興焉雖徧設之而不
以爲多常廩之而不以爲濫數年之後風
===
俗丕變家誦詩書戶習禮樂入以事其父
兄出以事其長上此萬世之功也或曰是
役也必勞民必傷財作無益害有益譬之
牧者驅之廣野順其性焉可也是不然凡
吾府庫之所有者皆吾民之所共者也吾
民之所有者皆府庫之所未共者也吾之
積也凡以濟民以利用者也出吾之所有
以衞吾民吾民安則一境之內舉安旣安
且富則民自足府庫之未共者可長共也
punctuated:
惟可以必其成就，而比屋之民寧不樂歸至化哉？近馬龍、六凉、祿豐之建學，雖其情懇，乃爲之請，然馬龍、六凉、祿豐宜建學，而新興、霑益獨不宜建乎？武定、路南、彌勒、建水、廣通、定邊諸州縣獨不宜建乎？夫一士之失所，吾之責也，而况不止於一士乎？誠能毅然必行，有教無類，合酋長之子弟，羣民間之俊秀，而黌舍興焉，雖徧設之而不以爲多，常廩之而不以爲濫。數年之後，風俗丕變，家誦詩書，戶習禮樂，入以事其父兄，出以事其長上，此萬世之功也。
或曰：「是役也，必勞民，必傷財，作無益害有益。譬之牧者，驅之廣野，順其性焉，可也。」是不然。凡吾府庫之所有者，皆吾民之所共者也；吾民之所有者，皆府庫之所未共者也。吾之積也，凡以濟民、以利用者也。出吾之所有以衞吾民，吾民安則一境之內舉安。旣安且富，則民自足，府庫之未共者可長共也。
translation_en:
…provided that their successful completion can be assured, would not the people in every household gladly submit to the highest transforming influence? Recently, schools were established in Malong, Liuliang, and Lufeng. Although petitions were submitted on their behalf because their requests were earnest, if Malong, Liuliang, and Lufeng ought to have schools, should Xinxing and Zhanyi alone not have them? Should the other subprefectures and counties—Wuding, Lunan, Mile, Jianshui, Guangtong, and Dingbian—alone not have them? If even one scholar lacks his proper place, that is our responsibility; how much more so when it concerns more than one scholar! If we can truly resolve to carry this out, providing instruction without distinction of kind, assembling the sons and younger kinsmen of the chieftains and gathering the outstanding talents among the common people, then schools will flourish. Even if we establish them everywhere, we should not consider them too numerous; even if we regularly provide their students with grain allowances, we should not consider this excessive. After several years, customs will be profoundly transformed: every family will recite the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, and every household will practice rites and music. At home they will serve their fathers and elder brothers; outside they will serve their elders and superiors. This will be an achievement lasting for myriad generations.
Someone may say: “This undertaking will certainly burden the people and deplete resources. To create what is useless harms what is useful. Take the example of a herdsman: driving his animals into open country and letting them follow their nature is sufficient.” This is not so. Everything in our public treasuries and granaries has been supplied by our people; everything our people possess is what has not yet been contributed to those repositories. All that we accumulate is intended to relieve the people and make resources useful. If we expend what we possess to protect our people, then, when our people are secure, the whole territory will be secure. Once secure and prosperous, the people will have enough for themselves, and what has not yet been contributed to the public treasuries and granaries can continue to supply them indefinitely.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
孝弟忠信士之懿德也而聰俊黠桀者乃
民間之美質也可與爲善可與爲不善者
也推士之懿德以成其美質美質成則一
方之教以興旣興且洽則無兵守固吾之
所有者可長有也且禦菑捍患以爲民也
移風易俗以善治也政之大經也
國初新造猶築城如彼建學如彼樓櫓壯麗
文教勃興況今承平之日財賦充溢而可
少靳於此乎故曰論大計者不惜小費又
===
曰見小利則大事不成通達國體者必有
以審此矣雖然猶有幾焉天下之事每患
於議論多而成功少者何也任之者難其
人也昔禹治洪水八年而後底績井田學
校孟子爲滕計者詳矣而陰壞於許行事
之難成易敗也類如此今欲築城建學非
有身任其責及同心體國之君子相爲先
後焉吾未見其可也噫此固滇之一大幾
也愚端有望於今日之百執事
punctuated:
孝弟忠信，士之懿德也；而聰俊黠桀者，乃民間之美質也，可與爲善，可與爲不善者也。推士之懿德以成其美質，美質成則一方之教以興；旣興且洽，則無兵守固，吾之所有者可長有也。且禦菑捍患，以爲民也；移風易俗，以善治也：政之大經也。國初新造，猶築城如彼，建學如彼，樓櫓壯麗，文教勃興；況今承平之日，財賦充溢，而可少靳於此乎？故曰：「論大計者不惜小費。」又曰：「見小利則大事不成。」通達國體者，必有以審此矣。

雖然，猶有幾焉。天下之事，每患於議論多而成功少者，何也？任之者難其人也。昔禹治洪水，八年而後底績。井田學校，孟子爲滕計者詳矣，而陰壞於許行。事之難成易敗也，類如此。今欲築城建學，非有身任其責及同心體國之君子相爲先後焉，吾未見其可也。噫！此固滇之一大幾也。愚端有望於今日之百執事。
translation_en:
Filial devotion, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness are the admirable virtues of scholars. Intelligence, talent, shrewdness, and forcefulness are fine natural endowments found among the common people, yet those possessing them can be guided toward either good or evil. Extend the admirable virtues of scholars to bring these fine endowments to fulfillment. Once they are perfected, moral instruction throughout the region will flourish. Once it flourishes and spreads everywhere, defenses will be secure even without troops, and what we possess can remain ours for long. Moreover, warding off calamities and averting dangers serves the people; transforming customs and changing habits brings good government. These are the great guiding principles of governance. Even at the dynasty’s founding, when everything was newly established, city walls and schools were built on such a scale: towers and watchtowers were magnificent, and cultural instruction flourished vigorously. How much less, now in an age of enduring peace, with abundant revenue, can we begrudge even a little expenditure on these things? Thus it is said, “Those who deliberate on great plans do not begrudge small expenses.” It is also said, “If one looks to small gains, great undertakings will not succeed.” Those who understand the essentials of governing the state will surely know how to weigh this.

Nevertheless, a crucial point remains. Why is it that undertakings throughout the realm so often suffer from much discussion but little accomplishment? Because it is difficult to find the right people to take responsibility for them. In antiquity, Yu brought the great flood under control only after eight years of labor. Mengzi’s plans for Teng concerning the well-field system and schools were detailed indeed, yet Xu Xing covertly undermined them. That undertakings are difficult to accomplish and easy to ruin is generally like this. If we now wish to build city walls and establish schools, unless there are gentlemen who personally assume responsibility and others who share their purpose and keep the state’s interests at heart, supporting one another in leading and following, I cannot see how it can be done. Alas! This is indeed a great turning point for Dian. I, in my humble judgment, place my hopes squarely upon all those holding office today.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
嘉靖丙午雲南鄉試事竣洛
濫司考校例當序諸末簡洛
嘗讀漢書至肅宗元和間滇
池出龍馬四白烏見因興起
學校漸遷其俗則知滇之有
學自漢始及讀司馬相如諸
===
傳其使西南夷嘗略斯榆舉
苞蒲而南中人士往往有受
學相如歸教鄉人者乃又知
西南之文業自相如始逮夫
五季之衰敝於南詔宋代之
末淪為異壤遂使碧雞金馬
徒聞其神黑水葉榆莫詳其
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序

嘉靖丙午，雲南鄉試事竣，洛濫司考校，例當序諸末簡。洛嘗讀漢書，至肅宗元和間，滇池出龍馬四，白烏見，因興起學校，漸遷其俗，則知滇之有學自漢始。及讀司馬相如諸傳，其使西南夷，嘗略斯榆，舉苞蒲，而南中人士往往有受學相如、歸教鄉人者，乃又知西南之文業自相如始。逮夫五季之衰，敝於南詔；宋代之末，淪為異壤。遂使碧雞金馬徒聞其神，黑水葉榆莫詳其
translation_en:
Postface to the Yunnan Provincial Examination Record

In the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], the Yunnan Provincial Examination was completed. I, Luo, having undeservedly been entrusted with examining the candidates, am required by customary practice to supply a postface at the end of the record. I once read in the History of the Han that during the Yuanhe era of Emperor Suzong, four dragon horses emerged from Dianchi and a white crow appeared. Schools were consequently established, gradually transforming local customs. From this I learned that schooling in Yunnan began under the Han. Later, reading the biographies of Sima Xiangru, I learned that on his mission to the southwestern peoples he had brought Siyu under control and taken Baopu [?]. Men of the southern region often studied under Xiangru and returned to teach the people of their home communities. Thus I further learned that literary learning in the southwest began with Xiangru. During the decline of the Five Dynasties, the region suffered under Nanzhao; by the end of the Song, it had fallen into foreign hands. Consequently, of Biji and Jinma only their spirits were heard of, while of Heishui and Yeyu no one knew in detail their …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
地文教方興而復斁其將有
所待哉洪惟我
高皇帝至仁洋溢長駕遠撫兼容
並包使六合八方懷生之物
皆得涵濡於休澤雖滇南亦
罔遐遺焉故甞
諭將臣有曰雲南之地稽之古
===
典氣厚風和人民尚兵上古
以爲遐荒中古禹蹟所至以
別水土故地屬梁州之域自
漢隋唐皆爲中國所統大哉
聖謨注意西南蓋其詳矣故今逖
陬裔土旣皆脫枹鼓以脩爼
豆且百餘年今
punctuated: 地。文教方興而復斁，其將有所待哉？洪惟我高皇帝，至仁洋溢，長駕遠撫，兼容並包，使六合八方懷生之物皆得涵濡於休澤，雖滇南亦罔遐遺焉。故甞諭將臣有曰：「雲南之地，稽之古典，氣厚風和，人民尚兵。上古以爲遐荒，中古禹蹟所至，以別水土，故地屬梁州之域。自漢隋唐，皆爲中國所統。」大哉聖謨！注意西南，蓋其詳矣。故今逖陬裔土，旣皆脫枹鼓以脩爼豆，且百餘年。今
translation_en:
