…their location. Civilizing instruction had scarcely begun to flourish before it again fell into decay. Was it perhaps awaiting something yet to come?

Great indeed was our Emperor Gao! His consummate benevolence overflowed; he extended his reach afar and brought comfort to distant lands, embracing and encompassing all. He enabled every living being throughout the universe and in every direction to be steeped in his gracious beneficence. Even distant southern Yunnan was not neglected. Thus he once instructed his generals, saying: “Examining the ancient classics, we find that the land of Yunnan has a rich vital energy and gentle winds, and its people esteem martial pursuits. In high antiquity it was regarded as a remote wilderness. In middle antiquity, Yu reached it in his travels to distinguish the waters and lands; thus it belonged within the territory of Liangzhou. From the Han through the Sui and Tang, it was under the rule of China.”

How great was this sagely design! His attention to the southwest was indeed thorough. Thus, by now, these remote corners and outlying lands have all laid aside drumsticks and war drums to cultivate the rites of sacrificial vessels, and have done so for more than a hundred years. Now…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天子則天象地制禮作敎復以
聖學旨要揭爲敬一箴頒布寰海
西南雖遠而臣民之游庠序
皆得仰窺千聖相傳之心法
有非漢代詞章之習所能彷
彿於萬一者於戲盛哉滇士
之生於斯時何其幸也洛菲
===
譾叨校文之役竊謂文章也
者志氣之所發也然本于敎
化繫于風俗佐于山川今觀
滇士之文其舉理精而考辭
達非
聖學融液爲之本歟其思致深而
寄寓遠非漢文淵源爲之繫
punctuated: 天子則天象地，制禮作敎，復以聖學旨要揭爲《敬一箴》，頒布寰海。西南雖遠，而臣民之游庠序，皆得仰窺千聖相傳之心法，有非漢代詞章之習所能彷彿於萬一者。於戲，盛哉！滇士之生於斯時，何其幸也！洛菲譾，叨校文之役，竊謂文章也者，志氣之所發也，然本于敎化，繫于風俗，佐于山川。今觀滇士之文，其舉理精而考辭達，非聖學融液爲之本歟？其思致深而寄寓遠，非漢文淵源爲之繫
translation_en:
…the Son of Heaven takes Heaven as his rule and Earth as his model, establishes rites and institutes instruction. He has further set forth the essentials of sagely learning in the Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi zhen), promulgating it throughout the realm. Remote though the southwest is, subjects who attend its schools can all reverently glimpse the teachings of the mind transmitted from sage to sage. This is something that the Han dynasty’s cultivation of literary composition could not resemble even in the slightest. Ah, how splendid! How fortunate are the scholars of Yunnan to have been born in this age!

I, Luo, shallow and limited as I am [?], have undeservedly been entrusted with examining their compositions. I venture to say that writing expresses aspiration and vital spirit, yet is rooted in moral instruction, bound to local customs, and aided by mountains and rivers. Looking now at the writings of Yunnan’s scholars, I find their exposition of principles precise and their choice of words lucid. Is this not because sagely learning, thoroughly assimilated, provides their foundation? Their thought is profound and what they convey has far-reaching implications: is this not bound to the wellsprings of Han writing …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
歟其負氣厚而稱物芳非碧
雞黑水爲之佐歟故是錄之
作有以見四履之盛焉有以
見化成之候焉有以見
大明之隆焉而人文之宣鬱風氣
之開塞係乎一方者非所論
矣多士旣躬逢
===
盛際而獲登是錄可不思自樹
立以求無負於
聖化哉若相如特援以遡文業之
自爾非敢以是望多士也多
士幸相與勗哉
河南開封府中牟縣儒學教
諭彭洛謹序
punctuated:
歟？其負氣厚而稱物芳，非碧雞黑水爲之佐歟？故是錄之作，有以見四履之盛焉，有以見化成之候焉，有以見大明之隆焉。而人文之宣鬱、風氣之開塞，係乎一方者，非所論矣。多士旣躬逢盛際，而獲登是錄，可不思自樹立，以求無負於聖化哉？若相如，特援以遡文業之自爾，非敢以是望多士也。多士幸相與勗哉！
河南開封府中牟縣儒學教諭彭洛謹序。
translation_en:
…is it not so? Their vital spirit is substantial, and their descriptions of things are splendid: is this not aided by Biji and Heishui? Thus, the compilation of this record reveals the flourishing of the realm, the signs of transformation through instruction, and the grandeur of the Great Ming. As for the flourishing or suppression of literary culture and the opening or obstruction of intellectual currents insofar as these concern a single region, these are not what is at issue here. You many scholars have yourselves encountered this flourishing age and gained inclusion in this record. Should you not strive to establish yourselves, seeking to prove worthy of the sage sovereign’s transforming influence? As for Xiangru, I have invoked him merely to trace the origins of literary accomplishment; I would not presume to make him the measure of my expectations for you. May you scholars encourage one another!
Preface respectfully composed by Peng Luo, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhongmu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄序
夫命鄉論秀其猶古之遺乎
然而法制之畀藝極之陳風
聲之樹蓋至我
聖朝而獨備矣茲歲丙午大比維
期先時禮部覈故事集羣議
請于
===
上乃降發
綸音凡以登賢剔弊申敕有加雲
南於諸藩最遠尤汲汲先事
之備維歲首月巡按御史郝
銘輒謀于藩臬緘詞束幣走
使四方徵校職以司文柄其
他繕場屋庀器具以至筐篚
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄序

夫命鄉論秀，其猶古之遺乎？然而法制之畀、藝極之陳、風聲之樹，蓋至我聖朝而獨備矣。茲歲丙午，大比維期，先時禮部覈故事，集羣議，請于上，乃降發綸音，凡以登賢剔弊，申敕有加。雲南於諸藩最遠，尤汲汲先事之備。維歲首月，巡按御史郝銘輒謀于藩臬，緘詞束幣，走使四方，徵校職以司文柄。其他繕場屋、庀器具，以至筐篚
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

Is not the command that local communities assess their outstanding men a legacy of antiquity? Yet the provision of laws and regulations, the setting forth of standards for literary accomplishment, and the establishment of an inspiring influence attained their full realization only under our sagely dynasty. This year, bingwu [1546], the triennial examination fell due. In advance, the Ministry of Rites examined precedents, gathered opinions, and submitted a request to the Emperor. An imperial pronouncement was then issued, with renewed and strengthened injunctions for advancing the worthy and eliminating abuses.

Yunnan, the most distant of the provinces, was particularly urgent in making preparations beforehand. In the first month of the year, Regional Inspector Hao Ming consulted the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, sealed letters and bundled gifts of silk, and dispatched messengers in all directions to recruit educational officials to take charge of literary assessment. Other preparations included repairing the examination compound and procuring equipment, down to the baskets …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
餼牽之細咸戒有司調度以
需期且届御史劉廷儀奉
命代至毅然曰惟是監臨豈異人
任爰殫厥心力諸所規畫益
慎而詳于時鎮守黔國公沐
朝輔素敦儒雅樂觀
盛典巡撫右僉都御史應大猷
===
綏懷善類式增士氣考試官
則佐偕教諭彭洛同考試官
則教諭莫遺賢胡悊劉濟民
羅萬鵬咸應聘而至提調則
右叅政劉伯躍右叅議沈繼
美監試則副使譙孟龍僉事
李文鳳自餘百執事咸慎簡
punctuated: 餼牽之細，咸戒有司調度以需。期且届，御史劉廷儀奉命代至，毅然曰：「惟是監臨，豈異人任？」爰殫厥心力，諸所規畫益慎而詳。于時，鎮守黔國公沐朝輔素敦儒雅，樂觀盛典；巡撫右僉都御史應大猷綏懷善類，式增士氣。考試官則佐偕教諭彭洛，同考試官則教諭莫遺賢、胡悊、劉濟民、羅萬鵬，咸應聘而至。提調則右叅政劉伯躍、右叅議沈繼美，監試則副使譙孟龍、僉事李文鳳。自餘百執事，咸慎簡
translation_en:
…down to such details as provisions and livestock, the responsible officials were all instructed to arrange supplies in readiness. As the appointed time approached, Censor Liu Tingyi arrived under imperial orders to take over. He declared resolutely: “As for supervising this examination, could that responsibility belong to anyone else?” He therefore devoted all his energies to the task, making every arrangement still more careful and thorough. At this time, Mu Chaofu, Duke of Qian, who commanded the regional garrison, had long cultivated scholarly refinement and welcomed the prospect of witnessing this grand occasion. The Grand Coordinator, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Ying Dayou, fostered and comforted worthy men, thereby raising the scholars’ spirits.

The Examiners were Zuo and Peng Luo, Instructor; the Associate Examiners were the Instructors Mo Yixian, Hu Zhe, Liu Jimin, and Luo Wanpeng. All arrived in response to their invitations. The Proctors were Liu Boyue, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, and Shen Jimei, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner. Those overseeing the examination were Qiao Menglong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Li Wenfeng, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. All the remaining functionaries were carefully selected…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以充比入鎖院乃合陞任提
學副使吳鵬署管僉事楊儒
魯所選士千五百有奇三試
之拔其儁者四十人幷錄文
之優者以
獻蓋昔者解額嘗羨于此而貴
州之士附焉今雖稍損而雲
===
南之士顓之顧人文勃鬱以
興主司有不獲盡取之憾亶
乎盛哉事旣竣佐乃再拜颺
言曰首庶物而寧萬國者惟
聖乎曠千載而幸一遘者惟
時乎雲南山川形勢之勝誠
亦天地奧區然故靡莫之域
punctuated:
以充。比入鎖院，乃合陞任提學副使吳鵬、署管僉事楊儒魯所選士千五百有奇，三試之，拔其儁者四十人，幷錄文之優者以獻。蓋昔者解額嘗羨于此，而貴州之士附焉；今雖稍損，而雲南之士顓之。顧人文勃鬱以興，主司有不獲盡取之憾，亶乎盛哉！
事旣竣，佐乃再拜颺言曰：「首庶物而寧萬國者，惟聖乎！曠千載而幸一遘者，惟時乎！雲南山川形勢之勝，誠亦天地奧區，然故靡莫之域，
translation_en:
…to fill the posts. When we entered the examination compound to be secluded, we assembled the more than fifteen hundred candidates selected by Wu Peng, promoted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, and Yang Rulu, acting Surveillance Assistant Commissioner. We examined them in three sessions and selected forty of the most outstanding, also transcribing the best essays for presentation to the throne. In former times, the quota of provincial graduates had exceeded this number, but candidates from Guizhou were then included. Now, although the quota has been somewhat reduced, candidates from Yunnan have it to themselves. Yet literary cultivation has flourished so vigorously that the examiners regretted being unable to select all the worthy candidates. Truly, how splendid!
When the proceedings were complete, Zuo bowed twice and proclaimed: “Surely it is the Sage who presides over all things and brings peace to the myriad states! Surely this is an age one is fortunate to encounter even once in a thousand years! With its magnificent mountains and rivers and commanding terrain, Yunnan is indeed one of the hidden treasures of Heaven and Earth. Yet it was formerly the territory of the Mimo…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而西南徼外地也唐虞聲敎
所未之訖成周禮樂所未之
覃秦漢而降威嚴綏輯所未
之能必而定也迨我
聖祖高皇帝混一寰區誕敷文德
籍其地而郡邑之淑其人而
庠校之斂其才而科目之蓋
===
始駸駸乎振起莫不誦法孔
子而業專經術矣重以
列聖休澤熈洽
皇上道化彌隆沾濡涵煦百八十
禩于茲蒸蒸乎蜚英騰茂人
懷利賓固其宜也易恒之彖
曰聖人久於其道而天下化
punctuated: 而西南徼外地也，唐虞聲敎所未之訖，成周禮樂所未之覃，秦漢而降威嚴綏輯所未之能必而定也。迨我聖祖高皇帝混一寰區，誕敷文德，籍其地而郡邑之，淑其人而庠校之，斂其才而科目之，蓋始駸駸乎振起，莫不誦法孔子而業專經術矣。重以列聖休澤熈洽，皇上道化彌隆，沾濡涵煦百八十禩于茲，蒸蒸乎蜚英騰茂，人懷利賓，固其宜也。《易》恒之彖曰：「聖人久於其道而天下化
translation_en:
…and lay beyond the southwestern frontier. The civilizing influence of Tang and Yu had not reached it, nor had the rites and music of the Zhou extended to it. From the Qin and Han onward, neither imposing authority nor measures of pacification could assuredly bring it under settled rule. Only when our sagely progenitor, Emperor Gao, unified the realm and widely spread his civil virtue did he register its lands and organize them into prefectures and counties, improve its people through schools, and gather its talented men through the examination system. Then advancement began to gather pace: all recited and emulated Confucius, devoting their studies to mastery of the Classics.
Added to this were the beneficent blessings of successive sage emperors, spreading in harmony, and the ever greater transforming influence of His Majesty’s Way. These have nourished and fostered the people for 180 years down to the present. Eminent talent has flourished increasingly and won renown; it is surely fitting that everyone should cherish the prospect of being received as a guest at court. The Commentary on the Judgment for the hexagram Heng (Constancy) in the Book of Changes says: “The sage abides long in his Way, and all under Heaven is transformed…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
成夫恒之為卦有雷風相與
之象焉風行雷動含生之類
莫不鬯達昭蘇矧靈秀攸鍾
有弗靡然響應其庸以遐阻
自外乎雖然古之取士或以
德進或以事舉或以言揚言
固其又次也至論不朽有三
===
立德立功立言復並舉之蓋
功以德立臯夔旦奭其選也
言以德立典謨訓誥其選也
夫何軒輊之有諸士今之見
錄有司固惟其言矣嗣是宣
猷展采惟所任使以圖稱塞
無寧弗以道德自命邪誠自
punctuated: 成。夫恒之為卦，有雷風相與之象焉。風行雷動，含生之類莫不鬯達昭蘇。矧靈秀攸鍾，有弗靡然響應，其庸以遐阻自外乎？雖然，古之取士，或以德進，或以事舉，或以言揚，言固其又次也。至論不朽有三：立德、立功、立言，復並舉之。蓋功以德立，臯夔旦奭其選也；言以德立，典謨訓誥其選也。夫何軒輊之有？諸士今之見錄有司，固惟其言矣。嗣是宣猷展采，惟所任使，以圖稱塞，無寧弗以道德自命邪？誠自
translation_en:
…is transformed. The hexagram Heng (Constancy) presents the image of thunder and wind acting together. As wind blows and thunder stirs, all living things flourish and revive. How much more must those endowed with exceptional spiritual gifts respond wholeheartedly! Could they exclude themselves on account of remoteness and difficult access?

Nevertheless, in antiquity men were selected for service through advancement for virtue, recommendation for deeds, or recognition for words; words certainly ranked after the other two. Yet when discussing the three forms of imperishability—establishing virtue, establishing achievements, and establishing words—all three are again placed together. For achievements are established through virtue, with Gao, Kui, Dan, and Shi as outstanding examples; words are established through virtue, with the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements as outstanding examples. What grounds, then, are there for ranking one above another?

You gentlemen have now been selected by the responsible officials, admittedly on the strength of your words alone. Hereafter, you will set forth your plans and carry out your undertakings according to the duties entrusted to you, striving to fulfill your responsibilities worthily. Surely you must take the Way and virtue as your own calling? If you truly …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
命以道德乃明庶敷納有功
不惟敘言不惟服斯未之信
也夫昔也猶未免鄉國之士
矣茲進而與天下士埒又安
得弗尚友古之人邪詩有之
高山仰止景行行止嚮往之
志曷惟其已昔祁奚能舉善
===
人之稱之也曰唯善故能舉
其類佐也不佞竊願徼有榮
譽于諸士是舉也綜理于外
則右布政使劉佐右叅政程
資左叅議郝維嶽副使余承
業僉事文衡安如山都指揮
僉事石邦憲汪勲其宣力維
punctuated:
命以道德，乃明庶敷納，有功不惟敘，言不惟服，斯未之信也。夫昔也，猶未免鄉國之士矣；茲進而與天下士埒，又安得弗尚友古之人邪？詩有之：「高山仰止，景行行止。」嚮往之志，曷惟其已？昔祁奚能舉善，人之稱之也曰：「唯善，故能舉其類。」佐也不佞，竊願徼有榮譽于諸士。
是舉也，綜理于外，則右布政使劉佐、右叅政程資、左叅議郝維嶽、副使余承業、僉事文衡、安如山、都指揮僉事石邦憲、汪勲，其宣力維
translation_en:
…take morality as their own calling. Then, in assessing accomplishments and receiving statements [?], that their merits should go unrecognized and their words unheeded is something I cannot believe. Formerly, they were still merely scholars of their native region; now they have advanced to stand alongside scholars throughout the realm. How could they fail to seek fellowship with the men of antiquity? The Book of Odes says: “We look up to the lofty mountain; we travel along the great road.” How could their aspiration toward such examples ever cease? In ancient times, Qi Xi could recommend worthy men. Those who praised him said: “Because he is worthy, he can recommend others of his kind.” I, Zuo, though untalented, privately hope to gain some reflected honor from you scholars.
For this examination, those who managed affairs outside the examination compound were Liu Zuo, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Cheng Zi, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Hao Weiyue, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Yu Chengye, Surveillance Deputy Commissioner; Wen Heng and An Rushan, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Shi Bangxian and Wang Xun, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. Their exertions were…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
均者也從役于公則左布政
使曾存仁左叅政黄行可按
察使蔡雲程副使岑萬皆先
事與勞者也宜備書焉
直隷池州府建德縣儒學教
諭朱佐謹序
punctuated:
均者也。從役于公，則左布政使曾存仁、左叅政黄行可、按察使蔡雲程、副使岑萬，皆先事與勞者也，宜備書焉。
直隷池州府建德縣儒學教諭朱佐謹序。
translation_en:
…were equal in their contributions. Those who assisted in this public undertaking—Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zeng Cunren, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Huang Xingke, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Cai Yuncheng, and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Cen Wan—all shared in the work of preparation. It is fitting to record them all here.
Respectfully prefaced by Zhu Zuo, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiande County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili).

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
孔子曰君子有九思視思明聽思聰色思
温貌思恭言思忠事思敬疑思問忿思
難見得思義
可以贊天地之化育則可以與天地參矣
夫世祿滕固行之矣詩云雨我公田遂及
我私惟助爲有公田由此觀之雖周亦
助也設爲庠序學校以敎之庠者養也
===
校者敎也序者射也夏曰校殷曰序周
曰庠學則三代共之皆所以明人倫也
人倫明於上小民親於下
易
文言曰坤至柔而動也剛至靜而德方
豚魚吉信及豚魚也
子曰易有聖人之道四焉者此之謂也
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

孔子曰：「君子有九思：視思明，聽思聰，色思温，貌思恭，言思忠，事思敬，疑思問，忿思難，見得思義。」

可以贊天地之化育，則可以與天地參矣。

夫世祿，滕固行之矣。詩云：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」惟助爲有公田。由此觀之，雖周亦助也。設爲庠序學校以敎之。庠者，養也；校者，敎也；序者，射也。夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠；學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。人倫明於上，小民親於下。

易

文言曰：「坤至柔而動也剛，至靜而德方。」

「豚魚吉」，信及豚魚也。

子曰「易有聖人之道四焉」者，此之謂也。

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Confucius said: “The gentleman has nine considerations: when looking, he considers how to see clearly; when listening, how to hear distinctly; in his expression, how to be warm; in his bearing, how to be respectful; in speaking, how to be sincere; in handling affairs, how to be reverent; when in doubt, how to inquire; when angry, what trouble may follow; and when he sees an opportunity for gain, what is right.”

“If one can assist the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth, one can then stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third.”

“As for hereditary stipends, Teng has indeed already put them into practice. The Book of Odes says: ‘Let rain fall on our public field, and then reach our private fields.’ Only the system of assistance has public fields. Viewed in this light, even the Zhou used the system of assistance. Establish xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools to instruct the people. Xiang means nourishing; xiao means teaching; xu means archery. Under the Xia they were called xiao, under the Yin, xu, and under the Zhou, xiang. The xue was common to all three dynasties. All served to clarify human relationships. When human relationships are made clear above, the common people below are affectionate toward one another.”

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Words of the Text says: “Kun is supremely yielding, yet firm in its movement; supremely still, yet square in its virtue.”

“‘Good fortune with piglets and fish’ means that trustworthiness extends even to piglets and fish.”

“This is what the Master meant when he said, ‘The Book of Changes contains four aspects of the way of the sages.’”

“In ancient times, when the sages composed the Book of Changes, they intended to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the way of Heaven as yin and yang, and the way of Earth as yielding …

剛故易六位而成章
書
愼徽五典五典克從納于百揆百揆時叙
賓于四門四門穆穆
若金用汝作礪若濟巨川用汝作舟楫若
歲大旱用汝作霖雨
公其以予萬億年敬天之休
===
惟周公克愼厥始惟君陳克和厥中惟公
克成厥終三后恊心同底于道道洽政
治澤潤生民
詩
于以盛之維筐及筥于以湘之維錡及釡
牧人乃夢衆維魚矣旐維旟矣大人占之
衆維魚矣實維豐年旐維旟矣室家溱
溱
王遣申伯路車乘馬我圖爾居莫如南土
punctuated:
與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書
愼徽五典，五典克從；納于百揆，百揆時叙；賓于四門，四門穆穆。
若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。
公其以予萬億年敬天之休。
惟周公克愼厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。三后恊心，同底于道；道洽政治，澤潤生民。

詩
于以盛之？維筐及筥。于以湘之？維錡及釡。
牧人乃夢：衆維魚矣，旐維旟矣。大人占之：衆維魚矣，實維豐年；旐維旟矣，室家溱溱。
王遣申伯，路車乘馬。我圖爾居，莫如南土。
translation_en:
…and the firm; they established the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They combined the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and doubled each; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin from yang and alternated the yielding and the firm; thus the six positions in the Changes form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents
He carefully brought the five teachings into harmony, and the five teachings were obeyed. He was appointed to oversee the hundred affairs, and the hundred affairs were duly ordered. He received guests at the four gates, and all at the four gates was reverent and harmonious.
If I am metal, I shall use you as a whetstone; if I am crossing a great river, I shall use you as a boat and oars; if the year brings a great drought, I shall use you as abundant rain.
May you, my lord, enable me for countless ages to honor Heaven’s favor.
The Duke of Zhou was able to exercise care at the beginning; Jun Chen was able to bring harmony in the middle; and you, my lord, can bring the work to completion at its end. These three lords, united in purpose, all attained the Way. The Way prevailed, government was well ordered, and beneficence nourished the people.

Book of Odes
In what shall we put them? In square baskets and round baskets. In what shall we cook them? In cauldrons with legs and pots without legs.
The herdsmen had a dream: the multitudes became fish, and the tortoise-and-snake banners became falcon banners. The diviner interpreted it: “The multitudes becoming fish means a year of abundant harvests; the tortoise-and-snake banners becoming falcon banners means households will be teeming with people.”
The king sent off the Earl of Shen with a grand carriage and a team of four horses. “I have considered where you should dwell; nowhere is better than the southern lands. …”

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
錫爾介圭以作爾寶往近王舅南土是
保
懷柔百神及河喬嶽
春秋
滕子來朝桓公二年齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰
田定公十年
春齊人陳人曹人伐宋莊公十有四年
盟于召陵僖公四年會于蕭魚襄公十有
一年
===
夏公會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷定公十
年
禮記
先王之立禮也有本有文忠信禮之本也
義理禮之文也無本不立無文不行
善歌者使人繼其聲善教者使人繼其志
然後聖人作為父子君臣以為紀綱紀綱
既正天下大定天下大定然後正六律
和五聲弦歌詩頌
punctuated:
錫爾介圭，以作爾寶。往近，王舅，南土是保。
懷柔百神，及河喬嶽。
《春秋》
滕子來朝，桓公二年。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田，定公十年。
春，齊人、陳人、曹人伐宋，莊公十有四年。

《禮記》
先王之立禮也，有本有文。忠信，禮之本也；義理，禮之文也。無本不立，無文不行。
善歌者，使人繼其聲；善教者，使人繼其志。
然後聖人作為父子、君臣，以為紀綱。紀綱既正，天下大定。天下大定，然後正六律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌，
translation_en:
… I bestow upon you a great jade tablet to serve as your treasure. Go now [?], royal uncle, and safeguard the southern lands.
He propitiates the hundred spirits, including those of the Yellow River and the lofty mountains.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The Viscount of Teng came to pay court. Second year of Duke Huan.
The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. Tenth year of Duke Ding.
In spring, the men of Qi, Chen, and Cao attacked Song. Fourteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
A covenant was concluded at Shaoling. Fourth year of Duke Xi.
A meeting was held at Xiaoyu. Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.
In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. Tenth year of Duke Ding.

Record of Rites
When the former kings established ritual, it had both a foundation and an outward form. Loyalty and trustworthiness are the foundation of ritual; righteousness and proper principles are its outward form. Without a foundation, it cannot stand; without an outward form, it cannot be practiced.
A skilled singer enables others to carry on his melody; a skilled teacher enables others to carry on his aspirations.
Then the sages established the relationships of father and son, ruler and minister, to provide the framework of order. Once this framework was set right, all under Heaven attained great stability. Once all under Heaven attained great stability, they then rectified the six pitch standards, harmonized the five notes, and sang the poems and hymns to the accompaniment of stringed instruments …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
此五行者足以正身安國矣彼國安而天
下安故曰吾觀於鄉而知王道之易易
也
第貳塲
論
道以中庸爲至
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢議可以佐百姓者詔後元年

===
擬宋建邇英延義二閣成羣臣賀表景祐
二年
判語五條
同僚代判署文案
器用布絹不如法
見任官輒自立碑
隱匿孳生官畜產
官吏詞訟家人訴
第叄塲
punctuated:
此五行者，足以正身安國矣。彼國安而天下安，故曰：「吾觀於鄉，而知王道之易易也。」

第貳塲
論：道以中庸爲至。
詔誥表內科一道：
擬漢議可以佐百姓者詔，後元年。
擬唐以狄仁傑爲侍御史誥，儀鳳元年。
擬宋建邇英延義二閣成羣臣賀表，景祐二年。

同僚代判署文案。
器用布絹不如法。

隱匿孳生官畜產。

第叄塲
translation_en:
…These five practices suffice to rectify oneself and bring peace to the state. When the state is at peace, all under Heaven is at peace. Thus it is said: “By observing the village ceremonies, I understand how very easy the kingly Way is to realize.”

Second Session
Discourse: The Way reaches its highest expression in the Mean and the Constant.
One question from among imperial edicts, proclamations, and memorials [科, apparently indicating selection, is doubtful]:
Compose, as if for the Han court, an edict calling for deliberation on measures that could assist the common people. First year of Houyuan.
Compose, as if for the Tang court, a proclamation appointing Di Renjie as Palace Censor. First year of Yifeng.
Compose, as if for the Song court, a congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials on the completion of the Erying and Yanyi pavilions. Second year of Jingyou.
Five legal judgments:
A colleague adjudicates and signs case documents on another official’s behalf.
Utensils, cotton cloth, and silk fail to conform to statutory standards.
An incumbent official erects a commemorative stele for himself without authorization.
Concealing the offspring of government-owned livestock.
In litigation involving officials or clerks, members of their households lodge the complaint.

Third Session

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第五道
問先聖後聖其揆一也矧一代之興創守
中興之賢聖祖孫相紹盛德大業宜無
有不一者如成湯建中高宗協德文武
受命宣王中興其德業相望者可徵矣
自漢以下光武之於高祖豁達大度史
稱同符憲宗之於文皇勵精求治庶幾
貞觀似矣其視商周果若是班乎洪惟
我
===
太祖高皇帝肇建華夏功德之盛誠有以軼殷
周而陋漢唐矣迨我
皇上晉臨區宇懋昭大德並隆治功丕顯丕承
猗歟休哉顧其間致治之迹雖不能以
皆同然亦有默契焉者本諸身而達之
家國天下不知凡幾其大且著者昭如
日月則天下臣民之所共仰也可得聞
歟仰惟
至德至治宜無待仰賛一詞而臣子愛
punctuated:
第五道
問：先聖後聖，其揆一也。矧一代之興，創守中興之賢聖祖孫相紹，盛德大業宜無有不一者。如成湯建中，高宗協德，文武受命，宣王中興，其德業相望者可徵矣。自漢以下，光武之於高祖，豁達大度，史稱同符；憲宗之於文皇，勵精求治，庶幾貞觀，似矣。其視商周，果若是班乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇建華夏，功德之盛，誠有以軼殷周而陋漢唐矣。迨我皇上晉臨區宇，懋昭大德，並隆治功，丕顯丕承，猗歟休哉！顧其間致治之迹，雖不能以皆同，然亦有默契焉者。本諸身而達之家國天下，不知凡幾。其大且著者，昭如日月，則天下臣民之所共仰也，可得聞歟？仰惟至德至治，宜無待仰賛一詞，而臣子愛
translation_en:
Fifth Question
The question asks: The sages of earlier and later ages followed the same standard. How much more should this hold within a single dynasty, where worthy and sagely ancestors and descendants succeed one another in founding, maintaining, and restoring its rule? Their abundant virtue and great achievements ought surely to be at one. Thus Cheng Tang established the mean, Gaozong brought his virtue into accord with it, Wen and Wu received Heaven’s mandate, and King Xuan restored the dynasty. Evidence attests to the correspondence between their virtues and achievements.
From the Han onward, the histories describe Guangwu and Gaozu as matching one another in open-mindedness and magnanimity. Xianzong, in relation to Emperor Wen of the Tang, exerted himself in pursuit of good government and came close to the achievements of the Zhenguan reign: here too there seems to have been a likeness. Yet, when compared with the Shang and Zhou, were they truly of the same rank?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao founded his rule over the Chinese realm. The magnificence of his achievements and virtue truly surpassed the Yin and Zhou and made the Han and Tang appear paltry. Now our reigning Emperor has ascended to rule the realm, splendidly manifesting great virtue and bringing the achievements of government to equal heights. Gloriously he reveals and carries forward his inheritance. Ah, how excellent!
Yet although their methods of bringing about good government cannot all have been identical, there are points of unspoken accord between them. Who knows how many instances there are of principles rooted in their own persons and extended to the family, the state, and all under Heaven? The greatest and most conspicuous shine like the sun and moon and are revered alike by all officials and people throughout the realm. May we hear an account of them?
We reverently consider that supreme virtue and supreme government should have no need of even a word of praise from below; yet the love that subjects bear …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
君之誠尤有不能自已者不知我
太祖聖神功化之極可爲
今日中興萬一之助者何歟諸士子躬逢其
盛鋪張揚厲之下必有先得我心之所
同然者願備陳之以共效芹曝之獻
問古樂之作可以感神人移風俗世之君
子嘗究心焉試舉其槩與諸士商之粤
自易象豫雷書命后夔樂作敎興邃矣
大矣然音起於聲而調於均均之調爲
===
難於是古樂遂廢而其說固在也觀諸
大司樂掌成均之灋以樂德樂語樂舞
敎國子而和之以六律六同之聲音伶
州鳩亦謂古之神瞽考中聲而量之以
制度律均鍾因幷著六律六閒之名義
而中聲之說世尤宗焉何歟自漢以下
類多作者惟蔡元定律呂新書明白淵
深縝密通暢諸儒莫及而元定又謂律
呂之器不可復見然古人制樂之意則
punctuated:
君之誠，尤有不能自已者。不知我太祖聖神功化之極，可爲今日中興萬一之助者何歟？諸士子躬逢其盛，鋪張揚厲之下，必有先得我心之所同然者，願備陳之，以共效芹曝之獻。
問：古樂之作，可以感神人，移風俗，世之君子嘗究心焉。試舉其槩，與諸士商之。粤自易象豫雷，書命后夔，樂作敎興，邃矣，大矣！然音起於聲，而調於均，均之調爲難。於是古樂遂廢，而其說固在也。觀諸大司樂掌成均之灋，以樂德、樂語、樂舞敎國子，而和之以六律六同之聲音。伶州鳩亦謂古之神瞽考中聲而量之以制，度律均鍾，因幷著六律六閒之名義，而中聲之說，世尤宗焉，何歟？自漢以下，類多作者，惟蔡元定《律呂新書》明白淵深，縝密通暢，諸儒莫及。而元定又謂律呂之器不可復見，然古人制樂之意則
translation_en:
…their sincere devotion to their ruler is especially something they cannot restrain. Which aspects of the consummate achievements and transforming influence of our sagely and divine Taizu might offer even the slightest assistance to the present restoration? You candidates have personally encountered this flourishing age. In your expansive celebration of its glories, there must be insights that anticipate what we alike recognize in our hearts. Please set them forth fully, so that together we may offer our humble contributions, like gifts of celery and the sun’s warmth.
Question: The creation of ancient music could move spirits and human beings and transform customs. Gentlemen throughout the ages have devoted thought to this. Let us outline its essentials and discuss them with you candidates. From the thunder in the image of the hexagram Yu in the Book of Changes, and the appointment of Hou Kui in the Book of Documents, the creation of music and the development of instruction have been profound and momentous indeed! Yet musical tones arise from sounds and are harmonized through pitch standards; bringing those standards into harmony is difficult. Thus ancient music eventually fell into disuse, although its theories certainly survive. Consider how the Director of Music administered the regulations of the Chengjun school, teaching the sons of the state through musical virtues, musical speech, and musical dances, and harmonizing them through the sounds of the six yang pitch standards and six yin pitch standards. Ling Zhoujiu also said that the divinely skilled blind musicians of antiquity examined the central tone and measured it to establish standards, calibrating pitch pipes and tuning bells. He also set forth the names and meanings of the six pitch standards and the six intervening pitches. Why has the theory of the central tone been particularly revered by later generations? From the Han onward, many have written on such matters. Yet Cai Yuanding’s New Book on Pitch Standards (Lülü xinshu), lucid and profound, meticulous and coherent, was beyond the achievement of other scholars. Yuanding nevertheless also said that the instruments embodying these pitch standards could no longer be seen again, but that the intentions of the ancients in establishing music …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
猶可考其詳可得聞歟玆欲上窮作樂
之本下達樂制之宜推其異而合之同
舉其粗而會之精不泥於形器而能深
契作者之意以成一代之制如之何則
可
問古帝王當治平之時恒以閱武爲重乆
安長治良必由之是故大司馬四時各
有所敎名各不同義亦迥異且一歲之
間王再臨焉而幷及蒐狩何歟漢唐宋
===
立國代有其制軍儀詡然載在史冊班
班可考于時嗣君遵而行之有講武于
平樂于驪山于近郊于東武者雖優劣
不同要皆足以作將士之氣懾華夷之
心非以好大而窮黷也我
國家經制大備悉倣諸古維是大閱之儀尚
少遺焉豈有待哉邇者殘胡豨突本兵
旰食諸臣論列蓋亦廣矣何將士驕惰
邊務縱弛猶夫昔也議者謂宜稽古制
punctuated:
猶可考。其詳可得聞歟？玆欲上窮作樂之本，下達樂制之宜，推其異而合之同，舉其粗而會之精，不泥於形器而能深契作者之意，以成一代之制，如之何則可？

問：古帝王當治平之時，恒以閱武爲重，乆安長治良必由之。是故大司馬四時各有所敎，名各不同，義亦迥異。且一歲之間，王再臨焉，而幷及蒐狩，何歟？漢唐宋立國，代有其制，軍儀詡然，載在史冊，班班可考。于時嗣君遵而行之，有講武于平樂、于驪山、于近郊、于東武者。雖優劣不同，要皆足以作將士之氣，懾華夷之心，非以好大而窮黷也。我國家經制大備，悉倣諸古，維是大閱之儀尚少遺焉，豈有待哉？邇者殘胡豨突，本兵旰食，諸臣論列蓋亦廣矣。何將士驕惰，邊務縱弛，猶夫昔也？議者謂宜稽古制
translation_en:
…can still be investigated. May we hear the details? We now wish to probe upward to the foundations of creating music and extend downward to the proper arrangements of musical institutions; to trace their differences and reconcile them in unity, and to take their broad outlines and bring them together in their essential subtleties. How can we avoid being confined to material forms and instruments, deeply comprehend the intentions of those who created music, and thereby establish a system for our dynasty?

Question: When the emperors and kings of antiquity enjoyed orderly and peaceful rule, they invariably attached great importance to military reviews. Lasting peace and enduring order surely depended upon them. Thus the Grand Marshal provided different instruction in each of the four seasons: the names differed, and their meanings were also quite distinct. Moreover, within a single year the king attended twice, and these occasions also included the spring and winter hunts. Why was this? When the Han, Tang, and Song established their states, each dynasty had its own system. Their imposing military ceremonies [?] are recorded in the histories and can be examined in detail. Successive rulers followed these practices, conducting military exercises at Pingle, Lishan, the nearby suburbs, and Dongwu. Although these varied in quality, all were sufficient to rouse the spirits of officers and soldiers and inspire awe among Chinese and non-Chinese alike. They were not undertaken out of a taste for grandeur or a desire to exhaust resources through reckless warfare. Our dynasty’s established institutions are comprehensive, all modeled on antiquity. Yet the ceremonial arrangements for the grand military review remain somewhat incomplete. Could they be awaiting something? Recently, the remnant northern invaders have charged in like wild boars, and the Minister of War has had to postpone his meals until late in the day. The various officials have also discussed and submitted proposals on these matters extensively. Why, then, are officers and soldiers still arrogant and indolent, and frontier affairs still lax and neglected, just as before? Those offering counsel say that we should examine the ancient institutions…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而作六師則轉移之機有不令而從者
果然歟抑别有鼓舞駕馭之術安邊固
圉之策歟諸士子抱藝而來必有識時
務賛
廟謨者試陳之毋讓
問能自得師學者事也古之君子言道德
則孔孟言功業則伊周宋人乃曰立志
以明道希文自期待何歟且自宋祖開
基天象兆祥英賢輩出有沉潛體道者
===
有剛毅自立者有明睿燭幾者有誠篤
憤悱者其道德豈不足多或者獨以孟
子之後一人稱明道者豈無謂歟無亦
以其所賦之美所學之正徵諸處已接
人事君澤物者知其中之所存果有大
過人歟慶曆以後名臣接踵有豐功偉
量者有清忠粹德者有抗論虜庭者有
文章擅名者其功業豈不足尚或者惟
以第一流人物稱希文者抑獨何歟無
punctuated:
而作六師，則轉移之機有不令而從者，果然歟？抑别有鼓舞駕馭之術、安邊固圉之策歟？諸士子抱藝而來，必有識時務、賛廟謨者，試陳之，毋讓。
問：能自得師，學者事也。古之君子，言道德則孔孟，言功業則伊周。宋人乃曰：「立志以明道、希文自期待。」何歟？且自宋祖開基，天象兆祥，英賢輩出，有沉潛體道者，有剛毅自立者，有明睿燭幾者，有誠篤憤悱者，其道德豈不足多？或者獨以孟子之後一人稱明道者，豈無謂歟？無亦以其所賦之美、所學之正，徵諸處已接人、事君澤物者，知其中之所存果有大過人歟？慶曆以後，名臣接踵，有豐功偉量者，有清忠粹德者，有抗論虜庭者，有文章擅名者，其功業豈不足尚？或者惟以第一流人物稱希文者，抑獨何歟？無
translation_en:
…and rouse the Six Armies, would this bring about a change whereby they obeyed without being ordered? Is this indeed so? Or are there other methods of inspiring and directing them, other policies for securing the frontier and strengthening its defenses? You candidates have come equipped with your learning; surely some among you understand the affairs of the time and can contribute to the court’s deliberations. Set forth your views without reserve.
Question: Finding a teacher for oneself is the business of a learner. Among the gentlemen of antiquity, when discussing moral virtue one looked to Kongzi and Mengzi; when discussing achievements in government, to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. Yet a man of the Song said, “In setting your aspirations, expect of yourself what Mingdao and Xiwen achieved.” Why was this? From the time the Song founder established the dynasty, celestial signs heralded auspicious fortune, and outstanding worthies emerged in succession. Some quietly immersed themselves in embodying the Way; some established themselves with firmness and resolve; some possessed the clarity and insight to discern the first stirrings of events; and some were sincere and earnest, striving to understand and give expression to their understanding. Was their moral virtue not worthy of abundant praise? Yet some singled out Mingdao (Cheng Hao) as the one man since Mengzi. Surely this judgment had a reason? Might it be that, examining the excellence of his natural endowments and the correctness of his learning as manifested in his personal conduct, dealings with others, service to his ruler, and beneficence toward all things, they recognized that what he held within truly far surpassed other men?
After the Qingli era, eminent ministers followed one another in succession. Some possessed great achievements and extraordinary magnanimity; some were incorruptible and loyal, with unalloyed virtue; some argued fearlessly at foreign courts; and some won renown for their literary compositions. Were their achievements not worthy of esteem? Yet some reserved the designation “a figure of the very first rank” for Xiwen (Fan Zhongyan). Why single him out? Could it be …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
乃卽其直亮之節仁明之才發諸匡時
濟世知人料敵者驗其志之所向果非
尋常可及歟今明道希文之所以自待
與諸賢門人之所以稱之者固在也豈
皆無可議歟然志士尚友惟以是爲的
歟抑將進於是歟今之學者類能談道
德功業以聖賢自期其於體用本末視
二子果能兼舉否歟愛其人故得其行
事之詳況願學如明道希文者乎盍各
===
言之以觀諸士子之志
問滇古黔中之地靡莫哀牢之屬也自南
詔啓土中國人士多流寓焉逮我
太祖取而郡縣之揆文奮武休養生息以迄于
今其山河之固人材之盛固足以防患
而飾治矣然散處之民尚有可虞黌序
之建尚多未備議者謂宜設險以衛民
生明教以興民德然歟滇有故城
國初又爲增築諸城往日草竊之生或恃有
punctuated:
乃卽其直亮之節、仁明之才，發諸匡時濟世、知人料敵者，驗其志之所向，果非尋常可及歟？今明道、希文之所以自待，與諸賢門人之所以稱之者，固在也，豈皆無可議歟？然志士尚友，惟以是爲的歟？抑將進於是歟？今之學者類能談道德功業，以聖賢自期，其於體用本末，視二子果能兼舉否歟？愛其人，故得其行事之詳，況願學如明道、希文者乎？盍各言之，以觀諸士子之志？
問：滇，古黔中之地，靡莫、哀牢之屬也。自南詔啓土，中國人士多流寓焉。逮我太祖取而郡縣之，揆文奮武，休養生息，以迄于今，其山河之固、人材之盛，固足以防患而飾治矣。然散處之民尚有可虞，黌序之建尚多未備。議者謂宜設險以衛民生，明教以興民德，然歟？滇有故城，國初又爲增築諸城，往日草竊之生，或恃有
translation_en:
…might it be that, from his integrity and forthrightness, his benevolence and discernment, manifested in setting the age aright and aiding the world, judging men and assessing enemies, they discerned that the aims of his resolve were indeed beyond the reach of ordinary men? Now, the standards Mingdao and Xiwen set for themselves, and the grounds on which the worthy men and their disciples praised them, are certainly on record. Is there nothing in any of these open to discussion? When men of aspiration seek friendship with the worthies of the past, should they take these alone as their goal? Or should they advance beyond them? Scholars today can generally discuss moral virtue and achievement, and aspire to become sages and worthies. Yet, compared with these two men, can they truly embrace both substance and function, root and branch? Affection for a man leads one to learn the details of his conduct; how much more should this be true of those who wish to learn to be like Mingdao and Xiwen? Let each of you explain, so that we may discern your aspirations.
Question: Dian was the ancient territory of Qianzhong, belonging to such peoples as the Mimo and Ailao. From the time Nanzhao established its domain, many men of the Central Lands sojourned and settled there. When our Taizu took it and organized it into prefectures and counties, he directed civil affairs and exerted military power, allowing the people to recuperate and prosper. Down to the present, its natural defenses of mountains and rivers and its abundance of talent have surely sufficed to ward off trouble and enhance good government. Yet there remain grounds for concern about the people living in scattered settlements, and the provision of schools is still incomplete in many places. Some maintain that defensive barriers should be established to protect the people's livelihood, and moral instruction made clear to foster their virtue. Is this so? Dian had existing walled towns, and at the beginning of our dynasty additional town walls were built. When bandits arose in former days, some relied on having …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
城而無恐或以無城而大被荼毒者故
鑑此請城鶴慶是已然宜城者豈獨鶴
慶已乎舍近而圖遠均之未爲衞也滇
舊有學
國初又爲增建諸學近日人材之出或以有
學而益盛或以無學而日就荒落者故
緣此請建馬龍諸學是已然宜建者豈
獨馬龍已乎舉彼而遺此猶之未爲興
也或又有勞民費財徒設無益之譏何
===
歟將事有重且大者宜不計小費不恤
浮言歟諸士子生長茲土平居相與得
諸輿人之誦審矣願計其便
punctuated: 城而無恐，或以無城而大被荼毒者。故鑑此請城鶴慶，是已。然宜城者豈獨鶴慶已乎？舍近而圖遠，均之未爲衞也。滇舊有學，國初又爲增建諸學。近日人材之出，或以有學而益盛，或以無學而日就荒落者。故緣此請建馬龍諸學，是已。然宜建者豈獨馬龍已乎？舉彼而遺此，猶之未爲興也。或又有勞民費財、徒設無益之譏，何歟？將事有重且大者，宜不計小費，不恤浮言歟？諸士子生長茲土，平居相與得諸輿人之誦審矣，願計其便。
translation_en: …walls and thus had no fear, while others, lacking walls, suffered grievous devastation. In light of this, the proposal to build walls around Heqing is sound. Yet is Heqing alone in need of walls? To neglect nearby places while making plans for distant ones is equally a failure to provide protection. Yunnan had schools in former times, and at the beginning of the dynasty further schools were established. In recent years, some places have produced ever more men of talent because they have schools, while others, lacking schools, have fallen into increasing neglect and decline. Accordingly, the proposal to establish schools in Malong and other places is sound. Yet is Malong alone in need of a school? To promote one place while overlooking another is likewise a failure to foster learning. Some, however, criticize these undertakings as burdening the people and wasting resources, creating institutions that serve no useful purpose. Why is this? Or, when an undertaking is weighty and important, should one disregard minor expenses and pay no heed to idle criticism? You candidates were born and raised in this land; in your everyday dealings with one another, you have gained a thorough understanding of what the people are saying. I ask you to consider what measures would be advantageous.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
孔子曰君子有九思視思明聽思聰色思
温貌思恭言思忠事思敬疑思問忿思
難見得思義
石雷
同考試官教諭莫批約而達雅而健結復合九
思為一蓋有得於本原者錄之
考試官教諭彭批精當
===
考試官教諭朱批整潔
聖人論君子慎思之學皆求得乎理而已夫理
無不在而思則得之也君子之所思者何往而
非求得其理哉夫子欲學者之求諸心也故其
言曰心主乎一身而其體足以管乎衆理理散
於天下而其妙不外乎一心人惟未之思也則
心學荒而離道遠矣君子隨事窮理已豫夫致
知之功觀物察則罔忽於物交之感其有感而
思者大凡有九焉何則目以司視耳以司聽聰
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

孔子曰：「君子有九思：視思明，聽思聰，色思温，貌思恭，言思忠，事思敬，疑思問，忿思難，見得思義。」

石雷

同考試官教諭莫批：「約而達，雅而健，結復合九思為一，蓋有得於本原者，錄之。」

考試官教諭彭批：「精當。」

考試官教諭朱批：「整潔。」

聖人論君子慎思之學，皆求得乎理而已。夫理無不在，而思則得之也。君子之所思者，何往而非求得其理哉？夫子欲學者之求諸心也，故其言曰：心主乎一身，而其體足以管乎衆理；理散於天下，而其妙不外乎一心。人惟未之思也，則心學荒而離道遠矣。君子隨事窮理，已豫夫致知之功；觀物察則，罔忽於物交之感。其有感而思者，大凡有九焉。何則？目以司視，耳以司聽，聰
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Confucius said: “The gentleman has nine considerations: when looking, he considers how to see clearly; when listening, how to hear distinctly; in his expression, how to be amiable; in his bearing, how to be respectful; in speaking, how to be sincere; in conducting affairs, how to be reverent; when in doubt, how to inquire; when angry, what troubles may follow; and when seeing an opportunity for gain, what is right.”

Shi Lei

Comment by Associate Examiner Mo, Instructor: “Concise yet expressive, elegant yet vigorous. The conclusion reunites the nine considerations as one. This is evidently someone who has grasped their fundamental source. Select it for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: “Precise and apt.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Orderly and polished.”

When the Sage discusses the gentleman’s learning through careful reflection, it is entirely a matter of seeking to apprehend principle. Principle is present everywhere, and through reflection one apprehends it. Wherever the gentleman directs his thoughts, is he not seeking to apprehend the principle involved? The Master wished learners to seek it within their own minds; hence his words mean: the mind governs the entire person, and its constitution is sufficient to encompass all principles. Principle is dispersed throughout the world, yet its subtle workings do not extend beyond the single mind. It is only because people fail to reflect upon it that the learning of the mind falls into neglect and they become distant from the Way. The gentleman investigates principle in each affair, already undertaking the work of extending knowledge. He observes things and examines their governing patterns, neglecting none of the responses elicited by encounters with things. Broadly speaking, there are nine circumstances in which he responds and reflects. Why is this? The eyes govern seeing, and the ears govern hearing. Acuity of hearing…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
明者乃其德之懿也君子則思其作哲思其作
謀而聰明適得吾體焉耳色見於面貌動乎容
温恭者固其則之嘉也君子則思其可親思其
可象而温恭不失吾常焉耳言不忠事不敬弗
可行也君子必慮其終而思忠焉稽其敝而思
敬焉蓋於言行無所苟而已矣疑不問忿不懲
將益滋也君子必思問以解其惑焉思難而平
其氣焉蓋於私意無所留而已矣見得則利心
生焉人之恒也君子則以取與之未審恐性分
===
之有累如其義焉斯受之矣非其義也肯貨取
乎吁君子可謂善事其心者矣玆其非夫人之
可及也與雖然君子之學分而言之固有九思
合而言之實一理而已苟無得於大本大原之
所在徒欲因事而思逐物而會則其心益病其
思益鑿其學無統矣然則將廢思乎曰居敬以
立其本主靜以致其功則思作睿睿作聖無思
而無不通矣其善學哉
可以贊天地之化育則可以與天地參矣
punctuated:
明者乃其德之懿也。君子則思其作哲，思其作謀，而聰明適得吾體焉耳。色見於面，貌動乎容，温恭者固其則之嘉也。君子則思其可親，思其可象，而温恭不失吾常焉耳。言不忠，事不敬，弗可行也。君子必慮其終而思忠焉，稽其敝而思敬焉，蓋於言行無所苟而已矣。疑不問，忿不懲，將益滋也。君子必思問以解其惑焉，思難而平其氣焉，蓋於私意無所留而已矣。見得則利心生焉，人之恒也。君子則以取與之未審，恐性分之有累。如其義焉，斯受之矣；非其義也，肯貨取乎？吁！君子可謂善事其心者矣。玆其非夫人之可及也與！雖然，君子之學，分而言之，固有九思；合而言之，實一理而已。苟無得於大本大原之所在，徒欲因事而思，逐物而會，則其心益病，其思益鑿，其學無統矣。然則將廢思乎？曰：居敬以立其本，主靜以致其功，則思作睿，睿作聖，無思而無不通矣。其善學哉！

可以贊天地之化育，則可以與天地參矣。
translation_en:
…clarity is an excellence of these faculties. The gentleman therefore considers how sight may yield discernment and hearing may yield sound judgment, so that acuity of hearing and clarity of vision properly fulfill their inherent capacities in him. Expression appears in the face, and demeanor manifests itself in bearing; warmth and respect are indeed the admirable standards for them. The gentleman considers how his expression may invite approach and how his demeanor may serve as an example, so that warmth and respect remain his constant qualities. Speech without sincerity and conduct without reverence are unacceptable. The gentleman must consider the outcome of his words and think of sincerity; he must examine the failings to which his actions are liable and think of reverence. This simply means allowing no carelessness in speech or conduct. Doubts left unquestioned and anger left unchecked will only grow. The gentleman must think of asking questions to resolve his perplexities, and think of the troubles anger may bring so as to calm his temper. This simply means allowing no selfish intentions to linger. When an opportunity for gain appears, the desire for profit arises: this is common human behavior. The gentleman, however, fears that insufficient scrutiny of taking and giving may compromise his moral nature. If accepting something accords with righteousness, he accepts it; if it does not, would he take it for material gain [?]? Ah! The gentleman may indeed be called one who serves his own mind well. Surely this is beyond the reach of ordinary people!

Nevertheless, considered separately, the gentleman’s learning indeed comprises nine considerations; considered together, it is truly nothing more than a single principle. If one has no grasp of where the great foundation and ultimate source lie, but merely seeks to think in response to affairs and pursue understanding by chasing after things, the mind becomes increasingly afflicted, thought increasingly forced, and learning loses its unifying thread. Should one then abandon thought? The answer is: maintain reverence to establish the foundation, and make stillness central to bring the work to fruition. Then thought produces sagacity, and sagacity produces sagehood: without deliberate thought, there is nothing one does not comprehend. How well such a person learns!

“Being able to assist the transforming and nourishing activity of Heaven and Earth, one can then stand as a third alongside Heaven and Earth.”

translation_en:
Lan Zhuo 蘭𣵠.

Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “In discussing participation in and assistance to Heaven and Earth, his understanding is intimate and exact. His literary conception is fresh [?], and his organizing approach differs markedly from ordinary compositions. Is he not truly a scholar who has penetrated principle and attained understanding? He certainly deserves a high recommendation.”

Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: “Clear and clean.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Pure and precise.”

The sage brings the capacities of Heaven and Earth to fulfillment and thereby establishes his position between them. To assist their transforming and nourishing activity and stand alongside Heaven and Earth—nothing can surpass the grandeur of this achievement. Unless one possesses utmost sincerity and fully realizes the nature of things, who could participate in this? It is fitting that the Doctrine of the Mean invokes this to illuminate the Way of Heaven. Its meaning is that human beings are born standing between Heaven and Earth. At the beginning, when they inherit goodness, they share their substance; at the culmination of numinous transformation, they indeed share their work. Never have they failed to correspond to them. Once fettered by selfishness and obstructed in their transformation, however, they depart very far from them.

Those of utmost sincerity fully realize their own nature together with the natures of other people and things. Thus the common people dwell in harmony, and all things accord with their proper order. Their great undertaking shines without limit, and supreme harmony pervades everything without a gap. Heaven and Earth take generation and completion as their virtue, yet are deficient in governance and thus cannot entirely avoid being partial. Only after the sage fully carries out the work of shaping and completing does transformation and nourishment achieve its full effect. Thus Heaven and Earth provide the beginning, while the means of bringing their work to completion on their behalf resides in the sage. Is this not using what he can accomplish to assist with what they cannot accomplish?

Qian and Kun exercise their capacities through ease and simplicity, yet, constrained by their respective allotted roles, they still seem to await something. translation_en:
…it is Heaven and Earth that initiate the incipient workings; yet it rests with the sage to carry out their work on their behalf. Is this not to use what he can do to assist them in what they cannot? Such is the way utmost sincerity assists their transforming and nourishing activity. Although it is said that no models are greater than Heaven and Earth, the sage differs from them in form while sharing their substance: therein lies the principle of resemblance. He differs from them in physical constitution while sharing their spiritual efficacy: therein the Way of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—is complete. Qian is called father, and Kun is called mother. The sage takes being father and mother to all under Heaven as the kingly Way, and thus has the means to stand at the center of the world. Heaven occupies its position above, and Earth its position below. Through ease and simplicity, the sage grasps the principles of all under Heaven and can establish his position between them. If so, Heaven and Earth cannot be called greater, nor the sage lesser. What does he lack that would prevent him from standing alongside them as a third? Why is this? Only by fully realizing one's nature and reaching what Heaven has ordained does one's efficacy become complete; those unable to fulfill what their bodily form embodies have no means of becoming their counterpart. Otherwise, the sage is merely of the same kind as ordinary people: how could he stand foremost and be uniquely preeminent?

I have examined this in the Book of Changes, which says, “In Return, do we not see the heart of Heaven and Earth?” It also says, “Thunder moves beneath Heaven; all things participate in freedom from falsity.” Thus every human being embodies a Heaven and Earth. Only the sage fully realizes human relationships; only the true king fully establishes institutions. Could they add anything to what is inherent in their nature? Thus fully realizing one's nature is precisely bringing equilibrium and harmony to their utmost; standing alongside Heaven and Earth and assisting them means precisely that they take their proper positions and all things are nourished. If learners return before straying far from this and emulate the benevolence with which the former kings amply responded to Heaven, they may hope to become counterparts of Heaven and Earth. But those who wish to discuss ritual and music and speak of ordering the world without investigating human nature and Heaven's mandate concern themselves with mere peripheral matters. How could they be fit to discuss the Way of standing alongside Heaven and Earth and assisting them?

As for hereditary stipends, Teng has certainly already put them into practice. The Book of Odes says, “Rain upon our public fields, and then reach…”

The great worthy enlightened the ruler of Teng about the need to implement the labor-assistance system, and thereby showed him that moral instruction must command his attention. Hereditary stipends depend upon the labor-assistance system, and moral instruction flourishes amid material sufficiency. Examining antiquity and testing it against the present, is not the way of government plainly visible? It was fitting that Mencius should use this to enlighten Duke Wen of Teng. His meaning was that, for the people, making a livelihood and cultivating virtue are inherently linked in principle and cannot be separated; for the ruler, enriching and instructing the people are mutually complementary ways of governing, neither of which may be neglected. Thus, in regulating holdings and levying contributions from the people, truly nothing surpasses the labor-assistance system. 獨所未舉則取民無制豈王政之本乎體國經

可阜矣養之有素則民行可興矣設為庠序學

===

性牖民使其帝則之必察夫惟教隆於上而五

原諸性善而必稱堯舜論治惟重教養而必徵

punctuated: 定焉。自今觀之，世禄之法，滕固已行之矣；助法獨所未舉，則取民無制，豈王政之本乎？體國經野，吾且有徵於周矣。《詩》云：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」然惟助為有公田，而上下之分辨焉。由此觀之，助法之善，雖周亦行之矣；滕獨在所不講，則憲章未備，豈法祖之治乎？誠能取之有道，則民生可阜矣；養之有素，則民行可興矣。設為庠序學校，所以教之也。綱維制度，豈無所於稽邪？庠取諸養，校取諸教，序取諸射，鄉學之建，義各有攸當也。夏則曰校，殷則曰序，周則曰庠，國學之崇，名則其所同也。縁道立教，一皆人倫之是明；因性牖民，使其帝則之必察。夫惟教隆於上，而五品遜焉，有以昭率乂於大公；由是俗美於下，而百姓親焉，有以成雍睦於大順。正德厚生，畢遂其願，為國之道，不外此而得之矣。滕君尚知所力行也哉！抑可見孟子之學，識其大者焉。論學原諸性善，而必稱堯舜；論治惟重教養，而必徵諸三代之盛王。豈以滕文果足與有為，而告之
translation_en:
…are thereby settled. Viewed from the present, Teng has indeed already implemented hereditary stipends. Only the assistance system remains unimplemented; thus, exactions from the people lack a fixed standard. Can this be the foundation of kingly government? For organizing the capital and laying out the countryside, I can moreover find evidence in the Zhou. The Book of Odes says: “Rain upon our public fields, and then reach our private fields.” Only the assistance system has public fields, through which the respective shares of ruler and people are distinguished. Viewed in this light, the assistance system is so beneficial that even the Zhou practiced it. If Teng alone leaves it unexamined, its institutions remain incomplete. Can this be government modeled on the ancestors? If what is taken from the people truly accords with the proper Way, their livelihoods can flourish; if their sustenance is regularly provided for, their conduct can improve.

Establishing xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools is the means of educating them. Can there be no precedents to consult for their organization and institutions? Xiang takes its meaning from nourishing, xiao from teaching, and xu from archery: each type of local school has its appropriate significance. Under the Xia they were called xiao, under the Yin xu, and under the Zhou xiang; as for the schools established in the capital, all shared the name xue. Education is established in accordance with the Way, entirely to illuminate human relationships. The people are enlightened in accordance with their nature, so that they will assuredly discern Heaven’s standards. When education flourishes above, the five human relationships become harmonious, making it possible to manifest obedience and good order in complete impartiality. Consequently, customs improve below and the people become affectionate toward one another, bringing concord and amity to fulfillment in perfect harmony. Their virtue is rectified and their livelihoods enriched, and all their aspirations are fulfilled. The Way of governing a state is attained without going beyond this. May the ruler of Teng recognize what he should strive to put into practice!

Here, moreover, we can see that Mencius’s learning grasped what was fundamental. In discussing learning, he traced it to the goodness of human nature and invariably cited Yao and Shun; in discussing government, he emphasized education and nourishment and invariably adduced the illustrious kings of the Three Dynasties. Could it have been because Duke Wen of Teng was indeed capable of accomplishing something with him that he told him…

文言闡坤德極其順而健也夫柔靜者坤之順
剛方則健矣順而健坤德其至矣哉夫子文言
釋牝馬之貞意謂天下之言坤者則順而已矣
孰知其有不倚於順者乎試以貞言之是故應
乾從事居後爲得而無所於擅夫坤可謂至柔
也已至柔若不足於剛矣然承天以爲動也氣
閉而卽藏大化不愆其期道斂而卽歸成物不
失其令翕然闔者其機也浩然成者其勢也舉
punctuated:
以是，以廣其所未聞也乎？噫！此帝德之盛，王道之全也，雖謂爲萬世立準焉可也。故先儒謂孟子之學識其大。

易
文言曰：「坤至柔而動也剛，至靜而德方。」
湯憲

同考試官教諭羅批：講柔剛靜方處，辭不繁而意自足，子其深於易者邪？
考試官教諭彭批：理趣深長，筆力精健。
考試官教諭朱批：脫去陳言，當是作者。

文言闡坤德，極其順而健也。夫柔靜者，坤之順；剛方則健矣。順而健，坤德其至矣哉！夫子文言釋牝馬之貞，意謂天下之言坤者，則順而已矣，孰知其有不倚於順者乎？試以貞言之。是故應乾從事，居後爲得，而無所於擅，夫坤可謂至柔也已。至柔若不足於剛矣，然承天以爲動也，氣閉而卽藏，大化不愆其期；道斂而卽歸，成物不失其令。翕然闔者，其機也；浩然成者，其勢也。舉
translation_en:
…with this, to broaden what he had not yet heard? Ah! This is the fullness of imperial virtue and the completeness of the kingly Way. One may indeed say that it establishes a standard for all ages. Thus earlier Confucian scholars said that Mencius’s learning grasped what was fundamental.

Book of Changes
The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) says: “Kun is supremely yielding, yet firm in its movement; supremely still, yet square in its virtue.”
Tang Xian

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: “In explaining yielding and firmness, stillness and squareness, the language is economical yet the meaning fully conveyed. Are you perhaps one who has a profound understanding of the Changes?”
Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: “The implications of the principles are profound and far-reaching; the writing is refined and vigorous.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Free of hackneyed expressions: surely the work of an accomplished writer.”

The Commentary on the Words of the Text elucidates Kun’s virtue, bringing out to the fullest its compliance and strength. Yielding and stillness constitute Kun’s compliance; firmness and squareness constitute its strength. Compliant yet strong—how consummate is Kun’s virtue! In the Commentary on the Words of the Text, the Master explains the constancy of the mare. His meaning is that people everywhere who speak of Kun speak only of compliance. Who recognizes that it possesses something that does not rest upon compliance alone? Let us discuss this in terms of constancy. Thus, Kun responds to Qian and follows it in action, finding its proper place in coming after and presuming to act independently in nothing. Kun may indeed be called supremely yielding. Supreme yielding might seem deficient in firmness. Yet Kun moves in obedience to Heaven: when the vital breath closes in, it immediately stores it away, and the great transformation never misses its appointed time; when the Way contracts, it immediately returns, and the completion of things never misses its season. Closing tightly is its inner working; bringing things to completion on a vast scale is its momentum. Throughout…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天下莫之能撓而亦莫之能禦也何剛如之夫
柔與剛本相悖也動焉而剛豈坤之戾其常哉
蓋柔之一者乃所以爲剛否則爲懦弱而不振
矣何以言天下之至柔也故柔不足以盡坤柔
而剛焉斯其至矣神功收斂機緘不露而無所
於擾夫坤可謂至靜也已至靜若不足於方矣
然生物以爲德也萬一各正不顯其致役之勞
大小有定咸囿於代終之化羣而分者物也區
以別者類也亘古今莫之有改而亦莫之或紊
===
也何方如之夫靜與方非一致也靜焉而方豈
坤之過其則哉蓋靜之極者乃所以爲方否則
爲雜亂而不恒矣何以言天下之至靜也故靜
不足以盡坤靜而方焉斯其至矣用是而觀柔
以爲剛剛非外於柔也靜以爲方方非外於靜
也靜柔而剛方以寓坤之道貞夫一而已矣抑
天之陰陽也地之柔剛也人之仁義也天地人
之至理也奈何夫人失之於動也擾之於靜也
六鑿攘而三極荒至德孤而大道隱始與天地
punctuated: 天下莫之能撓，而亦莫之能禦也，何剛如之！夫柔與剛本相悖也，動焉而剛，豈坤之戾其常哉？蓋柔之一者，乃所以爲剛，否則爲懦弱而不振矣，何以言天下之至柔也？故柔不足以盡坤，柔而剛焉，斯其至矣。神功收斂，機緘不露，而無所於擾，夫坤可謂至靜也已。至靜若不足於方矣，然生物以爲德也，萬一各正，不顯其致役之勞；大小有定，咸囿於代終之化。羣而分者，物也；區以別者，類也。亘古今莫之有改，而亦莫之或紊也，何方如之！夫靜與方非一致也，靜焉而方，豈坤之過其則哉？蓋靜之極者，乃所以爲方，否則爲雜亂而不恒矣，何以言天下之至靜也？故靜不足以盡坤，靜而方焉，斯其至矣。用是而觀，柔以爲剛，剛非外於柔也；靜以爲方，方非外於靜也。靜柔而剛方以寓，坤之道貞夫一而已矣。抑天之陰陽也，地之柔剛也，人之仁義也，天地人之至理也。奈何夫人失之於動也，擾之於靜也？六鑿攘而三極荒，至德孤而大道隱，始與天地
translation_en:
… nothing in all the world can bend it, nor can anything withstand it. What firmness could equal this! Yielding and firmness are fundamentally opposed; yet when Kun acts, it is firm. Could this mean that Kun departs from its constant nature? Rather, its undivided yielding is precisely what enables it to be firm. Otherwise, it would be mere weakness, unable to rouse itself. How could one then call it the utmost yielding in the world? Thus, yielding alone does not fully describe Kun: yielding yet firm—there lies its perfection.

Its wondrous efficacy is gathered inward, its workings remain concealed, and nothing disturbs it. Kun may indeed be called utterly still. Utter stillness might seem insufficient to give it squareness, yet its virtue lies in bringing things to life. The myriad things, each and every one, attain their proper condition, without its revealing the toil of its service; great and small have their fixed places, all encompassed within the transforming activity by which it carries things to completion on Heaven’s behalf. Things form groups yet remain distinct; kinds are set apart and differentiated. Throughout antiquity and the present, nothing has altered this order, nor has anything thrown it into confusion. What squareness could equal this! Stillness and squareness are not identical; yet Kun is still and square. Could this mean that Kun exceeds its proper rule? Rather, its utmost stillness is precisely what enables it to be square. Otherwise, it would be confused and inconstant. How could one then call it the utmost stillness in the world? Thus, stillness alone does not fully describe Kun: still yet square—there lies its perfection.

Viewed in this light, yielding gives rise to firmness: firmness is not external to yielding. Stillness gives rise to squareness: squareness is not external to stillness. Within its stillness and yielding reside firmness and squareness. The Way of Kun consists simply in constancy to the one.

Furthermore, yin and yang in Heaven, yielding and firmness on Earth, and benevolence and righteousness in humanity are the ultimate principles of Heaven, Earth, and humanity. Why, then, do people lose these principles in activity and disturb them in stillness? The six bodily apertures contend, and the three ultimate principles fall into neglect; consummate virtue stands forsaken, and the Great Way becomes hidden. Only then, in relation to Heaven and Earth, do people …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不相似矣兼體而不累夫其惟聖人乎君子脩
之敬義而已矣
子曰易有聖人之道四焉者此之謂也
蘭𣸸
同考試官教諭羅批論易道而歸於聖人之神
非有得於易者不能到可以式矣
考試官教諭彭批潔淨精微僅見此作
考試官教諭朱批說理明瑩讀之令人豁然
大傳論易道歸於聖人者以易用之原於聖人
===
也蓋辭占象變易之所有者也而皆原於聖心
之神爲之則謂之聖人之道宜矣大傳歷言人
之尚易而歸功於聖人蓋曰人非易無以制其
用而易非聖人無以妙其用故爲用而不尚諸
易何以妙推行之利語易而不歸諸聖何以發
精微之蘊哉彼繫辭以盡言因變以著占是辭
也占也乃易所以開天下之物通天下之志者
也而極其精矣極數以定象化裁以爲變是象
也變也乃易所以定天下之業成天下之務者
punctuated:
不相似矣。兼體而不累，夫其惟聖人乎？君子脩之，敬義而已矣。

子曰：「易有聖人之道四焉。」者，此之謂也。

蘭𣸸

同考試官教諭羅批：論易道而歸於聖人之神，非有得於易者不能到，可以式矣。

考試官教諭彭批：潔淨精微，僅見此作。

考試官教諭朱批：說理明瑩，讀之令人豁然。

大傳論易道歸於聖人者，以易用之原於聖人也。蓋辭、占、象、變，易之所有者也，而皆原於聖心之神爲之，則謂之聖人之道宜矣。大傳歷言人之尚易而歸功於聖人，蓋曰：人非易無以制其用，而易非聖人無以妙其用。故爲用而不尚諸易，何以妙推行之利？語易而不歸諸聖，何以發精微之蘊哉？彼繫辭以盡言，因變以著占，是辭也、占也，乃易所以開天下之物、通天下之志者也，而極其精矣。極數以定象，化裁以爲變，是象也、變也，乃易所以定天下之業、成天下之務者
translation_en:
…they cease to resemble one another. To embody both without being encumbered by either—is this not possible only for the sage? The gentleman cultivates this through reverence and righteousness, and nothing more.

The Master's saying, “The Changes contains four aspects of the way of the sages,” refers to this.

Lan Tian 蘭𣸸

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: In discussing the way of the Changes, this essay traces it back to the sage's spiritual efficacy. Only someone who has gained insight into the Changes could reach this point. It may serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: Purity, refinement, and subtlety: I have seen these only in this composition.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Its exposition of principle is clear and luminous; reading it brings sudden understanding.

The Great Commentary, in discussing the way of the Changes, traces it back to the sages because the functioning of the Changes originates with them. Statements, prognostications, images, and transformations are all contained in the Changes. Yet all originate in the workings of the spiritual efficacy of the sage's mind; it is therefore fitting to call them the way of the sages. The Great Commentary enumerates the ways people esteem the Changes, but attributes the achievement to the sages. Its meaning is that without the Changes people could not regulate their practical activity, while without the sages the Changes could not function with such subtle efficacy. Thus, if in practical activity one does not esteem the Changes, how can one realize the subtle benefits of putting it into operation? If one discusses the Changes without tracing it back to the sages, how can one disclose its store of refined and subtle meaning?

Attaching statements to give full expression to meaning, and drawing on transformations to make prognostications manifest: these statements and prognostications are the means by which the Changes reveals the things of the world and gives expression to the intentions of all under Heaven, carrying its refinement to the utmost. Exhaustively exploring numbers to establish images, and adapting and shaping to produce transformations: these images and transformations are the means by which the Changes establishes the undertakings of all under Heaven and brings their affairs to completion…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也而極其變矣是四者皆變化之道神之爲也
無一而非易之蘊則無一而非易之道矣乃謂
易有聖人之道者正以辭占至精而所以精者
易不得而與也乃聖人以其至精之神而極之
也深極於聖人則聖人之精因易以示矣象變
至變而所以變者易不得而與也乃聖人以其
至變之神而研之也幾研於聖人則聖人之變
因易以發矣深以通志而其通也極天下之至
神聖人精神心術之所運也豈易之自能邪幾
===
以成務而其成也極天下之至妙聖人妙道精
義之所發也豈易之自爲邪所謂易有聖人之
道者以此此其所以爲人所尚而有功於天下
也與雖然深也幾也神也一而已矣不在易而
在吾心者也是故洗心退藏齋戒神明聖人之
心何假於物哉人惟無得於象數之外而惟滯
於形器之粗意見梏而虚靈蔽則吾心亦物而
易道隱矣乃欲假區區術數以自神如京房延
壽之爲吁易之神固如此哉
punctuated: 也，而極其變矣。是四者，皆變化之道、神之爲也。無一而非易之蘊，則無一而非易之道矣。乃謂易有聖人之道者，正以辭占至精，而所以精者，易不得而與也，乃聖人以其至精之神而極之也。深極於聖人，則聖人之精因易以示矣。象變至變，而所以變者，易不得而與也，乃聖人以其至變之神而研之也。幾研於聖人，則聖人之變因易以發矣。深以通志，而其通也，極天下之至神，聖人精神心術之所運也，豈易之自能邪？幾以成務，而其成也，極天下之至妙，聖人妙道精義之所發也，豈易之自爲邪？所謂易有聖人之道者，以此。此其所以爲人所尚，而有功於天下也與！雖然，深也、幾也、神也，一而已矣，不在易而在吾心者也。是故洗心退藏，齋戒神明，聖人之心何假於物哉？人惟無得於象數之外，而惟滯於形器之粗，意見梏而虚靈蔽，則吾心亦物，而易道隱矣。乃欲假區區術數以自神，如京房延壽之爲。吁！易之神固如此哉？
translation_en:
…and thus carry transformation to its utmost extent. These four are all the Way of change and transformation, the workings of spiritual efficacy. Since none lies outside what the Changes contains, none lies outside its Way. To say that the Changes possesses the Way of the sages is precisely to recognize that, although its statements and prognostications are supremely subtle, the Changes itself cannot take credit for what makes them so. Rather, the sages bring them to their fullest extent through their own supremely subtle spiritual efficacy. When the sages plumb the depths, their subtlety is revealed through the Changes. Its images and transformations exhibit change to the utmost, yet the Changes itself cannot take credit for what makes them change. Rather, the sages investigate them through their own supremely transformative spiritual efficacy. When the sages investigate the incipient impulses of change, their powers of transformation find expression through the Changes.

Through depth they comprehend intentions; this comprehension reaches the utmost spiritual efficacy in the world and is the operation of the sages’ vital spirit and arts of the mind. How could the Changes accomplish it by itself? Through the incipient impulses of change they accomplish affairs; this accomplishment reaches the utmost subtlety in the world and issues from the sages’ wondrous Way and refined understanding of what is right. How could the Changes bring it about by itself? This is what is meant by saying that the Changes possesses the Way of the sages. Surely this is why people esteem it and why it benefits the world!

Nevertheless, depth, incipient impulse, and spiritual efficacy are ultimately one. They reside not in the Changes but in our own minds. Thus, cleansing their minds and withdrawing into concealment, purifying themselves through fasting and abstinence to attain spiritual illumination, how could the sages’ minds depend on external things? People fail to apprehend anything beyond images and numbers and remain mired in the coarseness of physical forms and implements. Their opinions fetter them and obscure the mind’s open, spiritual awareness; our minds then become mere things, and the Way of the Changes is hidden. Yet they seek to make themselves spiritually potent by relying on petty divinatory techniques, as did Jing Fang and Yanshou. Alas! Is the spiritual efficacy of the Changes really like this?

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
書
若金用汝作礪若濟巨川用汝作舟楫若
歲大旱用汝作霖雨
石雷
同考試官教諭莫批高宗命傅說納誨屢託之
喻眞有見於相道之關君德如此是篇形容殆盡宜
錄以式
考試官教諭彭批親切
考試官教諭朱批典實
===
賢王命大臣以納誨必屢託喻以深致其望焉
夫相道之繫於君德也大矣賢王屢託喻以求
誨其望治之心不亦切乎想高宗之命傅說及
此意謂上下交而德業成君臣之相須也久矣
我之望汝納誨者何以擬諸其形容哉彼金所
以利用非礪則金無所成顧予德有未脩而弗
類之偏不能以自克者似之也其用汝以作礪
乎則夫斷同心之利以變化其氣質懋淬礪之
功以堅定其德性者於汝有深賴焉猶未也險
punctuated:
書

若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。

石雷

同考試官教諭莫批：高宗命傅說納誨，屢託之喻，眞有見於相道之關君德如此。是篇形容殆盡，宜錄以式。

考試官教諭彭批：親切。

考試官教諭朱批：典實。

賢王命大臣以納誨，必屢託喻以深致其望焉。夫相道之繫於君德也大矣！賢王屢託喻以求誨，其望治之心不亦切乎？想高宗之命傅說及此，意謂上下交而德業成，君臣之相須也久矣。我之望汝納誨者，何以擬諸其形容哉？彼金所以利用，非礪則金無所成。顧予德有未脩，而弗類之偏不能以自克者，似之也。其用汝以作礪乎？則夫斷同心之利，以變化其氣質，懋淬礪之功，以堅定其德性者，於汝有深賴焉。猶未也，險
translation_en:
Book of Documents

“If I am metal, I shall use you as a whetstone; if I am crossing a great river, I shall use you as a boat and oars; if the year brings a great drought, I shall use you as timely, soaking rain.”

Shi Lei

Comment by Associate Examiner Mo, Instructor: When Gaozong commanded Fu Yue to offer instruction, he repeatedly expressed himself through analogies. He truly understood how the Way of the chief minister bears upon the ruler’s virtue. This essay describes that relationship almost exhaustively and should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: Direct and apt.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Grounded in the classics and substantial.

When a worthy king commands his great minister to offer instruction, he must repeatedly resort to analogies to convey fully the depth of his expectations. For the Way of the chief minister has a profound bearing upon the ruler’s virtue! When a worthy king repeatedly uses analogies to seek instruction, does this not show how urgently he hopes for good government? We may imagine that, when Gaozong’s charge to Fu Yue reached this point, his meaning was as follows: Through communion between those above and below, virtue and achievement are brought to fruition. Long indeed have ruler and minister depended upon each other. To what can I compare my hope that you will offer me instruction, so as to give it fitting expression? Metal becomes an effective implement only through sharpening; without a whetstone, nothing can be made of it. Looking to myself, I find my virtue still uncultivated in some respects, and deviations from goodness that I cannot overcome unaided: my condition resembles that of the metal. Shall I therefore use you as a whetstone? In this, I depend deeply upon you: with the cutting sharpness of united hearts [?], to transform my disposition, and through diligent tempering and sharpening, to make my moral nature firm. Yet this does not exhaust the matter. As for peril …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
莫甚於巨川非舟楫則無以利涉顧予德有未
進而向往之機罔知津涯者似之也其用汝作
舟楫乎則夫引其不逮以弘濟乎艱難示我攸
往以誕登于道岸者於汝尤深賴焉猶未也大
旱之於霖雨望莫切焉者也顧予樹德之滋弗
遂而罔顯之學就荒者猶夫大旱也其用汝作
霖雨乎則夫發久閟之蒙以資潤身之德沛時
雨之化以植澤物之本者又非賴汝相須以有
成邪吁高宗命傅說至此言愈切而意愈深矣
===
則夫說之納誨以輔德者豈容已哉抑論高宗
奮起積衰恭默思道以端化理似無藉於臣之
啓沃矣今觀其託物之喻真若弗類而惓惓焉
厥後麴糱鹽梅之喻股肱惟人之喻不一而足
真聖不自聖之心也嗚呼憲天法祖遜志典學
之訓說之獻納於高宗者亦詳矣卒之君臣協
德為有商一代之賢君名佐有自哉
公其以予萬億年敬天之休
陶鑾
punctuated:
莫甚於巨川，非舟楫則無以利涉。顧予德有未進，而向往之機罔知津涯者似之也。其用汝作舟楫乎？則夫引其不逮，以弘濟乎艱難，示我攸往，以誕登于道岸者，於汝尤深賴焉。猶未也，大旱之於霖雨，望莫切焉者也。顧予樹德之滋弗遂，而罔顯之學就荒者，猶夫大旱也。其用汝作霖雨乎？則夫發久閟之蒙，以資潤身之德，沛時雨之化，以植澤物之本者，又非賴汝相須以有成邪？吁！高宗命傅說至此，言愈切而意愈深矣。則夫說之納誨以輔德者，豈容已哉？抑論高宗，奮起積衰，恭默思道，以端化理，似無藉於臣之啓沃矣。今觀其託物之喻，真若弗類而惓惓焉。厥後麴糱鹽梅之喻、股肱惟人之喻，不一而足，真聖不自聖之心也。嗚呼！憲天法祖、遜志典學之訓，說之獻納於高宗者亦詳矣。卒之君臣協德，為有商一代之賢君名佐，有自哉！

公其以予萬億年敬天之休
陶鑾
translation_en:
…none is greater than a mighty river: without a boat and oars, there is no means of crossing successfully. Consider how my virtue has yet to advance, while my impulse to press onward knows neither ford nor shore: it is like this. Should I not employ you as my boat and oars? To guide me where I fall short, carrying me safely through difficulties, and to show me where to go, bringing me fully onto the shore of the Way—in these things I depend upon you still more profoundly. Nor is this all. In a great drought, nothing is more earnestly awaited than ample rain. Consider how the nourishment needed to cultivate my virtue fails to reach it, while my learning, still without manifest achievement, falls into neglect: this resembles a great drought. Should I not employ you as ample rain? To dispel the ignorance long shut away within me, nourishing the virtue that enriches the person, and to pour forth transformation like timely rain, establishing the foundation for benefiting all things—does not accomplishment in these matters likewise depend upon your assistance?

Ah! At this point in Gaozong’s charge to Fu Yue, his words become ever more earnest and his meaning ever more profound. How, then, could Yue cease offering instruction to assist his ruler’s virtue? Yet consider Gaozong: he roused himself amid accumulated decline, reverently maintained silence and contemplated the Way, and thereby set the work of transformation and government on a proper course. It would seem that he had no need for his minister to enlighten and nurture him. Yet when we examine his analogies drawn from material things, he truly seems to regard himself as unequal to his task, so earnest is his concern. Later came his analogies of yeast and ferment, of salt and sour plums, and of the arms and legs that make a person complete—too many to enumerate. This was truly the heart of a sage who did not consider himself a sage. Alas! Yue’s instructions to Gaozong—to take Heaven as his pattern and his ancestors as his models, to humble his will and devote himself constantly to learning—were also full and detailed. In the end, ruler and minister united in virtue, becoming a worthy sovereign and a celebrated minister of the Shang dynasty. Surely there was a reason for this!

“May you, Duke, enable me for countless years reverently to receive Heaven’s favor.”
Tao Luan

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭莫批文氣沛然周公謀國之忠
發揮殆盡且結内體出終不果遷之故尤見學識録
之
考試官教諭彭批通暢
考試官教諭朱批得旨
賢王於大臣之宅洛而美其遠有所期也夫洛
邑之作將以凝天命於無窮也成王叙以美之
其深識周公之心哉且其授使者復公之詞若
曰人臣之愛君也深故其謀國也遠公之作洛
===
也而豈徒哉彼朝諸侯而撫商民天固眷我有
周矣使自服土中者無其地則克紹上帝者無
其基何以永承天休邪辨方位而卜洛都公固
作周匹休矣然經始之旣周則區畫之必當抑
豈近謀逸豫邪披其圖而審其勢規模弘遠蓋
欲我宅中國大兢兢焉祗承天眷於無窮卽其
卜而稽其兆思慮深長蓋欲我居重馭輕翼翼
焉敬迓天休於勿替故自今以至萬億年之乆
恒來百辟之享則恒受申命之休而昌而富俾
punctuated:
同考試官教諭莫批：文氣沛然，周公謀國之忠發揮殆盡，且結内體出終不果遷之故，尤見學識，録之。
考試官教諭彭批：通暢。
考試官教諭朱批：得旨。
賢王於大臣之宅洛，而美其遠有所期也。夫洛邑之作，將以凝天命於無窮也。成王叙以美之，其深識周公之心哉！且其授使者復公之詞，若曰：「人臣之愛君也深，故其謀國也遠。公之作洛也，而豈徒哉？彼朝諸侯而撫商民，天固眷我有周矣。使自服土中者無其地，則克紹上帝者無其基，何以永承天休邪？辨方位而卜洛都，公固作周匹休矣。然經始之旣周，則區畫之必當，抑豈近謀逸豫邪？披其圖而審其勢，規模弘遠，蓋欲我宅中國，大兢兢焉祗承天眷於無窮；卽其卜而稽其兆，思慮深長，蓋欲我居重馭輕，翼翼焉敬迓天休於勿替。故自今以至萬億年之乆，恒來百辟之享，則恒受申命之休，而昌而富，俾
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: “The writing flows abundantly, bringing out almost fully the Duke of Zhou’s loyal concern in planning for the state. Moreover, the conclusion discerns the reason why the move was ultimately not carried out, particularly demonstrating the writer’s learning and insight. Select it.”
Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: “Clear and fluent.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Captures the meaning.”
The worthy king praises his great minister’s establishment of a residence at Luo for its far-reaching aims. The building of Luoyi was intended to secure Heaven’s Mandate forever. King Cheng recounts and praises this: how deeply he understands the Duke of Zhou’s heart! The words he entrusts to the envoy in reply to the Duke are as though he said:
“A minister’s love for his sovereign is deep; therefore his planning for the state reaches far. Could your building of Luo have been without purpose? In receiving the regional lords at court and soothing the people of Shang, we have indeed enjoyed Heaven’s favor toward our Zhou. If there were no place from which to exercise rule at the center of the land, there would be no foundation for carrying forward the work of the Lord on High. How, then, could we receive Heaven’s blessings forever? By determining the orientation and divining the site of the capital at Luo, you have indeed brought Zhou a corresponding glory. Since the initial planning was comprehensive, the disposition of the site must also be fitting. Could this have been merely a short-sighted plan for ease and pleasure? Unrolling its map and examining its configuration, I see a grand and far-reaching design. Surely you wish me to dwell in the central lands and, with the utmost vigilance, reverently receive Heaven’s favor without end. Examining the divination and considering its omens, I see profound and enduring deliberation. Surely you wish me to occupy the commanding center and govern the subordinate regions, respectfully and cautiously welcoming Heaven’s blessings without interruption. Thus, from now through ten thousand times a hundred million years, if the offerings of the many lords constantly come, we shall constantly receive the blessing of the renewed Mandate, flourishing and prospering, so that …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
卜休之兆眞有符焉耳永奠商民之居則永膺
申祐之眷益隆益熾伻恒吉之徵眞有見焉耳
可大之業寔寓夫可乆之規天之基命定命予
雖弗及知也而以人驗天竊自慶其貽翼之有
託矣相宅定宅公雖略示其槩也而以意逆志
已預覘其遠猷之有在矣噫周公忠君愛國之
心非成王其孰能知之哉雖然伻來命寧之後
卒不果遷者何也蓋自時中乂者周公之心亦
召公之心也而未欲捨鎬京以廢祖宗之舊者
===
則成王意也且祈天之實敬德誠民爲要區區
形勢抑其次耳則又何擇於鎬與洛之都也善
觀有周卜世之長者當在此而不在彼矣
詩
牧人乃夢衆維魚矣旐維旟矣大人占之
衆維魚矣實維豐年旐維旟矣室家溱
溱
李廷詔
同考試官教諭劉批作文不知關鍵雖文無益
punctuated:
卜休之兆眞有符焉耳。永奠商民之居，則永膺申祐之眷，益隆益熾，伻恒吉之徵眞有見焉耳。可大之業，寔寓夫可乆之規。天之基命定命，予雖弗及知也，而以人驗天，竊自慶其貽翼之有託矣；相宅定宅，公雖略示其槩也，而以意逆志，已預覘其遠猷之有在矣。噫！周公忠君愛國之心，非成王，其孰能知之哉？雖然，伻來命寧之後，卒不果遷者，何也？蓋自時中乂者，周公之心，亦召公之心也；而未欲捨鎬京以廢祖宗之舊者，則成王意也。且祈天之實，敬德誠民爲要，區區形勢，抑其次耳，則又何擇於鎬與洛之都也？善觀有周卜世之長者，當在此而不在彼矣。
詩
牧人乃夢：衆維魚矣，旐維旟矣。大人占之：衆維魚矣，實維豐年；旐維旟矣，室家溱溱。
李廷詔
同考試官教諭劉批：作文不知關鍵，雖文無益
translation_en:
…and the auspicious signs revealed by the divination will truly find their fulfillment. By securing the dwellings of the Shang people forever, we shall forever receive Heaven’s renewed favor and protection, growing ever more flourishing and prosperous; the signs promising lasting good fortune will truly become manifest. An undertaking capable of greatness indeed embodies a plan capable of enduring. Though I cannot fully understand how Heaven establishes and confirms its mandate, judging Heaven’s intentions through human affairs, I privately rejoice that the plans bequeathed to aid posterity have found a sure foundation. Though you, my lord, have shown only the broad outlines of your selection and determination of the capital’s site, by considering your intention I have already discerned where your far-reaching plans lie.
Ah! Who but King Cheng could have understood the Duke of Zhou’s loyalty to his ruler and love for his state? Yet why, after the duke sent a messenger to report that the site was settled, was the move ultimately not carried out? To govern from this central place was the wish of the Duke of Zhou and also of the Duke of Shao; but it was King Cheng’s intention not yet to abandon Haojing and thereby discard the ancestral establishment. Moreover, the substance of seeking Heaven’s favor lies chiefly in reverencing virtue and dealing sincerely with the people; mere geographical advantages are secondary. What need, then, to choose between Hao and Luo as the capital? Those who rightly understand the long duration divined for the Zhou dynasty should look to this, rather than to that.
Book of Odes
“The herdsmen had dreams: the multitude became fish; tortoise-and-snake banners became falcon banners. The diviner interpreted them: ‘The multitude becoming fish means truly a year of abundance; tortoise-and-snake banners becoming falcon banners means households teeming with people.’”
Li Tingzhao
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “If, in composing an essay, one does not grasp the crucial point, even literary elegance is of no benefit…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也是篇美牧事而歸重富庶足闡詩人之旨末復推
本明德仁民又發詩人所未發者滇士有此可爲西
南得人慶矣
同考試官教諭胡批理眞辭達
考試官教諭彭批形容中興氣象宛然在目
是善作雅義者
考試官教諭朱批宏偉
詩人敘牧人感夢之異而兆富庶之祥焉蓋庶
而且富國家莫大之福也牧人感夢而兆是祥
===
非宣王中興之盛何以致之哉此詩美牧事有
成作也意謂天下之治無往不復國家之興有
開必先不驗諸今日中興之盛乎維彼牧人知
自盡其有事而已感夢之異則非緣舊於習心
者焉故其精神凝會之餘夢衆也而維魚也變
動莫之或居宜必有未然之徵也夢旐也而維
旟也恍惚不可爲象宜必有非常之應也於是
獻之天子占之大人蓋以曰衆曰魚皆以豐年
而後盛者也然人之多猶不若魚之多今夢衆
punctuated:
也。是篇美牧事而歸重富庶，足闡詩人之旨；末復推本明德仁民，又發詩人所未發者。滇士有此，可爲西南得人慶矣。
同考試官教諭胡批：理眞辭達。
考試官教諭彭批：形容中興氣象，宛然在目，是善作雅義者。
考試官教諭朱批：宏偉。
詩人敘牧人感夢之異，而兆富庶之祥焉。蓋庶而且富，國家莫大之福也。牧人感夢而兆是祥，非宣王中興之盛，何以致之哉？此詩美牧事有成作也。意謂天下之治，無往不復；國家之興，有開必先。不驗諸今日中興之盛乎？維彼牧人，知自盡其有事而已。感夢之異，則非緣舊於習心者焉。故其精神凝會之餘，夢衆也而維魚也，變動莫之或居，宜必有未然之徵也；夢旐也而維旟也，恍惚不可爲象，宜必有非常之應也。於是獻之天子，占之大人。蓋以曰衆曰魚，皆以豐年而後盛者也。然人之多，猶不若魚之多。今夢衆
translation_en:
… This essay praises the work of herding while placing its chief emphasis on wealth and a numerous population, adequately elucidating the poet’s intent. At the end, it further traces these blessings to their source in manifesting virtue and treating the people humanely, bringing out what the poet himself left unexpressed. That Yunnan has a scholar like this is cause to celebrate the emergence of talent in the southwest.
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: The principles are true, and the language conveys them clearly.
Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: Its portrayal makes the flourishing scene of resurgence seem vividly present before one’s eyes. This is someone skilled in composing expositions of the meaning of the Odes of the Kingdom.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Grand and imposing.
The poet recounts the marvel of the herdsmen’s dreams, which portend the auspicious blessings of wealth and a numerous population. For a state, there is no greater good fortune than a population both numerous and prosperous. How could the herdsmen’s dreams have brought such auspicious portents, had it not been for the flourishing resurgence under King Xuan? This poem was composed to praise success in the work of herding. Its meaning is that order in the world, though it departs, always returns; and a state’s rise is always preceded by signs of its beginning. Is this not borne out by the flourishing resurgence of the present day? Those herdsmen knew only to devote themselves fully to their duties. The strange things that came to them in dreams did not arise from familiar impressions long lodged in their minds.
