以樂舞敎國子其曰雲門大卷大咸大磬
大夏大濩大武者觀其成也以六律六同
和聲音變呂言同亦或謂之閒者獨陰獨
陽其能同乎陰配於陽樂斯同矣呂閒於
律聲斯和矣州鳩之言曰律所以立均出
度也古之神瞽考中聲而量之以制度律
punctuated:
前，夫人能知之也；語樂於三代之後，雖君子亦未之或知也。何也？古之君子之論樂曰：「其數可陳也，其義難知也。」今之君子之論樂曰：「其義可知也，其器難明也。」蓋制度之末，當時之所通知，故棄而不載，而所載者精微玄妙而已耳。孰知千載之下，其器不可復見，而其制無復能知？由是古樂遂廢，而好古之士尚猶幸夫名義之存，由精以求粗，因時以制宜，不能無望於積德百年之餘也。
故觀諸大司樂，以樂德敎國子，其曰中和祇庸孝友者，本諸身也；以樂語敎國子，其曰興道諷誦言語者，和其聲也；以樂舞敎國子，其曰雲門、大卷、大咸、大磬、大夏、大濩、大武者，觀其成也。以六律六同和聲音，變呂言同，亦或謂之閒者，獨陰獨陽，其能同乎？陰配於陽，樂斯同矣；呂閒於律，聲斯和矣。州鳩之言曰：「律所以立均出度也。古之神瞽考中聲而量之以制，度律
translation_en:
…before the Three Dynasties, everyone could understand it; when music is discussed after the Three Dynasties, even gentlemen may fail to understand it. Why is this? When ancient gentlemen discussed music, they said: “Its numerical principles can be set forth, but its meaning is difficult to understand.” When gentlemen today discuss music, they say: “Its meaning can be understood, but its instruments are difficult to comprehend.” The minor details of its institutions and arrangements were common knowledge at the time, so they were omitted from the records; only the subtle, profound, and mysterious aspects were recorded. Who could have known that a thousand years later its instruments would no longer be seen and its arrangements would no longer be understood? Thus ancient music fell into disuse. Yet scholars devoted to antiquity still count themselves fortunate that its terminology and meanings survive. Seeking the tangible through the subtle, and devising suitable arrangements according to the times, they cannot but place hopes in more than a hundred years of accumulated virtue.
Thus, consider the Grand Director of Music. He taught the sons of the state through musical virtues: centrality, harmony, reverence, constancy, filial devotion, and brotherly affection. These were rooted in personal conduct. He taught them through musical expression: evocation, guidance, recitation without a text, chanting, speaking, and conversation. These harmonized their voices. He taught them through musical dances: Yunmen, Dajuan, Daxian, Daqing [?], Daxia, Dahu, and Dawu. Through these their accomplishments could be observed. He harmonized sounds with the six yang pitch standards and the six yin pitch standards. Why replace the designation lü for the yin standards with tong, “accord,” and sometimes call them jian, “interposed”? Could yin alone or yang alone produce accord? When yin is paired with yang, music achieves accord; when the yin standards are interposed among the yang standards, sounds achieve harmony. Zhou Jiu said: “Pitch standards establish musical balance and yield measures. The divine blind musicians of antiquity examined the central pitch and measured it to establish a standard, calibrating the pitch pipes…”

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
均鍾平之以六成於十二天之道也夫六
中之色也故名之曰黃所以宣養六氣九
德也二曰太簇所以金奏贊陽出滯也三
曰姑洗所以脩潔百物考神納賓也四曰
蕤賓所以安靖神人獻酬交錯也五曰夷
則所以咏歌九則平民無貳也六曰無射
所以宣布哲人之令德示民軌儀也爲之
六閒以陽沉伏而默散越也元閒大呂助
宣物也二閒夾鍾出四隙之細也三閒中
===
呂宣中氣也四閒林鍾和展百事俾莫不
任肅純恪也五閒南呂贊陽秀也六閒應
鍾均利器用俾應復也律呂不易無姦物
也細均有鍾無鎛昭其大也大均有鎛無
鍾甚大無鎛鳴其細也大昭小鳴和之道
也此其名義居然可見其所謂中聲者實
作樂之要也是黃鍾之聲也卽所謂元聲
也兹義也在樂爲中聲在天爲中氣在人
爲喜怒哀樂之未發及發而中節者也其
punctuated:
均鍾，平之以六，成於十二，天之道也。夫六，中之色也，故名之曰黃，所以宣養六氣九德也。二曰太簇，所以金奏贊陽出滯也。三曰姑洗，所以脩潔百物，考神納賓也。四曰蕤賓，所以安靖神人，獻酬交錯也。五曰夷則，所以咏歌九則，平民無貳也。六曰無射，所以宣布哲人之令德，示民軌儀也。爲之六閒，以陽沉伏而默，散越也。元閒大呂，助宣物也。二閒夾鍾，出四隙之細也。三閒中呂，宣中氣也。四閒林鍾，和展百事，俾莫不任肅純恪也。五閒南呂，贊陽秀也。六閒應鍾，均利器用，俾應復也。律呂不易，無姦物也。細均有鍾無鎛，昭其大也；大均有鎛無鍾，甚大無鎛，鳴其細也。大昭小鳴，和之道也。

此其名義，居然可見。其所謂中聲者，實作樂之要也，是黃鍾之聲也，卽所謂元聲也。兹義也，在樂爲中聲，在天爲中氣，在人爲喜怒哀樂之未發，及發而中節者也。其
translation_en:
…and tune the bells, balancing them by six pitch standards and completing them in twelve: this is the Way of Heaven. Now, six is the color of the center [?]; hence it is named Huang, “Yellow.” It serves to diffuse and nourish the six vital energies and the nine virtues. The second is Taicu, which, through performance on metal instruments, assists yang and releases what is obstructed. The third is Guxian, which purifies all things, honors the spirits, and receives guests. The fourth is Ruibin, which brings peace to spirits and people as offerings and reciprocal toasts pass back and forth. The fifth is Yize, which gives voice in song to the nine norms and brings the people into accord without divided allegiance. The sixth is Wuyi, which proclaims the excellent virtue of wise men and shows the people standards of conduct.

For these, six intervening pitches were established, so that yang, when submerged, hidden, and silent, might spread forth. The first intervening pitch, Dalü, helps things unfold. The second, Jiazhong, brings forth the subtle energies of the four interstices [?]. The third, Zhonglü, diffuses the central vital energy. The fourth, Linzhong, harmonizes and advances the hundred affairs, so that all are undertaken with reverence, purity, and earnest care. The fifth, Nanlü, assists yang in bringing things to maturity. The sixth, Yingzhong, regulates and perfects implements for use, enabling them to respond in the returning cycle. When the yang and yin pitch standards are not interchanged, there are no aberrant things. For a high-pitched tuning there are zhong bells but no bo bells, to bring out its deeper tones; for a low-pitched tuning there are bo bells but no zhong bells, while for an extremely low tuning there are no bo bells, to sound its finer tones. Bringing out the deeper tones and sounding the finer ones is the way of harmony.

The meanings of these names are thus readily apparent. What is called the central tone is truly the essential principle of making music. It is the tone of Huangzhong, the Yellow Bell, and is precisely what is called the primal tone. This principle is the central tone in music and the central vital energy in Heaven. In human beings, it is joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure before they have arisen, and their attainment of due measure when they do arise. Its …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
輕重清濁疾徐之節蓋有促之不能使之
密豁之不能使之疎損之不能使之少益
之不能使之多者漢初古樂猶存文帝謙
讓未遑武帝雖有志於樂然所好者特世
俗之樂非先王之制也嗣是魏用杜夔隋
用鄭譯何妥宋用和峴胡瑗輩非不留心
於鍾律而卒無所得焉惟蔡元定旁搜遠
取巨細不捐積之累年乃若冥契著爲新
書明白而淵深縝密而通暢不爲牽合附
===
會之談其言雖出於近世之所未講而實
無一字不本古人已試之成法觀其黃鍾
圍徑之法則漢斛之積分可考寸以九分
爲法則淮南太史小司馬之說可推五聲
二變之數變律半聲之例則杜氏通典具
焉變宮變徵之不得爲調則孔氏之禮䟽
在焉元定嘗曰律呂之器不可復見然古
人制樂之意則猶可考信斯言也則其書
固在而作者之意固可推也然古樂終不
punctuated: 輕重清濁疾徐之節，蓋有促之不能使之密、豁之不能使之疎、損之不能使之少、益之不能使之多者。漢初，古樂猶存，文帝謙讓未遑，武帝雖有志於樂，然所好者特世俗之樂，非先王之制也。嗣是，魏用杜夔，隋用鄭譯、何妥，宋用和峴、胡瑗輩，非不留心於鍾律，而卒無所得焉。惟蔡元定旁搜遠取，巨細不捐，積之累年，乃若冥契，著爲新書，明白而淵深，縝密而通暢，不爲牽合附會之談。其言雖出於近世之所未講，而實無一字不本古人已試之成法。觀其黃鍾圍徑之法，則漢斛之積分可考；寸以九分爲法，則淮南、太史、小司馬之說可推；五聲二變之數、變律半聲之例，則杜氏《通典》具焉；變宮、變徵之不得爲調，則孔氏之《禮䟽》在焉。元定嘗曰：「律呂之器不可復見，然古人制樂之意則猶可考。」信斯言也，則其書固在，而作者之意固可推也。然古樂終不
translation_en:
…in its gradations of weight, clarity and turbidity, and speed, there is a measure that cannot be made denser by compression, sparser by expansion, less by subtraction, or more by addition. At the beginning of the Han, ancient music still survived. Emperor Wen, in his modest restraint, had not found leisure to attend to it. Although Emperor Wu had aspirations concerning music, what he enjoyed was merely the popular music of his age, not the institutions of the former kings. Thereafter, Wei employed Du Kui; Sui employed Zheng Yi and He Tuo; and Song employed He Xian, Hu Yuan, and others. It was not that they failed to attend to bells and pitch standards, yet in the end they achieved nothing.

Cai Yuanding alone searched widely and reached far, discarding nothing, great or small. After accumulating his findings over many years, he seemed to attain an unspoken accord with the ancients. He composed a new book, lucid yet profound, meticulous yet coherent and fluent, avoiding forced connections and contrived explanations. Although his statements addressed matters that recent generations had not discussed, in fact not a single word failed to rest upon established methods already tested by the ancients. Examining his method for determining the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe, one can verify its basis in the calculation of the Han hu measure’s volume. For his rule that one cun comprises nine fen, one can trace the explanations of the Master of Huainan, the Grand Historian, and the Younger Sima. The numerical values of the five notes and two altered notes, and the rules for altered pitches and half-pitches, are fully provided in Du’s Comprehensive Institutions (Tongdian). As for why the altered gong and altered zhi notes cannot serve as the basis of modes, Kong’s Subcommentary on the Rites provides the evidence.

Yuanding once said: “The instruments embodying the pitch standards can no longer be seen, but the intentions with which the ancients established music can still be investigated.” If these words are true, then his book certainly remains, and the intentions of those who created the music can certainly be inferred. Yet ancient music ultimately cannot…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
可復者豈世無古之人邪吁必待后夔而
後作樂必待師曠而後聽音斯人不世出
而樂在天下不可一日無也而音豈不可
聽哉世無后夔師曠而后夔之心師曠之
耳則固未甞無也故房庶有曰古樂與今
樂本末不遠上古世質而聲樸後世稍變
焉亦猶大輅起於推輪龍艘生於落葉耳
庶之言及此其達樂之變乎方今重熈累
洽和氣薰蒸真所謂大定大順之世此千
===
載一時也然則魯兩生之說詎可緩乎誠
得夫開物成務之才妙解音律之士叅酌
乎周禮大師之所掌禮運樂記之所記國
語之所述史記之所書因文焉以會其意
引緒焉以求其端即名義度數之可稽達
天人淵微之至妙會而通之與時宜之隨
絲竹金石秬黍之所寓均之而使適其宜
裁之而使中其度古樂之宜於古而復宜
於今者則因之宜於古而不宜於今者則
punctuated:
可復者，豈世無古之人邪？吁！必待后夔而後作樂，必待師曠而後聽音，斯人不世出，而樂在天下不可一日無也，而音豈不可聽哉？世無后夔、師曠，而后夔之心、師曠之耳，則固未甞無也。故房庶有曰：「古樂與今樂，本末不遠。上古世質而聲樸，後世稍變焉，亦猶大輅起於推輪，龍艘生於落葉耳。」庶之言及此，其達樂之變乎！
方今重熈累洽，和氣薰蒸，真所謂大定大順之世，此千載一時也。然則魯兩生之說，詎可緩乎？誠得夫開物成務之才、妙解音律之士，叅酌乎《周禮》大師之所掌、《禮運》《樂記》之所記、《國語》之所述、《史記》之所書，因文焉以會其意，引緒焉以求其端，即名義度數之可稽，達天人淵微之至妙，會而通之，與時宜之，隨絲竹金石秬黍之所寓，均之而使適其宜，裁之而使中其度。古樂之宜於古而復宜於今者，則因之；宜於古而不宜於今者，則
translation_en:
…cannot be restored—is this because the world lacks men like those of antiquity? Alas! If we must await a Hou Kui before making music, and a Shi Kuang before discerning tones, such men do not appear in every generation; yet the world cannot go a single day without music. Can its tones really not be discerned? Though the world lacks Hou Kui and Shi Kuang, it has certainly never lacked minds like Hou Kui’s or ears like Shi Kuang’s. Thus Fang Shu said: “Ancient and present-day music are not far apart in their fundamentals and details. In high antiquity the world was simple and its sounds unadorned; later ages gradually altered them. This is just as the great ceremonial carriage developed from the rudimentary wheel, and the dragon boat arose from a falling leaf.” In saying this, did not Fang Shu understand how music changes!
Today, successive ages of brilliance and accumulated good government have filled the world with harmonious influences. This is truly what is called an age of great stability and perfect concord—an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. Given this, could the pronouncement of the two scholars of Lu justify delay? [?] If we could indeed obtain talented men who illuminate things and bring affairs to completion, scholars with a subtle understanding of musical pitches, they could consult and weigh the duties of the Grand Music Master in the Rites of Zhou, the records in “The Conveyance of Rites” and “The Record of Music,” the accounts in the Discourses of the States, and the writings in the Records of the Grand Historian. Following the texts, they could grasp their meaning; tracing their threads, they could seek their beginnings. Through verifiable terminology, meanings, measurements, and numbers, they could attain the utmost subtleties of the profound relationship between Heaven and humanity. They could bring these together into a comprehensive understanding and adapt them to the times. Wherever musical pitches are embodied—in silk strings, bamboo pipes, metal bells, stone chimes, or black millet grains—they could tune them to their proper fit and regulate them to their correct measure. Those elements of ancient music that suited antiquity and also suit the present should be retained; those that suited antiquity but do not suit the present should…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
變之因其所當因變其所可變或由今之
器以寄古之聲或以古之器而象今之德
去其忲懣靡曼之聲而歸之中和雅正之
樂則音容節奏之間可以備天地萬物之
理而臻雍熈太和之盛矣是固
聖人在天子之位建中和之極操制作之柄者
之能事也記曰五帝殊時不相沿樂迂儒
是古而非今曲士貴耳而賤目故曰非常
之原黎民懼焉及臻厥成天下晏如也執
===
事以爲何如
第三問
蘭漵
同考試官教諭批策士非徒取其記問蓋欲
驗其才識此作援古證今確有定見末歸之選將之
精待將之厚馭將之嚴非出入韜略者不能及此
考試官教諭彭批駕馭之策統馭之才子皆
兼之矣敬服敬服
考試官教諭朱批有籌略有斷制
punctuated:
變之。因其所當因，變其所可變，或由今之器以寄古之聲，或以古之器而象今之德，去其忲懣靡曼之聲，而歸之中和雅正之樂，則音容節奏之間，可以備天地萬物之理，而臻雍熈太和之盛矣。是固聖人在天子之位，建中和之極，操制作之柄者之能事也。記曰：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂。」迂儒是古而非今，曲士貴耳而賤目，故曰：「非常之原，黎民懼焉；及臻厥成，天下晏如也。」執事以爲何如？

第三問
蘭漵

同考試官教諭批：策士非徒取其記問，蓋欲驗其才識。此作援古證今，確有定見，末歸之選將之精、待將之厚、馭將之嚴，非出入韜略者不能及此。

考試官教諭彭批：駕馭之策，統馭之才，子皆兼之矣。敬服！敬服！

考試官教諭朱批：有籌略，有斷制。
translation_en:
…change them. Preserve what ought to be preserved and change what may be changed. One might use present-day instruments to convey ancient sounds, or use ancient instruments to embody the virtue of the present age. Eliminate sounds of extravagance, discontent, and seductive softness [?], and return to music that is balanced, harmonious, refined, and correct. Then its sounds, ceremonial movements, rhythms, and measures can fully embody the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, bringing about the flourishing condition of concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony. This is indeed within the capacity of a sage who occupies the position of Son of Heaven, establishes the ultimate standard of balance and harmony, and holds the authority to institute rites and music. The Record of Rites says: “The Five Emperors lived in different ages and did not follow one another’s music.” Pedantic scholars approve of antiquity and condemn the present; narrow-minded scholars value what they hear and disparage what they see. Thus it is said: “At the inception of an extraordinary undertaking, the common people are afraid; once it reaches completion, all under Heaven are at ease.” What is your judgment, sir?

Third Question
Lan Xu 蘭漵

Comment by the Associate Examiner, an Instructor: Examining scholars through policy essays is not merely a matter of testing their memorized learning; its purpose is to assess their ability and judgment. This essay draws on antiquity to substantiate its arguments about the present and displays firm, considered views. It concludes by emphasizing care in selecting commanders, generosity in treating them, and strictness in controlling them. Only someone thoroughly versed in military strategy could attain this level.

Comment by Examiner Peng, an Instructor: You possess both the methods for directing commanders and the talent for exercising command. I admire you! I admire you!

Comment by Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: There is strategic planning, and there is decisive judgment.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
兵無常形在鼓舞之何如耳將無常能在
駕馭之何如耳何則人有勇怯而鼓舞之
也存乎倡將有賢愚而駕馭之也原於擇
倡則勇者成其能擇則賢者畢其用是故
聖人之治兵親簡閱以定其趨慎選擇而
重其託是以六師奮而四夷寧兆民安而
外患息轉移之機其在茲乎夫兵者國之
大事也愚嘗讀商周之書究韜略之㫖而
知其槩矣又嘗竊怪夫漢之文帝時當承
===
平雍容謙讓若無事於武者一旦匈奴擾
其北鄙帝也赫然震怒拊髀興懷思得頗
牧之將勞軍細柳亟稱亞夫之能卒之匈
奴北去兵雖不試他日七國之變終收亞
夫之功何其英明哉幾於大勇矣是故經
武之要不可不講也講武之禮不可不行
也易曰隨無故也蠱則飭也夫隨以無故
而偷安蠱以有事而始飭故鐫金石者其
功難摧枯朽者其力易勢則然也周禮大
punctuated: 兵無常形，在鼓舞之何如耳；將無常能，在駕馭之何如耳。何則？人有勇怯，而鼓舞之也存乎倡；將有賢愚，而駕馭之也原於擇。倡則勇者成其能，擇則賢者畢其用。是故聖人之治兵，親簡閱以定其趨，慎選擇而重其託。是以六師奮而四夷寧，兆民安而外患息。轉移之機，其在茲乎！夫兵者，國之大事也。愚嘗讀商周之書，究韜略之㫖，而知其槩矣。又嘗竊怪夫漢之文帝，時當承平，雍容謙讓，若無事於武者。一旦匈奴擾其北鄙，帝也赫然震怒，拊髀興懷，思得頗牧之將；勞軍細柳，亟稱亞夫之能。卒之匈奴北去，兵雖不試，他日七國之變，終收亞夫之功。何其英明哉！幾於大勇矣！是故經武之要，不可不講也；講武之禮，不可不行也。《易》曰：「隨，無故也；蠱則飭也。」夫隨以無故而偷安，蠱以有事而始飭。故鐫金石者，其功難；摧枯朽者，其力易。勢則然也。《周禮》大
translation_en:
Troops have no fixed disposition: it depends on how they are inspired. Generals have no fixed capacity: it depends on how they are directed. Why is this? Men differ in courage and timidity, and inspiring them depends on taking the lead; generals differ in worth and folly, and directing them begins with selection. With leadership, the brave can realize their abilities; with selection, the worthy can put their talents fully to use. Thus, in managing troops, the sage personally selects and reviews them to establish their direction, carefully chooses commanders, and treats the responsibilities entrusted to them as weighty. Accordingly, the Six Armies are roused and the peoples of the four quarters remain quiet; the myriad common people are secure and external troubles cease. Surely the key to transforming affairs lies here!

Military affairs are a great concern of the state. I, in my ignorance, have read the writings of the Shang and Zhou, investigated the essentials of military strategy, and come to understand their broad outlines. I have also privately marveled at Emperor Wen of the Han. Living in a time of established peace, he was composed, gracious, modest, and deferential, seemingly unconcerned with warfare. Yet when the Xiongnu disturbed his northern frontier, the emperor blazed with anger. Slapping his thigh in deep feeling, he longed to obtain generals like Lian Po and Li Mu. Visiting the troops at Xiliu to reward their service, he repeatedly praised Zhou Yafu’s ability. In the end, the Xiongnu withdrew northward. Although the troops were not put to the test, Yafu’s achievements ultimately bore fruit during the later Rebellion of the Seven States. How discerning and enlightened the emperor was! He came close to possessing great courage!

Thus, the essentials of military preparedness must be studied, and the rites of military training must be performed. The Book of Changes says: “Following means having no troubles; Decay means putting things in order.” In Following, the absence of trouble encourages complacent ease; in Decay, only when trouble arises does one begin to restore order. Thus, engraving metal and stone is difficult work, while breaking down withered and rotten wood requires little effort. The circumstances make it so. In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
司馬中春敎振旅中夏敎茇舍中秋敎治
兵中冬敎大閱振旅者所以斂耕作之民
也茇舍者所以敎夜戰之法也治兵者所
以敎晝戰之法也至於大閱則合三時而
敎之矣中春振旅王執路鼓中秋治兵王
載太常是一歲之間天子再臨焉又於簡
閱之後因行蒐狩之禮其所往也有地其
與期也有時有地則不害稼有時則不妨
農一遊一豫惟禮惟仁而豈徒哉是以將
===
===
帥士卒有所畏而各精其能夷狄姦宄有
所警而各戢其暴周所以延八百年之祚
者不爲無助也由周而下稱治者漢唐宋
也漢當十月之時行斬牲之禮會五營之
兵爲八陳之肄貙劉以誓衆乘之以習兵
乘輿駕白馬朱鬣親臨幸焉唐於中冬之
月定講武之期兵部承詔將士爲墠尚書
肅奉引之儀將帥嚴旗鼓之節天子乘革
輅至墠歲一臨焉宋制始於建隆而定於
punctuated:
司馬：中春敎振旅，中夏敎茇舍，中秋敎治兵，中冬敎大閱。振旅者，所以斂耕作之民也；茇舍者，所以敎夜戰之法也；治兵者，所以敎晝戰之法也；至於大閱，則合三時而敎之矣。中春振旅，王執路鼓；中秋治兵，王載太常。是一歲之間，天子再臨焉。又於簡閱之後，因行蒐狩之禮。其所往也有地，其與期也有時。有地則不害稼，有時則不妨農。一遊一豫，惟禮惟仁，而豈徒哉？是以將帥士卒有所畏，而各精其能；夷狄姦宄有所警，而各戢其暴。周所以延八百年之祚者，不爲無助也。
由周而下，稱治者漢、唐、宋也。漢當十月之時，行斬牲之禮，會五營之兵，爲八陳之肄，貙劉以誓衆，乘之以習兵。乘輿駕白馬朱鬣，親臨幸焉。唐於中冬之月，定講武之期。兵部承詔，將士爲墠；尚書肅奉引之儀，將帥嚴旗鼓之節。天子乘革輅至墠，歲一臨焉。宋制始於建隆，而定於
translation_en:
…the Minister of War: in mid-spring he teaches the mustering of troops; in mid-summer, encampment; in mid-autumn, military drill; and in mid-winter, the grand review. Mustering serves to assemble the people who work the fields; encampment serves to teach the methods of night combat; military drill serves to teach the methods of daytime combat. The grand review combines the instruction of the three preceding seasons. At the mid-spring muster, the king holds the great drum; at the mid-autumn drill, the king’s carriage bears the great banner. Thus, within a single year, the Son of Heaven attends twice. After inspecting the troops, he also conducts the rites of seasonal hunting. There are prescribed places to which he goes and prescribed times for these occasions. Prescribed places prevent damage to crops; prescribed times prevent interference with farming. Each excursion and each recreation accords with ritual and benevolence: how could these be undertaken without purpose? Consequently, commanders and soldiers have something to hold in awe, and each perfects his abilities; the peoples beyond the borders and evildoers within are put on their guard, and each restrains his violence. This was no small help in enabling the Zhou to prolong its dynastic mandate for eight hundred years.
After the Zhou, the dynasties renowned for good government were the Han, Tang, and Song. Under the Han, in the tenth month, they performed the rite of slaughtering sacrificial animals, assembled the troops of the Five Encampments, and practiced the eight battle formations. Through the chuliu hunting rite they solemnly admonished the troops, taking the occasion to practice warfare. The emperor’s carriage was drawn by white horses with red manes, and he attended in person. Under the Tang, a date for military exercises was fixed in the mid-winter month. The Ministry of War received the imperial command, and officers and soldiers prepared a cleared ground. The minister solemnly observed the ceremonial procedures for leading the imperial procession, while the commanders strictly maintained the prescribed signals of flags and drums. The Son of Heaven rode to the ground in a leather-covered chariot, attending once each year. The Song system began in the Jianlong reign period and was established in …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
咸平其教射之法教陳之規尤爲精嚴講
武之日帝乗馬登臺臨觀焉然中平之世
講武於平樂觀先天之初講武於驪山宋
太宗講武於近郊真宗講武於東武村此
四君者雖人品不同其車馬之盛紀律之
嚴足以嚴内治備外攘者則一而已矣就
而論之玄宗正郭元振唐紹虧失軍容之
罪奨薛訥解琬戎陳堅肅之美其得將將
之道乎太宗嚴木鏃相射之法定韋稍相
===
擊之等其得練士之道乎其所以身致太
平取威制勝誠萬世所宜法也我
國家簡閱之制操練有時更番有期遴選而
爲三千諸營合之而爲十二大團營有大
將以總督之有參將諸臣以分攝之可謂
精且練矣然邇者殘胡爲寇戕我邊鄙雖
無足慮而守備空虚上厪
宵旰之憂臣工論列章數十上備禦之策似
已詳盡然求其威敵制勝之將投石超距
punctuated:
咸平。其教射之法、教陳之規，尤爲精嚴。講武之日，帝乗馬登臺臨觀焉。然中平之世，講武於平樂觀；先天之初，講武於驪山；宋太宗講武於近郊，真宗講武於東武村。此四君者，雖人品不同，其車馬之盛、紀律之嚴，足以嚴内治、備外攘者，則一而已矣。就而論之，玄宗正郭元振、唐紹虧失軍容之罪，奨薛訥、解琬戎陳堅肅之美，其得將將之道乎？太宗嚴木鏃相射之法，定韋稍相擊之等，其得練士之道乎？其所以身致太平、取威制勝，誠萬世所宜法也。
我國家簡閱之制，操練有時，更番有期，遴選而爲三千諸營，合之而爲十二大團營。有大將以總督之，有參將諸臣以分攝之，可謂精且練矣。然邇者殘胡爲寇，戕我邊鄙，雖無足慮，而守備空虚，上厪宵旰之憂。臣工論列，章數十上，備禦之策似已詳盡。然求其威敵制勝之將、投石超距
translation_en:
…in the Xianping reign period. Its methods for teaching archery and its rules for training in formations were especially meticulous and strict. On the day of military exercises, the emperor rode out and ascended a terrace to observe them in person. During the Zhongping reign period, military exercises were held at Pingle Belvedere; at the beginning of the Xiantian reign period, at Mount Li. Emperor Taizong of the Song held military exercises in the nearby suburbs, and Emperor Zhenzong at Dongwu Village. Although these four rulers differed in personal character, they were alike in this: the magnificence of their chariots and horses and the strictness of their discipline sufficed to strengthen internal governance and prepare to repel external foes. To consider particular cases, Xuanzong punished Guo Yuanzhen and Tang Shao for breaches of military decorum, and commended Xue Ne and Xie Wan for the firmness and orderliness of their formations. Had he not grasped the way to command commanders? Taizong strictly enforced the methods for shooting at one another with wooden arrowheads and established graded rules for striking at one another with leather-tipped spears [?]. Had he not grasped the way to train soldiers? The means by which they personally brought about peace, established their might, and secured victory truly deserve to be emulated for all ages.
Under our dynasty’s system of selecting and reviewing troops, drills are held at set times and rotations follow fixed schedules. Selected men constitute the Three Thousand Camp and the other camps, which are combined into the Twelve Great Training Camps. Senior commanders exercise overall command, while assistant regional commanders and other officers supervise their respective divisions. These forces may indeed be called select and well trained. Recently, however, remnant barbarian forces have raided and ravaged our borderlands. Although they are no great cause for alarm, our defenses are depleted, burdening His Majesty with cares that keep him awake before dawn and delay his meals until late in the day. Officials have presented their arguments in dozens of memorials, and the plans for defense seem already to have been exhaustively discussed. Yet when we seek commanders who can overawe the enemy and secure victory, and men capable of hurling stones and leaping great distances…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之兵尚未有聞焉議者以為演武之地近
在北郊竊有望於
翠華之臨以示親閱六師之義賞其戎陣之
嚴整者罰其行伍之失次者拔其梟健之
可用者汰其老弱之不堪者威嚴之下號
令一新鼓舞之餘旗幟皆變使天下曉然
知選將練兵之誠攘夷固圉之意非襲故
常非飾虛文則庶幾上可以備一代未備
之制下可以動天下將士之心是俄頃功
===
化足以昭文德張武威
大聖人之所作為出於尋常萬萬矣兵法曰器
械不利以其卒予敵也卒不練習以其將
予敵也將不知兵以其君予敵也君不擇
將以其國予敵也是故講武所以練兵也
所以選將也選將也者尤練兵之首事也
奈之何膏粱紈綺世代因仍平時飾貌作
威旣乏統馭之才有警束手無策安望守
禦之績變而通之庸可泥乎魏元忠言於
punctuated:
之兵，尚未有聞焉。議者以為，演武之地近在北郊，竊有望於翠華之臨，以示親閱六師之義。賞其戎陣之嚴整者，罰其行伍之失次者，拔其梟健之可用者，汰其老弱之不堪者。威嚴之下，號令一新；鼓舞之餘，旗幟皆變。使天下曉然知選將練兵之誠、攘夷固圉之意，非襲故常，非飾虛文，則庶幾上可以備一代未備之制，下可以動天下將士之心。是俄頃功化，足以昭文德、張武威，大聖人之所作為，出於尋常萬萬矣。
兵法曰：「器械不利，以其卒予敵也；卒不練習，以其將予敵也；將不知兵，以其君予敵也；君不擇將，以其國予敵也。」是故講武所以練兵也，所以選將也。選將也者，尤練兵之首事也。奈之何膏粱紈綺，世代因仍，平時飾貌作威，旣乏統馭之才，有警束手無策，安望守禦之績？變而通之，庸可泥乎？魏元忠言於
translation_en:
…soldiers of such prowess have yet to be heard of. Those discussing the matter believe that the military drill ground lies nearby in the northern suburbs, and humbly hope that Your Majesty’s imperial carriage will come there, demonstrating the principle of personally reviewing the Six Armies. Reward those whose battle formations are disciplined and orderly; punish those whose ranks fall out of order; promote the fierce and vigorous who are fit for service; and dismiss the old and weak who cannot serve. Under imperial majesty, commands would be renewed; inspired and encouraged, the forces beneath every banner would be transformed. Let all under Heaven clearly understand the sincerity of the effort to select generals and train troops, and the resolve to repel the barbarians and secure the frontiers: this would neither perpetuate old routines nor embellish empty formalities. Then we might hope, above, to complete the institutions still incomplete under this dynasty and, below, to stir the hearts of generals and soldiers throughout the realm. The achievements and transforming influence of this brief moment would suffice to display civil virtue and extend military might. The deeds of the great sage would surpass the ordinary ten thousand times over.
The military treatise says: “If weapons and equipment are not sharp and effective, this is to give one’s soldiers to the enemy. If the soldiers are not trained, this is to give one’s general to the enemy. If the general does not understand warfare, this is to give one’s ruler to the enemy. If the ruler does not select his generals carefully, this is to give his state to the enemy.” Thus, military exercises serve to train soldiers and to select generals. Selecting generals is, above all, the foremost task in training troops. How can sons raised on rich food and clothed in fine silk simply succeed one another generation after generation? In peacetime they cultivate appearances and put on an imposing manner, yet lack the ability to command; when an alarm comes, they are helpless and without a plan. How can one expect achievements in defense from them? Changes must be made so that the system can function: how could one cling rigidly to precedent? Wei Yuanzhong said to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其君曰今朝廷用人類取將門子弟及死
事之家彼皆庸人豈足當閫外之任古之
名將皆出貧賤而立殊功未聞其家代爲
將也忠也斯言其見今時之弊於千載之
上何其明且智哉誠用元忠之言博求材
武之士不拘一途若衞青之在奴僕郭子
儀之在儒臣畢誠之在侍從狄青之在走
卒皆得以見推於縉紳列名於將帥而隂
令本兵徐察其能而爲之等第以備
===
萬幾之暇時
賜召見或詢其謀或試其勇或較其藝或辨
其材將必有卓異者出於其間然後倣古
人推轂之儀體唐人親送之意授之以節
鉞之柄予之以賞罰之權厚其所以充賞
之貲嚴其所以致罰之條不牽之以文法
使之得以行其志俟其賞罰旣行號令旣
一人心旣齊地利旣熟則可投之所向無
不如意俾之練兵則援枹而鼓義不反顧
punctuated: 其君曰：「今朝廷用人，類取將門子弟及死事之家。彼皆庸人，豈足當閫外之任？古之名將，皆出貧賤而立殊功，未聞其家代爲將也。」忠也斯言，其見今時之弊於千載之上，何其明且智哉！誠用元忠之言，博求材武之士，不拘一途，若衞青之在奴僕、郭子儀之在儒臣、畢誠之在侍從、狄青之在走卒，皆得以見推於縉紳，列名於將帥，而隂令本兵徐察其能，而爲之等第，以備萬幾之暇，時賜召見，或詢其謀，或試其勇，或較其藝，或辨其材，將必有卓異者出於其間。然後倣古人推轂之儀，體唐人親送之意，授之以節鉞之柄，予之以賞罰之權，厚其所以充賞之貲，嚴其所以致罰之條，不牽之以文法，使之得以行其志。俟其賞罰旣行，號令旣一，人心旣齊，地利旣熟，則可投之所向，無不如意。俾之練兵，則援枹而鼓，義不反顧。
translation_en:
…to his ruler, saying: “Nowadays, when the court appoints men, it generally selects sons and younger kinsmen of military families and members of families whose men have died in service. These are all ordinary men: how could they be equal to independent military command beyond the palace gates? The famous generals of antiquity all rose from poverty and humble station to establish extraordinary achievements. I have never heard that their families supplied generals generation after generation.” In these words, how clearly and wisely Wei Yuanzhong perceived, a thousand years ago, the abuses of our own time! If his advice were truly followed, men of military talent and prowess would be sought widely, without restricting recruitment to a single avenue. Men such as Wei Qing among slaves and servants, Guo Ziyi among scholar-officials [?], Bi Cheng among palace attendants [?], and Di Qing among common soldiers could all be recommended by the officials and enrolled among the commanders. The Minister of War should then be secretly instructed to assess their abilities gradually and rank them, so that, in moments of leisure from the myriad affairs of government, Your Majesty might occasionally grant them an audience. By questioning their plans, testing their courage, comparing their military skills, or discerning their talents, outstanding men would surely emerge among them.

Then, following the ancient ceremony of pushing a departing commander's carriage wheels and embodying the spirit of the Tang emperors’ personal send-offs, you should confer on them the authority symbolized by the commander's tally and battle-axe and grant them power to reward and punish. Supply ample funds for their rewards and establish strict provisions for their punishments. Do not constrain them with bureaucratic regulations, but allow them to carry out their intentions. Once rewards and punishments have been put into effect, commands unified, the men's hearts brought into accord, and the advantages of the terrain thoroughly understood, they may be deployed wherever needed, and everything will proceed as desired. Set them to training troops, and when they take up the drumsticks and beat the drums, the soldiers, moved by duty, will not turn back …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聞命而趨馬首是瞻赴湯蹈火殆將能之
而況使之嘗敵乎俾之備邊則遠斥候詞
敵情敵來或堅壁清野憑城審勢以待其
惰歸或輕騎斫營據險逆擊以奪其銳氣
梟敵得儁往無不利而何有於堅敵乎俾
之爲大將則申嚴戎政務存大體而無幸
功之心俾之爲偏裨則賈勇深入直趨虜
帳而破敵人之膽是衛郭畢狄皆在任使
何憂乎套虜何畏乎殘胡何言乎借才於
===
異代也哉雖然擇將貴精待將貴厚而馭
之之道尤貴於嚴何者三軍之命繫於一
人一方之恃在於一將北虜之衆不足以
當中國之一大縣然莫之禦者法之玩也
僨軍而必罰者古今之大法也明法以肅
令者人主之大柄也罰一人而千萬人懼
又使千萬人皆全其生天下之至仁也或
者猶以爲疑皆未足以語兵也是故正樊
愛能之辟者五季之頹風且振責陳曙之
punctuated:
聞命而趨，馬首是瞻，赴湯蹈火，殆將能之，而況使之嘗敵乎？俾之備邊，則遠斥候，詞敵情；敵來，或堅壁清野，憑城審勢，以待其惰歸；或輕騎斫營，據險逆擊，以奪其銳氣。梟敵得儁，往無不利，而何有於堅敵乎？俾之爲大將，則申嚴戎政，務存大體，而無幸功之心；俾之爲偏裨，則賈勇深入，直趨虜帳，而破敵人之膽。是衛郭畢狄皆在任使，何憂乎套虜，何畏乎殘胡，何言乎借才於異代也哉？
雖然，擇將貴精，待將貴厚，而馭之之道尤貴於嚴。何者？三軍之命繫於一人，一方之恃在於一將。北虜之衆不足以當中國之一大縣，然莫之禦者，法之玩也。僨軍而必罰者，古今之大法也；明法以肅令者，人主之大柄也；罰一人而千萬人懼，又使千萬人皆全其生，天下之至仁也。或者猶以爲疑，皆未足以語兵也。是故正樊愛能之辟者，五季之頹風且振；責陳曙之
translation_en:
…They would hasten upon hearing orders, following wherever their commander's horse led; they could probably even brave boiling water and tread through fire. How much more readily, then, could they be sent to test the enemy? If such a commander were assigned to defend the frontier, he would send scouts far afield and ascertain the enemy's circumstances [?]. When the enemy arrived, he might strengthen fortifications and clear the countryside, relying on the walls and assessing the situation while waiting for the enemy to withdraw in weariness. Or he might raid their camp with light cavalry and occupy difficult terrain to intercept and strike them, breaking their fighting spirit. Slaying enemies and capturing their finest warriors, he would succeed wherever he went: what difficulty would even a formidable enemy present? If appointed commander-in-chief, he would enforce military discipline strictly, attend to the overall situation, and have no thought of seeking success through sheer luck. If appointed a subordinate commander, he would press boldly deep into enemy territory, advance straight upon their tents, and break their courage. Thus men like Wei, Guo, Bi, and Di would all be available for service. Why worry about the barbarians of the Hetao, fear the brutal Hu, or speak of borrowing talent from another age?
Even so, commanders must be selected with care and treated generously, while the means of controlling them must above all be strict. Why? The lives of the armies depend upon one man; the security of a region rests upon one commander. The northern barbarians are not numerous enough to match even one large county of China. Yet no one can hold them off, because the law is treated lightly. That those who bring disaster upon an army must be punished is a fundamental law of past and present. Making the law clear so that commands are rigorously observed is a great prerogative of the ruler. To punish one man so that thousands upon thousands are afraid, and thereby enable those thousands upon thousands to preserve their lives, is the highest benevolence under Heaven. Any who still doubt this are not yet fit to discuss warfare. Thus, when Fan Aineng was duly subjected to capital punishment, even the declining military ethos of the Five Dynasties was revived; when Chen Shu was held accountable for his …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
敗者崑崙之露布尚傳彼何人也一轉移
之間猶足以振頹而告捷況天下之大四
海之廣握是以馭之能無濟乎
第四問
石雷
同考試官教諭莫批道德功業本非二致然必
體用本末兼舉斯爲合一之學是作得之
考試官教諭彭批是蓋志明道希文而有得
者
===
考試官教諭朱批發言不羣可以知其志矣
善學者求諸聖人而已矣善學聖人者求
諸賢人而已矣賢之與聖其道本無不同
而希賢與聖其序自不容紊也循其序以
至於道此入聖之途也作聖之階也陵節
焉則銳躐等焉則疎銳與疎非學也故曰
行遠自邇也登高自卑也夫是謂之善學
夫是謂之有本之學是故君子愼趨而戒
速此執事發問意也且孔孟之道德伊周
punctuated:
敗者，崑崙之露布尚傳。彼何人也？一轉移之間，猶足以振頹而告捷，況天下之大、四海之廣，握是以馭之，能無濟乎？

第四問
石雷

同考試官教諭莫批：道德功業，本非二致，然必體用本末兼舉，斯爲合一之學。是作得之。

考試官教諭彭批：是蓋志明道、希文而有得者。

考試官教諭朱批：發言不羣，可以知其志矣。

善學者，求諸聖人而已矣；善學聖人者，求諸賢人而已矣。賢之與聖，其道本無不同，而希賢與聖，其序自不容紊也。循其序以至於道，此入聖之途也，作聖之階也。陵節焉則銳，躐等焉則疎，銳與疎，非學也。故曰：「行遠自邇也，登高自卑也。」夫是謂之善學，夫是謂之有本之學。是故君子愼趨而戒速，此執事發問意也。且孔孟之道德，伊周
translation_en:
…those who held Chen Shu accountable for his defeat—the victory proclamation from Kunlun is still transmitted. What manner of men were they? With a single change of course, they could still reverse decline and announce victory. How much more, with all the vastness of the realm and the breadth of the Four Seas, could one fail to achieve results by wielding this principle to govern it?

Fourth Policy Question
Shi Lei

Comment by Associate Examiner Mo, Instructor: Moral virtue and meritorious achievement are fundamentally not two separate pursuits. Yet only by embracing both substance and function, root and branches, can learning unite them as one. This composition grasps that principle.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Instructor: This is surely the work of someone who aspires to emulate Mingdao and Xiwen and has gained something from them.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: His words rise above the ordinary; from them one can discern his aspirations.

Those who learn well seek their models in the sages, and that is all. Those who learn well from the sages seek their models in the worthies, and that is all. The Way of the worthies and the sages is fundamentally the same, yet the order in which one aspires to become a worthy and then a sage must not be confused. Following that sequence to arrive at the Way is the path into sagehood, the stairway to becoming a sage. Overstepping the stages makes one impetuous; skipping the grades makes one superficial. Impetuosity and superficiality are not learning. Thus it is said: “To travel far, begin nearby; to ascend high, begin below.” This is what is called learning well; this is what is called learning with a foundation. Therefore the gentleman proceeds carefully and guards against haste. This is the intent behind the question you have posed. Now, as for the moral virtue of Kongzi and Mengzi, and Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之事業人皆仰之然或以其道大且至而
其世遠且久則望之若不可企及由是向
慕之心或幾乎息羹墻之念無由以興也
故胡安國曰立志以明道希文自期待豈
非以聞知者不若見知者之爲詳取法於
古者不若取法於今之者之易於感發乎
去明道希文之世若此其甚近也而可忽
乎哉粤自有宋開基忠厚立國五星聚奎
旣朕兆賢哲之生仁育義正復培植豪傑
===
之氣故至仁宗之時英賢輩出窮理盡性
咸達精微之蘊若周敦頤之沉潛體道張
載之剛毅自立邵雍之明睿燭幾謝良佐
之誠篤憤悱其於道統之傳皆能有得程
頤於明道獨稱之曰孟子之後一人何哉
蓋其資稟超邁氣質純粹得諸天者固非
諸賢之所可及沉潛六經寤寐羣聖淑諸
人者亦非諸賢之所能盡也是故雲淡風
輕之咏浴沂之氣象也春陽和氣之度申
punctuated:
之事業，人皆仰之。然或以其道大且至，而其世遠且久，則望之若不可企及。由是向慕之心或幾乎息，羹墻之念無由以興也。故胡安國曰：「立志以明道、希文自期待。」豈非以聞知者不若見知者之爲詳，取法於古者不若取法於今之者之易於感發乎？去明道、希文之世若此其甚近也，而可忽乎哉？
粤自有宋開基，忠厚立國，五星聚奎，旣朕兆賢哲之生；仁育義正，復培植豪傑之氣。故至仁宗之時，英賢輩出，窮理盡性，咸達精微之蘊。若周敦頤之沉潛體道，張載之剛毅自立，邵雍之明睿燭幾，謝良佐之誠篤憤悱，其於道統之傳，皆能有得。程頤於明道獨稱之曰：「孟子之後一人。」何哉？蓋其資稟超邁，氣質純粹，得諸天者固非諸賢之所可及；沉潛六經，寤寐羣聖，淑諸人者亦非諸賢之所能盡也。是故雲淡風輕之咏，浴沂之氣象也；春陽和氣之度，申
translation_en:
…and their achievements—all people look up to them. Yet some, considering their Way so great and consummate, and their age so distant and long past, regard them as beyond reach. Thus their longing and admiration may nearly cease, and the yearning to behold the sages, even in soup or against a wall, has no means of arising. Hence Hu Anguo said: “In setting your aspirations, take Mingdao and Xiwen as the standards you expect yourself to attain.” Was this not because knowledge gained through hearing is less detailed than knowledge gained through seeing, and taking models from antiquity less readily inspires people than taking models from more recent times [?]? We are so very close to the age of Mingdao and Xiwen—Cheng Hao and Fan Zhongyan—how could we disregard them?
When the Song dynasty was founded, it established its rule upon loyalty and generosity. The gathering of the five planets in the Kui constellation already portended the birth of worthy and wise men; nurturing through benevolence and rectifying through righteousness further fostered the spirit of outstanding men. Thus, by the reign of Renzong, eminent worthies emerged in succession. Investigating principles and fully realizing human nature, they all penetrated its subtle depths. Such men as Zhou Dunyi, who deeply immersed himself in embodying the Way; Zhang Zai, who established himself through firmness and resolve; Shao Yong, whose clear insight illuminated the first stirrings of things; and Xie Liangzuo, whose sincerity and earnestness drove him to strive for understanding and expression—all attained something of the transmission of the succession of the Way. Yet Cheng Yi singled out Mingdao for this praise: “The one man since Mencius.” Why was this?
His innate endowments were outstanding and his disposition utterly pure: what he received from Heaven was beyond the reach of the other worthies. He immersed himself deeply in the Six Classics and dwelt upon the sages waking and sleeping: the cultivation he derived from others likewise surpassed what the other worthies could fully achieve. Thus his verse about “thin clouds and a gentle breeze” expressed the spirit of bathing in the Yi River; his bearing, like the spring sunshine and its mild warmth, … [the final character 申 is unclear here].

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天之容色也致君堯舜責難之恭也視民
如傷安人之仁也此其泛應曲當渾然天
成庶幾乎廓然太公物來順應之域矣其
言曰以聖人之訓爲必當從先王之治爲
必可法吕大臨曰其自任之重寧學聖人
而未至不以一善而成名朱光庭亦曰先
生得聖人之誠者也才周萬物而不自以
爲高學際三才而不自以爲足行貫神明
而不自以爲異識照古今而不自以爲得
===
蓋其所知上極堯舜帝王三代之治其所
包博大悠遠上下與天地而同流斯言也
明道非眞有所見則趨向取舍何以致若
是之决諸生非眞登明道之堂安能形容
至此乎是故明道當之無愧色稱諸後世
無異詞此其所以大過人者哉固萬世學
者之師也若夫慶曆之間名臣接踵多所
建樹以成一代之治若韓琦之豐功偉量
司馬光之清忠粹德富弼之抗論虜庭歐
punctuated:
天之容色也。致君堯舜，責難之恭也；視民如傷，安人之仁也。此其泛應曲當，渾然天成，庶幾乎廓然太公、物來順應之域矣。其言曰：「以聖人之訓爲必當從，先王之治爲必可法。」吕大臨曰：「其自任之重，寧學聖人而未至，不以一善而成名。」朱光庭亦曰：「先生得聖人之誠者也。才周萬物，而不自以爲高；學際三才，而不自以爲足；行貫神明，而不自以爲異；識照古今，而不自以爲得。蓋其所知，上極堯舜帝王三代之治；其所包，博大悠遠，上下與天地而同流。」斯言也，明道非眞有所見，則趨向取舍何以致若是之决？諸生非眞登明道之堂，安能形容至此乎？是故明道當之無愧色，稱諸後世無異詞。此其所以大過人者哉！固萬世學者之師也。

若夫慶曆之間，名臣接踵，多所建樹，以成一代之治。若韓琦之豐功偉量，司馬光之清忠粹德，富弼之抗論虜庭，歐
translation_en:
…the countenance of Heaven [?]. Bringing his ruler to the level of Yao and Shun expressed the reverence of demanding difficult achievements of him; regarding the people as though they were wounded expressed the benevolence of bringing them peace. His responses to every circumstance were fitting in every particular, perfectly integrated and naturally accomplished. He thus approached the state of expansive impartiality [?], responding appropriately to things as they came. He said: “The teachings of the sages must surely be followed, and the government of the former kings must surely be taken as a model.” Lü Dalin said: “So weighty were the responsibilities he assumed that he preferred to study the sages, even without attaining their level, rather than make a name for himself through a single good deed.” Zhu Guangting also said: “The Master attained the sincerity of the sages. His abilities encompassed all things, yet he did not consider himself exalted; his learning extended to the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—yet he did not consider it sufficient; his conduct penetrated the divine, yet he did not consider himself extraordinary; his discernment illuminated antiquity and the present, yet he did not consider himself to have attained understanding. His knowledge reached back to the government of Yao and Shun, the emperors and kings, and the Three Dynasties. What he embraced was vast, profound, and far-reaching; above and below, he moved in the same stream as Heaven and Earth.” As these words show, had Mingdao not truly possessed insight, how could his aims and his choices of what to accept and reject have been so decisive? Had his students not truly entered Mingdao’s hall of learning, how could they have described him so well? Thus Mingdao could accept this praise without embarrassment, and later generations voiced no dissent from it. Was this not what made him so greatly surpass others? He was indeed a teacher for scholars of all ages.

During the Qingli reign period, eminent ministers appeared in succession, accomplishing much and bringing about good government for their age. Among them were Han Qi, with his abundant achievements and great magnanimity; Sima Guang, with his unsullied loyalty and pure virtue; Fu Bi, who argued unyieldingly at the court of the northern foreigners; and Ouyang …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
陽脩之文章擅名其於事功之建皆能成
章朱熹於希文獨稱之曰有宋第一流人
物何哉蓋其自秀才時便以天下爲己任
其於富貴貧賤毀譽欣戚不一動其心是
故論上壽之儀去貪墨之吏識胡瑗之賢
發中庸之蘊服富弼之心策韓琦之敗妙
捄荒之術溥南園之施此其規模宏闊莫
窺其際庶幾乎一夫不獲時予之辜矣其
言曰先天下之憂而憂後天下之樂而樂
===
又曰不得爲宰相則願爲良醫曾鞏稱之
曰事有天下非之君子非之而公獨曰是
天下是之君子是之而公獨曰非其旣也
君子自以爲不及天下亦曰范公之守是
也斯言也希文非真有所得則負荷擔當
何以能如是之審子固非真知希文之心
何以揄揚至此乎是故即希文之自待與
子固之所以稱之者誠非尋常可及者哉
固萬世學者之宗也夫明道所學聖人之
punctuated: 陽脩之文章擅名，其於事功之建，皆能成章。朱熹於希文獨稱之曰：「有宋第一流人物。」何哉？蓋其自秀才時，便以天下爲己任，其於富貴貧賤、毀譽欣戚，不一動其心。是故論上壽之儀，去貪墨之吏，識胡瑗之賢，發中庸之蘊，服富弼之心，策韓琦之敗，妙捄荒之術，溥南園之施。此其規模宏闊，莫窺其際，庶幾乎「一夫不獲，時予之辜」矣。其言曰：「先天下之憂而憂，後天下之樂而樂。」又曰：「不得爲宰相，則願爲良醫。」曾鞏稱之曰：「事有天下非之，君子非之，而公獨曰是；天下是之，君子是之，而公獨曰非。其旣也，君子自以爲不及，天下亦曰：『范公之守是也。』」斯言也，希文非真有所得，則負荷擔當，何以能如是之審？子固非真知希文之心，何以揄揚至此乎？是故即希文之自待，與子固之所以稱之者，誠非尋常可及者哉！固萬世學者之宗也。夫明道所學，聖人之
translation_en: …Ouyang Xiu’s renown for his literary writings: in their practical achievements, all these men accomplished something distinguished. Yet Zhu Xi singled out Xiwen [Fan Zhongyan] for praise, saying, “A figure of the very first rank in the Song dynasty.” Why was this? From his days as a student, he took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself. Wealth and rank, poverty and low station, condemnation and praise, joy and sorrow—none could move his heart. Thus he deliberated on the ceremonial offering of birthday felicitations to the emperor, dismissed corrupt officials, recognized Hu Yuan’s worth, elucidated the profound meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean, won Fu Bi’s wholehearted respect, foresaw Han Qi’s defeat, devised ingenious methods of famine relief, and extended the beneficence associated with the Southern Garden [?]. His vision was so broad that no one could discern its limits. He came close to the ideal expressed in the words, “If even one person fails to find his proper place, it is my fault.” He said, “Be the first to worry over the troubles of all under Heaven, and the last to enjoy their pleasures.” He also said, “If I cannot become a chief councilor, I wish to become a good physician.” Zeng Gong praised him, saying, “There were matters that everyone under Heaven condemned, and that gentlemen condemned, yet he alone pronounced right; there were matters that everyone under Heaven approved, and that gentlemen approved, yet he alone pronounced wrong. In the end, the gentlemen acknowledged that they did not measure up to him, and everyone under Heaven also said, ‘Lord Fan was right in what he upheld.’” As these words show, had Xiwen not truly attained understanding, how could he have exercised such sound judgment in shouldering his responsibilities? Had Zigu [Zeng Gong] not truly understood Xiwen’s heart, how could he have praised him to this extent? Thus, considering both what Xiwen expected of himself and the grounds on which Zigu praised him, surely his attainment lay beyond the reach of ordinary men! He is indeed an exemplar for scholars for ten thousand generations. Now what Mingdao studied was the sages’…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
事也而其所至則顏孟之域也希文所學
亦聖人之事也而其所得則伊尹之任也
大而未化也復而未至也是學者之軌也
循其軌而漸造其域至其域則亦大有所
得矣抑安敢自畫自棄而員天之所以與
我者乎世之士聰明才辨非不多談道德
功業非不廣然或得其體而不適其用或
專徇其末而莫探其本其最下者猶或藉
此爲蹊徑陰以徼名而侔利則亦安望其
===
窺二子之藩籬而與之論道德功業也哉
雖然君子不敢有輕天下之心也精以擇
之仁以居之勇以行之不爲詭異之行不
趨世俗之名道德也而孔孟而業未甞不
廣功業也而伊周而德未甞不崇是故聖
人學之的也弗至弗止者學者事也又安
知天下果無若人乎是豪傑之士也嗚呼
聖人吾不得而見之矣得見明道希文者
斯可矣志明道希文之志以奮乎五百年
punctuated:
事也，而其所至則顏孟之域也。希文所學亦聖人之事也，而其所得則伊尹之任也。大而未化也，復而未至也，是學者之軌也。循其軌而漸造其域，至其域則亦大有所得矣。抑安敢自畫自棄，而員天之所以與我者乎？世之士，聰明才辨非不多，談道德功業非不廣，然或得其體而不適其用，或專徇其末而莫探其本。其最下者，猶或藉此爲蹊徑，陰以徼名而侔利，則亦安望其窺二子之藩籬，而與之論道德功業也哉？
雖然，君子不敢有輕天下之心也。精以擇之，仁以居之，勇以行之，不爲詭異之行，不趨世俗之名。道德也而孔孟，而業未甞不廣；功業也而伊周，而德未甞不崇。是故聖人，學之的也；弗至弗止者，學者事也。又安知天下果無若人乎？是豪傑之士也。嗚呼！聖人吾不得而見之矣，得見明道希文者斯可矣。志明道希文之志，以奮乎五百年
translation_en:
…the undertakings of the sages, and the realm he attained was that of Yan Hui and Mengzi. What Xiwen studied was likewise the undertakings of the sages, and what he attained was Yi Yin’s sense of responsibility. To be great without yet having reached spiritual transformation, to return toward the Way without yet having arrived: these provide a course for learners. Following that course, they may gradually approach that realm; upon reaching it, they too will have attained much. How could we dare to set limits upon ourselves and abandon ourselves, thereby squandering [?] what Heaven has bestowed upon us? Among the scholars of the age, those possessing intelligence, ability, and eloquence are far from few, and their discussions of moral virtue and meritorious achievement are far from narrow. Yet some grasp the substance without putting it to fitting use; others pursue only the peripheral aspects without exploring the root. The lowest among them may even use these things as a shortcut, secretly seeking fame and pursuing profit. How could one expect them even to glimpse the outer precincts of these two masters, much less discuss moral virtue and meritorious achievement with them?
Nevertheless, the gentleman does not dare harbor contempt for the people of the world. He chooses with discernment, abides in his choice through benevolence, and carries it out with courage. He neither engages in outlandish conduct nor pursues worldly renown. In moral virtue, Kongzi and Mengzi are the exemplars [?], yet their achievements were never less than extensive; in meritorious achievement, Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou are the exemplars [?], yet their virtue was never less than exalted. Thus, sagehood is the target of learning, and refusing to stop before reaching it is the learner’s task. How can we know that the world truly contains no such people? These are men of outstanding ability. Alas! I cannot hope to see a sage; it would suffice to see someone like Mingdao or Xiwen. To make the aspirations of Mingdao and Xiwen one’s own and rise to action five hundred years …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之後者存乎其人耳愚生亦竊有志焉而
未之逮也惟執事與其進
第五問
楊一麒
考試官教諭彭批築城建學乃滇中第一事
是作卓識遠見鑿鑿可行昔人謂識時務者在俊傑
子非其人邪
考試官教諭朱批老成練達不鑿不浮佳士
也
===
爲治之道二安民也養士也安民而求以
衞其生則安之也至矣養士而求以興其
德則養之也至矣是故爲之城焉爲之學
焉匪徒爲目前之謀而責效旦夕者將以
垂可久可大之規也執事爲滇謀尚有踰
此者乎愚雖不敏請誦其所聞以備采擇
焉夫滇在星野屬井鬼之墟在禹貢爲梁
州之域三代以前未始通中國也漢武時
始隸益州沿至南詔屢入西蜀取其士民
punctuated:
之後者，存乎其人耳。愚生亦竊有志焉，而未之逮也，惟執事與其進。

第五問
楊一麒
考試官教諭彭批：築城建學，乃滇中第一事。是作卓識遠見，鑿鑿可行。昔人謂識時務者在俊傑，子非其人邪？
考試官教諭朱批：老成練達，不鑿不浮，佳士也。

爲治之道二：安民也，養士也。安民而求以衞其生，則安之也至矣；養士而求以興其德，則養之也至矣。是故爲之城焉，爲之學焉，匪徒爲目前之謀而責效旦夕者，將以垂可久可大之規也。執事爲滇謀，尚有踰此者乎？愚雖不敏，請誦其所聞，以備采擇焉。夫滇，在星野屬井鬼之墟，在禹貢爲梁州之域。三代以前，未始通中國也。漢武時，始隸益州。沿至南詔，屢入西蜀，取其士民
translation_en:
…five hundred years later: this depends upon the individual alone. I, an unworthy student, privately cherish this aspiration too, but have yet to attain it. I ask only that you encourage my progress.

Fifth Policy Question
Yang Yiqi

Comment by Examiner Peng, an Instructor: Building city walls and establishing schools are the foremost tasks in Yunnan. This composition displays outstanding discernment and foresight; its proposals are demonstrably practicable. An ancient said that those who understand the needs of the times are outstanding men. Are you not such a man?

Comment by Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: Mature and experienced, neither forced nor superficial—a fine scholar.

The way of governing has two aspects: securing the people's peace and nurturing scholars. To secure the people's peace while seeking to safeguard their lives is to bring that work to its fullest realization; to nurture scholars while seeking to advance their virtue is to bring their nurture to its fullest realization. Thus one builds city walls for them and establishes schools for them. These are not merely plans for present needs, with results demanded overnight; they are intended to leave a framework capable of enduring and expanding. In planning for Yunnan, do you have anything that surpasses these measures? Though I am not gifted, allow me to recount what I have heard for your consideration and selection.

In the celestial divisions corresponding to terrestrial regions, Yunnan belongs to the domain of the lunar lodges Well and Ghost; in the Tribute of Yu, it lies within the territory of Liangzhou. Before the Three Dynasties, it had not yet established communication with the Central States. Under Emperor Wu of the Han, it first came under Yizhou. By the time of Nanzhao, its forces repeatedly entered western Shu and seized its scholars and common people…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而分置之文物之美漸以繁矣及洪武十
五年我
太祖遣三將軍帥師二十萬取其土地而郡縣
之治化之敷漸以溥矣繼而復徙天下豪
右以實之先後三十萬休養百餘年至於
今民庶熙熙人材彬彬外戶之不閉也垣
墉之不限也郁乎鄒魯之名區也淳乎蘇
湖之風聲也固將因俗順治與斯人相忘
於逸樂可也然或者以為意外之虞雖盛
===
世所不免目前之患在今日所當鑒也且
其地西通西域北接吐蕃南連交廣東限
羅夷俯而視之不知其幾千里誠邊徼沃
衍之所也人生其間者性習殊途風俗異
齊變故百出難於逆覩是故屯營之獷悍
也夷漢之侵侮也撲拇之相噬也僰玀之
相訾也沙儂之角毒也蒲縹之獰肆也雖
平定安集之謀招徠拊循之策在所當急
然久安長治之道潜移默化之術尤不可
punctuated:
而分置之，文物之美漸以繁矣。及洪武十五年，我太祖遣三將軍帥師二十萬，取其土地而郡縣之，治化之敷漸以溥矣。繼而復徙天下豪右以實之，先後三十萬。休養百餘年，至於今，民庶熙熙，人材彬彬，外戶之不閉也，垣墉之不限也。郁乎鄒魯之名區也，淳乎蘇湖之風聲也。固將因俗順治，與斯人相忘於逸樂可也。
然或者以為，意外之虞，雖盛世所不免；目前之患，在今日所當鑒也。且其地西通西域，北接吐蕃，南連交廣，東限羅夷，俯而視之，不知其幾千里，誠邊徼沃衍之所也。人生其間者，性習殊途，風俗異齊，變故百出，難於逆覩。是故屯營之獷悍也，夷漢之侵侮也，撲拇之相噬也，僰玀之相訾也，沙儂之角毒也，蒲縹之獰肆也，雖平定安集之謀、招徠拊循之策，在所當急，然久安長治之道、潜移默化之術，尤不可
translation_en:
…and settled them in various places, so that the splendor of its cultural life gradually flourished. In the fifteenth year of Hongwu, our Taizu dispatched three generals commanding an army of two hundred thousand, took possession of the territory, and organized it into prefectures and counties. The reach of government and moral transformation gradually broadened. Subsequently, powerful families from throughout the realm were again relocated there to populate it, totaling three hundred thousand people in successive migrations. After more than a hundred years of repose and recuperation, the common people today live contentedly, and men of talent display cultivated refinement. Outer doors are left unclosed, and walls impose no barriers. In cultural flourishing, it is a renowned region like Zou and Lu; in the purity of its customs, it enjoys the reputation of Suzhou and Huzhou. Surely one might govern in accordance with its customs and prevailing order, sharing such ease and happiness with these people that ruler and ruled forget one another.
Yet some hold that unforeseen dangers cannot be avoided even in a flourishing age, and that the troubles before our eyes demand scrutiny today. Moreover, this territory communicates with the Western Regions to the west, adjoins Tufan to the north, connects with Jiao and Guang to the south, and is bounded by the Luo peoples to the east. Looking down over it, one cannot tell how many thousands of li it extends: it is indeed a fertile and spacious frontier region. The people born there differ in dispositions and habits, and their customs vary in character. Unexpected disturbances arise in countless forms and are difficult to foresee. Thus there are the fierceness of the garrison troops, encroachments and insults between indigenous peoples and Han, mutual predation among the Pu and Mu [?], mutual recriminations among the Bo and Luo, contests in malice among the Sha and Nong, and the unbridled ferocity of the Pu and Piao [?]. Although plans for pacification and peaceful settlement, and policies for attracting people to submit and reassuring them, must receive urgent attention, the means of securing lasting peace and enduring order, and the arts of gradually and imperceptibly transforming customs, especially cannot be …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
無者故建城廣教此今日之所當預而圖
之當以漸者也易曰天險不可升也地險
山川丘陵也王公設險以守其國因天地
之險而為之城池緩急有所恃而趨焉此
聖人保民之心也後世若周城朔方以防
狄患漢令縣邑城以剗秦弊蓋亦有見乎
此滇之有故城惟雲南大理洪武中沐英
等增脩之又分命將校相地築城始於曲
靖達於騰衝南竟臨安西掎景東衛所相
===
望大小相維可謂周悉矣然土地既廣城
郭自遠往日安鳳之變起於尋甸首犯鄰
境嵩明之民扶老攜幼以奔滇城賊尾其
後慘不可言向使是州有城可恃且戰且
守與楊林相為掎角非惟可以保其室家
而烏合之衆豈敢徑趨滇城哉近築鶴慶
之城雖微意所在不敢與知然鶴慶當城
而澂江廣西諸府獨不當城乎昆陽晉寧
新興石屏劔川路南諸州縣獨不當城乎
punctuated:
無者。故建城廣教，此今日之所當預而圖之、當以漸者也。《易》曰：「天險不可升也，地險山川丘陵也，王公設險以守其國。」因天地之險而為之城池，緩急有所恃而趨焉，此聖人保民之心也。後世若周城朔方以防狄患，漢令縣邑城以剗秦弊，蓋亦有見乎此。滇之有故城，惟雲南、大理。洪武中，沐英等增脩之，又分命將校相地築城，始於曲靖，達於騰衝，南竟臨安，西掎景東，衛所相望，大小相維，可謂周悉矣。
然土地既廣，城郭自遠。往日安鳳之變，起於尋甸，首犯鄰境。嵩明之民扶老攜幼以奔滇城，賊尾其後，慘不可言。向使是州有城可恃，且戰且守，與楊林相為掎角，非惟可以保其室家，而烏合之衆豈敢徑趨滇城哉？近築鶴慶之城，雖微意所在不敢與知，然鶴慶當城，而澂江、廣西諸府獨不當城乎？昆陽、晉寧、新興、石屏、劔川、路南諸州縣獨不當城乎？
translation_en:
…cannot be dispensed with. Thus building city walls and extending education are matters that must now be planned in advance and pursued gradually. The Book of Changes says: “Heaven’s natural defenses cannot be ascended; earth’s natural defenses are mountains, rivers, hills, and ridges. Kings and lords establish defenses to safeguard their states.” Taking advantage of the natural defenses of heaven and earth to construct walls and moats, so that people have something to rely on and somewhere to flee in an emergency: this expresses the sage’s concern to protect the people. Later instances, such as the Zhou building walls at Shuofang to guard against incursions by the Di, and the Han ordering county towns to be walled to eliminate the abuses of Qin, likewise presumably reflected an understanding of this principle. In Dian, only Yunnan and Dali had old city walls. During the Hongwu reign, Mu Ying and others enlarged and repaired them. They also dispatched military officers to survey sites and build walls, beginning at Qujing and extending to Tengchong, reaching Lin’an in the south and securing Jingdong on the western flank. The guards and battalions stood within sight of one another, the larger and smaller supporting each other. These arrangements could indeed be called comprehensive.
Yet the territory is vast, and the walled towns are consequently far apart. In former days, An Feng’s rebellion arose in Xundian and first struck neighboring territory. The people of Songming supported their elderly and led their children as they fled toward the provincial capital, with the rebels pursuing them from behind. The misery was beyond words. Had that subprefecture possessed walls on which to rely, its people could have fought while defending themselves and provided mutual support with Yanglin. Not only could they have protected their households, but how would that motley rebel force have dared advance directly on the provincial capital? Walls have recently been built at Heqing. Although I dare not presume to know the subtle intentions behind this, if Heqing ought to have walls, should the prefectures of Chengjiang and Guangxi alone go without them? Should the subprefectures and counties of Kunyang, Jinning, Xinxing, Shiping, Jianchuan, and Lunan alone go without walls?

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
夫一人之失所吾之憂也而況不止於一
人乎誠能超然遠覽度地相時順人心之
所欲藉和雇以鳩工而版築興焉諸處並
舉而不以爲勞盡出官帑而不以爲費數
年之後城郭完固無事則散處以就耕牧
之便有警則入保以免劫掠之虞此萬世
之安也記曰古之教者家有塾黨有庠州
有序國有學因人性之同教之以學校明
道義而需器使焉此聖人養士之心也後
===
世若漢令天下郡邑建學唐四夷遣子入
學要亦有得乎此滇之舊有學亦惟雲南
大理洪武中張統等增置之乃令各有司
隨處建學因其郡縣相其州衛師儒有所
廩餼有常相觀而善相師以成可謂詳備
矣然初制有禁生徒未繁近日科目之盛
多在城市間及附郭下邑之士遠涉久出
以就師友力有不足業自中廢若使隨處
有學可依且耕且讀與諸生相爲切磋非
punctuated:
夫一人之失所，吾之憂也，而況不止於一人乎？誠能超然遠覽，度地相時，順人心之所欲，藉和雇以鳩工，而版築興焉，諸處並舉而不以爲勞，盡出官帑而不以爲費，數年之後，城郭完固，無事則散處以就耕牧之便，有警則入保以免劫掠之虞，此萬世之安也。
記曰：「古之教者，家有塾，黨有庠，州有序，國有學。」因人性之同，教之以學校，明道義而需器使焉，此聖人養士之心也。後世若漢令天下郡邑建學，唐四夷遣子入學，要亦有得乎此。滇之舊有學，亦惟雲南、大理。洪武中，張統等增置之，乃令各有司隨處建學，因其郡縣，相其州衛，師儒有所，廩餼有常，相觀而善，相師以成，可謂詳備矣。然初制有禁，生徒未繁。近日科目之盛，多在城市間及附郭。下邑之士遠涉久出，以就師友，力有不足，業自中廢。若使隨處有學可依，且耕且讀，與諸生相爲切磋，非
translation_en:
If even one person lacks a secure place, it is cause for my concern; how much more so when it is not merely one person? If we could truly take a broad and far-sighted view, assess the terrain and the timing, and follow the people’s wishes, we could assemble workers through paid hiring and begin building rammed-earth walls. Undertaking the work in all these places together should not be regarded as too burdensome, nor paying for it entirely from public funds as too costly. After a few years, the walls would be complete and secure. In peaceful times, people could live dispersed for convenience in farming and herding; when danger arose, they could enter the walls for protection and avoid the threat of plunder. This would bring security for ten thousand generations.
The Record of Rites says: “In the teaching of antiquity, there was a school at the household level, a xiang school in the dang, a xu school in the zhou, and an academy in the capital.” Taking account of the common nature of human beings, the sages educated them through schools, clarified the Way and righteousness, and prepared them for service according to their abilities. Such was the sages’ intention in nurturing scholars. In later ages, the Han ordered schools established in commanderies and towns throughout the realm, and under the Tang the peoples of the four quarters sent their sons to study. These, too, surely grasped something of this intention. The only places in Dian that had schools of old were Yunnan and Dali. During the Hongwu reign, Zhang Tong and others established additional schools; the responsible authorities were then ordered to establish schools everywhere, according to the distribution of prefectures and counties and with due consideration for subprefectures and guards. Teachers had places to teach, and grain allowances were regularly provided. Students improved by observing one another and achieved proficiency by learning from one another. These arrangements may be called thorough and complete. Yet the original regulations imposed restrictions, and students were not numerous. Recently, success in the examinations has been concentrated mostly in cities and towns and in the areas adjoining their walls. Scholars from outlying towns travel far and remain away for long periods to seek teachers and companions. When their means prove insufficient, their studies inevitably cease midway. If there were schools everywhere on which they could rely, they could farm while studying and refine their learning together with their fellow students; not only …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
惟可以必其成就而比屋之民寧不樂歸
至化哉近馬龍六凉祿豐之建學雖其情
懇乃為之請然馬龍六凉祿豐宜建學而
新興霑益獨不宜建乎武定路南彌勒建
水廣通定邊諸州縣獨不宜建乎夫一士
之失所吾之責也而況不止於一士乎誠
能毅然必行有教無類合酋長之子弟羣
民間之俊秀而黌舍興焉雖徧設之而不
以為多常廩之而不以為濫數年之後風
===
俗丕變家誦詩書戶習禮樂入以事其父
兄出以事其長上此萬世之功也或曰是
役也必勞民必傷財作無益害有益譬之
牧者驅之廣野順其性焉可也是不然凡
吾府庫之所有者皆吾民之所共者也吾
民之所有者皆府庫之所未共者也吾之
積也凡以濟民以利用者也出吾之所有
以衞吾民吾民安則一境之内舉安既安
且富則民自足府庫之未共者可長共也
punctuated:
惟可以必其成就，而比屋之民寧不樂歸至化哉？近馬龍、六凉、祿豐之建學，雖其情懇，乃為之請，然馬龍、六凉、祿豐宜建學，而新興、霑益獨不宜建乎？武定、路南、彌勒、建水、廣通、定邊諸州縣獨不宜建乎？夫一士之失所，吾之責也，而況不止於一士乎？誠能毅然必行有教無類，合酋長之子弟、羣民間之俊秀而黌舍興焉，雖徧設之而不以為多，常廩之而不以為濫。數年之後，風俗丕變，家誦詩書，戶習禮樂，入以事其父兄，出以事其長上，此萬世之功也。
或曰：「是役也，必勞民，必傷財，作無益害有益。譬之牧者，驅之廣野，順其性焉，可也。」是不然。凡吾府庫之所有者，皆吾民之所共者也；吾民之所有者，皆府庫之所未共者也。吾之積也，凡以濟民、以利用者也。出吾之所有以衞吾民，吾民安則一境之内舉安。既安且富，則民自足，府庫之未共者可長共也。
translation_en:
…only could their success be assured, but would not the people of every household gladly embrace the highest civilizing influence? Recently, schools were established in Malong, Liuliang, and Lufeng because their requests were earnest and petitions were therefore submitted on their behalf. Yet if Malong, Liuliang, and Lufeng ought to have schools, should Xinxing and Zhanyi alone have none? Should the subprefectures and counties of Wuding, Lunan, Mile, Jianshui, Guangtong, and Dingbian alone have none? If even one scholar lacks a proper place, that is our responsibility; how much more so when there is more than one! If we could resolutely put into practice the principle of education without distinctions of kind, bringing together the sons and younger kinsmen of chieftains and the outstanding talents among the common people, and establish schools for them, we would not consider the schools excessive even if they were established everywhere, nor consider regular stipends for their students indiscriminate. Within a few years, customs would be greatly transformed: every family would recite the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, and every household would practice rites and music. At home they would serve their fathers and elder brothers; outside they would serve their elders and superiors. This would be an achievement enduring for ten thousand generations.
Someone may say: “This undertaking will surely burden the people and deplete resources. Making what is useless harms what is useful. Consider a herdsman: he need only drive his animals onto the open plain and let them follow their nature.” This is not so. Everything in our treasuries and storehouses has been supplied by our people; what our people possess is what has not yet been supplied to those treasuries and storehouses. All that we accumulate is intended to aid the people and make resources useful. If we draw upon what we possess to protect our people, then when our people are secure, the whole territory will be secure. Once secure and prosperous, the people will have enough for themselves, and what they have not yet supplied to the treasuries and storehouses can continue to be supplied indefinitely.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
孝弟忠信士之懿德也而聰俊黠桀者乃
民間之美質也可與爲善可與爲不善者
也推士之懿德以成其美質美質成則一
方之教以興旣興且洽則無兵守固吾之
所有者可長有也且禦菑捍患以爲民也
移風易俗以善治也政之大經也
國初新造猶築城如彼建學如彼樓櫓壯麗
文教勃興況今承平之日財賦充溢而可
少靳於此乎故曰論大計者不惜小費又
===
曰見小利則大事不成通達國體者必有
以審此矣雖然猶有幾焉天下之事每患
於議論多而成功少者何也任之者難其
人也昔禹治洪水八年而後底績井田學
校孟子爲滕計者詳矣而陰壞於許行事
之難成易敗也類如此今欲築城建學非
有身任其責及同心體國之君子相爲先
後焉吾未見其可也噫此固滇之一大幾
也愚端有望於今日之百執事
punctuated: 孝弟忠信，士之懿德也；而聰俊黠桀者，乃民間之美質也，可與爲善，可與爲不善者也。推士之懿德以成其美質，美質成則一方之教以興；旣興且洽，則無兵守固，吾之所有者可長有也。且禦菑捍患，以爲民也；移風易俗，以善治也：政之大經也。國初新造，猶築城如彼，建學如彼，樓櫓壯麗，文教勃興；況今承平之日，財賦充溢，而可少靳於此乎？故曰：「論大計者不惜小費。」又曰：「見小利則大事不成。」通達國體者，必有以審此矣。雖然，猶有幾焉。天下之事，每患於議論多而成功少者，何也？任之者難其人也。昔禹治洪水，八年而後底績；井田學校，孟子爲滕計者詳矣，而陰壞於許行。事之難成易敗也，類如此。今欲築城建學，非有身任其責及同心體國之君子相爲先後焉，吾未見其可也。噫！此固滇之一大幾也。愚端有望於今日之百執事。
translation_en: Filial devotion, respect for elder brothers, loyalty, and trustworthiness are the fine virtues of scholars. Intelligence, talent, shrewdness, and boldness are fine natural endowments found among the common people; those possessing them can be guided toward either good or wrongdoing. Extend the fine virtues of scholars to bring these natural endowments to fulfillment. Once they are fulfilled, moral instruction throughout the region will flourish. Once it flourishes and permeates society, defenses will be secure even without troops, and what we possess can remain ours for a long time. Moreover, warding off disasters and averting harm serve the people; transforming prevailing customs promotes good government. These are the great guiding principles of administration. Even at the dynasty’s founding, when all was newly established, city walls and schools were built on such a scale: gate towers and watchtowers were imposing and splendid, and literary and moral instruction flourished vigorously. How much less, in these days of enduring peace, with tax revenues abundant, can we begrudge even a little expenditure on these things? Thus it is said: “Those who deliberate on great plans do not begrudge small expenses.” It is also said: “If one looks to small gains, great undertakings will not be accomplished.” Those who understand the essentials of governing the state will surely discern this clearly. Nevertheless, there remains a crucial consideration. Why is it that affairs throughout the realm so often suffer from abundant discussion but little accomplishment? Because it is difficult to find the right people to take responsibility for them. In ancient times, Yu brought the great flood under control, achieving success only after eight years. Mencius’s plans for Teng concerning the well-field system and schools were detailed, yet they were undermined covertly by Xu Xing. Such is the general pattern: undertakings are difficult to accomplish and easy to ruin. If we now wish to build city walls and establish schools, unless there are gentlemen who personally assume responsibility, together with others united in purpose and mindful of the state, supporting one another in leading and following, I cannot see how it can be done. Alas! This is indeed a momentous turning point for Dian. In my humble judgment, I place my hopes squarely in all those holding office today.

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
嘉靖丙午雲南鄉試事竣洛
濫司考校例當序諸末簡洛
嘗讀漢書至肅宗元和間滇
池出龍馬四白烏見因興起
學校漸遷其俗則知滇之有
學自漢始及讀司馬相如諸
===
傳其使西南夷嘗略斯榆舉
苞蒲而南中人士往往有受
學相如歸教鄉人者乃又知
西南之文業自相如始逮夫
五季之衰敝於南詔宋代之
末淪為異壤遂使碧雞金馬
徒聞其神黑水葉榆莫詳其
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序

嘉靖丙午，雲南鄉試事竣。洛濫司考校，例當序諸末簡。洛嘗讀《漢書》，至肅宗元和間，滇池出龍馬四，白烏見，因興起學校，漸遷其俗，則知滇之有學自漢始。及讀司馬相如諸傳，其使西南夷，嘗略斯榆，舉苞蒲，而南中人士往往有受學相如、歸教鄉人者，乃又知西南之文業自相如始。逮夫五季之衰，敝於南詔；宋代之末，淪為異壤。遂使碧雞金馬，徒聞其神；黑水葉榆，莫詳其
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In the bingwu year of Jiajing [1546], the Yunnan Provincial Examination was completed. I, Luo, having undeservedly been entrusted with examining the candidates, am customarily obliged to append a postface to the record. I once read in the History of the Han that during the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Suzong, four dragon-horses emerged from Lake Dian and white crows appeared. Schools were consequently established, gradually transforming local customs. From this I learned that schooling in Yunnan began under the Han. Later, reading the biographies of Sima Xiangru, I learned that on his mission to the southwestern peoples he had subdued Siyu [?] and taken Baopu [?], and that men of the southern region frequently studied under Xiangru and returned to teach their fellow villagers. From this I further learned that literary learning in the southwest began with Xiangru. During the decline of the Five Dynasties, however, the region suffered under Nanzhao; by the end of the Song, it had fallen into foreign hands. Thus, of Biji and Jinma, only their spirits remained known by report; as for Heishui and Yeyu, no one knew in detail their …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
地文敎方興而復斁其將有
所待哉洪惟我
高皇帝至仁洋溢長駕遠撫兼容
並包使六合八方懷生之物
皆得涵濡於休澤雖滇南亦
罔遐遺焉故甞
諭將臣有曰雲南之地稽之古
典氣厚風和人民尚兵上古
以為遐荒中古禹蹟所至以
別水土故地屬梁州之域自
漢隋唐皆為中國所統大哉
聖謨注意西南蓋其詳矣故今逖
陬裔土旣皆脫枹鼓以脩爼
豆且百餘年今
punctuated: 地。文敎方興而復斁，其將有所待哉？洪惟我高皇帝，至仁洋溢，長駕遠撫，兼容並包，使六合八方懷生之物皆得涵濡於休澤，雖滇南亦罔遐遺焉。故甞諭將臣有曰：「雲南之地，稽之古典，氣厚風和，人民尚兵。上古以為遐荒，中古禹蹟所至，以別水土，故地屬梁州之域。自漢隋唐，皆為中國所統。」大哉聖謨！注意西南，蓋其詳矣。故今逖陬裔土，旣皆脫枹鼓以脩爼豆，且百餘年。今
translation_en: …their locations. Literary culture and education had scarcely begun to flourish before declining again. Were they perhaps awaiting something yet to come? We reverently reflect that our Emperor Gao, his utmost benevolence overflowing, extended his reach afar to bring peace, embracing and accommodating all, so that every living creature throughout the universe and in every direction could be steeped in his gracious blessings. Even distant southern Yunnan was not neglected. Thus he once instructed his generals, saying: “Examining the ancient classics concerning the land of Yunnan, we find its vital energies abundant, its winds mild, and its people devoted to arms. In high antiquity it was regarded as a remote wilderness. In middle antiquity, Yu reached it in his travels to distinguish the waters and soils; hence its territory belonged within Liangzhou. Under the Han, Sui, and Tang, it was in each case governed by China.” How great was his sagely planning! His attention to the southwest was indeed thorough. Thus, throughout these distant corners and frontier lands, all have laid aside drumsticks and war drums to cultivate the rites of sacrificial vessels, and this has continued for more than a hundred years. Now …

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天子則天象地制禮作敎復以
聖學旨要揭爲敬一箴頒布寰海
西南雖遠而臣民之游庠序
皆得仰窺千聖相傳之心法
有非漢代詞章之習所能彷
彿於萬一者於戲盛哉滇士
之生於斯時何其幸也洛菲
謭叨校文之役竊謂文章也
者志氣之所發也然本于敎
化繫于風俗佐于山川今觀
滇士之文其舉理精而考辭
達非
聖學融液爲之本歟其思致深而
寄寓遠非漢文淵源爲之繫
punctuated:
天子則天象地，制禮作敎，復以聖學旨要揭爲《敬一箴》，頒布寰海。西南雖遠，而臣民之游庠序，皆得仰窺千聖相傳之心法，有非漢代詞章之習所能彷彿於萬一者。於戲，盛哉！滇士之生於斯時，何其幸也！

洛菲謭，叨校文之役，竊謂文章也者，志氣之所發也，然本于敎化，繫于風俗，佐于山川。今觀滇士之文，其舉理精而考辭達，非聖學融液爲之本歟？其思致深而寄寓遠，非漢文淵源爲之繫
translation_en:
…the Son of Heaven models himself on Heaven and patterns himself on Earth, establishes ritual and institutes instruction. He has further set forth the essential principles of sage learning in the Admonition on Revering the One (Jingyi zhen) and promulgated it throughout the realm. Although the southwest is distant, his subjects who study in its schools can all reverently glimpse the teaching of the mind transmitted from sage to sage through the ages—something that the Han dynasty’s practice of literary composition could not remotely approach, even in the smallest degree. Ah, how splendid! How fortunate are the scholars of Yunnan to have been born in this age!

I, Luo, humble and shallow in learning, have undeservedly been entrusted with evaluating examination essays. I venture to say that literary composition expresses aspiration and vital spirit; yet it is rooted in moral instruction, bound to local customs, and aided by mountains and rivers. Looking now at the writings of Yunnan’s scholars, I find their exposition of principles precise and their choice of words lucid. Is this not because the permeating influence of sage learning provides their foundation? Their thought is profound and the significance conveyed far-reaching: is this not because they are linked to the deep sources of Han writing…

title: 嘉靖二十五年雲南鄉試錄
text:
歟其負氣厚而稱物芳非碧
雞黑水爲之佐歟故是錄之
作有以見四履之盛焉有以
見化成之候焉有以見
大明之隆焉而人文之宣鬱風氣
之開塞係乎一方者非所論
矣多士旣躬逢
===
盛際而獲登是錄可不思自樹
立以求無負於
聖化哉若相如特援以遡文業之
自爾非敢以是望多士也多
士幸相與勗哉
河南開封府中牟縣儒學敎
諭彭洛謹序
punctuated:
歟？其負氣厚而稱物芳，非碧雞黑水爲之佐歟？故是錄之作，有以見四履之盛焉，有以見化成之候焉，有以見大明之隆焉。而人文之宣鬱、風氣之開塞，係乎一方者，非所論矣。多士旣躬逢盛際，而獲登是錄，可不思自樹立，以求無負於聖化哉？若相如，特援以遡文業之自爾，非敢以是望多士也。多士幸相與勗哉！
河南開封府中牟縣儒學敎諭彭洛謹序。
translation_en:
…is it not? Their writing has substantial vital force and describes things with elegance: is this not owing to the supporting influence of Biji Mountain and the Heishui River? Thus, the compilation of this record reveals the flourishing condition of the realm’s territories, the signs of transformation through instruction, and the greatness of the Great Ming. As for the flourishing or suppression of literary culture, and the openness or obstruction of prevailing influences insofar as these concern a single region, these are beyond the present discussion. Having personally encountered this flourishing age and gained inclusion in this record, how can these many scholars fail to consider establishing themselves, seeking thereby not to fall short of the sage sovereign’s transforming instruction? As for Xiangru, I have cited him merely to trace the origins of literary accomplishment; I would not presume to make this the measure of my expectations for these scholars. May you scholars encourage one another!
Preface respectfully composed by Peng Luo, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhongmu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.
